Short form of August. This name is also sometimes considered a direct adoption of Estonian agu "early dawn".
Derived from Guanche *awabanahizan, meaning "son of the climber".
Derived from Guanche *awaboreg, meaning "son of the proud".
Derived from Guanche awašîš, meaning "son of brightness".
Derived from Guanche awakoromos, meaning "son of the wrinkled".
Derived from Guanche awaleš, meaning "committed; upright; telling".
Derived from Guanche awamuh, meaning "son of the mumbling".
Derived from Guanche awanaɣuš, meaning "son of the cutter".
Means "Holy Waters" in Spanish. This name is given after a local title of Mary, Nuestra Señora de Agua Santas (meaning "Our Lady of Holy Waters") venerated in Villanueva del Río near Sevilla, Spain.
Of uncertain meaning, this was the personal name of the founder of the Jin dynasty, Emperor Taizu.
Unaccented form of Águeda that is used mainly in America.
Gascon, Provençal and Niçard variant of Agata.
Interpreted to mean "the great sun" in Taino.

Means "eagle" in Spanish (see Aquila), taken from the titles of the Virgin Mary, La Virgen del Águila and Nuestra Señora del Águila, meaning "The Virgin of the Eagle" and "Our Lady of the Eagle" respectively.She is the patroness of Alcalá de Guadaíra in the Andalusian province of Sevilla, hence the name's very high concentation there.
Galician variant of Agilulf.Aguiúlfo was an obscure king of Galicia from 456.
Sundanese diminutive of masculine names containing the sound gum (or other similar sounds), such as Gumilar.
Derived from Persian آخوند (akhund) meaning "cleric, teacher". This is the name of a heroine in the Nart sagas.
Derived from the Germanic name elements agi "awe, terror" or egg "edge of a weapon" and gunnr "battle, fight".
Means "stranger" or "gathered together" in Hebrew. In the Bible, he is a son of Jakeh and a contributor to Proverbs.

column3: 亜久里, 安久里, 阿久里, 亜久利, 安久利, 阿久利, 亜久梨, 亜久理, 亜久莉(Japanese Kanji)|あぐり(Japanese Hiragana)|アグリ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: As a unisex name, this name combines 亜 (a, tsu.gu) meaning "Asia, come after, rank next," 安 (an, yasu, yasu.i, yasu.maru, yasu.raka, a) meaning "cheap, low, peaceful, rested" or 阿 (a, o, omone.ru, kuma) meaning "corner, flatter, nook" with 久 (kyuu, ku, hisa.shii) meaning "long time" & 里 (ri, sato) meaning "parent's home, ri (unit of distance - equal to 3.927 km), village."As a masculine name, it's the same except that the last kanji is replaced by 利 (ri, ki.ku) which means "advantage, benefit, profit, gain."As a feminine name, it combines 亜 with 久 & 梨 (ri, nashi) meaning "pear tree," 理 (ri, kotowari) meaning "justice, logic, reason, truth" or 莉 (rai, ri, rei), part of 茉莉 (matsuri) meaning "jasmine."One (male) bearer of this name is former racing driver Aguri Suzuki (鈴木 亜久里) (1960-).
Short form of Agustín and Agustina.
Means "the whirling dancer", deriving from the Akkadian words gâšum ("to dance") and gūštum ("dance"). Attested as an epithet for Ishtar in the Hymn of Agushaya.
From the name of the month of August (Agustus in Indonesian), usually used as a given name for a child born in August.

Variant of Augustine 1. Mexican army general and politician Augustine I of Mexico (1783 - 1824) is a notable bearer.
Corsican and Sicilian form of Augustinus.
Allegedly a Lugbara name from Uganda.
Means "mistress of fire" in Kalmyk Orit, possibly influenced by the Russian word огонь (ogon') meaning "fire".
Means "eloquent and long-lived" in Mongolian, ultimately derived from Tibetan ངག་དབང་ (ngag-dbang) meaning "powerful speech, empowered word" and ཚེ་རིང་ (tshe-ring) meaning "long life."
Norwegian and Swedish form of Agvaldr.
Derives from Old Norse elements agi "awe, fear" and valdr "ruler".

Haitian name meaning "spirit of the sea". In Vodou, and especially in Haiti, Agwé (also spelt Goue, Agoueh, or Agive), is a loa who rules over the sea, fish, and aquatic plants, as well as the patron loa of fishermen and sailors.

Germanic name, in which the second element is win meaning "friend". The first element, ag, is of uncertain origin, though the accepted explanation is that it comes from Proto-Germanic *agjo "sharp, pointed". Because of that, it also means "edge", as in the sharp cutting side of a sword - which is why the meaning of the element has ultimately come to be "sword". See also Anglo-Saxon ecg (in e.g. Egbert) or Old High German ekka (New High German ecke "corner"; see Ekkehard). Other possibilities for the meaning and origin of ag include: Gothic agan "to fear, to be afraid", Old Norse agi "unrest, agitation", Gothic ahjan "to believe" and Old Norse aka "to do, to act".
A form of Igraine, the mother of King Arthur
Means "saviour of the nation" in Akan.
Tatar and Bashkir form of Azam.
From the Bashkir Аҡ (Aǩ) meaning "white, bright, pure" and зибә (zibä) meaning "beautiful".
Means "one, unique, matchless" in Arabic. In Islamic tradition الأحد (al-Ahad) is one of the 99 names of Allah. This name is also used as an alternate transcription of Azerbaijani Əhəd.
Possibly derived from ahahuiya "to rejoice, to celebrate, to take pleasure".

From Sanskrit अहल्य (ahalya) meaning "unploughed, unfurrowed, not arable". In Hindu literature this is the name of the wife of the sage Gautama Maharishi. After being seduced by Indra (disguised as Gautama), she is cursed by her husband but eventually freed by the hero Rama.

From Sanskrit अहन् (áhan) meaning "day". Ahaan is a more common transcription of this name.

column12: One of the elements of this name is the goddess Neith.
Ahania is the Emanation, or female counterpart, of Urizen, Zoas of reason, in William Blake's mythology. She is the representation of pleasure and the desire for intelligence.
Possibly a Belarusian form of Agape.
Meaning "behind the rampart." In 1 Chronicles 4:8, Aharhel is the son of Harum of the tribe of Judah.
Armenian form of Aaron, derived directly from Hebrew Aharon.
Feminine form of Aharon. A known bearer of the name is Israeli singer-songwriter Rona Kenan, full name Aharona Rachel Kenan (1979-).
Ahasbai, the son of the Maachathite, was the father of Eliphelet, one of King David's Warriors (2 Samuel 23:34).
An alias used by Newel K. Whitney in a few chapters of Mormon scripture.
Means "their sister", deriving from the Akkadian element aḫātu ("sister") combined with the suffix -(aš)šunu ("for them (masculine plural), to them, towards them"),
German form of the Biblical name Ahasueros.The name was borne by Ahasver von Brandt, a German historian.The name is also tied to the lengends about the Wandering Jew.
German form of Ahasueros as used in current bible translations.

Possibly means "sister of the king" in Amorite. Name borne by a princess of Amurru (fl. 1265 BCE), who would go on to become queen of Ugarit (modern day Ras Shamna in Northern Syria) as the wife of King Niqmepa.
Variant of Ahava, used to describe the love of God. Famous bearer is Israeli Muay Thai fighter Ahavat Hashem Gordon (born 2.5.2006)

Ahaya (ca. 1710 – 1783) was the first recorded chief of the Alachua band of the Seminole tribe. He was born to the Muskogean-speaking Oconee, who were originally from central Georgia. His people settled along the Chattahoochee River in North Florida when he was a small boy. They were among the Native Americans who left Georgia and Alabama to escape encroachment by English colonists.
Meaning "has held" in Hebrew, from a diminutive form of Jehoahaz.

From Hebrew אֲחַזְיָהוּ (ʼĂḥazyāhū) meaning "held by Yahweh", derived from the roots אֲחַזְ ('ahaz) meaning " to hold, to grasp" and יְהוֹ (yeho) referring to the Hebrew God. The name Jehoahaz is derived from the same roots in reverse order. This was the name of two kings, one in Israel and one in Judah.
Variant of Abbe recorded in the 19th century in East Frisia.
An Egyptian derivative of Abraham, according to a book on the language, written by Joseph Smith.
An Egyptian variation of Abram 1 according to Joseph Smith. It is defined as "father of the faithful".
Alternate transcription of Ahsan chiefly used in Northern Africa.
Means "one who has stars for a blanket" in Cree.
Meaning unknown. This is the Mayan god of eclipses.
From Arabic عَهْد (ʿahd) meaning "knowledge, fulfillment, observance".
From Arabic عَهْد (ʿahd) meaning "knowledge", "observance, adherence, fulfillment", or "commitment, obligation".
Etymology uncertain, possibly from the Uzbek word ahd meaning "oath, pact".
Derived from the word (ahea) meaning "gentle breeze" or "soft wind" in Hawaiian.
Means "(maternal) uncle" in ancient Hebrew. (compare Ahab). This name is derived from the combination of the elements אח (ah') "brother" and אם (em) "mother"

Of unknown origin and meaning, albeit a connection to Welsh aches, a word denoting the sound of the water clashing on the shore, has been suggested. In Breton legend, Ahez is always described as the daughter of King Gralon, sometimes described as a sorceress, enchantress, fairy or giantess, and often, though not always, considered identical with Dahud. Gralon was the king of Kêr-Is, a city built on land reclaimed from the sea and rich in commerce and the arts which was protected from the water by a dike with a gate that was opened for ships during low tide. Unlike her pious father, Ahez was a wayward and frivolous young woman, an unrepentant sinner. One night, while the king slept, Ahez stole the keys, a symbol of royalty, from her father, either to allow her lover inside for a banquet or after being persuaded to do so by her lover. Believing she was opening the city gates, the princess mistakenly opened the gates of the dike and the sea inundated the city. Everyone in the city was killed, apart from Ahez and Gralon who had been woken up by the voice of a saint who urged him to flee. The king took his daughter with him, but as the water was about to overtake Gralon, a voice called out: "Throw the demon thou carriest into the sea, if thou dost not desire to perish." The father threw the daughter off the horse's back and was saved. When the waves swallowed her, Ahez became a mermaid who continues haunting the sea. To this day, she can be seen combing her golden hair and singing sad songs.

From Egyptian jꜥḥ-ḥtp meaning "Iah is satisfied" or "the moon is content", derived from the name of the god Iah (literally "the moon") combined with ḥtp "peace, satisfaction". Name borne by a Queen consort of Egypt, Great Royal Wife and Queen Regent of the Seventeenth Dynasty of Egypt.
Means "my brother is help" or "my brother is a helper" in Hebrew. This is the name of two Old Testament characters.
From Navajo ahigą́ "they fight or combat each other; they kill each other" or ahígą́ "you fight or combat each other; you kill each other".
Prince of the tribe of Asher.

Means "brother of Yahweh" in Hebrew, derived from אָח (ʾaḥ) meaning "brother" and יָהּ (yah) referring to the Hebrew God. In the Old Testament, this was the name of several characters, including a Levite prophet in Shiloh who foretold Jeroboam that he would be king.
From ahikāroa meaning "burning fires of continuous occupation" in Māori.
Means "my brother has risen, raised brother" in Hebrew, derived from אָח (ʾaḥ) meaning "brother" and קוּם (qum) meaning "to raise". This is the name of a delegate in the Old Testament.
Bosnian and Croatian form of Achilles.

Ahilud is the father of Jehoshaphat, who serves as court recorder to David (2 Samuel 8:16) and Solomon (1 Kings 4:3). In 1 Kings 4:12, Ahilud is the father of Baana, an official in Solomon's court sent to gather provisions in Taanach and Megiddo, and Beth Shan.

From Hebrew אֲחִימַעַץ‎ (ʾĂḥīmaʿaṣ) meaning "brother of the council", from the combination of אָח (ʾaḥ) meaning "brother" and מוֹעָצָה (mo'atsá) meaning "council". This was the name of the son of the high priest Zadok, who was the first to bring the news of the defeat of Absalom to King David.
Meaning "brother of the right hand / brother of a gift."

Means "my brother is king" in Hebrew, from אָח (ʾaḥ) meaning "brother" combined with י (i) "my" and מֶלֶךְ (meleḵ) "king". This is the name of several characters in the Old Testament, including a high priest of Israel who is wrongly executed for treason on King Saul's orders.
From Japanese 愛(a) meaning "love", 日(hi) meaning "day" and 美(mi) meaning "beautiful". Other kanji combinations are also possible.

From Japanese 明日 (ahi) meaning "tomorrow" combined with 南 (na) meaning "south". Other kanji combinations are possible.

Meaning, "My Brother Is Noble." Son of Iddo, is one of the twelve commissariat officers appointed by Solomon in so many districts of his kingdom to raise supplies by monthly rotation for his household. He was appointed to the district of Mahanaim (1 Kings 4:14), east of Jordan.
Name born by German-Bulgarian singer Nora Nova, Ahinora Kumanova

From the Aramaic name hyqr meaning "My brother is precious".The Story of Ahiqar, also known as the Words of Ahikar, is a story first attested in Aramaic from the fifth century BCE that circulated widely in the Middle and Near East. It has been characterised as one of the earliest 'international books' of world literature.This name appears in the deuterocanonical Book of Tobit, where he is a relative of Tobit who becomes a prominent administrator in the court of king Sennacherib.
Means "my brother is evil" in Hebrew. In the Bible, Ahira was a son of Enan. He was the chief of the tribe of Naphthali at the time of the census in the wilderness of Sinai.
Means "brother of craft" or "my brother is exalted" in Hebrew. In the Bible, he is a son of Benjamin.

column12: Means "brother of support" or "my brother supports", derived from the Hebrew noun אָח (ʾaḥ) meaning "brother" (combined with the letter י (i) "my", thus "my brother" or "brother of") and the verb סמך (samak) "to support, to uphold". In the Old Testament Ahisamach of the tribe of Dan was the father of Aholiab.
Means "my brother has sung" in Hebrew. In 1 Kings, he is mentioned in Solomon's list of heads of department.

Means "my brother is goodness" or "brother of goodness" in Hebrew, from אָח (ʾaḥ) meaning "brother" combined with י (i) "my" and טוֹב (ṭov) meaning "good". This was the name of a High Priest of Israel.

Possibly means "turtle", deriving from the Classic Maya element ahk-al. This was occasionally used as an element in the names of Maya royalty.
Combination of Sami ahke "age" and Beaivi.
Combination of Sami ahke "age" and Mielat.
Female version of Ahki which means Brother

In Eskimo folklore there is a skeleton-ghost named Ahkiyyini. He was always dancing when he was alive, and his skeleton comes back every so often to do a jig that shakes the ground and turns boats over in the river. He makes his own music, using his arm bone as a drumstick and his shoulder blade as the drum.
From Sanskrit आह्लादिनी (āhlādinī) meaning "causing delight, bestowing joy".

This name comes from the root אחל ('hl), which has no known meaning. The root derives from אחלה ('ahlah), meaning "ah that...!". The majority belief is that the name means "O Would That!".There are two people named Ahlai in the Bible. The first, mentioned in 1 Chronicles 2:31, is the child of Sheshan. Some versions of the Bible translate the verse as Ahlai being the son of Sheshan, but 1 Chronicles 2:34 states that Sheshan has only daughters, meaning this Ahlai is most likely a woman.The second Ahlai, mentioned in 1 Chronicles 11:41, is the father of Zabad, one of David's warriors.
Ukrainian Orthodox canonical form of Ahlaya.
Variant of Ale 2 recorded in the 17th century for men and in the 17th and 18th century for women in East Frisia.
Alternate transcription of Arabic احلام (see Ahlam) chiefly used in North Africa.
Variant of Ahle recorded in the 17th century in East Frisia.
Low German variant of Adelheid used in the 17th and 18th centuries.
Danish and Swedish form of Adelmann.
Containing name elements adal and rîki recorded from the 15th to 20th centuries in East Frisia.
Combination of the name Ahmad and Persian جان (jān) meaning "soul".
Combination of the given name Ahmad and the Turkic title khan meaning "ruler, leader".
Form of Ahmad used in parts of French-influenced West Africa.
Combination of Ahmad and Reza. It is sometimes transcribed into Latin characters with a dash or a space.
Combination of the name Ahmad and Persian شاه (shah) meaning "king".
Combination of Ahmad and دين (dīn) meaning "religion, faith, belief".
A Persian combination of Ahmad and Abdullah.
Means "red" in Arabic from the root ح-م-ر (ḥ-m-r) related with this colour.
Alternate transcription of Uyghur ئەخمەتجان (see Ehmetjan).
Combination of the Islamic name Ahmed and the Kazakh word jan, meaning "soul" (of Persian origin). Kazakh variant spelling of Akhmetzhan.
Means "I bring" or "I carry" in Arabic.
Means "immortal, something that does not die" in Nahuatl, derived from the negative prefix a- and micqui "corpse, dead body".
Compound name composed of Ahmet or Ahmyet, the Tatar version of Ahmad and galii, from the same root as Ali 1. It is often stated to mean 'Celebrated Ali' and given as the given name of the saint Ali.
Tatar and Bashkir form of Ahnaf.
Means "bent, crooked, clubfooted" in Arabic. It can also figuratively mean "devout, pious" (in the sense of being 'bent' towards religion).
Variant of Anne 2 recorded in the 16th century in East Frisia.
Belarusian and Ukrainian form of Agniya.
Alternate transcription of Korean Hangul 안종 (see Anjong).
Means "line" in Māori. Also means "to shine light" in Māori.
Name of Ewa origin, meaning "peaceful" or "bringer of peace".

Means "day god; day has dawned; feast day" in Tongan. Ahoeitu was the first king of the Tu'i Tonga dynasty in Tongan mythology. The god Eitumatupua climbed down from the sky on a great tree, and took a worm descendant, Ilaheva, as his wife. Returning to the sky, the god left the woman and her child, Ahoeitu, on the Earth.

Means "father's tent", derived from the Hebrew nouns אֹהֶל ('ohel) meaning "tent" and אָב (ʾav) meaning "father". In the Old Testament, Aholiab or Oholiab son of Ahisamakh, of the tribe of Dan, worked under Bezalel as the deputy architect of the Tabernacle (also known as the Tent of Meeting) and the implements which it housed, including the Ark of the Covenant. He is described in Exodus 38:23 as a master of carpentry, weaving and embroidery.
Means "shining sky" in Māori, from aho "light" and rangi "sky".
Means "bright moonlight" in Maori. From aho "light" and roa "big".
Derived from Baoulé we "Thursday", referring to the day of the week on which the child was born and hence to be understood as "born on Thursday".
Means "she who is the beginning and end" in Meitei.
Means "wooden lance" or "kills with a lance" in Kiowa. Ahpeahtone (1856–1931) was a chief of the Kiowa tribe in Oklahoma, who is regarded as the last traditional chief of the tribe.
Prefer to earn there keep instead of it being a given or birthright those that prefer not to have hand out instead work hard for there position.
Means "ripe chestnut" or "ripe acorn" in Korean.
From Arabic أحرار (aḥrar), the plural form of حر (ḥurr) meaning "free, unimpeded" as well as "genuine, pure, good".

column3: 아리(Korean Hangul)|雅利, 䢝里, etc.(Korean Hanja)

column12: Variant of Aaron. Ahron was given to 59 boys in 2018 per the SSA.
Tajik and Uzbek form of Ahrar.
From the Uzbek word ahror meaning "one able to free oneself from worldly desires".
Combination of the given name Ahror and the Persian word جان (jân) meaning "soul, life".
Etymology uncertain, perhaps an Uzbek femnine form of Ahsan.

column3: احسان الحق(Pashto, Shahmukhi, Sindhi-Arabic, Urdu)|ਅਹਿਸਾਨ-ਉਲ-ਹੱਕ(Gurmukhi)|अहसान-उल-हक(Hindi)|اہسان‌الہک(Balochi)|এহসান উল হক(Bengali)|یِحسانُ الحَق(Kashmiri Arabic)|यिह्सान-उल-हक(Kashmiri Devanagari)
column12: Perso-Arabic-origin compound name consisting of the elements Ahsan and ḥaqq.

Created from an anagram of Ashoka, pitched by George Lucas after Ashoka the Great, the Indian Emperor of the Maurya Empire. Ahsoka Tano is a Jedi knight first introduced as Anakin Skywalker's Padawan apprentice in 'Star Wars: the clone Wars'.
From Sino-Korean 我 (a) meaning "the self, the ego" and 先 (seon) meaning "first".
Tatar version of the masculine given name Akhtar.
Variant of Ate 3 recorded in the 17th and 19th century in East Frisia.
Derived from Arabic أدهم‎‎ (ādham) meaning "black, dark".
Derived from Cheyenne ȧhtóno'e "under, below" and vé'ho'e "trickster, spider, white man". This is the name of a Cheyenne god who lives under the ground.

Variant of Atziri.For some reason, in the United States, the spelling Ahtziri emerged as the most popular (of Atziri, Ahtziri, Atziry, Ahtziry, and Athziri, all of which occur in the U.S. Social Security Administration public name dataset) during the second half of the 1990s.
Means "to tend, to foster, to bring up" in Maori.
Meaning associated with health, strength, and rapid growth.
Means "joyous waters", derived from Nahuatl ahuiliztli "joy, pleasure, enjoyment, recreation; pleasant" and atl "water".
Means "otter" in Nahuatl, derived from atl "water" and huitzotl "porcupine".Borne by a ruler of the Aztecs from 1468 to 1502.
Means "sky alter" in Hawaiian, from the elements ahu, meaning "alter" and lani, meaning "sky, heaven".
Derived from Tahitian ahu meaning "clothes, tapa cloth" and mere meaning "parental grief, grief of a parent".

From the name of a mountain in the Basque region of Spain whose Basque name Ahuñamendi is derived from Basque ahuña "small goat" and mendi "mountain".In Basque mythology, this mountain is home to Jaun Gorri (known as the "Seigneur rouge" in French) who guards an orchard on the mountain top in which the fruits of immortality grow.
Referring to either the creator god Ahura Mazda or the various other ahuras of the Avesta. Meaning, "lord" or "spirit."

Means "she who belongs to Ahura" in Avestan, from the name Ahura, referring to either the creator god Ahura Mazda or the various other ahuras of the Avesta, combined with the feminine suffix -ani meaning "companion, wife, mate". In ancient Persian mythology this referred to a class of female water divinity.
Borne by a notable Guanche ambassador from Gran Canaria.
From Tahitian ahu meaning "clothes, fabric, garment" and tiare meaning "flower, blossom".
Means "red dress" from the Tahitian phrase ʻahu ʻura ariʻi o te toʻo ao te rā meaning "royal red robe of the sunset".
From ahu ura nui meaning "big hot flame" or "large red cloth".
Borne by Ahuzam, son of Ashur, the father or founder of Tekoa. (1 Book of Chronicles 4:6).
Means "possession" in Hebrew. This name is borne by an associate of Abimelech, king of Gerar.
Ahva is from the Hebrew word, Ahava (ah-hav-ah.) Ahva is a twist on the more common, Ava. It sounds more exotic and lively. Ahva can be used for either gender.
Finnish form of Agabus or Afanasi.
Ayah is a name referencing a verse in the Quran. An Ayah makes up chapters in the Surah.Arabic meaning: "sign," "miracle," or "verse"

column3: 아현(Korean Hangul)|雅賢, 亜賢, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 雅 (a) meaning "elegant, graceful, refined" combined with 賢 (hyeon) meaning "virtuous, worthy, wise". Other hanja combinations are possible.

column3: 아연(Korean Hangul)|娥娟, 娥緣, 娥淵, etc.(Korean Hanja)

column12: Meaning unknown. A famous person is John Brant, who was a Mohawk leader and had a role in the War of 1812.
From the battle of trench (Ahzab)It is also a surah in quranMeans groups or parties
Derived from Old Norse ái meaning "great-grandfather, ancestor". In Norse mythology, this is the name of both a dwarf and the husband of Edda 2.
Sundanese diminutive of feminine names containing the sound ai (or other similar sounds), such as Aisyah or Anggraini.

column3: 皑皑, 爱爱, 艾艾, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 皑皑 (ái'ái) meaning "snow-white". This name can be formed from other hanzi as well.
Aiai is a fisherman from Hawaiian mythology. Derived from a'ia'i meaning "bright, fair, clear" or 'ai'ai meaning "dependent" in Hawaiian.
Means "son of Aiakes/Aiakos" in Greek, derived from the name Aiakes or Aiakos combined with the patronymic suffix ἴδης (ides).
Possibly related to Aiara. This is the name of an hermitage in the town of Alegría-Dulantzi in Álava, Spain, located in the famous pilgrimage route of St. James's Way.
Possibly a form of Aia or Aina 2 or Ian.
Invented name based on names like Edurne and Bakarne.
Means "son of Ajax" in Greek. It is derived from the name Aias (the original Greek form of Ajax) combined with the patronymic suffix ἴδης (ides).
From the name of a town in the Basque region of Spain.
Possibly derived from Basque aiher "slope" or alha "pasture" (see Ayala). This is the name of a town in the Basque Country.
From Turkic ay meaning "moon, month" and beg meaning "chieftain, master".
Derived from Kazakh aй (ai) meaning "moon" and бала (bala) meaning "child". Some provide the meaning as "like the moon" or "beautiful like the moon".
From Kazakh ай (ay) meaning "moon" and Persian بانو (bânu) meaning "lady, woman".
Derived from Kazakh ай (ay) meaning "moon" and барша (barsha) "fabric, brocade, cloth" (of Persian origin).

A majestic name combining Ai ("Moon") and Barshyn ("brocade" / "gold-woven fabric" / "female eagle"). Historically, "Barshyn" signifies both the regal texture of ancient silks and the fierce spirit of a nomadic huntress. As the heroine of the legendary Epic of Alpamysh, she embodies the pinnacle of loyal, sharp-witted feminine power. This name represents a woman who is as radiant and unattainable as the moon, yet possesses the unbending courage of a warrior.
From Kazakh ай (ay) meaning "moon" and the past tense of беруге (beruge) "to give".
This name was used in the poem "A Kite for Aibhín" by Seamus Heaney, published in 2010.
Means "beautiful" or "the lovely one" in Irish. It's an alternate name for an Irish spirit and queen of the Banshees, also known as Aeval.
From Scottish Gaelic aibhse meaning "sprite" or "specter".

column3: 亜以美, 愛美, 藍弥, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 愛 (ai) meaning "love, affection" combined with 美 (bi) meaning "beautiful". Other combinations of kanji characters are possible.This name is also used as a variant of Aimi, influenced by the name and English word Ivy.
Possibly an alteration of Abilene influenced by Maybelline. This is the name of one of the main characters in Kathryn Stockett's novel 'The Help' (2009) and the subsequent movie adaptation (2011).

column3: 爱兵, 艾兵, 艾冰, 皑炳, etc.(Chinese)|愛兵, 艾兵, 艾冰, 皑炳, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love, affection", 艾 (ài) meaning "sagebrush, wormwood" or 皑 (ái) meaning "pure white, snow white" combined with 兵 (bīng) meaning "army, troops, weapon, soldier", 冰 (bīng) meaning "ice" or 炳 (bǐng) meaning "bright, luminous, glorious". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
Either a Sami form of Aimo or taken from Sami áibmu "air".
Derived from Kazakh ай (ay) meaning "moon" and бол (bol) meaning "to be, to occur".
From Kazakh ай (ay) meaning "moon" and болат (bolat) meaning "steel" (of Persian origin).
Derived from the Irish word for April.
From the Germanic element ag, possibly meaning "edge" or "sharp".
Western African elaboration of Aïcha (see Aisha).

column3: 蔼琛, 爱忱, 爱臣, 霭琛, 霭宸, etc.(Chinese)|藹琛, 愛忱, 愛臣, 靄琛, 靄宸, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From the Chinese 蔼 (ǎi) meaning "lush, affable, friendly", 爱 (ài) meaning "love, affection", or 霭 (ǎi) meaning "mist, haze" and 琛 (chēn) meaning "treasure", 忱 (chén) meaning "sincerity, honesty", 臣 (chén) meaning "minister, statesman", or 宸 (chén) meaning "mansion, palace". Other character combinations are also possible.

column3: アイチ(Japanese Katakana)|愛知, 亜壱, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: Like the surname and place name, it could be from 愛 (ai) meaning "love, affection" and 知 (chi) meaning "wisdom, knowledge, intelligence". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Combination of Ai 1 and Chiyo.This was also a masculine name, being used as the childhood name of Sengoku period general Edo Michimasa (江戸 通政) (1538-1567).This name is extremely rare.
Gallicized version of Aichouche, ''Lalla Aicha'' an regent of Touggourt during the minority of her son Abd ar-Rahman (1833–1846) can be known as Aïchouche
From the Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love, affection" and 春 (chūn) meaning "spring (season)". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From Kyrgyz ай (ay) meaning "moon" combined with чурек (churek), a type of sweet flatbread baked in Central Asia. In the Kyrgyz epic Manas, Aichurek is the wife of Semetey, and the mother of Seitek.
From Kyrgyz ай (ay) meaning "moon" combined with чүрөк (churok) meaning "duck", used as an epithet of beauty in Kyrgyz folklore.
From the Chinese 蔼 (ǎi) meaning "lush, affable, friendly" and 慈 (cí) meaning "kind, loving".
Variant of Aisha possibly modelled on Alicia.
A diminutive of any of various names whose prototheme is a derivative of Proto-Germanic *aiganą 'to own, to possess'.
From Arabic عِيد (ʿīd) meaning "festival, holiday, feast".
In former times, this name was a diminutive of Adélaïde. Nowadays, however, it is usually used as the Gallicized form of Aida.
Variant of Ada 1 or feminine form of Aidan.
Alternate transcription of Arabic عائدة (see Aida), as well as the Indonesian and Malay form.
From Turkish ay meaning "moon, month" combined with demir "iron".

column3: Айдархан, Айыыдархан(Kazakh, Tatar, Kyrgyz, Yakut)|ايدارخان(Kazakh Arabic)
column12: Alternate transcription of Kazakh/Tatar/Kyrgyz/Yakut Айдархан (see Aydarkhan).
Derived from Basque aide "air", Aide is a supernatural entity that either helps or hinders the living. He could manifest herself in both good (gentle breeze) and evil (storm wind) forms.
Variant of Haidee. This name is borne by New Zealandish actress and director Aidee Walker in whose case it is a diminutive of Adrianne.
It is a name that asks a question, meaning "what did he/she desire?"
Aideko is the supernatural aspect of Aide (as opposed to Berezko who represents Aide's natural aspect).

Meaning uncertain, perhaps an elaboration of Haydée or Aída using the popular name suffix liz (which in turn is derived from Lizbeth or a related name). It was brought to some public attention in 2008 by Puerto Rican beauty pageant contestant Aideliz Hidalgo (1986-), who competed on the reality television series/beauty pageant Nuestra Belleza Latina 2008.
Derived from Ancient Greek αἴδεσις (aidesis) meaning "respect". Masculine form of Aidesia.
Meaning ‘Beautiful’ in Assamese. A famous person with that name was Aideu Handique.
Means "no one can change my destiny but God" in Yoruba.
Derived from Arabic عيد ال ('id al) meaning "festival of the, feast of the", used in the names of several Islamic holidays such as Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha.
Means "only" in Northern Sami, making this a cognate of Finnish Aino.
Means "moon" in the Romulan language created by Diane Duane for her non-canon series of science fiction novels Star Trek: Rihannsu.
Referring to our aid coming from God.
Means "shame, respect, reverence, awe" in Ancient Greek, the name of the Greek goddess and personification of shame, modesty, and humility.
From the Germanic name Aldric. This was the name of a 9th-century saint.
Diminutive of Adrian and Aidan for men, and Adelaide for women. Also compare Adie.

column3: あいえ(Japanese Hiragana)|アイエ(Japanese Katakana)|愛恵, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 愛 (ai) meaning "love, affection" combined with 恵 (e) meaning "favour, benefit". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Name of an invisible being in Basque folklore, from an oral variant of the name Aideko, ultimately from Basque aireko meaning "of the air".
Aierkana meaning “breathe of life” or “revival healing of life”
Name documented in Navarre in 1149, of unknown meaning. It has been revived in modern times.
Made up from Ayesha and the popular name ending leigh (see lee). A famous bearer is the New Zealand born rugby player Aieshaleigh Smalley.
From Basque aietz, dialectal variant of aihotz meaning "machete".
From the Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love" and 菲 (fēi) meaning "fragrant, luxuriant".

column3: 愛芽, 藍芽, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 藍 (ai) meaning "indigo" combined with 芽 (ga) meaning "bud, sprout". Other kanji combinations are possible.
The name of a Guanche man from La Palma who was christened in Seville.
Derived from ай (ay) meaning "moon" and the title khan meaning "king, ruler"
From Kazakh ай (ay) meaning "moon" and ханым (khanym) meaning "mistress, madam, lady".
Means "God or a king can never be extinguished or killed," signifying eternal reign and divine protection.

Probably derived from Greek αἰγίς (aigis) meaning "goatskin, fleece", but that can also refer to the shield of Zeus. Also compare Greek αἴγειος (aigeios) meaning "of a goat". Another possibility is that it was derived from Greek αἴξ (aix) meaning "a tall wave". This name is usually latinized to Aegeas.
Derived from Ancient Greek αἴγειρος (aígeiros) meaning "black poplar". This was the name of one of the eight hamadryad daughters of Oxylos and Hamadryas, associated with the black poplar tree.
Aigel is the first name of Aigel Gaysina, the lead singer of the Russian band AIGEL. It is probably a form of Aygül.
Combination of Sami áige meaning "time" and a second element of unknown meaning.
Means "shining moon" in Mongolian. This is the name of one of Kublai Khan's nieces.
Derived from the Greek noun αἴγλη (aigle) meaning "light (of the sun or moon)" as well as "radiance" and "glory" (see Aegle) combined with the Greek noun ἀνήρ (aner) meaning "man".

An Arthurian knight introduced in the Vulgate Cycle as the nephew of Kay of Estral.In the early days of Arthur's reign, fought against the Saxons at the battle of Carhaix, against Raolais at Estremores, and against Agrippe in the Waste Land. He participated in quests to learn the fate of Merlin and to locate Lancelot. He brought news of Lancelot's conquest of Dolorous Guard to Arthur's court. He eventually became a companion of Kahedin and Gaheris of Carahew. In Claris et Laris, he saves some nuns from a marauder.
French form of Anianus. Saint Aignan (358–453) was Bishop of Orléans, France, and assisted Roman general Flavius Aetius in the defense of the city against Attila the Hun in 451.
Epithet of the Greek god Pan meaning "goat-horned", derived from Greek αἴξ (aix) "goat" and κέρας (keras) "horn". This is also the Greek name for the astrological sign of Capricorn.
From Tatar and Bashkir ай (ay) meaning "moon" combined with гөл (göl) "flower".
From Chinese 爱国 (àiguó) meaning "be patriotic". Other character combinations are possible but rare.

Derived from the old Lithuanian verb aiti meaning "to go, to walk" combined with the old Lithuanian verb gusti meaning "to get used to, to inure, to accustom oneself" as well as "to learn". This name is not to be confused with Augustas.
Feminine form of Aigustas. This name is not to be confused with Augustė.

column5: /ai̯.ɡýp.ti.os/(Greek Mythology, Classical Greek)|/ɛ.ˈʝyp.ti.os/(Greek Mythology, Classical Greek)|/e.ˈʝip.ti.os/(Greek Mythology, Classical Greek)
column12: Means "Egyptian, Someone from Egypt" in Greek. From Αἴγυπτος (aíguptos, “Egypt”) and‎ -ιος (-ios, adjective suffix).

column3: 藍巴, 愛羽, 愛葉, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 藍 (ai) meaning "indigo" and 巴 (ha) meaning "comma". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Means the sea of love. Combination of ai which means love and hai which means sea. The meaning of the name is "the sea of love".
From the Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love" and 含 (hán) meaning "cherish, contain".

column3: 愛平, 藍平(Japanese Kanji)|あいへい(Japanese Hiragana)|アイヘイ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Ai 1 combined with 平 (hei) meaning "even, flat."This name is very rarely used.
From Japanese 愛 (ai) meaning "love, affection" combined with 妃 (hi) meaning "a ruler's wife; queen; empress". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Japanese 愛 (ai) meaning "love, affection" combined with 彦 (hiko) meaning "boy, prince". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 愛姫, 藍姫, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 愛 (ai) meaning "love, affection" or 藍 (ai) meaning "indigo" combined with 姫 (hime) meaning "princess". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Japanese 相 (ai) meaning "appearance, look" combined with 仁 (hito) meaning "benevolence". Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.

column3: 方爱红, 爱虹, 蔼鸿, etc.(Chinese)
爱华, 愛華, 瑷华(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love" or 瑷 (ài) meaning "fine quality jade" and 华 (huá) meaning "prosperous, splendid, flowery, illustrious, China". Other characters can also form this name.

column3: 瑷晖, etc.(Chinese)|璦暉, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 瑷 (aì) meaning "fine quality jade", combined with 晖 (huī) meaning "sunshine, sunlight". See also Aìhuī.

column3: あいい(Japanese Hiragana)|藍井, 愛似, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 愛 (ai) meaning "love, affection" combined with 似 (i) meaning "resemble". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 愛一, 藍一, 亜伊智, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 愛 (ai) meaning "love, affection" combined with 一 (ichi) meaning "one". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Japanese 愛 (ai) meaning "love, affection", 一 (ichi) meaning "one" combined with 郎 (rou) meaning "son". Other combinations of kanji characters are also possible.
Meaning unknown, or could be from the Hanja letters 愛 (meaning love), and the Hanja character 子 (meaning child). A famous person with this name is Ai-ja Kim (1940-1987).

From an Old Testament place name meaning "place of gazelles" in Hebrew (compare Ayala). Aijalon or Ajalon was the name of several biblical locations, including the valley in Dan where the Israelites defeated the Amorites while the sun and moon stood still in answer to their leader Joshua's prayer.
From the Chinese 蔼 (ǎi) meaning "lush, affable, friendly" and 玑 (jī) meaning "pearl that is not quite round".
From the Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love" and 嘉 (jiā) meaning "fine, good, auspicious, excellent".
From the Chinese 瑷 (ài) meaning "fine quality jade" and 交 (jiāo) meaning "associate with, join, meet, mix, intersect".

column3: 愛人, 愛臣, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|瑷锦(Chinese)
column12: From Japanese 愛人 (aijin) meaning "lover". Other kanji or kanji combinations can form this name as well.
From the Chinese 嫒 (ài) meaning "daughter" and 炯 (jiǒng) meaning "bright, brilliant".

column3: 愛次郎, 愛二郎, 藍二郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 藍 (ai) meaning "indigo" or 愛 (ai) meaning "love, affection", and 二 (ji) meaning "two" or 次 (ji) meaning "next, second", and 郎 (ro) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 愛次郎, 愛二郎, 藍二郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column12: A form of word äijä, old man. Also name variant for Ukko the god of the sky, weather, harvest and thunder in Finnish mythology.
From the Chinese 嫒 (ài) meaning "daughter" and 菊 (jú) meaning "chrysanthemum".
From the Chinese characters 叆 (ài) meaning "cloudy sky; dark, obscure" and 娟 (juān) meaning "beautiful; graceful".
Aijuka means "he knew' or 'he understands' in reference to gaining knowledge & education.

column3: 爱军, 愛軍, 爱俊, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love" and 军 (jūn) meaning "army" or 俊 (jùn) meaning "talented, handsome". Other characters can also form this name.

column3: 愛華, 愛花, 愛香, 愛加, 愛歌, 愛嘉, 藍花, 藍香, 藍加, 藍華, 藍嘉, 藍歌(Japanese Kanji)|あいか(Japanese Hiragana)|アイカ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name combines 愛 (ai, ito.shii, o.shimu, kana.shii, mana, me.deru) meaning "affection, love" or 藍 (ran, ai) meaning "indigo" with 華 or 花 (ka, ke, hana) which both mean "flower," 香 (kyou, kou, ka, kao.ri, kao.ru) meaning "incense, perfume, smell", 加 (ka, kuwa.eru, kuwa.waru) meaning "add, include, join", 歌 (ka, uta, uta.u) meaning "sing, song, poem" or 嘉 (ka, yoi, yomi.suru) meaning "applaud, esteem, praise."

column3: あいかこ(Japanese Hiragana)|愛花子, 愛香子, 藍香子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 愛 (ai) meaning "love, affection" or 藍 (ai) meaning "indigo", combined with 花 (ka) meaning "flower, blossom" or 香 (ka) meaning "fragrance", and 子 (ko) meaning "child, sign of the rat". More kanji combinations are possible.
Old Finnish name according to Kustaa Vilkuna (a Finnish ethnologist, linguist and historian).

Means "man-eater" in Hawaiian, from Hawaiian ʻai "to eat, to taste" and kanaka "human being". This was the name of a high chief of the Kingdom of Hawaii and the grandfather of two of Hawaii's future monarchs, Kalākaua and Liliʻuokalani.
Means "fell fire". This is the Quenya form of Aegnor.

column3: あいき(Japanese Hiragana)|アイキ(Japanese Katakana)|愛気, 愛木, 藍貴, 愛輝, 藍姫, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column12: Diminutive of Finnish names beginning with Ai-.
Short form of names containing the Germanic name element agjō or agil "edge (of a sword)", such as Ekkehard or Aai.

column3: 藍空, 愛来, 愛空, 愛久, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 愛 (ai) meaning "love, affection" or 藍 (ai) meaning "indigo" combined with 空 (ku) meaning "sky", 久 (ku) meaning "long time" or 来 (ku) meaning "to come". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Means "plenty, abundance (of food or refreshments)" in Sanskrit.
Inari Sami variant form of Áile and Aili possibly related to Láilá.

Modern Scottish Gaelic origin, exact etymology unclear, meaning "noble one", "harmonious" and "cheerful". Possibly a combination of the names Alana and Eilidh, or an potential anglicization/variant of Eilionoir.
Means "loving, in love" in Hawaiian. Note: without the 'okina (= the diacritical mark), "ailana" could refer to sexual intercourse.
Variant of Ailani. Like Ailani and other variations, this name is mostly used by Spanish speakers.
Dithematic name formed from the Germanic name elements agil "edge (of a sword)" and bern "bear."
Possibly from Adaldag or its Old English cognate Ætheldæg.
Variant of Estonian Aili, itself a borrowing of Finnish Aili.
Name of former Bad Girl, Ailea Carr. Carr featured in the show Bad Girls Club (2006-2017).
From the name Delia 1 written backwards.
Form of Elizabeth found in the Gothic Bible.
Borne by Ailerán the Wise, Irish scholar and saint.
Medieval English form of Old English Æðelgifu.
Medieval form of Ælfgifu or Æðelgifu.
Diminutive form of a personal name derived from Irish áilghean "mild, gentle, noble".
Estonian short form of both Alice and Adelheid as well as an adoption of Finnish Aili.
From the Chinese 嫒 (ài) meaning "daughter" and 莲 (lián) meaning "lotus, water lily".
Of uncertain origin and meaning. This name is, however, considered both an Anglicization of Eilidh and a diminutive of Aileen and Ailison.
Diminutive of Aili and Aila, occasionally used as a given name in its own right.
Hawaiian form of Aileen, Eileen, Irene and Ainsley.
Used by J.R.R. Tolkien, this is a Quenya name of unknown meaning. It likely comes from ailin meaning "lake" combined with the feminine suffix el.
From Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love, affection" combined with 玲 (líng) meaning "tinkling of jade". Other hanzi combinations are possible. This name may also be a Chinese transliteration of Eileen.
From ailinon meaning "water lily" in Quenya, a language invented by Tolkien.

Irish form of Eleanor (probably via Latin Alienora). This name occurs in medieval Irish annals, belonging to two Anglo-Norman noblewomen living in Ireland. It may or may not have been adopted by Gaels.
Probably a combination of the prefix ai- and Lisa.

Of uncertain derivation. This was the name of the title character in the Irish Arthurian romance Céilidhe Iosgaide Léithe (The Visit of the Grey-Hammed Lady). She married King Arthur when she took him and his knights to the Otherworld. She was the daughter of Daire, a fairy king, by Rathlean. She was said to have shapeshifted from time to time into a deer.
From the Chinese 瑷 (ài) meaning "fine quality jade" or 爱 (ài) meaning "love" and 茏 (lóng) meaning "tall grass" or 隆 (lóng) meaning "prosperous, plentiful, abundant".
Derived from Old English Æðelleofu, composed of elements æðele "noble" and lufu "love".
Diminutive of Alison. In recent years, this name has occasionally been used as a diminutive of Ailsa.
From the Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love" and 銮 (luán) meaning "bells".

Ai meaning love in Chinese (愛). Namesake also refers to the Ailuen in C.O.R.E. Mythology, a young girl spotted playing french horn at the top of a mountain until she was knocked down by the sun god for her over-radience.
Means "cat" in Ancient Greek. The Egyptian goddess Bastet was known by this name in Ancient Greek religion.
Latinized medieval form of Aliward. Ailuuardus Belli from the Domesday Book appears to be a son of Bell whose family was documented in 1086.
Coalescence of several Old English names: Æðelwig "noble battle", Ealdwig "ancient battle", and Ælfwig "elf battle".
Name of a king of Libya in the 4th century BCE.
Possibly a variant of Aylín; an Hispanic variant of Eileen (i.e. using Spanish spelling conventions). A known bearer is the Spanish singer Ailyn (1982-), real name Pilar Giménez García.
Variant of Aileen. Also compare Ailyn.
Possibly from Natsilingmiut aimavik "home", Kivalliq aivuq "s/he goes towards", Greenlandic aivâ "fetches it", or Greenlandic airuq "coming home". It may also be a variant of Aumaĸ.
Provençal, Niçard and Languedocian form of Amata.
Alternate trancsription of Arabic أيمن (see Aiman 2) chiefly used in Northern Africa (using French-influenced orthography).
Diminutive of Aima, using the suffix -nnguaq "sweet, dear".
Combination of Tahitian ai "in possession of" and mata, derived from the word Matamua meaning "eldest sibling". This name was traditionally given to the firstborn child of a family.

column3: 愛芽, 愛夢, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
嫒美, 嫒梅, 蔼枚(Chinese)
column12: From the Chinese 嫒 (ài) meaning "daughter" or 蔼 (ǎi) meaning "lush, affable, friendly" and 美 (měi) meaning "beauty, beautiful", 梅 (méi) meaning "plum" or 枚 (méi) meaning "stalk, trunk".

Irish sun godess. This name appears to be derived from Proto-Celtic aidu-mandā. The name literally means "burning stain," which may have been a byword for the notion of ‘sunburn.’ The Romano-British form of this Proto-Celtic name is likely to have been Aedumanda.

column3: アイミコ(Japanese Katakana)|藍美子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 藍 (ai) meaning "indigo", 美 (mi) meaning "beauty, beautiful" and 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations can be used.
Manx feminine form of Aemilius (see Emil).
From the Chinese set phrase 爱民如子 (àimínrúzǐ) meaning "love the subjects as if they were one’s own children". Other homophonic hanzi combinations can be used to give the name extra meaning.
Derived from Ай (ai) meaning "moon" and Мöкö (mökö) meaning "strong man".
Medieval Walloon, Languedocian and Provençal form of Haimo.
Italian form of Haimo. This name has been often used by members of the House Savoy.

column3: 愛夢, 逢夢, 彩夢, 曖夢, 亜以夢, 亜衣夢, 亜好夢, 亞衣夢, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 愛 (ai) meaning "love, affection", 逢 (ai) meaning "meeting, tryst, date, rendezvous", 彩 (ai) meaning "colour", 曖 (ai) meaning "dark, not clear", 亜 or 亞 (a) meaning "second, Asia", 以 (i) meaning "by means of, because, in view of, compared with", 衣 (i) meaning "garment, clothes, dressing" or 好 (i) meaning "fond, pleasing, like some" combined with 夢 (mu) meaning "dream". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Means "may he not die" in Amharic.

column3: 아인(Korean Hangul)|亞仁, 妸仁, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Combination of an a hanja, like 亞 meaning "next, second" or 妸 meaning "beautiful," and an in hanja, e.g. 仁 meaning "benevolent, kind, virtuous."

column3: アイン(Japanese Katakana)|あいん(Japanese Hiragana)|亜寅, 遭韻, 合胤, 恵鬱, 曖壮, 惠盛, 合昌, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: Means "eye" in Arabic. This is the traditional name of the star Epsilon Tauri in the constellation Taurus.
Means "not to be beaten" in Yoruba, from the negative prefix àì- combined with nà "to beat, hit, flagellate; to defeat". Given to children born with an umbilical cord around their neck; compare Ojo.
From Kazakh айна (aina) meaning "mirror" and гүл (gul) meaning "flower".
Means "white land" from ʻāina meaning "land" and kea meaning "white, clear".
Indonesian, Malay and Bengali variant of Ainul.
Means "heavenly land" in Hawaiian, from the elements ʻāina "land", and lani "sky, heaven".
Derived from Arabic عين الرامي ʽain al-rāmī meaning "eye of the archer". This is the traditional name for the triple star system Nu¹ Sagittarii.
Means "beautiful land" in Hawaiian, from the elements ʻāina, meaning "land" and nani, meaning "beauty".
Derived from Kazakh ай (ay) meaning "moon" combined with Arabic نَار (nār) meaning "fire, flame, light" or Persian نار (nâr) meaning "pomegranate" (or also, "fire").
Containing name elements agi and hard.
Variant of Ainara using the modern feminine suffix -e.
Derived from Kazakh айна (ayna) meaning "mirror", of Persian origin.
Possibly derived from anfa meaning "storm, tempest" and diminutive suffix -ín.
The name of the titular heroine in the Peruvian Film Ainbo Spirit of the Amazon. It descends from aĩβo, which means “woman” in Shipibo Conibo, a Panoan language.
Aindavi is sanskrit female name.Meaning: lunar, like the Moon.

column3: 愛音, 藍子, 藍音, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 愛 (ai) meaning "affection, love" and 音 (ne) meaning "sound". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Either a Lithuanian borrowing of Latvian Aina 4 or derived from Lithuanian ainis "descendant, offspring".
Possibly means "careful, thoughtful" from the Irish negative prefix ain- combined with éislis "negligence, remissness".
Modern coinage derived from Manx ainle "angel" and the diminutive suffix -ag, this name is intended as a Manx equivalent to Angela.
Aragonese, Languedocian and Gascon form of Agnes.
Means "praise of the people", from Greek αἴνεσις (ainesis) meaning "praise", itself derived from αἰνέω (aineo) "to praise", and δημος (demos) meaning "the people".

Basque feminine form of Aingeru and cognate of Ángeles and Angèle. In the Basque Country, this name is considered an amuletic name: it is usually given in reference to the guardian angels and folk lore has it that children bearing this name will be particularly protected.
Stage name of actress Uhm In-gi.

Taken from the name of a town, Ainhize-Monjolose, in the Pyrénées-Atlantiques department in the Nouvelle-Aquitaine region in southwestern France. It is located in the former province of Lower Navarre, not far from the "Croix de Galcetaburu", and used to be the town where meetings were held in Lower Navarre. The toponym was first recorded as Anfiz in 1135; according to Jean-Baptiste Orpustan, its origin and meaning is lost to time. The medieval village of Monjolose was established in 1240 as subject to the King of Navarre. Formerly subject to Ainhize, they were reunited on 16 August 1841.

Uncertain etymology. This may have been the name of an Amazon depicted as fighting against Achilles on an Attic terracotta relief fragment, but it may have instead been a depiction of Penthesilea labeled with the name of her town of origin.
Estonian diminutive of Aina 1, used as a given name in its own right.
Diminutive of Aini and Aino, occasionally used as a given name in its own right.
Meaning unknown, though it is believed that her name is a corruption of the name Danina, derived from Georgian da and nana. Ainina is a Georgian goddess and in a pair with the deity Danina.
Possibly derived from Greenlandic aaniin "short time".
From the Chinese 嫒 (ài) meaning "(your) daughter" or 爱 (ài) meaning "love" and 宁 (níng) meaning "peaceful, calm".
Derived from Arabic ayn meaning "eye" and nur meaning "light", ultimately meaning "light of the eyes".
From the Arabic عَيْن‎ (ʿayn) meaning "eye" and نور (nur) meaning "light".
Latvian masculine form of Aina 4 and Lithuanian masculine form of Ainė.
From the Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love" and 妞 (niū) meaning "girl".
Variant of Ainhize. Ainize Barea Nuñez (born 25 January 1992), often known as Peke Barea, is a Spanish footballer from the Basque Country.
Means "great lord". A king of Tara bore this name.

column3: あいの(Japanese Hiragana)|アイノ(Japanese Katakana)|亜祈, 愛希, 愛祈, 藍希, 和野, 亜委乃, 亜委野, 阿委乃, 阿委野, 安以野, 安惟乃, 安惟野, 安意乃, 安意野, 安維乃, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: This name can be spelled with 安 (a) meaning "low, cheap, inexpensive, rested, peace, quiet" combined with 以 (i) meaning "by means of, because, in view of, compared with", 委 (i) meaning "committee, entrust to, leave to, devote, discard", 惟 (i) meaning "consider, reflect, think", or 意 (i) meaning "idea, mind, heart, taste, thought, desire, care, liking", that is then combined with 祈 (ino, no) meaning "pray, wish". Or it could be spelled with 藍 (ai) meaning "indigo" or 和 (ai) meaning "peace, harmony, Japanese style, Japan" that is then combined with 希 (no) meaning "hope, beg, request, rare, few" or 野 (no) meaning "area, field". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Means "no one is greater than God" in Esan.

column3: あいのすけ(Japanese Hiragana)|アイノスケ(Japanese Katakana)|会之介, 会之祐, 合之佑, 相之助, 相之佑, 藍之丞, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 愛 (ai) meaning "love, affection", 之 (no), a possessive marker, combined with 輔 (suke) meaning "help". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Used for a fairy in Thomas Keightley's The Fairy Mythology, released in 1870. Ainsel was a fairy who came down the chimney to play with a little boy.
Transferred use of the surname Ainsworth.
From the Malagasy aina meaning "life" and soa meaning "good".
First part of compound Arabic names beginning with عين ال (ʾayn al) meaning "eye of the".
From Arabic عيون ('aynun) meaning "eyes", the plural of عين ('ayn) meaning "eye".

column3: あいお(Japanese Hiragana)|アイオ(Japanese Katakana)|愛緒, 愛男, 愛夫, 愛雄, 愛郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: The kanji used for males is 愛 (ai) meaning "love, affection" combined with 男 (o) meaning "male" or 緒 (o) meaning "thread" for girls. Other kanji combinations are possible.

Means "long period of time; lifetime, generation, eternity, forever" in Ancient Greek. In Greek mythology, Aion is a deity associated with time, the zodiac, and circles, considered the personification of eternity.

column3: 藍央菜, 藍央, 愛欧奈, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 藍 (ai) meaning "indigo", 央 (o) meaning "centre, middle" combined with 菜 (na) meaning "vegetables, greens". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Unknown etymology. This is the name of one of seven Hesperides (nymphs of the evening) depicted on a Late Classical period vase, along with Antheia, Donakis, Calypso, Mermesa, Nelisa and Tara.
In Inuit mythology, Aipaloovik is an evil sea god associated with death and destruction.
From the Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love" and 朋 (péng) meaning "friend".
Alternate transcription of Kyrgyz Айпери (see Ayperi).

column3: 爱萍, 爱平, etc.(Chinese)|愛萍, 愛平, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love, affection" combined with 萍 (píng) meaning "wander, travel, duckweed" or 平 (píng) meaning "level, even, peaceful". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
From the Chinese 瑷 (ài) meaning "fine quality jade" and 谦 (qiān) meaning "humble, modest".
From the Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love" and 勤 (qín) meaning "industrious, diligent, attentive".

column3: 爱青, 爱清, etc.(Chinese)|愛青, 愛清, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love, affection" combined with 青 (qīng) meaning "blue, green, young" or 清 (qīng) meaning "clear, pure, clean". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 爱琼, 蔼琼, etc.(Chinese)|愛瓊, 藹瓊, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love, affection", 蔼 (ǎi) meaning "friendly, lush" combined with 琼 (qióng) meaning "red jade". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
From Germanic aigan "to possess" and helm "protection".
From initals of Aleksey Ivanovich Rykov, Soviet politician and revolutionary.

column3: アイラ(Japanese Katakana)|あいら(Japanese Hiragana)|藍良, 愛良, 藍麗, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|ऐरा(Sanskrit)
column12: Of uncertain origin and meaning. Theories include a derivation from Latvian airene "ryegrass, darnel", a contracted form of Airisa and a modern coinage with no set meaning.
Name of a 12th century French Carthusian monk and bishop of Saint-Jean-de-Maurienne.
Possibly a variant of Aaralyn or Aralyn.

column3: 愛蘭, 藍蘭, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|爱然, 爱燃(Chinese)

column12: Derived from the Germanic elements heri "army" and hard "brave, hardy" (compare Erhard).
Galician version of Aires. This was the name of several Galician medieval poets, like Airas Nunes. It has seen a revival in Galicia since the 2000's.
Diminutive of Iravati. Airavata is the elephant mount of Indra and the son of Iravati. He is described as being pure white with multiple heads, tusks and trunks.

column3: 愛恋, 愛玲, 愛麗, 愛玲, 亜衣礼, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column12: Old Irish name meaning "having many followers". This name dates back to the seventh and eighth centuries and was the name of at least one king of Ireland.
Derived from airelle, the French name for the plant genus Vaccinium. The French derived the name from Portuguese airella, which in turn was derived from Latin atra "dark, black, gloomy".
A mythological Irish king, often presented as the Irishcounterpart of King Arthur.

column3: 愛蓮, 愛恋, 藍蓮, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 愛 (ai) meaning "love, affection" combined with 蓮 (ren) meaning "lotus". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Unknown origin, possibly a short form of Germanic names begining with the root hari meaning "army".
Transferred usage of the surname Airey.
Of uncertain origin and meaning. Theories include a borrowing of Finnish Airi 2 and a variant of Aili.
Variant of Arianna. It was given to 23 girls born in the United States in 2011 (Aireanna: 20; Airiana: 19; Airyana: 15; Aireona: 13; Aireonna, Airyanna: 10 (each); Airyonna: 5).
Variant of Arielle influenced by the English word air.
Combination of Aire and Riin. It is occasionally also treated as a variant of Irene (mimicking the English pronunciation of this name) and an Estonian borrowing of Erin.

From Japanese 愛 (ai, ito, mana) meaning "love, affection" and 利 (ri, ki.ku) meaning "advantage, benefit, profit, gain", combined with 子 (ko, shi, su) meaning "child, the sign of the rat, 1st sign of the Chinese zodiac". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From kazakh ай (ay) meaning "moon" combined with Arabic ريم (rim) meaning white "antelope"
Spanish variant of Irene, reflecting the English pronunciation of the name.

column3: আইরিন(Bengali)|あいりん(Japanese Hiragana)|愛林, 愛隣, 愛凛, 藍琳, 愛依林, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|애린, 아이린(Korean Hangul)
column12: Bengali form of Irene reflecting the English pronunciation.
Adaption and phonetic approximation to English Iris.

Means "jumping water" or "crossing water", from Indonesian air meaning "water" combined with Sanskrit लङ्घन (laṅghana) meaning "passing over, jumping, crossing". This was the name of an 11th-century king of eastern Java, so named because he crossed the Bali Strait from Bali (his birthplace) to Java.
Transferred use of the surname Airlie.

column3: アイロ(Japanese Katakana)|あいろ(Japanese Hiragana)|愛楼, 鮎朗, 哀浪, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
アイロ(Japanese Katakana)|あいろ(Japanese Hiragana)|愛楼, 鮎朗, 哀浪, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 愛 (ai) meaning "love, affection" combined with 郎 (rou) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations are possible.A famous bearer was Airou Kitayama (1950-2002), Japanese politician.

column3: あいる(Japanese Hiragana)|アイル(Japanese Katakana)|愛入, 愛蕗, 愛璃, 愛留, 藍瑠, 阿惟瑠, 愛衣琉, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|皑如, 爱儒, 蔼如, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Japanese 愛 (ai) meaning "love, affection" combined with 入 (ru) meaning "enter, insert", 蕗 (ru) meaning "butterbur, bog rhubarb", 璃 (ru) meaning "glassy, lapis lazuli" or 留 (ru) meaning "detain, fasten, halt, stop". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From the Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love" or 蔼 (ǎi) meaning "lush, affable, friendly" and 睿 (ruì) meaning "shrewd, astute, clever".
Feminine variant of Aaron. Notably used by Robert De Niro's daughter.

column3: アイサ(Japanese Katakana)|あいさ(Japanese Hiragana)|愛沙, 藍彩, 愛紗, 藍砂, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|Αἶσα(Ancient Greek)

column12: Indonesian and Malay form of Aisha.
Fijian and Tongan form of Isaac, meaning "he laughs".

Means "protector of the truth" from the Arabic root ع-ص-م (ʿ-ṣ-m) meaning "protector, guardian" combined with حقّ (ḥaqq) meaning "truth".A famous bearer is Aisam-ul-Haq who is a Pakistani professional tennis player who specialises in doubles. He is the only Pakistani player ever to reach a Grand Slam final, having done so in both men's and mixed doubles at the 2010 US Open, alongside Rohan Bopanna and Květa Peschke respectively.
Uncertain etymology, perhaps related to Αἴσαρος (Aisaros), the Ancient Greek name of the Esaros river in Italy. Alternatively, it could be a mistaken rendering of the masculine name Ἀρέσας (Aresas).
Derived from Greek αἶσχος (aischos) meaning "shame, timidity, disgrace".
Variant of Aischris. In Greek mythology, this was the name of one of the fifty daughters of King Thespius, mother of Leucones by Heracles.
Derived from Ancient Greek αἰσχρός (aischros) meaning "causing shame, dishonouring, disgraceful, infamous" or "ugly, deformed".
Frisian short form of names containing the nane elements agi and/or egg.
Fijian, Samoan and Tongan form of Isaiah.
From Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love, affection" or 艾 (ài) meaning "sagebrush, wormwood" combined with 森 (sēn) meaning "forest". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

Ai — often used as a prefix of endearment or respect, especially for a girl or beloved person (like “dear” or “beloved”).Seng — in Tai-Ahom and related Tai languages, it can mean bright, pure, or blessed.Fa — means heaven or sky (connected to divinity or celestial blessings).So, it can be interpreted as: "The Beloved Blessed by Heaven" or "Pure soul under Heaven’s blessing".

column3: アイシャ(Japanese Katakana)|あいしゃ(Japanese Hiragana)|娃沙, 藍謝, 逢砂, 鮎汝, 哀紗, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|ऐशा(Hindi)
column12: From Japanese 愛 (ai) meaning "love, affection" combined with 謝 (sha) meaning "to thank". Other kanji combinations are possible.Usage of this name is influenced by the name Aisha.
Combination of Aisha meaning "life" with Hafsat meaning "gathering".
From the Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love" and 珊 (shān) meaning "coral".
From the Chinese 瑷 (ài) meaning "fine quality jade" and 劭 (shào) meaning "encourage, excel, excellent".
Georgian and Romani (i.e. Gypsy) form of Aisha.
Albanian form of Aisha, referring to Muhammad's third and youngest wife.

column3: 嫒诗, 爱实, 蔼石, etc.(Chinese)

column12: Means "divine, relating to Shiva 1" in Sanskrit.
Means "relating to Lord Shiva 1" in Sanskrit.
Derived from Kazakh ай ‎(ay) meaning "moon" combined with шолпан (sholpan) "Venus (the planet)".
From the Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love" and 霜 (shuāng) meaning "frost".
Perhaps a misspelling of Ailsi, a form of Æthelsige. This name 'occurs nowhere else outside Domesday Book', according to the Prosopography of Anglo-Saxon England.
Derived from the given name Aisimos and the patronymic suffix ἴδης (ides).
Means "destined, fatal" or "fitting, suitable, right" in Greek, ultimately derived from αἶσα (aisa) meaning "fate, destiny".
Alternate transcription of Aisha, mainly used in Dutch-influenced regions of the continent.

A variant of the Tatar name ”Aisä” (Mishar Tatar) and ”Ğäisä” (Kazan Tatar). This version has been used in Finland, among the small community of Tatars.In Russia, it is also used as a surname, with the added -in suffix (Aisin).
Diminutive of names containing the element agi "terror".
Possibly a variant of Asli or Aisling.

column5: AYZ-lin(American English)|AYS-lin(American English)|IES-lin(American English)|IEZ-lin(American English)|ASH-lin(American English)

column12: Variant of Aislinn. The pronunciation usually differs from the original Irish pronunciation of Aislinn or Aisling.
Form of Isa 1 used in Northern Africa and other French-influenced regions of the continent.
Form of Aisha used in West African countries (primarily Mali, Senegal, and Cameroon).
Form of Aisha used in parts of French-influenced western Africa.
Possibly from the gothic verb áistan "to reverence."

Derived from Aisčiai, which is the Lithuanian name for the Aesti, a Baltic tribe (or people) that was first described by the Roman historian Tacitus (born c. 56 AD, died c. 120 AD) in his treatise Germania. He referred to them as Aestiorum gentes in his work. The etymology of the tribe's name is uncertain: some scholars believe that its meaning is "oriental, eastern", whilst others see a connection with the Gothic verb aistan meaning "to respect, to fear" and/or with Middle Low German eiste or ēste meaning "oast, kiln" or "threshing barn".

column3: 愛輔, 愛介, 愛祐, 相助, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 愛 (ai) meaning "love, affection" combined with 輔 (suke) meaning "help". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Alternate transcription of Kazakh Айсұлу (see Aysulu).
Alternate transcription of Kyrgyz Айсулуу (see Aysuluu).
From the Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love" and 索 (suǒ) meaning "rope", "laws, rules" or "search, inquire, demand".

Derived from the old Lithuanian verb aiti meaning "to go, to walk" combined with Baltic vyd meaning "to see" (see Vytautas). Also compare other names that end in -vydas, such as Alvydas and Tautvydas.
Means "one who belongs to Iswara (the Lord)" in Sanskrit.
Possibly a diminutive of Aisyah or Quraisy
The Etruscan god of the underworld. He is identical with the Greek Hades and the Roman god Pluto.
From the Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love" and 泰 (tài) meaning "great, superior, exalted".
This is the name of a Christian saint, most likely from a Persian source meaning "light; bright." The name was borne by the Polish mayor of Sanok Aital Witoszyński (1898-1905).
Derived from Kazakh ай (ay) meaning "moon" combined with таң (tañ) meaning "dawn, daybreak", though it is also considered a variant of the name Aidana.
Basquified form of Aitana using the modern feminine suffix -e. It is often reinterpreted as derived from the word aita ("father").
From the Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love" and 棠 (táng) meaning "wild plums".
From the Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love" and 桃 (táo) meaning "peach, marriage".
The first element of this name may be Old High German eit meaning "fire; brilliant". The second element is Old Saxon hard "strong, hard" (Old High German hart).
Means "son of Aithalos" in Greek, derived from the name Aithalos combined with the patronymic suffix ἴδης (ides).

Derived from Ancient Greek αἰθαλίων (aithalion) meaning "swarthy, dusky; browned, toasted". It is also possible that this name means "son of Aithalos", in which case it consists of the name Aithalos and the patronymic suffix -ίων (-ion).

Derived from either Ancient Greek αἴθαλος (aithalos) meaning "thick smoke, smoky flame" or αἰθάλη (aithale) meaning "soot", both of which ultimately derived from αἰθος (aithos) meaning "fire, burning heat", which itself is derived from αἴθω (aitho) meaning "to ignite, to light (up), to kindle, to burn".
'The name of a holy virgin, patroness of Cill Aithche in the barony of Kenry, Co. Limerick, where her feast-day (Jan. 15) was formerly kept as a holiday and a station held.'
Derived from Greek αἰθέριος (aitherios) meaning "of the upper air, high in the air" as well as "ethereal, heavenly", ultimately from αἰθήρ (aither) meaning "ether, heaven" (see Aether).
Alternate transcription of Thai อิทธิพล (see Itthiphon).
Alternate transcription of Thai อิทธิพล (see Itthiphon).

Derived from Ancient Greek αἴθων (aithon), which can mean "fiery, burning, fierce; tawny, red-brown" as well as "fire, burning heat", ultimately derived from αἴθω (aitho) meaning "to ignite, to light (up), to kindle, to burn".

Feminine participle of Ancient Greek αἴθων (aithon) meaning "fiery, burning, blazing, gleaming" as well as "red-brown, tawny", derived from αἴθω (aitho) meaning "to light up, kindle, burn, blaze". It coincides with the unrelated word αἴθουσα (aithousa) meaning either "portico, veranda" or "poison hemlock". In Greek mythology, Aithousa was the daughter of Poseidon and Alcyone, and a lover of Apollo with whom she had Eleuther. In the BBC television series Merlin (2008-2012), Aithusa is the name of a white dragon summoned by Merlin. On the show the name is said to mean "light of the sun" in Ancient Greek.
From the Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love" and 恬 (tián) meaning "quiet, calm, tranquil".
From the Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love" and 窕 (tiǎo) meaning "slender, charming, quiet and modest".
Derived from Old High German eit meaning "fire; brilliant" and Old High German hiltja meaning "battle".

column3: 霭婷, 霭汀, 瑷婷(Chinese)
column12: From the Chinese characters 霭 (ǎi) meaning "cloudy sky, haze; calm, peaceful" or 瑷 (ài) meaning "fine quality jade" and 婷 (tíng) meaning "pretty; attractive; graceful" or 汀 (tīng) meaning "sandbar, beach, bank, shore".
A hypocoristic of any of various names beginning with Old High German eit meaning "fire; brilliant".
Combination of Kazakh айт (ayt) meaning "holiday, festival, feast" (also referring to Eid, a Muslim festival), ultimately of Arabic origin, and the given name Mukhambet.

Greek form of Aetna. This was the name of a nymph of Mount Etna in Greek mythology, by many accounts the mother of the Palici (twin Sicilian chthonic gods of geysers) by either Zeus or Hephaestus. A moon of Jupiter is named after her.
From the Tahitian aito meaning "warrior" and ari'i meaning "noble".
Alternate transcription of Kazakh Айтолқын (see Aytolkyn).
From the Tahitian aito meaning "warrior" and nui, an archaic term meaning "big".
Alternate transcription of Thai อิทธิชัย (see Itthichai).

Means "ghost" and "spirit" in Māori, Samoan, Tongan and Tahitian. In Polynesian mythology Aitu are lesser gods of Atua "gods". In Māori aitu also refers to "sickness, calamity" and "malevolent spirit". Aitu is a cognate of Filipino anito and Indonesian antu.
Means “born during the moon” In Kazakh.
Means "pride" in Arabic. Aitzaz Hasan Bangash was a 15-year-old Pakistani student who died on 6 January 2014 while preventing a suicide bomber from entering his school in Ibrahimzai.

Used by the Basque writer and Catholic priest José de Ariztimuño Olaso (1896-1936), who was killed by the Fascists in the Spanish Civil War. Aitzol was a pseudonym possibly taken from letters in his surname, (A)r(iz)timuño (Ol)aso; or perhaps Aitzol came from the hypothetical Basque place name h(aitz ol)a meaning "quarry, stonemason's workshop" from the words haitz "rock, stone" and ola "workplace, factory".
Alternate transcription of Bengali আইয়ুব (see Ayub).
Famous bearer, Isabella Aiukli Cornell (Choctaw Nation of Oklahoma) is an activist for indigenous women.

A Germanic name formed from the name elements agin "edge (of a sword)" and wolf "wolf" (see Aginulf).As a medieval English name, it could either be a Scandinavian Norman name derived from Eyiólfr (or Eyjólfr) or a contraction of Old English Æðelwulf.
From Basque ainuria or aiuria meaning "howl".

From Latin āio meaning "to say, affirm", cognate to Etruscan 𐌀𐌉𐌖𐌔 (aius) meaning "omen, tell, response". Aius Locutius (meaning "spoken affirmation") was a Roman deity or numen associated with the Gallic invasions of Rome during the early 4th century BC.
Of uncertain origin and meaning. Theories include a feminine form of Aivars (cognate with the Estonian Aive) and a direct derivation from Latvian aiva "quince; quincetree".
Lithuanian form of the Scandinavian name Ivar, which is ultimately derived from the Old Norse name Ívarr (see Ivor).
Possibly an anglicized form of Aoibheann, Aoibhín or feminine Éimhín.
Georgianization of Ayvengo, which is the Russian form of Ivanhoe.The actual Georgian form of Ivanhoe is აივენჰო (Aivenho), but so far there is no evidence that it has ever been used as a given name.
A rare Kyrgyz name allegedly meaning "moon princess", in part from Turkic ay "moon".
Of unknown origin and meaning. Theories include a variant of Aivars and a masculine form of Aiva.
Originally a short form of Aivar, now used as a given name in its own right.

column3: 愛環, 愛和, 愛羽, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 愛 (ai) meaning "love, affection" combined with 環 (wa) meaning "circle, ring, wheel". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 爱婉, 爱晚, 蔼菀(Chinese)
column12: From the Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love" or 蔼 (ǎi) meaning "lush, affable, friendly" and 婉 (wǎn) meaning "amiable, congenial", 晚 (wǎn) meaning "night, evening" or 菀 (wǎn) meaning "luxuriance of growth".
From the Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love" and 维 (wéi) meaning "maintain, preserve" or 薇 (wēi) meaning "fern".

column3: 瑷玟, 瑷雯, 嫒雯(Chinese)
column12: From the Chinese 瑷 (ài) meaning "fine quality jade" or 嫒 (ài) meaning "daughter" and 玟 (wén) meaning "streaks in jade" or 雯 (wén) meaning "cloud patterns".

Another name for the wizard Radagast from JRR Tolkien's works. The name means "friend of birds, lover of birds" in the fictional Quenya language, from aiwë meaning "a small bird" and the suffix ndil meaning "devoted to".
Catalan variant of the arabic name Aisha, which means "alive" or "she who lives".

From Chinese 瑷 (ài) meaning "fine quality jade" combined with 禧 (xǐ) meaning "happiness, congratulations", 熙 (xī) meaning "bright, splendid, glorious" or 希 (xī) meaning "hope, expect, rare". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 爱霞, etc.(Chinese)|愛霞, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love, affection" combined with 霞 (xiá) meaning "rosy clouds, mist". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

From the Chinese characters 叆 (ài) meaning "cloudy sky; dark, obscure" or 瑷 (ài) meaning "fine quality jade" and 娴 (xián) meaning "elegant, refined; skillful" or 纤 (xiān) meaning "fine, delicate, graceful".
From the Chinese 蔼 (ǎi) meaning "lush, affable, friendly" and 肖 (xiào) meaning "look like, be like".

column3: 爱心, 爱新, 爱欣, 爱馨, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 爱心 (àixīn) meaning "compassion, kindness". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Chinese transliteration of the Manchu name ᠠᡳ᠌ᠰᡳᠩᡤᠠ (Aisingga) of uncertain meaning. This was the name of a 17th-century Qing dynasty general of Manchu origin.
From the Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love" and 煦 (xù) meaning "kind, gentle, gracious".
From the Chinese 嫒 (ài) meaning "daughter" and 雪 (xuě) meaning "snow".
From the Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love" and 寻 (xún) meaning "seek, search, look for".

column3: 愛夜, 愛映, 愛耶, 愛也, 愛哉, 愛矢, 愛八, 愛谷, 藍夜, 藍映, 藍耶, 藍也, 藍哉, 藍矢, 藍八, 藍谷, 相夜, 相映, 相耶, 相也, 相哉, 相矢, 相八, 相谷, 哀夜, 哀映, 哀耶, 哀也, 哀哉, 哀矢, 哀八, 哀谷(Japanese Kanji)

column12: From Japanese 愛 (ai, ito, mana) meaning "love, affection" and 椰 (ya) meaning "coconut palm tree", combined with 子 (ko, shi, su) meaning "child, the sign of the rat, 1st sign of the Chinese zodiac". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From the Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love" and 烨 (yè) meaning "bright, glorious", "firelight, flame".
From the Chinese characters 霭 (ǎi) meaning "cloudy sky, haze; calm, peaceful" and 萤 (yíng) meaning "glow-worm".

column3: アイヨ(Japanese Katakana)|はいよ(Japanese Hiragana)|愛代, 藍代, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 愛 (ai) meaning "love, affection" combined with 代 (yo) "world, society". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Japanese 愛 (ai, ito, mana) meaning "love, affection" and 代 (yo) meaning "world, society" combined with 子 (ko, shi, su) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Variant transcription of عائشة (Arabic), عائشہ (Urdu), and Айша (Kazakh) (see Aisha).
Means "descendant of Aiyy", referring to the Aiyy deities in Yakut mythology.

column3: 爱羽, 瑷瑜, 瑷羽(Chinese)
column12: From the Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love" or 瑷 (ài) meaning "fine quality jade" and 羽 (yǔ) meaning "feather" or 瑜 (yú) meaning "fine jade, virtues".

column3: 嫒原, 爱园, 爱缘(Chinese)
column12: From the Chinese 嫒 (ài) meaning "daughter" or 爱 (ài) meaning "love" and 原 (yuán) meaning "source, origin, beginning", 园 (yuán) meaning "garden, park, orchard" or 缘 (yuán) meaning "hem, margin; reason, cause; fate".
Combination of the names Ai 2 and Yun
From Yakut айыы (ayıı) meaning "creation", a derivative of ай (ay) "to create". In Yakut or Sakha mythology the Aiyy are good spirits who created the world.
Means "beautiful Aiyy" from the name of the Yakut Aiyy deities combined with куо (kuo) meaning "beautiful".
Means "grandson of Aiyy" from Yakut сиэн (sien) meaning "grandson" combined with the name of the Yakut Aiyy deities.
From Kazakh ай (ay) meaning "moon" and Persian زاده (zadeh) meaning "offspring".

Derived from Kazakh aй (ay) meaning "moon" and Persian زاده (zâde) "offspring, child". It is a feminine and masculine name in Kazakhstan, solely feminine in Kyrgyzstan, and solely masculine in Tatarstan.

Translates roughly to "divine offspring of the moon". Derived from the Kazakh word ay, meaning "moon", the Kazakh and Persian word zâde meaning "offspring", and the Kazakh and Arabic suffix -ullah, meaning "Allah (God)".

The name Aizen is derived from two Japanese kanji characters: “ai” (愛) meaning “love” or “affection,” and “zen” (善) meaning “good” or “virtuous.” Together, Aizen can be translated as “lover of good” or “one who does good deeds out of love and compassion.”Aizen has significant cultural roots in both Japanese and Buddhist traditions. In Japanese culture, Aizen is associated with the goddess of love and beauty, Benzaiten, who is often portrayed holding a biwa, a traditional Japanese lute. In Buddhist tradition, Aizen is one of the Five Wisdom Kings, a group of deities who represent different aspects of enlightenment. Aizen is specifically associated with desire, passion, and love, and is often depicted with a sword or a rope to symbolize his power over these emotions.
Old Basque name of unknown meaning, first recorded in Navarre in 1141.
From Chinese 艾 (ài) meaning "sagebrush, wormwood" combined with 真 (zhēn) meaning "real, genuine, true". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From the Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love" combined with 峥 (zhēng) meaning "high, noble". Other character combinations are possible.
From the Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love" and 枝 (zhī) meaning "branches" and 芷 (zhǐ) meaning "angelica, iris".
From Kazakh ай (ay) meaning "moon" and жүрек (zhurek) meaning "heart".

Derived from Basque aitz, a local variant of haitz, "stone, rock" and gorri "red; bare, naked". Aizkorri is a massif, the highest one of the Basque Autonomous Community (Spain). The goddess Mari 3 is said to live there in a cave called Aketegi.
Of uncertain origin and meaning. Theories include a derivation from Basque aitz "rock, stone".
Name taken from an eremitage dedicated to the Virgin Mary.
