column12: From Sanskrit अज (aja) or अजा (ajā), respectively the masculine and feminine word for "goat".
Means "ends conflict" or "end of a conflict" in Yoruba.
Taken from the Igbo phrase ana aja gi n’ihu ana ero gi n’azu, meaning "they praise you to your face and mock you behind your back".
In Genesis 36:24 and 1 Chronicles 1:40, Ajah is a son of Zibeon. Ajah means "hawk.
Greenlandic pet form of Aja, from a combination of Aja and the diminutive suffix -aaja, a Greenlandic affix used for and by children or a Greenlandic variant form of Ajajak.
Means "one who fights and escapes" in Yoruba, from jà "to fight, struggle" and já "to snap, break off, break loose".
Means "the one chanting 'ajaaja'" in Greenlandic. Ajaaja is an onomatopoeia.
Meaning unknown. It was borne by an Oyo emperor whose father was Oranyan and his brother was possibly the deity Shango.
Means "fights and survives" in Yoruba, from jà "to fight, struggle" and là "to survive". Alternatively, the final element could be lá "to lick; to become worn out".
Variant of Aijalon occurring in some translations of the Old Testament.
From Luo ajambo meaning "born in the evening" or "born in the night".
Directly taken from Hungarian ajándék "gift, present".
Means "one (we) fought to have" in Yoruba.
Derived from Kurdish ajda meaning "sprout, shoot".
Means "fought to be seen" in Yoruba, traditionally given to children born facing downwards.
Sundanese diminutive of masculine names containing the sound jat (or other similar sounds), such as Sudrajat.

Possibly from Finnish ajaa, menaing "to pursue", and the ending -tar, translates to "female pursuer". She is an evil, female spirit in Finnish Mythology. She lives in the woods on the Pohjola Mountains.
Phonetic spelling of the initials A and J. A famous bearer is Ajay Stevens, a musical artist.
Means "fought to turn" in Yoruba, traditionally given to children born facing downwards or sideways.
Likely a combination of the phonetic elements a and jay and Asia 1, similarly to Anasia.
One of the thirteen Mayan gods who created human beings. Ajbit assisted in the actual construction work.
Alternate transcription of Thai อัจฉรา (see Atchara).
Alternate transcription of Thai อัจฉราพร (see Atcharaphon).
Alternate transcription of Thai อัจฉรีย์ (see Atchari).

column3: อัจฉริยา, อัจฉริยะ(Thai)
column12: Alternate transcription of Thai อัจฉริยา or อัจฉริยะ (see Atchariya).
Local form of Agda traditionally found in Scania.
Means "wealth, money, profit" in Yoruba. This is the name of a goddess of wealth, prosperity, and business in Yoruba tradition.
From the brand of perfume called Ajee, which was introduced by Revlon in 1994. A known bearer is American runner Ajeé Wilson (1994-).

column3: 아정(Korean Hangul)|娥靜, 娥貞, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 娥 (a) meaning "good, beautiful" combined with 靜 (jeong) meaning "quiet, still, gentle" or 貞 (jeong) meaning "virtuous, chaste, loyal". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
Means "the goddess Aje has entered this house" or "wealth has come in" in Yoruba, from ajé "wealth, prosperity" and wọle "enter into" (itself from wọ "to enter" and ilé "house, home").

column3: 아지(Korean Hangul)|雅志, 娥志, 雅智, 娥智, 雅知, 娥知, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 雅 (a) meaning "elegant, graceful, refined" or 娥 (a) meaning "good, beautiful" combined with 志 (ji) meaning "will, purpose, ambition or 智 (ji) meaning "wisdom, intellect" or 知 (ji) meaning "know, perceive, comprehend". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
Means "valuable, auspicious, sacred" as well as "incantation, charm" and "king" in Indonesian.
Of uncertain meaning. This was the name of a prince of the Qing dynasty who held the title Prince Ying of the First Rank.
Possibly from the Manchu ᠠᠵᡳᡤᡝ ajige ("small, little, young"), this was the name of a concubine of Nurhaci.
Means "wakes up to be pampered" in Yoruba, from jí "to wake" and‎ kẹ́ "to care for, cherish".

column3: 아진(Korean Hangul)|雅真, 娥珍, 娥鎭, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Combination of an a hanja, like 雅 meaning "clean, pure" or 娥 meaning "pretty, lovely, beautiful," and a jin hanja, such as 真 meaning "true, real, genuine," 珍 meaning "treasure" or 鎭 meaning "quellable."
Rare masculine name of unknown meaning.

Means Invincible. Also another name of Lord Shri Krishna.-------------------------------------Ajinkyatara is the name of the great king Shivaji Maharaj's fort. It's meaning is "the on who can never be conquered. "
Spanish form of Ahinoam, occurring in several Spanish translations of the Bible. It is not commonly used as a given name.

column3: 紫陽花(Japanese Kanji)|あじさい(Japanese Hiragana)|アジサイ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 紫陽花 (ajisai) meaning "hydrangea" which comes from combining 紫 (murasaki) meaning "purple, violet", 陽 (yō) meaning "light, sun, male", and 花 (hana, ka) meaning "flower". Other kanji or combinations of kanji can also form this name.

Means "invincible lord" from Sanskrit अजित (ajita) meaning "unconquered, invincible" and नाथ (nātha) meaning "master, lord". In Jain tradition this is the name of the second of the 24 tirthankaras (enlightened spiritual teachers).
Possibly a Esperanto form of Aiki.
In Albanian mythology, Ajkuna is the wife of Muji.
Hungarian variant of Ayla 2. From Turkish origin.
Bosnian form of the Turkish name Aylin.
Means "most beautiful" in Arabic (a superlative of Jamal).
Sanskrit- means wisdom. It is the third-eye chakra is the sixth primary chakra according to Hindu tradition.
From the name of Fort Ajnácskő in Slovakia.

The god of the Lotuko, a Sudanese people. It was believed that he was benevolent, but only if men chose to keep him so. Family strife was seen to be the cue for death to enter the family, and indeed a story is told of a Lotuko mother who implored Ajok to restore her dead child to life. The god obliged, but the woman's husband was angry, and berated his wife, killing the child. Ajok, annoyed, declared that never again would he raise a Lotuko, and that from this on, death would be permanent for his people.
Means "jointly beloved" or "pampered by all" in Yoruba, from jọ "together, jointly; to assemble, congregate" and‎ kẹ́ "to care for, cherish".
Meaning uncertain. The best known bearer of this name is the Dutch television and radio presenter Ajouad El Miloudi (b. 1987), who is of Moroccan descent.
Modern coinage, intended as a feminine form of Ajtony.
Ajtony was an early-11th-century ruler in the territory now known as Banat in present-day Romania and Serbia.
One of the thirteen Mayan gods who created human beings. He did mainly the same work as Ajbit did.

column3: 아주(Korean Hangul)|雅周, 娥周, 雅珠, 娥珠, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 雅 (a) meaning "elegant, graceful, refined" or 娥 (a) meaning "good, beautiful" combined with 周 (ju) meaning "circumference" or 珠 (ju) meaning "jewel, pearl". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 아준(Korean Hangul)|娥俊, 娥埈, 娥峻, 雅俊, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Combination of an a hanja, like 娥 meaning "pretty, lovely, beautiful" or 雅 meaning "clean, pure," and a jun hanja, such as 俊 meaning "talented, capable; handsome," 埈 or 峻, both meaning "high, tall; steep."
Variant of Ajut using -na, a Greenlandic suffix indicating a personal name. In Greenlandic mythology, Ajuna is a woman who escapes from her pursuer and becomes the sun.

Ajuricaba (died c. 1728) was a leader of the Manaos indigenous nation in the early 18th century. He rebelled against the colonizers, refusing to serve as a slave where he became a symbol of resistance and freedom.
Derived from Canadian Arctic ajujuq meaning "runs away". In Greenland mythology Ajut is the name of the woman who flees from her pursuer and becomes the sun.
Means "horses" in Arabic, the plural of جواد (jawād) meaning "steed, horse".

Means "birthgiver" or "mother of cradles" in Yakut. Ajysyt wwas the mother goddess in Yakut mythology. She was said to be present whenever one of her people gave birth, and she brought with her the soul of the child, so that a complete human being could be brought into existence.

Directly taken from Japanese 赤 (aka) meaning "red". Red is the color of youth and celebration in Japan. This name was popular in the Edo Era, nowadays it's more popular as a name element as, for example, in Akari.
Alternate transcription of Hindi आकाश (see Akash).
From Russian академия (akademiya), meaning "philosophy of academia".

column3: 赤彦, 朱彦(Japanese Kanji)|あかひこ(Japanese Hiragana)|アカヒコ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From 赤/朱 (aka) meaning "red" combined with 彦 (hiko) meaning "boy, prince."This name is extremely rare.

column3: 赤人, 紅一, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 赤 (aka) meaning "red" and 人 (hito) meaning "person". Other kanji combinations can be used.A notable bearer is Yamabe no Akahito (fl. 724–736), a poet of the Nara period.
Means "undefeated, unbeatable", possibly taken from the title of the gospel song ‘Akahlulwa lutho uuJesu’.

column3: 愛海, 朱衣(Japanese Kanji)|あかい(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: From the Japanese kanji 愛 (a) meaning "love, affection" and 海 (kai) meaning "sea; ocean". It can also derive from 朱 (aka) meaning "crimson red" and 衣 (i) meaning "clothing".Other kanji combinations are possible.
Russian form of Achaikos via Achaicus.
Means "to singe" in Cook Islands Maori.
Direct translation is "big foot" or "big feet" referencing a less literal translation of "like a wolf with big paws, he can travel long distances over snow."
Derived either from causative prefix aka- and iti meaning "little, small" or from aka meaning "sin, fault" and iti meaning "little, small."
Possibly a combination of the phonetic prefix a and Kaya 2. It shares a sound with names such as Makiyah.
From Japanese 朱 (aka) meaning "crimson, red" combined with 希 (ki) meaning "Greece". Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.This is name is also used as a surname.
Greek form of Acacia or feminine form of Akakios.
Bulgarian, Russian and Ukrainian form of Akakios.

column3: あかこ(Japanese Hiragana)|アカコ(Japanese Katakana)|紅子, 朱子, 丹子, 赤子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 紅, 朱, 丹, or 赤 (aka) meaning "red" and 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Means "inner life" or "love" in Tamil. It refers to a genre of classical Tamil poetry.
Hawaiian name meaning "smart". Cognate of Atamai.

Possibly from Greek ἀκάμας (akamas) meaning "untiring, unwearying", a word derived from ἀ (a), a negative prefix, and κάμνω (kamno) "to grow weary, to be in distress". This was the name of several characters in Greek mythology.

Literally meaning "red eye", when taking a picture of someone using a flash, the person's eyes often appear red in the resulting photo - that phenomenon is called akame in Japanese. A fictional bearer of the name is Akame from the manga and anime Akame ga Kill.
From Japanese 愛 (a) meaning "love, affection", 奏 (ka) meaning "to play (music)" combined with 心 (mi) meaning "heart, mind, soul". Other kanji combinations are possible.

Means "she tries it for nothing" or "she does it there for nothing" in Jola-Fonyi. This is applied to a woman in reference to her repeated failure to carry a pregnancy to term, implying the bearer gets pregnant in vain.
Means "let the bones lie, make peace" in Cook Islands Maori.

column3: あかな(Japanese Hiragana)|アカナ(Japanese Katakana)|赤鳴, 紅魚, 朱捺, 赤梛, 紅生, 朱汝, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|𐰦𐰀 : 𐰴𐰀(Old Turkic)
column12: From Japanese 赤 (aka) meaning "red", 紅 (aka) meaning "crimson" or 朱 (aka) meaning "cinnabar, vermilion" combined with 汝 (na) meaning "thou, you", 鳴 (na) meaning "to sound, to ring, to echo" or 魚 (na) meaning "fish". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 茜子(Japanese Kanji)|あかねこ(Japanese Hiragana)|アカネコ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Akane combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child."This name is very rarely used.

From Japanese 茜 (akane) meaning "deep red, dye from the rubia plant" combined with 男 (o) meaning "male", 夫 (o) meaning "husband, man" or 雄 (o) meaning "masculine, male, hero, leader, superiority, excellence". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Fijian form of Angus, and Agnes.
Means "especially cared for" in Yoruba, from kàn "touch, concern" and kẹ́ "to care for, cherish".
Means "special to have" or "profitable encounter" in Yoruba.

column3: 緋乃, 丹野, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 緋 (aka) meaning "scarlet, red" combined with 乃 (no), a possessive particle. Other kanji combinations are possible.
Alternate transcription of Thai อัครชัย (see Akkharachai).
Alternate transcription of Thai อัครเดช (see Akkharadet).
Alternate transcription of Thai อัครเดช (see Akkharadet).
Alternate transcription of Thai อัครเดช (see Akkharadet).

Alternate transcription of Thai อัครพล (see Akkharaphon).

It could be from 朱 (aka) meaning "vermilion red" combined with 里 (ri) meaning "village", and 子 (ko) meaning "child, sign of the rat, first sign of the Chinese zodiac". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: あかる(Japanese Hiragana)|安加流, 晶琉, 明, 明日瑠, 明瑠, 耀, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 安 (a) meaning "peace", 加 (ka) meaning "add, addition, increase" combined with 流 (ru) meaning "to flow". Other kanji combinations are possible.

Used by author Anne Rice for a character in her 'Vampire Chronicles' series - introduced in the second novel, 'The Vampire Lestat' (1985) - where it belongs to a pre-Egyptian queen who becomes the first vampire and 'mother' of all vampires. Akasha was portrayed by Aaliyah in the 2002 movie 'Queen of the Damned'. Rice possibly intended the name to appear derived from the identical Sanskrit word आकाश (ākāśa) meaning "open space, sky, ether, quintessence".
Means "flew in the sky". It is one of the 108 names of the goddess Durga.

Means "heavenly womb" or "essence of space" from Sanskrit आकाश (ākāśa) meaning "open space, sky" and गर्भ (garbha) meaning "womb, interior, essence, substance". In Buddhist tradition this is the name of a bodhisattva associated with the element of space.

column3: あかし(Japanese Hiragana)|朱, 赫, 照石, 証, 丹, 燈, 明, 明志, 明石, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 朱 (akashi) meaning "vermilion, crimson". Other kanji or combinations of kanji can form this name as well.

column3: 赤鹿(Japanese Kanji)|あかしか(Japanese Hiragana)|アカシカ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 赤鹿 (akashika) meaning "red deer".
Meaning “one who is resilient or brave”.

Derived from the Greek adjective ἀκαταμάχητος (akatamachetos) meaning "unconquerable", which consists of the Greek negative prefix ἀ (a) and the Greek verb καταμάχομαι (katamachomai) meaning "to conquer, to subdue by fighting".Since medieval times (as early as the 11th century), Akatamachetos is also used as an epithet for the Virgin Mary.
Means "to observe and mark". This is the name of a star important for its use in navigation.
Meaning "one who is faithful", deriving from the verb kutendeka.

In the popular video game series 'The Elder Scrolls', Akatosh is the chief deity of the Nine Divines (the pantheon of gods in the game). He is generally considered to be the first of the Gods to form in the Beginning Place; after his establishment, other spirits found the process of being easier and the various pantheons of the world emerged. He embodies the qualities of endurance, invincibility, and everlasting legitimacy while promoting the virtues of duty, service, and obedience. His avatar is a dragon, and he is often called the Dragon God of Time, with Alduin sometimes being mistaken as an aspect of him. Akatosh is thought to be the father of all dragons, and the dragons' leader Alduin was titled "First-Born of Akatosh".
Means "beautiful, precious uncle (father's brother)" from Greenlandic Áka and -tsiaq "beautiful, precious".

column3: 暁, 暁月, 緋月, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|あかつき(Japanese Hiragana)|アカツキ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From 暁 (akatsuki) meaning "dawn, daybreak," shifted from earlier akatoki, made up of 明 (aka) meaning "bright" and 時 (toki) meaning "time."It can also be combined with 月 (tsuki) meaning "moon." Alternatively, the first kanji can be substituted with one that can be read as aka, e.g. 緋 meaning "scarlet."One bearer of this name was I-Novel author Akatsuki Kambayashi (上林 暁), born Iwaki Tokuhiro (徳廣 巌城) (1902-1980).This name is rarely used.
From Turkish ak, meaning "white" and ay, meaning "moon".
Variant of Kayla. It has been used since 1980.
From Japanese 緋 (aka) meaning "red, scarlet" combined with 世 (yo) meaning "world". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Possibly a phonetic spelling of Acacia.
Derived from Old Norse aka "to drive". This is a by-name for Odin in Norse mythology.
Means "she must be introduced" in Nguni.
Alternate transcription of Urdu اکبر (see Akbar).
From Kyrgyz ак (ak) meaning "white" and бермет (bermet) meaning "pearl".

Means "white serpent" or "white dragon", derived from Turkic ak meaning "white" combined with Turkic büge or büke meaning "serpent, snake" as well as "dragon" (ultimately from Proto-Turkic böke). Over time, the latter word eventually took on the secondary and figurative meaning of "wise person", due to the fact that the dragon was regarded as a representation of wisdom.The second element of this name is not to be confused with the derivatives of Proto-Turkic *buka meaning "bull" (see Bugha).In Turkic mythology, Akbugha is the god of health and healing/medicine.
Is a Mayan mythology name, which means, 'of the night.'
Means "dear friend" in Turkish. Combination of common Turkish words "ak" meaning "white", and "can" meaning "life".
From the Arabic أقدس (aqdes) meaning “most sacred, the holiest”.
From Turkish ak meaning "white" combined with döl meaning "progeny".
Short form of Aleksi or variant of Aake.
Meaning "yearning for wisdom," "philosophy," or "lover (ake) of wisdom (akamai)".

column3: 曙(Japanese Kanji)|あけぼの(Japanese Hiragana)|アケボノ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From 曙 (akebono) meaning "dawn, daybreak," derived from a combination of 明け (ake) meaning "daybreak" and 仄 (hono) meaning "faint."This name is rarely given, if at all.

Means "soldier" in Lakota. From the Lakota akíčhita "soldier, army, military, troops, police".Historically this would have been a term applied to warrior members of society whenever they were on duty (as camp police, during a communal hunt or war path, as scouts, etc). In modern times, it's sometimes applied to policemen or soldiers of the US army.This is the name of a character on HBO's series 'Westworld'.
Variant of Akilah popularized by the 2006 movie 'Akeelah and the Bee'.
The name Akeer is often associated with strength, leadership, and resilience in Dinka culture, native to South Sudan.

column3: 明久, 明寿, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 明 (ake, aki) meaning "bright, light, clear, daybreak" and 久 (hisa) meaning "long time, long time ago" or 寿 (hisa) meaning "long life, lifespan". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Variant of Akira. In some cases it can be a combination of the phonetic prefix a with the name Keira.
Combination of the prefix a and Keisha.
Alternate transcription of Kazakh Әкежан (see Akezhan).
Alternate transcription of Thai เอกราช (see Ekkarat 2).

column3: 晏気子, 朱子, 曙子, 明子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 晏 (a) meaning "late in the day", 気 (ke) meaning "spirit; mood" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Hawaiian form of Adele or Asher.
Direct adoption of the Dutch and German name for the flower Aquilegia vulgaris "columbine".
Hawaiian form of Adriel and Adriela, from Hebrew ʿeḏer meaning "flock" and ʾel meaning "God", interpreted by some as meaning "God's Majesty".

The custodian of the ferryboat who ferries the souls of the deceased to the Egyptian underworld of Duat, and he was also said to rule Duat in general on behalf of Osiris. He was typically depicted with the head of a ram. Over time he came to be known as Cherti (or Kherty), which likely influenced the development of the Greek ferryman Charon.

column3: あけの(Japanese Hiragana)|明乃, 明野, 曙埜, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 明 (ake) meaning "bright" and 乃 (no), a possessive particle. Other kanji combinations are also possible.
Russian and Serbian form of Akepsimas.

Hellenized form of the Persian name Aqebshma, of which the meaning is still uncertain.This was the name of a Christian saint and martyr, a bishop of Hnaita in western Persia who was tortured to death in 376 AD.

Literally meaning “Black goat” in Basque, this name belongs to a spirit/deity in Basque mythology. Usually depicted as a billy goat, the spirit was earlier seen as pagan deity of the protection of animals and houses. Later on, Akerbeltz was demonized by Christianity as a living image of the devil.
Means "one who becomes prominent at a young age" or "he who reduces (humbles) himself in order to become king" in Yoruba.
Unknown meaning. Possibly derived from Akira

column3: 明, 開, 空, 朱, 暁, 明琉, 旭流, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|あける(Japanese Hiragana)|アケル(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From verbs 明ける (akeru) meaning "to dawn, grow light," 開ける (akeru) meaning "to open, unwrap, unlock" or 空ける (akeru) meaning "to empty, remove, make room; to move/clear out," also written as 朱, from ake meaning "scarlet, red," or 暁, from Akatsuki.These single kanji, along with 旭, from Asahi, can be suffixed with a ru kanji, like 琉, part of 琉璃 (ruri) meaning "lapis lazuli," or 流 meaning "current, flow."This name is rarely used.
Means "healing of a man", derived from Greek ἄκεσις (akesis) "healing, curing" combined with Greek ἀνδρός (andros) "of a man".
Means "healing one", derived from Ancient Greek ἄκος (akos) meaning "cure, remedy". This was the name of the goddess of curing illness and healing wounds in Greek mythology, a daughter of Asclepius.
Uncertain etymology. In Greek Mythology, this was the name of a Thracian king of Pieria and eponymous founder of the Macedonian city Akesamenai.
Derived from the Greek noun ἀκεστής (akestes) meaning "healer, mender".
Derived from Ancient Greek ἀκέστωρ (akestor) meaning "healer, saviour".
Means "son of Akestor" in Greek, derived from the name Akestor combined with the patronymic suffix ἴδης (ides).
Means "born during a famine" in Luo.
Variant of Akilah influenced by Keyla.

column3: 明義, 開義, 空義, 朱吉, 暁吉, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 明 (ake) meaning "bright, light, clear, daybreak" and 義 (yoshi) meaning "righteous" or 吉 (yoshi) meaning "lucky, fortunate, auspicious, good". Other kanji combinations are possible.If ake is spelled using 明, then this name can be read as Akiyoshi.
From Kazakh әке (ake) meaning "father" and жан (zhan) meaning "soul".
From Kazakh ақ (aq) meaning "white" and гүл (gul) meaning "flower".
Means "white coloured girl" in Turkmen, from the name elements ak meaning "white" and kyz meaing "girl".
Alternate transcription of Thai อัครชัย (see Akkharachai).
Alternate transcription of Thai อัครเดช (see Akkharadet).
Alternate transcription of Thai อัครเดช (see Akkharadet).
Alternate transcription of Thai อัครพล (see Akkharaphon).
Alternate transcription of Thai อัครพล (see Akkharaphon).
Russian and Ukrainian form of Ahab.

MEANING : sorrowless; free from pain or depression . Here अ means not + खेद means sorrow, pain, affliction Usage : Sanskrit, Indian, Tamil, Telugu, Nepali, Sinhalese, Hindi, Sikh, Punjabi, Kannada, Marathi, Gujarati, Assamese,Malayalam, Bengali, Fijian, Hinduism
Bulgarian, Russian and Ukrainian form of Achaios.
From Sanskrit अखिल (akhila) meaning "whole, complete" and ईश (isha) meaning "lord, ruler".
Alternate transcription of Greek Ἀχιλλεύς (see Achilleus).

column3: อาคิรา, อาคีรา, อาคีระ(Thai)
column5: /ʔaː˧.kʰi˦˥.raː˧/(อาคิรา)|/ʔaː˧.kʰiː˧.raː˧/(อาคีรา)|/ʔaː˧.kʰiː˧.ra˦˥/(อาคีระ)
column12: Means "Sun, sunlight" in Thai.It can be spelt อาคิรา, อาคีรา or อาคีระ.
Means "morals, ethics" in Arabic, the plural form of خلق (khuluq) meaning "character, morals".

In Inuit mythology, Akhlut is a spirit that takes the form of both a wolf and an orca. It is a vicious, dangerous beast. Its tracks can be recognized because they are wolf tracks that lead to and from the ocean.
Combination of the given name Akhmad and Kazakh жан (zhan) meaning "soul", ultimately of Persian origin.
From the given name Akhmet combined with Kazakh жан (zhan) meaning "soul" (of Persian origin).
From Egyptian ꜥẖm meaning "falcon, cultivation image of a perching falcon" or "body of a god".
Means "bravery, valour, courage" in Ossetian. This is the name of a hero in the Nart sagas.
Combination of Akhsar and the Turkish military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".
Variant of Akhsar. This is the name of a hero in the Nart sagas.
Also is a name of a flower in Iran called گل اختر, which is Edible canna in English.
Combines elements of “star” and “king”; Akhtarmaluk means “star of kings”.
Means "star of the religion", from Persian اختر (akhtar) meaning "star" and Arabic دين (dīn) meaning "religion".
Means "star of Islam", from Persian اختر (akhtar) meaning "star" and Islam, the name of the religion (ultimately from Arabic إسلام).
Means "star of the era" from Persian اختر (akhtar) meaning "star" combined with Arabic زمان (zamān) meaning "time, age, era".
Alternate transcription of Bengali আখতারুজ্জামান (see Akhtaruzzaman).
Means "scholar", deriving from ākh meaning "mind, soul".
Derived from Arabic أخيار (ʾakhyār) meaning "best", the elative of خير (khayr) meaning "goodness, good".
Elaboration of Kiana 2 with the prefix a-

column3: アキアラ(Japanese Katakana)|あきあら(Japanese Hiragana)|明愛羅, 秋愛羅(Japanese Kanji)
column12: Usage of this name is influenced by the name Chiara. It can be spelled with 明 or 秋 (aki) meaning "bright" or "autumn", 愛 (a) meaning "love" and 羅 (ra) meaning "gauze"

column3: あきあつ(Japanese Hiragana)|アキアツ(Japanese Katakana)|明篤, 昭篤, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese combined with 明 (aki) or 昭 (aki) both meaning "bright" combined with 篤 (atsu) meaning "honest". Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.

column3: 彰近, 晶睦, 明親, 昭親, 章睦, 秋近, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 晶 (aki) meaning "clear, crystal", 明 (aki) or 昭 (aki) both meaning "bright, light, clear" or 秋 (aki) meaning "autumn" combined with 睦 (chika, mutsumi) meaning "friendly, amiable, peaceful, intimate, harmonious". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 晶子, 明子, 秋子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
哲文, 顕文, 晃史, 暁章, 秋文, 彰典, 昭文, 章史, 聡文, 彬史, 明章, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 暁 (aki) meaning "dawn, daybreak" or 聡 (aki) meaning "smart, clever" combined with 典 (fumi) meaning "ceremony" or 章 (fumi) meaning "section, chapter, badge". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 秋房, 章房, 明房, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 秋 (aki) meaning "autumn" and 房 (fusa) meaning "chamber, room". Other kanji combinations can be used.
Means "Rock Ptarmigan" in Greenlandic. A Rock Ptarmigan is a type of bird.

column3: あきは(Japanese Hiragana)|愛祈羽, 旭葉, 瑛華, 輝巴, 暁巴, 顕場, 燦華, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 亜 (a) meaning "second, Asia", 希 (ki) meaning "hope, rare" combined with 場 (ha) meaning "place". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 旭明, 旭春, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 旭 (aki) meaning "rising sun" combined with 明 (haru) meaning "bright". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 暁英, 暁秀, 顕栄, 顕秀, 彰英, 彰秀, 昌秀, 昭英, 章秀, 聡英, 聡秀, 耀英, 晟秀, 曉秀, 堯秀, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 暁 (aki) meaning "daybreak, dawn, occurance, event", 顕 (aki) meaning "appear, existing", 彰 (aki) meaning "clear, obvious", 昌 (aki) meaning "prosperous, good", 章 (aki) meaning "section, badge, chapter", 聡 (aki) meaning "intelligent, bright, smart", 耀 (aki) meaning "shine, sparkle, gleam, twinkle", or 晟 (aki) meaning "bright, clear" combined with 秀 (hide) meaning "exemplary, excel, excellence, outstanding", 英 (hide) meaning "hero, outstanding", or 栄 (hide) meaning "flourish, prosperity, honor, glory, splendor". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 秋姫, 章姫, 彬姫, 明姫, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 秋 (aki) meaning "autumn" or 章 (aki) meaning "chapter; section" combined with 姫 (hime) meaning "princess". Other kanji combinations are possible.This is also the name of Fragaria ananassa strawberries. They are known for being a bit tart.

column3: 明博, 昭博, 章博, 明宏, 昭宏, 明弘, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|あきひろ(Japanese Hiragana)|アキヒロ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 明 (aki) meaning "bright, light, clear", 昭 (aki) meaning "bright, luminous" or 章 (aki) meaning "chapter" combined with 博 (hiro) meaning "command, esteem", 宏 (hiro) meaning "wide, spacious, great, vast" or 弘 (hiro) meaning "enlarge, expand, great". Other combinations of kanji can form this name as well.

column3: アキヒサ(Japanese Katakana)|あきひさ(Japanese Hiragana)|明寿, 暁恆, 秋悠, 章契, 商尚, 晃恒, 彰久, 瑛央, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 明 (aki) meaning "bright" and 央 (hisa) meaning "centre, middle". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: あきほ(Japanese Hiragana)|アキホ(Japanese Katakana)|旭保, 秋穂, 明歩, 昭甫, 晶法, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 旭 (aki) meaning "rising sun" combined with 保 (ho) meaning "to protect, to safeguard, to defend". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Variant transcription of Aki 2 used during the Edo Period.
A variant of Akiki, Meaning ‘friend’ in Luo, Nyoro and Tooro.

column3: あきじ(Japanese Hiragana)|アキジ(Japanese Katakana)|晶慈, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 晶 (aki) meaning "clear, crystal" and 慈 (ji) meaning "mercy". Other kanji can be used.

column3: あきか(Japanese Hiragana)|アキカ(Japanese Katakana)|暁嘩, 陽芳, 亮河, 燦架, 旦革, 曉誇, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 瞭 (aki) meaning "obvious" combined with 穫 (ka) meaning "harvest". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 昭一, 昭和, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese kanji 明 (aki) meaning "bright" or 朗 (aki) meaning "bright, clear" or 昭 (aki) meaning "shining" combined with 和 (kazu) meaning "harmony, peace" or 一 (kazu) meaning "one". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Means "friend" in Nkore, spoken in Uganda.
Alternate transcription of Aqil and masculine form of Akilah.
Variant of Akilah or a combination of Akil with the phonetic element ee.
Hawaiian form of Adrian, meaning "from the city of Adria".
Finnish and Swedish form of Achilles.
Diminutive or feminine form of Akim.

column3: 明正, 昭正, 彰正, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|あきまさ(Japanese Hiragana)|アキマサ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 明 (aki) meaning "bright, light, clear", 昭 (aki) meaning "bright, luminous" or 彰 (aki) meaning "obvious, clear" combined with 正 (masa) meaning "right, proper, correct". Other combinations of kanji can form this name as well.
Means "My son has arrived." in celebration of a son being born from the Gur language elements “Aki-” meaning "he has arrived" and the suffix -me meaning “child”.

column3: アキミ(Japanese Katakana)|あきみ(Japanese Hiragana)|亜貴巳, 晶水, 赤君, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 赤 (a) meaning "red", 希 (ki) meaning "hope", and 見 (mi) meaning "view, see, perspective". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 明道, 昭道, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 明 (aki) or 昭 (aki) both meaning "bright" combined with 道 (michi) meaning "path, road, way". Other kanji combinations can be used.
Means "one who roams by the place under windows opposite the plank bed" in Greenlandic.
Means "influx, rush, invasion, raid" in Turkish.

column3: あきな(Japanese Hiragana)|アキナ(Japanese Katakana)|明奈, 明名, 明南, 秋菜, 秋名, 亜稀菜, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 明 (aki) meaning "bright", or 亜 (a) meaning "second, Asia" combined with 稀 (ki) meaning "scarce, rare" that is the combined with 奈 (na) meaning "Nara, what, apple tree" or 名 (na) meaning "name reputation". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 晶直, 明直, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 晶 (aki) meaning "clear, crystal", 明 (aki) meaning "bright, light, clear" or 秋 (aki) meaning "autumn" combined with 直 (nao) meaning "straight, direct". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 秋成, 旺成(Japanese Kanji)|あきなり(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: From the Japanese Kanji 秋 (aki) meaning "autumn" or 旺 (aki) meaning "prosperous; energic" combined with 成 (nari) meaning "to become".Other kanji combinations are possible.A famous bearer is Akinari Ueda (1734-1809), a Japanese author, scholar and waka poet, and a prominent literary figure in 18th-century Japan. He was an early writer in the yomihon genre and his two masterpieces, Ugetsu Monogatari ("Tales of Rain and the Moon") and Harusame Monogatari ("Tales of Spring Rain"), are central to the canon of Japanese literature.
Means "bravery comes with wealth" in Yoruba.
From Turkish akıncı meaning "akinji, cavalry soldier, raider".
Russian and Serbian form of Akindynos.
From Greek ἀκίνδυνος (akindynos) meaning "free from danger, without danger, harmless", composed of the negative prefix ἀ (a) and κίνδυνος (kindynos) "danger, hazard, venture".
From Japanese 旭 (aki) meaning "rising sun" combined with 音 (ne) meaning "sound". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Variant form of Iakinf, which itself is a variant form of Giakinf.
Means "bravery expands the coast of wealth" in Yoruba.
Variant form of Akinf, which itself is a variant form of Iakinf. A known bearer of this name was the Russian industrialist Akinfiy Demidov (1678-1745).
Means "valour has been added to me".

Means "bravery is honourable" or "valour has dignity" in Yoruba, from akín "courage, valour; brave person, warrior" and either ni "to be" or ní "to have, possess" combined ẹ̀yẹ "honour, respect, dignity".

column3: あきの(Japanese Hiragana)|あき野(Kanji/Hiragana)|旭乃, 昭乃, 秋乃, 明乃, 晶乃, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 旭 (aki) meaning "rising sun" combined with 乃 (no), a possessive particle. Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.

column3: 昭信, 顕信, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: Japanese masculine name derived from 昭 (aki) meaning "bright, luminous" and 信 (nobu) meaning "faith, trust, believe". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 明徳, 明紀, 明憲, 昭徳, 昭典, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|あきのり(Japanese Hiragana)|アキノリ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 明 (aki) meaning "bright, light, clear" or 昭 (aki) meaning "bright, luminous" combined with 徳 (nori) meaning "virtue, benevolence", 紀 (nori) meaning "record, chronicle", 憲 (nori) meaning "law" or 典 (nori) meaning "rule, ceremony". Other kanji combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 秋乃輔, 秋之助, 昭之助, 明之助, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 秋 (aki) meaning "autumn", 昭 (aki) meaning "shining" or 明 (aki) meaning "clear, bright" combined with 輔 (suke) meaning "help" or 助 (suke) meaning "assistance". Other kanji combinations are also possible.
Means “warrior of joy” or “ bravery brings joy”. From the Yoruba words “Akin" (meaning warrior, bravery, valour) and "tayo" (meaning joy, happiness).

秋郎, 晶朗, 旺郎, 映郎, 章郎, 爽郎, 明朗, 陽郎, 皓郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 秋 (aki) meaning "autumn" combined with 郎 (rou) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 昭, 明, 亮, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 昭 (akiru) meaning "bright", 明 (akiru) meaning "bright, clear, daybreak, light", or 亮 (akiru) meaning "clear". Other kanji or kanji combinations are possible.
Greek form of Acis as well as diminutive of many Greek names also very different from each other such as Theodoros, Andreas, Athanasios and Georgios.

column3: あきさだ(Japanese Hiragana)|アキサダ(Japanese Katakana)|顕定, 晶貞, 秋定, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 晶 (aki) meaning "clear, crystal", 明 (aki) meaning "bright, light, clear, daybreak" or 秋 (aki) meaning "autumn" combined with 貞 (sada) meaning "faithfulness, uprightness" or 定 (sada) meaning "determine, establish, decide". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Japanese 瑛 (aki) meaning "crystal" combined with 世 (se) meaning "generations". Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.
Combination of the prefix a and Kisha.

column3: 彰繁, 彰成, 明繁, 昭成, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From with 彰 (aki) meaning "clear, obvious" or 明 (aki) or 昭 (aki) both meaning "bright" combined with 繁 (shige) meaning "flourishing, luxuriant" or 成 (shige) meaning "become". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 顕輔, 顕亮, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 顕 (aki) meaning "evident, clear" combined with 輔 (suke) meaning "help" or 亮 (suke) meaning "clear". Other kanji combinations are also possible.

column3: あきた(Japanese Hiragana)|アキタ(Japanese Katakana)|昭太, 明大, 秋太, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 秋 (aki) meaning "autumn" and 太 (ta) meaning "big". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 丙正, 丙忠, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 丙 (aki, hei) meaning "third in rank" combined with 正 (tada, tadashi, masa) meaning "correct, proper, justice" or 忠 (tada, tadashi, chu) meaning "loyalty". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 明孝, 昭孝, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 明 (aki) or 昭 (aki) both meaning "bright" combined with 孝 (taka) meaning "filial piety" or 貴 (taka) meaning "expensive, valuable". Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.

column3: アキタケ(Japanese Katakana)|あきたけ(Japanese Hiragana)|昭武, 明丈, 秋武, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 秋 (aki) meaning "autumn" and 武 (take) meaning "military, martial". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 顕智, 晶智, 晶朋, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 顕 (aki.raka) meaning "to appear, apparent, visible" combined with 智 (tomo, chi) meaning "wisdom, intellect" or 朋 (tomo) meaning "friend". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 晃智, 秋登志, 彰利, 秋敏, 彰寿, 彰敏, 昭十四, 昭肇, 章年, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 晃 (aki) meaning "clear" combined with 智 (toshi) meaning "wisdom; knowledge; intelligence". Other kanji combinations are possible.

Other kanji combinations are possible.
Russian form of Acis or short form of Yakim or Akim.

column3: 明泰, 秋泰, 明保, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 秋 (aki) meaning "autumn" and 保 (yasu) meaning "to protect, to defend". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 明代, 聡世, 吾生洋, 阿葵陽, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 明 (aki) meaning "bright, clear" combined with 代 (yo) meaning "world, generation". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column12: From the Japanese kanji 昭 (aki) meaning "shining" or 章 (aki) meaning "chapter; section" combined with 良 (yoshi) meaning "good". It can also derive from 明 (aki) meaning "clear; bright; tomorrow" and 義 (yoshi) meaning "justice" or 好 (yoshi) meaning "fondness; what one likes".Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 昭如, 章之, 昭之 晃志(Japanese Kanji)|あきゆき(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: Derived from the Japanese kanji 昭 (aki) meaning "bright" or 章 (aki) meaning "chapter; section" or 晃 (aki) meaning "clear" combined with 如 (yuki) meaning "likeness; such as; to seem" or 之 (yuki) meaning "of; this" or 志 (yuki) meaning "purpose; will; ambition".Other characters combinations are also possible.
Name of a main character, Akiza Izinski, in the anime series 'Yu-Gi-Oh! 5D', known in Japan as Aki Izayoi (十六夜 アキ).

column12: Short form of Atsuko. Akko is a character in the popular Anime series "Little Witch Academia". It coincides with Japanese 悪狐 (akko) meaning "bad fox".

Variant of Achaab. In Ezra 2:45, Akkub is the head of a family of Nethinim. In 1 Chronicles 3:24, Akkub is a son of Elionenai, descendant of Solomon living in the Kingdom of Judah around 420 BCE. In 1 Chronicles 9:17, Ezra 2:42, and Nehemiah 7:45, Akkub is a Levite gatekeeper at the Temple in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian captivity.

Ak Kübey is traditionally interpreted as a celestial feminine entity within Turkic mythology, symbolizing the protector of innocence and the nurturer of souls. It is derived from Ak ("white," "pure," "sacred") and kübe/kübey (a term linked to kübe, meaning "vessel" or "womb," and küde-, "to guard/protect"). She represents the divine vitality of the World Tree, Ulu Kayın. Unlike mere deities, she is the silent pulse within the trunk, nourishing the primordial man Er Sogotoh with sacred life-force#. While some folklore connects her to Kayra Han, she operates as a distinct manifestation of primordial maternal creation, symbolizing the bridge between celestial purity and earthly life.
From Kazakh ақ (aq) meaning "white" and күміс (kümis) "silver".
From Turkish ak meaning "white" and kutlu meaning "happy, blessed".
From Kyrgyz ак (ak) meaning “white” and кыз (kyz) meaning “girl, daughter”.

Means "beautiful chosen one" in Quechua, from akllakuy, "to choose" and sumaq, "beautiful".

From the given name Akmat combined with beg meaning "chieftan, master".
Combination of the word ak, meaning "white", and the given name Myrat.
In Inuit mythology, Akna ("mother") is a goddess of fertility and childbirth. Akna is also the name of a goddess of motherhood and birthing in Mayan mythology.
From Kazakh ақ (aq) or Turkmen ak meaning "white" and Kazakh нұр (nur) or Turkmen nur meaning "light".

From Iteso in eastern uganda. Meaning nicelooking.

Akoma is the creator god of Pahuin mythology. His name Means “creator” in Pahuin, a common language in parts of São Tomé and Principe, southern Cameroon, much of northern Gabon, and mainland Equatorial Guinea.

In Greek mythology, this was the name of a young man who begged the goddess Artemis for help in marrying the maiden Cydippe. The two went on to become the ancestors of the Acontiadae tribe.
Nigerian name from the Idoma tribe of Benue State meaning "great warrior" or "war leader."

Feminine of Okoth, meaning born while it was raining

column12: From Japanese 亜 (a) meaning "second, Asia" or 安 (a) meaning "calm, peaceful" combined with 琴 (koto), which refers to a type of musical instrument similar to a harp. Other kanji combinations are also possible.
Akou is a name often given to a girl born on a Wednesday in Ewe culture.
Name of Ewe origin, meaning "God answered".
Means "first son of first daughter" in Ibibio.
From Turkic ak meaning "white" and parăs meaning "leopard".

Akrab is a name of a star in constellation Scorpius, also known as Beta Scorpii. Beta Scorpii bore the traditional names Acrab, Akrab or Elacrab, all deriving from the Arabic name (Arabic: العقرب‎) al-'Aqrab "the Scorpion"

Means "of the heights, extremities" in Ancient Greek, ultimately derived from ἄκρος (akros) meaning "edge, outermost, extreme; highest, top, best". This was the name of a Naiad daughter of the river Asterion in Greek mythology, who nursed the infant goddess Hera along with her sisters Euboea and Prosymna.
The God of Fertility and the turnip in Finnish Mythology. He was also the protector of beans, peas, cabbage, flax and hemp.
Means "unmixed, pure" as well as "violent, intemperate" in Ancient Greek. In some accounts this was another name for Acratopotes, a daemon of unmixed wine and incontinence.
Alternate transcription of Arabic أكرم (see Akram).
Derived from Sanskrit आकार (ākār) meaning "appearance, look" or "shape, form".
Means "expensive" and "precise" in Greek. Akrive was the name of a 4th-century Eastern Orthodox martyr, one of 40 holy virgins who were martyred with the deacon Ammon (or Ammoun) in Thrace.
Means "head of the community", derived from Ancient Greek ἄκρος (akros) meaning "highest, topmost" and δῆμος (demos) meaning "the people".
From a Greek word meaning "an elevation" or "point."

Derived from Turkish ak "white; clear; pure" and sel "flood; whitewater; torrent".

Variant (chiefly Odia) and feminine form (chiefly South Indian) of Akshay.

Means "indestructible mind" or "inexhaustible awareness" from Sanskrit अक्षय (akṣaya) meaning "undecaying, imperishable" and मति (mati) meaning "mind, thought". In Buddhist tradition this is the name of a bodhisattva associated with auspicious aeons in which buddhas emerge (bhadrakalpa).
Derived from the Sanskrit word "Aksha", which means "eyes". Akshika has a feminine connotation and means "one with good eyes."
Derived from Sanskrit अक्षित (akśita) meaning "undying, immortal".
Means "imperishableness; imperishable" in Sanskrit, Hindi and Marathi.
Means "immovable" in Sanskrit. This is the name of a buddha who represents consciousness and reflection in Mahayana and Vajrayana tradition.

Nordic and Serbian form of Aksinya.
From Turkmen ak meaning "white" combined with soltan "Sultan".

Formed from Ak "white, pure, clean" and Su "water." It denotes "the untainted essence of purity," mirroring the shimmering, crystal-clear water of mountain sources; also carries the weight of historical geography in East Turkestan.
Alternate transcription of Bengali আখতার (see Akhtar).

Derived from Ancient Greek ἀκτή (akte), which can mean either "headland, cape, promontory" or "corn, grain". This is the name of the ninth of the twelve Horai (hours) in Greek mythology, goddess of an hour of the afternoon associated with eating and pleasure.
Russian and Ukrainian form of Actaeus.
From Kazakh ақ (aq) meaning "white" and толқын (tolqyn) meaning "wave".

Means "father's wealth" in Igbo, from àkụ̀ meaning "property, wealth" and ńnà meaning "father".

Means "she's not discouraged" in Bette Obudu.
Notable bearer is child actor Akwiraron Louis Beauvais.
In Inuit mythology, Akycha is a solar deity worshipped in Alaska.
Derived from the Turkish word ak meaning "white" and yıldız meaning "star".
Derived from Kyrgyz акыл (akyl) meaning "mind, intellect, reason" and ай (ay) meaning "moon". and In the Kyrgyz poem the Epic of Manas, Akylai is one of the two wives of the hero Manas.
From Kyrgyz акыл (akyl) or Kazakh ақыл (aqyl) meaning "mind, intellect, reason" combined with the Turkish military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".

Ala was a Hittite and Luwian goddess of the wilderness and partner of the god Runtiya. Her name is likely derived from the Luwian adjective ala- "high".
