column12: From Japanese 亜 (a) meaning "second, Asia" or 安 (a) meaning "peace, quiet" combined with 波 (na) meaning "wave". Other kanji combinations are possible.

Meaning uncertain, possibly an invented name, popularly associated with Arabic أناب (ʾanāba) meaning "to return" (a word found in the Quran, which is also the source of Muniba and Munib). Furthermore, many websites falsely claim that this name means "door of heaven", though none of the doors of Paradise in Islam have a name similar to this.This was used for the title character of the 2016 Pakistani television series Anabia or Anabiya, played by actress Neelam Muneer.
In the Kabbalah, Anabeil can be called upon to cure stupidity.

Derived from anacã, which is the (Brazilian) Portuguese name for an Amazonian bird that is known as the red-fan parrot in English.A known recent bearer of this name is the son (born in October 2016) of the South African supermodel Candice Swanepoel (b. 1988) and her partner Hermann Nicoli Rosa (b. 1982), a Brazilian male model.

Means "golden flower" in Taíno, from ana "flower" and caona "gold". This was the name of the cacica (a female cacique, or queen) who ruled the native Taíno (Arawak) people of the Caribbean island of Hispaniola when the conquistadors settled there in 1492. She was killed by the Spaniards in about 1503.
Meaning unknown, possibly derived from Ancelle.This was the name of a 1998 cyclone near Mauritius.

Meaning uncertain, probably from Scythian. This was the name of a Scythian prince and philosopher from the 6th century BC, included among the Seven Sages of Greece. It is also self-given name of the French revolutionary and anarchist Anacharsis Cloots (1755–1794).
Feminine form and masculine variant of Anaclet.
Means "anchorite" in Spanish. A more common spelling is Anacorita.
French and Guernésiais form of Anakreon.
Latinized form of Anakreon. This name was borne by a Greek lyric poet from the 5th century BC.
Short form of Ana Cristina. Combination of Ana and Cristina.

Latinized form of the Greek Ἀνακτορία (Anaktoria), derived from ἀνακτόρῐος (anaktorios) "royal", literally "belonging to a king, a lord" from ἀνάκτωρ (anaktor) "lord", from ἄναξ (anax) "lord". This name was mentioned in a poem by the 7th-century BC lyric poet Sappho as a female lover of hers.
Artistic version of Anna, created by Hungarian author Lajos Zilahi as his 1928 novels' main character.
Variant of Enedelia or a combination of Ana and Delia 1.
The character Anadil from The School For Good And Evil by Soman Chainani bears this name.
Possibly a contraction of Ana and Nadir.
Means "emerging, rising from the sea", derived from Greek αναδύομαι (anadyomai) meaning "to surface, emerge, rise to the surface". This was an epithet of Aphrodite.
Coined in the 1960s as a Breton masculine form of Anne 1.
It could be a variant of Anayeli, variation of Anael, or a combination of Ana and Eli 3.
Either a contraction of Ana and Elina or a clearly feminine elaboration of Anael.
Means "soft, smooth" or "promise, offer" in Awajún.
Combination of the name elements Ana an emphasising prefix and Geir meaning "spear".
From Sanskrit अनघ (anagha) meaning "sinless, faultless, innocent".
Combination of Ana and Grace. Anagrace was given to 5 girls in 2013.
Old Cornish name, possibly from Welsh anaw "wealth" and Welsh gwystl "hostage" (Cornish cognate gostel).
Variation of Anah used in Maori bible translations
Goddess of purity, goddess of rain, fragrant flower
Likely and elaboration of Anahí unless a variant of Anaia.
Possibly a variant of Anahuacatl, meaning "inhabitant of Anahuac" or "person from near the water".
Means "inhabitant of Anahuac" or "person from near the water".
Portuguese form and Spanish variant of Anahí.
Variant of Aniyah. This name was given to 167 girls born in the USA in 2011.
Form of Anaiah used in the Greek and Latin bibles.
Meaning uncertain. Maybe be related to Anica.

Variant form of Anahid, although it should be noted that at least one source claims that the name is derived from Greek ἀναιδής (anaides) meaning "shameless".A known bearer of this name was the Armenian classical pianist Anaida Sumbatyan (1905-1985).
Portuguese form of Anaïs. A famous bearer was Brazilian poet Anaíde Beiriz (1905-1930).
Gallicized form of the Armenian given name Anaida.

From Greek ἀναίδεια (anaideia) meaning "shamelessness", derived from ἀν- (an-) "without" (alternative form of the negative prefix ἀ- (a-) used before a vowel) combined with αἰδώς (aidos) "shame, decency, regard for others, respect, reverence". In Greek mythology, Anaideia was the personification of shamelessness, ruthlessness and unforgiveness. She was a companion of Hybris. Her opposite was Eleos, the personification of mercy.

Means "holiest" in Quenya. In The Silmarillion by J. R. R. Tolkien Anairë is the wife of Fingolfin and mother of Fingon, Turgon, Aredhel and Argon. Unlike her husband and children, she chooses to remain in Valinor.
Mix of Ana and Iris. This name is used by Peurto Rican voice actress Anairis Quiñones.
English and Galician form of Anaïs and Spanish and Catalan variant of Anaís.
Anaisha means “day” in Sanskrit and is used in Parsi and Zoroastrian communities.
Derived from Shona anashe, meaning "who is with God".
Similar to Anaya meaning "look up to god".
Possibly a variant of Anaya or Anaia.
A modern variant of the name Annika
Bosnian and Croatian form of Anacharsis.
Alternate transcription of Malayalam അനഘ (see Anagha).
Means "Kiwa's cave" in Māori. Kiwa is the guardian of the ocean. In Te Reo Māori the Pacific Ocean is known as Te Moana nui a Kiwa meaning 'The great ocean of Kiwa'.
Bulgarian, Croatian, German, Polish and Russian form of Anakletos (see Anacletus).
Derived from Greek ἀνά (ana) meaning "up, against" and κρέων (kreon) meaning "lord, ruler, king" (also compare Kreon).
Meaning "fire." A Hindu attendant god. He is one of the eight vasu deities who serve the god Indra.
Name combination of Ana and Laura.

Means "satisfied joy" or "her joy" in Hawaiian from ana meaning "satisfied, too much" or āna meaning "his, her" and le'a meaning "joy". It was borne by Hawaiian chiefess Analeʻa Keohokālole (1816-1869), the mother of Queen Liliʻuokalani.
Combination of Ana with Leah or Aleah, or sometimes an anglicized variant of Analía.
Old High German version of Anláf.
Variant of Analeigh, or possibly an anglicized form of Spanish Analía.
Variant of Analía, especially used in Peru and Mexico.
Either a variant of Analía or a combination of Ana and the popular name suffix -lia.
Spanish contraction of Ana and Lisa and Romansh variant of Annalisa.
Variant of Analise that was given to 18 girls in 2017.
Masculine form of Anna. It originates from Lofoten in Norway.
Possibly an elaboration of Ana. This name is chiefly found in Costa Rica.
A combination of Anna and Liza or variant of Annalisa.
A blend of the names Ana and Elizabeth.
Combination of Ana and Luisa.18 babies were named this in the United States in 2003.
English of Annalynn as well as a Filipino combination of Ana and the diminutive suffix Lyn
Elaboration of Ana using the suffix -lys.
Possibly from the name of the sixth chapter of the Quran (surah al-An'am), which means "cattle" in Arabic.
Contraction of Ana and María. This name is borne by Mexican writer and academic Anamari Gomís (born Ana María Gomís Iniesta, 1950).
Variant of Anna Maria recorded in 1715 in the parish register of Finchley Church, England, referring to Anne, Queen of Great Britain, and her elder sister, Queen Mary II of England.
Means "your power is great" in Dagbani.

column3: อนันต์(Thai)|อานันท์(Thai)
column12: Means "infinite, endless" in Thai, ultimately from Sanskrit अनन्त (ananta).
From Thai อนันต์ (anan) meaning "infinite, endless" and ชัย (chai) meaning "victory".
Possibly the Mongolian form of Ananda.
Malayalam and Tamil form of Ananda.
The name is a confluence of two basic Sanskrit root words: Ananda = happiness and Rajyaha = Kingdom, thus resulting in: Anandaraj = Kingdom of Happiness
Alternate transcription of Tamil ஆனந்தி (see Ananthi).
A fallen angel mentioned in the Book of Enoch.
Meaning: Plenty of Stars; There are many stars; Many Stars; There is an abundance of Stars; Star Abundance
Georgian form of Hananiah via its hellenized form Ananias.

Means "cloud of Yahweh" or "Yahweh has covered", from the Hebrew nouns עָנָן (ʿanan) "cloud" and יָהּ (yah) referring to the Hebrew God. This is the name of a minor character mentioned in the Old Testament.
Spanish and Icelandic form of Hananiah, via Latin Ananias.
Polish form of Hananiah (via Latin Ananias).
French and Franco-Provençal form of Hananiah via its Hellenized form Ananias.

Ananiel, Anânêl (Aramaic: עננאל, Greek: Ανανιας) was the 14th Watcher of the 20 leaders of the 200 fallen angels who are mentioned in an ancient work titled the Book of Enoch. The name Ananiel is sometimes translated as "Rain of God" even though the name is often confused with the name Hananiel. Michael Knibb interprets his name to be "cloud of God". The name came into Arabic from the Coptics who in turn transliterated it from the Greeks.

Means "force, constraint, necessity" in Ancient Greek. Ananke was the personification of destiny, necessity and fate in Greek mythology, depicted as holding a spindle. She marks the beginning of the cosmos, along with Chronos.
From Thai อนันต (ananta) meaning "boundless, infinite, endless" and ชัย (chai) meaning "victory".

Means "boundless practice" from Sanskrit अनन्त (ananta) meaning "infinite, endless" and चारित्र (cāritra) meaning "conduct, behaviour, observance, practice". This is the name of a bodhisattva mentioned in the Buddhist text the Lotus Sutra, believed to represent eternity.

column3: อนันตศักดิ์(Thai)
column12: From Thai อนันต (ananta) meaning "boundless, infinite, endless" and ศักดิ์ (sak) meaning "power".
Derived from Sanskrit अनन्तविक्रमतुङ्गदेव (anantavikramatungadeva) meaning "infinite valor of the high god". This is part of Airlangga's regnal name, as well as that of his uncle, Dharmawangsa.
From Javanese ananta meaning "endless", ultimately from Sanskrit अनन्त (ananta).
Latinized form of Hanan 1 via it's Hellenized form Ananos.
From Sanskrit अनन्य (ananya) meaning "matchless, unique, without equal".
Known as "Little Grandmother," this goddess of the Koryak people of Siberia is Matron of Reincarnation. She was worshipped at ceremonies following the birth of a new child.

Derived from the Greek verb ἀναψύχω (anapsycho) meaning "to cool (off), to revive by fresh air, to refresh; to recover oneself". This was the name of a late Roman woman letter writer who corresponded with Saint Jerome of Striden.
Borne by a 20-year-old Guanche woman sold at the slave market in Valencia in 1494.
Means "radiant, glowing", from the أَنَارَ (ʔanāra) meaning "light, illuminate".
Feminine form of Anar 1 or Azerbaijani form of Anara.
Means "there is the little one!" in Greenlandic.
Derived from Welsh an, itself an intensifying prefix, and arawd "speech; praise".
Derived from Kazakh and Kyrgyz анар (anar) meaning "pomegranate" combined with the Turkish military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".

Perhaps based on the English word anarchy meaning "absence of government". A known bearer of this name was Anarcha Westcott, an Alabama slave woman who, in the latter 1840s, was subjected to years of surgical experimentation at the hands of gynecologist J. Marion Sims.
An elaboration of Ana created by Cervantes for his novel 'Don Quixote' (1605).
Possibly a blend of Anayeli and Arely.
Alternate transcription of Greek Ανάργυρη (see Anargyri), which is the feminine form of Anargyros.
Means "son of the sun" in Quenya. This was the name of the younger son of Elendil in Tolkien's works. He was a king of Gondor and slain in combat with Sauron.

Means "pomegranate blossom, pomegranate bud" in Hindi, from अनार (anār) meaning "pomegranate" (of Persian origin) combined with कली (kalī) meaning "flower bud". This is the name of a legendary Mughal woman said to be a lover of emperor Jahangir.
From анар (anar) meaning "pommegranite" and кан (kan) meaning "blood".
Derived from Old Norse anu "ancestor" and herr "army".
Variant of Annarr. This is the name of a dwarf in Norse mythology.
From the name of an ancient Native American people who lived in Utah and Colorado.
Likely a combination of the phonetic elements a and nay and Asia 1, also possibly influenced by Anaya.
Archaic spelling of Aanasiina using the old Kleinschmidt orthography.
Derived from the Greek noun ἄνασσα (anassa) meaning "queen, lady". In other words, one could say that this name is the feminine form of Anax.

Italian variant and Haitian Creole form of Anastasia. A famous bearer of this name is Anastagia Pierre (1988-) who is a Bahamian-Haitian-American beauty queen, model, spokesperson, and television host, elected as Miss Bahamas Universe 2011.
Modern Greek diminutive of Anastasios, as it contains the modern Greek diminutive suffix -άκης (-akis). This name is typically only used informally, meaning: it does not appear on birth certificates.
Coined by Sabino Arana Goiri and Koldo Elizalde as a Basque equivalent of Anastasia and Anastasie.
Variant of Anastasia. This name was given to 16 girls born in the USA in 1987.
Languedocian, Provençal, Niçard, Milanese Lombard and Piedmontese form of Anastasius.
Catalan, Provençal and Languedocian form of Anastasia.
Romanian and Sicilian form of Anastasius.
Greek diminutive of Anastasia. Also compare the short form Tasoula.
Estonian form and Germanized transcription of Anastasia.

Variant transcription of Anastasiy.Anastasy Andreyevich Vonsyatsky (Russian: Анаста́сий Андре́евич Вонся́цкий, Polish: Anastazy Wąsiacki; June 12, 1898 – February 5, 1965) was a Russian anti-Bolshevik émigré and fascist leader based in the United States from the 1920s.
Transcription of Anastasiya used by Ukrainians in Poland.
Variant of Anastasia. Apparently, this name is most prevalent in South Africa and Ireland.
Danish, Swedish, Sicilian and English modern variant of Anastasia as well as a traditional Czech variant of Anastázie.
Esperanto form of Anastasia and Anastasios.

Means "free from malice, not envious, without spite" from the negative prefix अन्- (an-) combined with असूया (asūyā) meaning "envy, jealousy, malice". In Hindu mythology this is the name of an ascetic woman and the wife of the sage Atri.
Means "command, order, mandate" in Thai, ultimately from Sanskrit आज्ञप्ति (ājñapti).
Alteration of Anatolia, perhaps influenced by Natalia. In some cases it may be a combination of Ana and Talia.
Possibly means "fast" or "swarthy" in Guanche. It was borne by an acting mencey (leader) of Tenerife at the time of the conquest of the Canary Islands by the Crown of Castille.

Name of the fictional character Ananthema Device from the show Good Omens inspired by Terry Pratchett Neil Gaiman's book. The name is derived from the word meaning "someone who is disliked" or "a curse by a pope or minister of the church", which makes sense as the character is an occultist.
Apparently means "answer to prayers" in Hebrew, with the first element derived from Hebrew anáh "to answer". In the bible, Anathoth was one of the sons of Becher, who in turn was the son of Benjamin.
Perhaps an 18th- and 19th-century American alteration of Arethusa, possibly arising from a typographical error.
English form of Anatolianus. This name was borne by a saint (who was also called Antholian) from the 3rd century AD.
Croatian form of Anatolius and alternate transcription of Anatoliy most common in Germany and Poland.
Italian, Galician and Spanish form of Anatolius.
Bulgarian and Russian form of Anatolia.
Norwegian male form of Anna or variation of Anton.

Dutch and Flemish form of Anatolius.In Belgium (specifically Flanders) and the Netherlands, this name is best known for being the name of the primary antagonist in the well-known Flemish comic strip Jommeke, which was first published in October 1955.
Means "to love the beautiful" in Tongan.

Combination of Ane 1 and the word haur, haurra "child".This name has traditionally been used to distinguish the younger of two sisters bearing the same name. In the region of Cize/Garazi, it is still in use to this day.
Alternate transcription of Thai อนวัช (see Anawat).
Likely a spelling variation of Anavai meaning "riverbed" or "fresh water cave" in Tahitian.

Means "exalted knowledge" from Sanskrit अनवम (anavama) meaning "high, exalted, illustrious" and दर्शिन् (darśin) meaning "knowing, understanding". In Buddhist tradition this is the name of the tenth of the 27 buddhas preceding Siddhartha Gautama, known in Pali as Anomadassī. It was also borne by a 13th-century Buddhist monk from Sri Lanka.
Alternate transcription of Thai อนวัช (see Anawat).
From ana meaning "cave" and vea meaning "chief" in Tongan, or from Samoan anafea meaning "when".
Combination of Ana and Olivia, or a variant of Anabia.
Derived from the word nirvana spelled backwards.
Alternate transcription of Thai อนวัช (see Anawat).
Means "blameless, flawless, faultless" in Thai, ultimately from Sanskrit अनवद्य (anavadya).
Combination of the name Ana and the feminine suffix -wati.

Derived from the Greek noun ἄναξ (anax) meaning "master, lord, chief". In ancient Greece, it was a title denoting a tribal king or military leader.In Greek mythology, Anax was a giant. He was the son of Uranus and Gaia, and father of Asterius. He was king of the town and territory Anactoria ("place of Anax"), which was later seized by a Cretan who killed Asterius and renamed the city Miletus after himself.Anax was also an epithet of the Greek gods in general, characterizing them as rulers of the world.
Galician, Spanish and Portuguese form of Anaxagoras.
Latinized form of Anaxandros. This name was borne by a king of Sparta (Greece) from the 7th century BC.

Feminine form of Anaxandros. In Greek legend this name was borne by the wife of King Procles of Sparta. It was also the name of a 3rd-century BC Greek painter, who is mentioned in Clement of Alexandria's essay 'Women as Well as Men Capable of Perfection'.
Catalan and French form of Anaxander.

Aeolic and Doric Greek form of Anaxandrides, because it contains ίδας (idas), which is the Aeolic and Doric Greek form of the patronymic suffix ἴδης (ides).This name was borne by two kings of Sparta: the first lived in the 7th century BC and the second in the 6th century BC.
Means "son of Anaxandros" in Greek, derived from the name Anaxandros combined with the patronymic suffix ἴδης (ides).This was the name of an Athenian Middle Comic poet from the 4th century BC.
Spanish and Portuguese form of Anaxander.
Means "master of a man", derived from Greek ἄναξ (anax) meaning "master, lord, chief" and ἀνδρός (andros) meaning "of a man" (genitive of ἀνήρ (aner) "man").
From Azerbaijani ana meaning "mother" and xanım meaning "madam, wife".
Derived from Greek ἄναξ (anax) meaning "master, lord, chief" and ἀνήρ (aner) meaning "man".Also compare the Greek name Anaxandros, which is closely related.

column5: /ˌæ.nəɡ.ˈzɑːr.kəs/(English)|/a.nák.sar.kʰos/(Attic Greek)|/a.ˈnak.sar.xos/(Koine Greek, Byzantine Greek, Constantinopolitan Greek)
column12: Derived from Greek ἄναξ (anax) meaning "master, lord, king" and ἀρχός (archos) meaning "master, ruler". Alternatively, the second element could derive from ἀρχή (arche) meaning "origin, source".
Latinized form of Anaxarchos. This name was borne by a Greek philosopher from the 4th century BC.
Galician and Spanish form of Anaxarchus.

Means "master of virtue", derived from Greek ἄναξ (anax) meaning "lord, master" and ἀρετή (arete) meaning "virtue". In Greek myth this name belonged to a Cypriot maiden whose rejection of Iphis incurred the wrath of Aphrodite. Anaxarete reacted so coolly to the shepherd's passionate love for her that he killed himself; when even the sight of Iphis' dead body did not move her, the goddess of love turned her into stone.
Variant of Anaxanor. This name was borne by a Greek citharode from Magnesia on the Maeander, who was a favourite of the Roman politician Mark Antony (1st century BC).
Feminine form of Anaxibios. This name is carried by several characters in Greek mythology.
Means "master of life", derived from Greek ἄναξ (anax) meaning "master, lord, chief" and βίος (bios) meaning "life".
Latinized form of Anaxibios, used by a 5th century bc Spartan admiral.
Latinized form of Anaxikrates. This name was borne by two eponymous archons of Athens, the earliest of which lived in the 4th century BC.
Spanish and Portuguese form of Anaxidamus.

Doric Greek form of Anaxidemos, because it contains δᾶμος (damos), which is the Doric Greek form of δῆμος (demos) meaning "people" as well as "country, land".This name was borne by a Eurypontid king of Sparta (7th century BC). He is better known under the latinized form of his name, which is Anaxidamus.
Latinized form of Anaxidamos. This was the name of a Eurypontid king of Sparta, who lived in the 7th century BC.
Derived from the Greek noun ἄναξ (anax) meaning "master, lord, chief" combined with the Greek noun δῆμος (demos) meaning "people" as well as "country, land".
Means "powerful master", derived from Greek ἄναξ (anax) meaning "master, lord, king" and κράτος (kratos) meaning "power, strength".
Means "master of the people", derived from Greek ἄναξ (anax) meaning "master, lord, chief" and λαός (laos) meaning "people, folk".
Latinized form of Anaxilaos. This name was borne by a Greek philosopher from the 1st century BC.
Catalan, Galician, Spanish and Portuguese form of Anaximenes.
Derived from Ancient Greek ἄναξ (anax) meaning "master, lord, king" and ἵππος (hippos) meaning "horse".
Latinized form of Anaxippos. This was the name of an Athenian comic poet from the 4th century BC.
Derived from Ancient Greek ἄναξ (anax) meaning "master, lord, king".

Feminine form of Anay, which is said to be derived from Sanskrit anay "misfortune, adversity; without a superior". In Hinduism, the masculine form Anay is an epithet of Vishnu, generally interpreted to mean "not conducted by anyone; he is one whom none can lead".

Invented by Panamanian author Octavio Méndez Pereira for his historical novel El tesoro del Dabaibe (1934), where it belongs to an indigenous princess, daughter of the cacique Careta, who falls in love with the Spanish conquistador Vasco Núñez de Balboa - a character based on a historical indigenous Panamanian woman. According to 16th-century Spanish chronicles, Careta gave Balboa his daughter as a peace offering, and she became Balboa's interpreter, guide, and companion. Her original indigenous name is unrecorded and lost. After her conversion to Christianity, she was baptized María.The derivation is uncertain; it is popularly claimed to be of indigenous American origin, possibly inspired by the phonetics of Ngäbe (Guaymí) and other Chibchan languages. In Panamanian national consciousness, Anayansi is often portrayed as a princess, a peacemaker, and a founding mother figure.
Etymology uncertain, probably uses the reverential or honorific suffix -tzin.
Derived from the native South American tribe, the Kogui people. It means "white flower" or "snow flower" in the Kogui language.
From the Karachay-Balkar анай (anay) meaning "mother" and кёз (köz) meaning "eye".
A modern blend of familiar name elements — especially from names like Ana + Layla — that are widely used across many cultures.
Transferred use of the surname Anazia.
New creation from Annunziata influenced by Ana.
From Sino-Vietnamese 安排 (an bài) meaning "to preordain, prearrange".
From the Chinese 安 (ān) meaning "quiet, calm, peaceful, tranquil" and 宝 (bǎo) meaning "treasure; precious, rare".
From the Chinese 安 (ān) meaning "quiet, calm, peaceful, tranquil" and 本 (běn) meaning "root, origin".
From the Chinese 岸 (àn) meaning "beach, shore" and 边 (biān) meaning "edge, border, side, margin".

column3: 安标, etc.(Chinese)|安標, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 安 (ān) meaning "quiet, peace" combined with 标 (biǎo) meaning "tip of a tree; mark, sign". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From the Chinese 岸 (àn) meaning "beach, shore" and 滨 (bīn) meaning "beach, coast, river bank".
Coined by Sabino Arana Goiri and Koldo Elizalde as a Basque equivalent of Ambrosia.

Derived from a descendent of the Proto-Indo-European root *h₂enk- meaning "curve, bent", possibly ἀγκάς (angkas) meaning "in the arms". This was the name of two members of the Argonauts in Greek mythology, one a son of Poseidon, the other of king Lycurgus of Arcadia.

A character in JRR Tolkien's works, the greatest of the fire dragons. The name is derived from the fictional Sindarin language and is possibly a compound of the word anc meaning "jaws" and the root word alak meaning "rushing".
Means "most bright" in Quenya. This was the name of the first Ruling Queen of Númenor in Tolkien's works. She was the daughter of Erendis and Tar-Aldarion.

A water goddess from Continental Celtic mythology known from inscriptions in the area of modern-day France and Germany.Her name has only been left in its Latinized form Ancamna; there have, however, been attempts to reconstruct a Gaulish form: Ankambona, which has then been interpreted to mean "very crooked river" (from Proto-Celtic *an-kambo-abon-ā).
Ancasta is the name of a little known goddess of Roman Britian.
Diminutive of Ana, Ane and Aneta.
Variant of Ansel.Famous bearers include Methodist minister Ancel Henry Bassett (1809–1886) and physiologist Ancel Keys (1904–2004).
Medieval French diminutive of Anselme. There are also instances where this name is the masculine form of Anceline, which is a French diminutive of Ancelle.

French diminutive of Ancelle. There are also instances where this name is the feminine form of Ancelin, which is a French diminutive of Anselme.It is worth noting that in the English-speaking world, there are very likely cases where this name is a feminization of Ansel. Also, in (at least) the Netherlands, there have been cases where this name is a variant spelling of Angeline.

French variant of Ancille, which has also been used in non-francophone countries over time. Note that in the English-speaking world, there are very likely cases where this name is a feminization of Ansel.The name has always been extremely rare in the French-speaking world, which is probably because the association with the French word ancelle "female servant" is too close. It appears that (where the francophone world is concerned) the name is no longer in use in France itself these days, but predominantly in African countries where French is one of the official national languages, such as Cameroon and the Republic of the Congo.
The sun god of the Tapirape, Brazil.
From Sanskrit अञ्चल (añcala), referring to the end of sari (a traditional dress worn by women in the Indian subcontinent).
Alternate transcription of Thai อัญชลี (see Anchali).
Means "salutation, expression of reverence" in Thai, ultimately from Sanskrit अञ्जलि (añjali).
From the Chinese 安 (ān) meaning "quiet, calm, peaceful" and 婵 (chán) meaning "beautiful, lovely".
From the Chinese 岸 (àn) meaning "beach, shore" and 潮 (cháo) meaning "tide".
Derived from Sanskrit अञ्जसा (anjasa) meaning "true, straight, right".
From the Chinese 岸 (àn) meaning "beach, shore" and 成 (chéng) meaning "become, succeed" or "completed, finished".
Judeo-Anglo-Norman name derived from Old High German ans "god".

The name of the Titan goddess of the warming heat of fire, the sister of Prometheus and mother of the metal-working Daktyloi. Her name may be derived from ank-, a prefix meaning "to reveal or uncover" and further elements meaning "heat". Further it might refer to ανκαλε (ankale), a bundle of firewood carried under the arm.

Means "flowing near" in Ancient Greek, derived from ἄγχι (anchi) meaning "near, nigh" or "like, resembling" and ῥοή (rhoe) meaning "flow, stream, river". This was the name of several naiads and nymphs in Greek mythology, as well as of a consort of Sithon who was also called Anchinoe or Archinoe.
Diminutive of Ana, Anana and Anano.
The name is either a masculine form of Anchoretta (finally going back to the Welsh name Angharad) or used with the literal meaning "anchor".
Alternate transcription of Thai อัญชุลี (see Anchuli).
Diminutive of Antanina, Antonija, Hanna 1 and Žana.

Meaning uncertain. Its use is probably influenced by the Latin title ancilla Dei meaning "handmaid of God".In the German-speaking world, the use of Ancilla and Anzilla dates back to at least the 10th century. In 990 AD, the birth of a certain Anzilla von Lenzburg was documented in Switzerland. She was the daughter of Arnold I, Count von Lenzburg, the imperial reeve of Zurich.In the Netherlands, a known bearer of this name is Ancilla van de Leest (b. 1985), a former model and television presenter who is now a politician on behalf of the Dutch Pirate Party.

French form of Ancilla, which has also been used in non-francophone countries over time. Also compare Ancelle.The name has always been extremely rare in the French-speaking world, which is probably because the association with the French word ancille "maidservant, handmaid" is too close. It appears that (where the francophone world is concerned) the name is not in use in France itself these days, but predominantly in African countries where French is one of the official national languages, such as Burundi and Rwanda.
Originally a diminutive of Ana, used as a given name in its own right.
Variant of Ankhesenamun used in 'The Mummy' film series.
Derived from French ancolie "columbine (of genus Aquilegia)".
Rare Sicilian derivative of Cono, typically given to boys born on June 3rd as a tribute to St. Cono
Meaning "crow's meat" from Ojibwe aandeg meaning "crow" and wiiyaas meaning "flesh, meat".
From Andalasia, the name of the fairy tale kingdom in the Disney films 'Enchanted' (2007) and 'Disenchanted' (2022).
Alternate transcription of Arabic عندليب or Bengali আন্দালিব (see Andalib).
From the name of an autonomous community in Spain, Andalusia, which is derived from the Arabic term 'al-andalus' meaning "land of the vandals".
Family name of one of the royal gates of Dagbong. Inherited traditional name".
Derived from Arabic أَنْدَر (ʾandar) meaning "rarer, stranger".
Derived from Arabic أَنْدَر (ʾandar) meaning "rarer, rarest, noble" combined with the Turkish military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".

Means "walker" in Spanish. This is not used as a name in Spanish whatsoever. Félix de la Caridad Carvajal y Soto, nicknamed Andarín Carvajal (1875-1949) was a Cuban mailman and long-distance runner who competed in the 1904 Summer Olympics.

Andarta was a goddess worshiped in southern Gaul (in present-day southern France and in Bern, Switzerland). Her name has traditionally been translated as "Great Bear" (from Gaulish artos "bear"), more recent analyses of the name, however, offer the translation "Well-fixed, Staying firm".
Derived from Old Norse elements and "opposite, against, towards" and hǫð "battle, combat".
Derived from Old Norse elements and "opposite, against, towards" and blað "leaf"; "leaf-like part" or "blade".
Unclear, possibly a theophoric name from the god Camulos, and the prefix ande meaning "inside",
In Heinrich von dem Türlin’s Diu Crône, an allusion is made to Gawain’s battle with one Iaphine, who had slain the lover of Lady Andeclis.
Name of a Circassian military hero from Kabardia.
Serbian and Croatian form of Angelia. Ćorava Anđelija ("One-eyed Anđelija") is a storm demon in Balkan mythology.
Croatian and Serbian form of Angelina.
Feminization of Andrew, as used for Andelina Darling-Walsh on The Andy Griffith Show.
Mother of Sir Durmart by King Jozefent. Her father was the King of Denmark.
A Knight of the Round Table who participated in the Grail Quest.
Derived from Basque andere "lady". It was popular during the middle ages and has been found in Aquitanian inscriptions as early as the 1st century AD.

First documented in inscriptions in Roman-era Aquitaine, this name was fairly common in the Middle Ages. Its origin and meaning are debated; theories include a derivation from Andos and a derivation from Basque andere "lady; woman; wife". In this day and age, it is considered a feminine form of Ander and a Basque cognate of Andresa and Andrée.
Derived from Basque andere "lady" in combination with a diminutive suffix.
Nyoro, Ganda, Tooro and Kiga variant of Andrew and Andrea 2.
Upper German diminutive of Andreas. Anderl Hinterstoißer (3 October 1914 – 21 July 1936) was a German mountain climber active in the 1930s. He died during an attempt to climb the Eiger north face.
Variant of Anderson or a transferred use of the surname Andersen.
Variant of Anders recorded in the 17th century.
Transferred use of the surname Andersson, or a variant of Anderson.
Variant or feminine form of Anderson.
Frisian form of Andhard or Andward.
From the Quechua word anti meaning "east". This is the name of a mountain range in South America.
Dari Persian form of Andisheh (which is a Persian name meaning "thought").
Possibly an invented name, using the same sounds found in names such as Andrea, Deitra and Demetria.
Derived from Old High German ando "fervor, zeal" combined with Gothic hardus (hart in Old High German) "brave, hardy".
Spelling variant of Anders found primarily in medieval records when there were no standardized spellings in Swedish.
Combination of and "against, opposite, hostile" and hrīm "rime, soot". In Norse mythology this is the name of both an eagle and a cook in Valhalla.
Feminine form of Andi 2 and Andis.
In Crow mythology, this is a legendary warrior-hero invincible to bullets.
Albanian form of Antigone and Greek variant transcription of Αντιγόνη (see Antigoni).
From an honorific term of address for a king or other person of high rank, of Javanese origin.
Possibly a French variant of Andrea.
Means "God the giver" in Ibibio and Efik.
Alternate transcription of Persian اندیشه (see Andisheh).
Means "thought, idea, reflection, meditation" in Persian.
Originally a short form of Angela, used as a given name in its own right.

Means "he of Andjet", the name of an ancient Egyptian city whose name was probably derived from ḏd "stability, durability".This was the name of one of the earliest gods in Egyptian mythology, possibly with roots in Predynastic Egypt, and a possible precursor to Osiris. As such he had many of the same duties as Osiris. He is typically depicted holding the crook and flail and a crown similar to Osiris' Atef crown. The first Pharaoh of Egypt to build a true pyramid, Sneferu, was depicted wearing a crown of Andjety, and in the temple of Seti I, the pharaoh is shown making an offering to Osiris-Andjety.
Diminutive of Anna and spelling variation of Andel.
Short form of Andres, used as a given name in its own right.

Possibly derived from Greek (anadokhe) meaning "a taking up, acceptance, taking charge of" or "surety, pledge, guarantee". Alternatively, ἄνθος (anthos) meaning "flower" or ἀνδρός (andros) meaning "of a man" combined with the patronymic suffix ἴδης (ides) have been suggested as elements.

Arthur’s host in the Kingdom of Damsels in Le Chevalier du Papegau.Arthur came to the kingdom to save its lady, Flor de Mont, from her late father’s steward, who had seized the land for himself. Andois declined to help the lady himself because he felt that her father, King Beauvoisin, had not sufficiently rewarded him for his service in foreign wars.
Coined by Sabino Arana Goiri and Koldo Elizalde as a Basque equivalent of Antolina.
Coined by Sabino Arana Goiri and Koldo Elizalde as a Basque equivalent of Antonia and Antoinette.
Combination of the names An 1 and Dong, and the Chinese form of Anton.
Feminine form of Andon and variant transcription of Αντωνία (see Antonia).
The first element is derived from Malagasy ando "dew" and the second, niaina, means "lived, expirience"
Older form of András. According to tradition, Andorás is a descendant of one of the leaders of the conquering Hungarians, the founder of the Andrássy family in Csíkszentkirály and Krasznahorka.
Directly taken from Icelandic andrá "breath of air; moment".

Latinized form of Greek Ἁνδραίμων (Andraimon), which is probably derived from Greek ἀνήρ (aner) meaning "man" (genetive ἀνδρός (andros)) and αἷμα (aima) meaning "blood". This name was borne by roughly five characters in Greek mythology, one of them being one of the suitors of Odysseus' wife Penelope.
According to Geoffrey of Monmouth, a king of Britain in the third or second century BC.He was the son of King Cherin. He succeeded his brother, King Eldad, and was succeeded by his son, King Urian.

According to the theories of Gilbert, Wilson and Blackett, there were two Arthurs who were, over time, melded into one by legend.The first of these Arthurs was known as Andragnathus. He was the son of Magnus Maximus (Macsen Wledig).
Irish form of Andromeda, used in Irish translations of Greek myths.

The name of a demon as described in the Lesser Key of Solomon as a creature with the body of an angel and an owl's head who rides a wolf. Andras commands thirty legions of lesser demons and his main purpose is to spread discord and violence amongst mortals.
Variant of Andreas. A well-known bearer of this name is Andrass Samuelsen (1873-1954), prime minister of the Faroe Islands (1948-1950).
Possibly derived from the Germanic name elements and "wrath" and ot "wealth" or walt "power, leader."

Variant of Andre. Known bearers of the name include Andray Baptiste (1977-), a Grenadian soccer player, and Andray Blatche (1986-), a retired American-born basketball player who has become a naturalized Filipino citizen.
Variant of Andres. Theories include, however, also a derivation from Antonius.
Short form of Andrea 1 and Andrèia.
Derived from Basque andere "lady" and Albira.

The name Andrealphus is often used as a Male name and is mostly used as a both first and last name.Andrealphus is predominantly used in countries such as France.Andrealphus is an Ars goetia, who resembles a peacock.
Derived from Basque andere meaning "Lady", and Auria.
Medieval Silesian German variant of Andreas.
Derived from Basque andere "lady" and Bita.
The cousin of Tristan in Arthurian legend.
Derived from Basque andere "lady" and Domeka.
Derived from Basque andere "lady" and Dota.
Limburgian form of Andreas (see Andrew) as well as a medieval Dutch variant of Andries.
Romansh form of Andrew, traditionally found in the Engadine valley and central Grisons.
Spanish and Portuguese form of Andreina.
Possibly derived from Greek ἀνδρεῖος (andreios) "manly, strong, brave".
Milanese Lombard feminine form of Andreja 2.
Originally a diminutive of Andreja 1, used as a given name in its own right.
This is the middle name of Keke Palmer's newborn son Leodis Jackson.
Borne by American baseball player Andrelton Simmons.
Derived from Basque andere meaning "Lady", and Mantzia.
Derived from Basque andere "lady" and Maria.
Tristan’s maternal grandfather. He married Felice, Arthur’s sister, and became the father of Elizabeth (Tristan’s mother).Andremo was cousin to Ban of Benoic (Lancelot’s father).
French form of Andraimon via its latinized form Andraemon.
Italian form of Andraimon via its latinized form Andraemon.
Italian and Spanish form of Andreus.
Derived from Basque andere "lady" and on "good".
Derived from Basque andere meaning "Lady", and Oneka.
Diminutive of Andrea 1, as -otto is an Italian masculine diminutive suffix.A known bearer of this name was Andreotto of Arborea (died in April 1308), who was a Giudice ("judge") of Arborea.
Unaccented form of Andrés used mainly in the Philippines.
Spanish and medieval Basque feminine form of Andrés as well as a Portuguese variant of Andressa.
Derived from Basque andere "lady" and Semena.
Diminutive of Andressa.Andressinha is a Brazilian football player and member of the 2019 FIFA women 's world cup team.
The name of a character in the Tristan and Isolde legends, a nephew of King Mark of Cornwall and cousin to Tristan. Andret, also spelled Andred, is a villainous character in later versions.
Means "patience" in Sindarin. Andreth was a wise-woman of the House of Bëor in J.R.R. Tolkien's legendarium.
Likely a transferred use of the surname Andretti. This is borne by Bahamian sprinter Andretti Bain (1985-).
Italian diminutive form of Andrew. It reached the top 1000 in Italy 1982-1985.

Medieval Italian diminutive of Andrea 1, as -uccio is an Italian masculine diminutive suffix.In literature, this name is borne by Andreuccio of Perugia, the protagonist of one of the novellas in Giovanni Boccaccio's The Decameron (written between 1348 and 1353).
Variant form of Andreas (see Andrew). In Greek mythology, Andreus was the son of the river god Peneus.
Breton feminine form of Andrev and Aragonese feminine form of Andreu.
Feminine version of Andrew combined with the name Netta 1.
Transferred use of the surname Andrews.
Transferred use of the surname Andrewson
Derived from Basque andere meaning "Lady", and Zuria meaning "white".
Short form of Andria. This name is pretty rare in Georgia nowadays; Andro is the more common short form.
Sicilian and Sardinian form of Andrea 1.

Andrianampoinimerina (1745–1810) ruled the Kingdom of Imerina from 1787 onwards, initiating the unification of Madagascar after more than seven decades of civil war. Therefore he is regarded as a cultural hero and holds near mythic status among the Merina people, being considered one of the greatest military and political leaders in the history of Madagascar.
From Malagasy andriana meaning "noble, sovereign, king" and nantenaina meaning "hoped for, expected".
Alternate transcription of Greek Ανδριανή (see Andriani).
Greek feminine form of Andreas; also compare Andriana.
From the Malagasy andrian meaning "king, royal" and tafika meaning "army".
Means "the royal without equal among great royals". This was the name of a king of Madagascar from 1650 to 1670.

Andriantsimitoviaminandriandrazaka (more commonly called Andriantsimitoviaminiandriana Andriandrazaka) was King of Madagascar from about 1710 to 1730. This is the longest name of any of the Madagascan monarchs, who are known to have long names (such as Andriantsimitoviaminandriandehibe).
From the Malagasy andrian meaning "king, royal" and soa meaning "good".
Variant of Andrea 2 influenced by the popular suffix -ella.
Swedish and Afrikaans variant of Andriette and Romansh feminine form of Andriu.
Allegedly a combination of Greek ἀνδρεῖος (andreios) "manly" or ανδρος (andros) "man" (compare Andreas) and ríkr "mighty, distinguished, rich".
Romansh form of Heinrich, traditionally found in the Engadine valley.
Feminine form of Andrin as well as a feminine form of Andreas.
Derived from Greek ἀνδρός (andros) meaning "of a man" combined with the Greek noun ἵππος (hippos) meaning "horse".
Romansh form of both Andreas and Heinrich.
Italian and Spanish form of Andriscus.
Latinized form of Andriskos. This was the name of the last king of Macedon, who lived in the 2nd century BC.
Derived from Greek ἀνδρός (andros) "of a man" combined with the Greek diminutive suffix -ισκος (-iskos).
Gascon variant of Andrieu and Romansh form of Andrew, traditionally found in the Surselva region.

Daughter of King Cador of Northumberland in Girart d’Amien’s Escanor.Her father threw a tournament at Banborc to find her a husband. Sir Cey (Cei), who later became better known as the Arthurian knight Sir Kay, distinguished himself in the tournament and fell in love with Andrivete, but, bashful, he returned to Arthur’s court without confessing his affections.On her father’s death her uncle, Ayglin, tried to get rid of her by marrying her off to someone unsuitable, a commoner. Kay learned of her plight, returned to Banborc, rescued Andrivete and married her. She prepared to overthrow her uncle, supported by her husband, and in later accounts with the support of King Arthur, but before any fighting could break out the people of Northumberland forced him to surrender before any violence could occur, and Andrivete regained her kingdom.Originally a story with only local Northumbrian significance, this story later passed into the Arthurian cycle because of the presence of Cei, or Sir Kay, in the story.In a romance preceding Girart’s, Andrivete is proven unfaithful by a chastity test at Arthur’s court involving a mantle.
Variant of Adriyan. Andriyan Nikolayev was a Soviet cosmonaut. In Ukraine, usage is likely influenced by Andriy.
Ukrainian form and Bulgarian variant transcription of Андриана (see Andriana). In Ukraine, this name is mostly used in west part of country.
Short form of Andres, used as a given name in its own right.

Derived from the Greek adjective ἀνδρόβουλος (androboulos) meaning "of manly counsel, man-minded", which consists of Greek ἀνδρός (andros) meaning "of a man" combined with the Greek noun βουλή (boule) meaning "counsel, advice" as well as "will, determination".Also compare the Greek verbs βουλεύω (bouleuo) meaning "to take counsel, to deliberate" and βούλομαι (boulomai) meaning "to will, to wish, to prefer".
Latinized form of Androboulos. This was the name of an ancient Greek sculptor.
Latinized form of Androkleides. This was the name of a Greek politician from Thebes (4th century BC).
Latinized form of Androkydes. Bearers of this name include a painter and a Pythagorean philosopher.

From Greek ἀνδροδάμας (androdamas) meaning "man-taming, man-slaying", itself from ἀνδρός (andros) "of a man" and δαμάζω (damazo) meaning "to tame". In Greek mythology Androdamas was the son of Phlias and Chthonophyle, daughter of King Sicyon.

Feminine form of Androdamas, meaning "man fighter" or "subduer of men", composed of Greek ἀνδρός (andros) "of a man" and δαμάζω (damazo) "to tame". In Greek mythology, this was the name of an Amazon who fought in the Attic War. Another Androdameia was a queen of the Thermodontine (Black Sea) Amazons, who defeated one of the leading Greek generals in single combat during the Third Doric Raid.
In La Tavola Ritonda, the King of Scotland in the time of Uther and in Arthur’s early days. He joined King Meliadus of Lyonesse’s war against Arthur.
Italian and Spanish form of Androgeus.
Catalan, Portuguese, and Romanian form of Androgeus.

Latinized form of Greek Ἀνδρόγεως (Androgeos), derived from ανδρος (andros) meaning "of a man" and the genitive of γῆ (ge) meaning "earth, land". In Greek mythology, Androgeus was the son of the Cretan king Minos and his wife Pasiphaë. This was also the name of a Greek soldier in the Aeneid.
Bulgarian and Russian form of Androgeus.
Means "son of Androkles" in Greek, derived from the name Androkles combined with the patronymic suffix ἴδης (ides).
Variant of Androkles. This was the name of the third recorded Ancient Greek Olympic victor during the 8th-century BCE.
Derived from Greek ἀνδρός (andros) meaning "of a man" combined with κῦδος (kydos) meaning "glory, renown".

Derived from Greek ἀνδρός (andros) meaning "of a man" combined with the Greek noun λόχος (lochos) meaning "childbirth" as well as "ambush". Through the latter meaning, the word later came to signify a tactical sub unit of the ancient Greek army, which further strengthened the word's connection to combat and the military. As such, this name most likely means something along the lines of "to ambush a man" or "military man". However, it is also quite possible that its meaning is "birth of a man" or "born a man" (probably in the figurative sense), so one should not be too quick to disregard either possibility and instead keep both in mind. Also compare Aristolochos.
Latinized form of Androlochos. This name was borne by a prominent citizen of the city of Elis, who was killed by the Achaeans during the Battle of Leontion in 217 BC.
Spanish and Portuguese form of Andromache.
Greek variant transcription of Ανδρομάχη (see Andromachi), as well as an Albanian form.
Galician and Spanish form of Andromeda.

In ancient Greek, there are two possible ways to write this name, and with each way the meaning is different.When written as Ἀνδρομέδης, this name is the masculine form of Andromeda. But when written as Ἀνδρομήδης, the name basically means "a man's plan" or even "to think like a man", derived from Greek ἀνδρός (andros) meaning "of a man" combined with the Greek verb μήδομαι (medomai) meaning "to think, to plan, to plot".In Greek mythology, Andromedes is one of the suitors of Penelope.
Ukrainian and Russian folk form of Andronicus.
Catalan form of Andronicus via Andronikos.
Feminine form of Andronicus. This is also the Latinized form of Andronika.
Spanish and Portuguese form of Andronikos.
Form of Andronikos (see Andronicus) in various languages. In Armenia, this name might also be a variant spelling or transcription of Andranik in some cases.
French form of Andronikos via Andronicus.
From Greek ἀνδρός (andros) meaning "of a man", a genitive form of ἀνήρ (aner) "man". In Greek mythology, this was the name of a son of Anius and grandson of Apollo.
Means "strength of a man", derived from Greek ἀνδρός (andros) meaning "of a man" and σθένος (sthenos) meaning "vigour, strength."
Derived from Greek ἀνδρός (andros) meaning "of a man" combined with the Greek verb τιμάω (timao) meaning "to honour, to esteem, to revere".
Diminutive of Androniki (the modern Greek feminine form of Andronikos) or possibly of Andriana.
Archaic English variant and Cornish form of Andrew. This was borne by Androw Myllar (floruit 1503-1508), the first Scottish printer.
Derived from Basque andere "lady" and ume "child".
Belarusian form of the name Andrew.
Czech diminutive of Andrea 2. Also compare Andruška.

Germanized form of Handroš. Andrusch is a minor character in Otfried Preußler's 1971 German fantasy novel 'Krabat' (published in English as 'The Satanic Mill' in 1972, 'The Curse of the Darkling Mill' in 2000 and 'Krabat' in 2011), which is based on a Sorbian legend.
Russian and Belarusian diminutive of Andrey.
Czech diminutive of Andrea 2. Also compare Andruša.
Variant of Andżela influenced by Andrzej.
Variant of Andżelika influenced by Andrzej.
Variant of Andżelina influenced by Andrzej.

Created by video game developer Blizzard Entertainment for several characters in the fantasy video game series "Warcraft". One notable bearer, Anduin Lothar, is the leader of Alliance forces during the First and Second Wars. Another bearer is Anduin Wrynn, the King of Stormwind who was named after Lothar.
Diminutive of Anna. Andula Sedláčková (born Anna Sedláčková, 1887-1967) was a theatre and movie actress; she is considered the first Czech movie star.

column5: /ʔaːn˧˧ zɨəŋ˧˧ vɨəŋ˧˧/(Vietnamese)|/ʔaːn˧˧ jɨəŋ˧˧ vɨəŋ˧˧/(Vietnamese)|/ʔaːŋ˧˧ jɨəŋ˧˧ vɨəŋ˧˧/(Vietnamese)
column12: Means "King of An Dương", from Sino-Vietnamese 安陽 (an dương) and 王 (vương) meaning "king". He was the king of Âu Lạc, an ancient Yue kingdom, and the leader of the Âu Việt tribes, uniting them with the Lạc Việt. His real name was Thục Phán (蜀泮). He was the father of Mỵ Châu. Although he was a real historical person, he is the subject of many legends around the founding of Vietnam.

Means "careful one". In Norse mythology Andvari was a dwarf who lived under a waterfall and could change himself into a fish at will. He had a pile of gold and a magical ring, Andvaranaut, which made him wealthy. Loki used a net stolen from Rán to capture him and steal his gold and ring.The character Alberich in Wagner's opera cycle Der Ring des Nibelungen is based in part on Andvari.
Possibly means "opponent, enemy" in Old Norse.
Derived from Old High German ando "fervor, zeal" combined with Old High German wart "guard."
Variant of Andilyn. Or a combination of Andy and Lyn.
Kashubian and Polish short form of Andżelika or Andżelina as well as a cognate of Angela.
Rare variant spelling of Andżelika, without Polish special characters.
Older form of Angèlin used in the Arpitan Valleys of Piedmont.
Variant of Anzhela influenced by Western pronunciation of Angela.
Greenlandic and older Walloon form of Ane 1.

column3: 亜音, 亜寧, 亜嶺, 天羽, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Greenlandic ane meaning "big brother of a girl".
Modern American feminized form of Neal, likely influenced by Amelia
Variant of Aniceta. In the Philippines, this name is much more common than Aniceta.
Variant of Aniceto. In the Philippines, this name is more common than Aniceto.
Derived from Nahuatl anecuyotl, a kind of headdress, or perhaps belt, made from paper and feathers, and chimalli "shield".
Perhaps a variant of the English name Andy. A known bearer is Anedie Azael (1988-), a Haitian beauty pageant contestant.
Alternate transcription of Anis as well as the Urdu form.
Alternate transcription of Arabic أنيسة (see Anisa), as well as the Urdu and Dhivehi form.
Alternate form of Aneira, with the Welsh element gwen meaning "white, blessed".
Means "let the gods not agree to bad things" in Igbo.
Short form of Ana Elena. A known bearer of this name is Ana Elena "Anel" Noreña Grass (1944-), a Mexican actress, vedette and former model.
Name from the Hawaiian word ʻānela meaning “angel”. Can also be interpreted as an equivalent of the English given name Angela.
Means "be enough; be sufficient; be adequate" in Zulu.
Anelida is the eponymous queen of Armenia in "Anelida and Arcite", a 357-line English poem by Geoffrey Chaucer. It tells the story of Anelida and her wooing by false Arcite from Thebes, Greece.
The name is derived from the Mordvin anelis, meaning "to pamper, indulge, treat, caress."
English and Luxembourgish cognate of Anneliese as well as a Luxembourgish contraction of Anna - Elisabeth.
It means "He (the Lord) is with you", or "one who is with you".
Derived from French anémone, referring to the anemone flower.
Russian and Serbian form of Anempodistos.
Italian and Spanish form of Anempodistus.
Derived from the Greek adjective ἀνεμπόδιστος (anempodistos) meaning "unhindered" as well as "not obscured, clear".
Latinized form of Anempodistos.A notable bearer of this name was saint Anempodistus of Persia (4th century AD).
Coined by Sabino Arana Goiri and Koldo Elizalde as a Basque equivalent of Aniano.
Meaning "one who has wisdom", this name can be shortened to Njere.
Of debated origin and meaning. Theories include a Gascon and Medieval Basque form of Asenarius, Asinarius, Aznar or Januarius.
Basque form of Inés and Agnès.
French form of Anesius. This name was borne by an obscure saint martyred alongside Théodule, Felix and Cornélie.

Means "giver of gifts" (or "she who sends forth gifts", "sender-up of gifts") or "spender of gifts" in Greek, derived from ἀνίημι (animi) "to send up, send forth, release, loosen" and δῶρον (doron) "gift". This was an epithet (and epiklesis) of the Greek goddesses Demeter, who had a temple under this name at Phlius in Attica, and of Gaia; it was also applied to Pandora.
A Shona name for girls. It means "God is with us".
Meaning "the Lord is with us", also a longer form of the name Anesu.
Kashubian diminutive of Ana and Hungarian variant of Anetta.
Walloon diminutive of Ane 1 and Ana and cognate of Annette.
Diminutive of Aneta, not used as a given name in its own right.
Hungarian variant of Anett, Polish, Czech and Slovak variant of Aneta and Romansh variant of Annetta.
From the Catalan title of the Virgin Mary, Mare de Déu d'Àneu, meaning "Mother of God of Àneu," the name of a sanctuary in the municipality of La Guingueta d'Àneu in the comarca of Pallars Sobirà.

Modern name of unknown meaning. It is likely invented, perhaps based on the sounds found in other names such as Nevaeh.Many baby name sites and books state that this name means 'superior' in 'Native American', but do not specify which tribe. No evidence can be found of this name meaning 'superior' in any Native American language.
Possibly a variant of Eneida, altered due to the influence of Aleyda.
Possibly an alternative transcription of Anas.
Means "profits, earnings, spoils" in Arabic, the plural of نفل (nafal) meaning "booty, gift". It is given in reference to the 8th chapter of the Quran (surah Al-Anfal).
From the Chinese 安 (ān) meaning "quiet, calm, peaceful, tranquil" and 方 (fāng) meaning "direction, power".
Of uncertain origin and meaning. It is most likely related to medieval English Amphelisa.
Possibly a variant of Anthony. This name was popularized by American basketball player Anfernee "Penny" Hardaway (1971-), thus peaking in 1996.
Russian form of Anthimos via Anthimus.
Estonian transcription of Russian Анфиса (see Anfisa).
Spanish and Asturian form of Amphitrite.
Probably derived from Old French enfertez or enfermetez meaning "infirmity". This was Wolfram's name for the wounded Fisher King in his epic 'Parzifal'.
From the Chinese 安 (ān) meaning "quiet, calm, peaceful, tranquil" and 富 (fù) meaning "abundant; rich, wealthy".
From Sino-Vietnamese 盎 (áng) indicating clouds and beautiful things, or meaning "water container" in Vietnamese.

From Chinese 昂 (áng) meaning "raise, soaring". Or from the Hokkien and Teochew romanization of 洪 (pinyin: Hong) or 汪 (pinyin: wāng) or other similarly pronounced names in these dialects. Other hanzi can form this name as well.
Means "the ways of war" in Tongan.
Means "he/she was given to me" in Rukiga.
Means "armband, bracelet worn on the upper arm" in Sanskrit. In the Hindu epic the Ramayana this is the name of a monkey king who assists Rama in finding his wife, Sita.
Saint Angadresma (or Angadrisma) was a 7th-century abbess and miracle worker venerated in Beauvais, France.
Old Swedish variant form of Arngærdh.
Old spelling of Angaju (according to the Greenlandic spelling reform of 1973).
Greenlandic name with the combination of Angajo and suffix -raq "young animal".
Means "older sibling of the same sex" in Greenlandic, thus either "big brother (to a boy)" or "big sister (to a girl)".
The lady of the castle Raguidel and a cousin of Lancelot.Her lord, an evil man named Marigart the Red, was slain by Sir Hector, who later rescued Angale from a pair of lions.
Variant of Angelina. A famous bearer is Angaleena Presley (1976-), an American country singer and member of the Pistol Annies.
Old variant of Engilram. This was the name of an 8th century bishop of Metz.
Variant of Aganetha, used by Mennonites.
Combination of Angâĸ and the diminutive suffix -nnguaq.
Archaic spelling of Anngannguujuk (using the old Kleinschmidt orthography).

Uncertain etymology, though it is known to be a cognate of Old English Ongenþeow and Old High German Angandio. The first element could derive from Old Norse angi "sweet odour", Old High German ango "hook, barb", Old English ongean "opposite, against", or perhaps the name of a tribe combined with either Old English þeow "servant, slave" (Old Norse -þér), or Old Norse týr "god" (see Týr). This was the name of three characters of the same family line in Norse mythology.
From name of river Angara in Irkutsk oblast.
Means "Mars (planet)" or "Tuesday" in Mongolian, ultimately from Sanskrit अङ्गार (angara) meaning "charcoal" or "Mars".
In the Vulgate IV Angares is a knight wrongly accused to have killed Lancelot. The damsel accusing him got Lionel to fight in order to avenge her lover’s death.
Variant of Wangari. Also a surname.
Possibly derived from Greenlandic angâtsiaq, meaning "long time".
One of the sons of Caw in medieval Welsh legend.

The meaning and origin of the first element is rather uncertain: we know that it comes from angil, but we don't exactly know where angil itself comes from. But there are a few possibilities. It might be an extended form of the element ang, which is derived from Old High German ango "prickle, thorn, sting" or encho "servant, lad, boy." The Angles, a Germanic tribe, might have derived their name from that element (so, angil might also refer to the Angles). An other possibility is that angil is an extended form of the element ingvi, which refers to the Norse god Ing or even to the Ingaevones, a Germanic tribe mentioned by Tacitus in his "Germania." Especially forms like Ingelbald remind one of that. And last but not least, angil might even be related to Gallic eingeal "light." The second element in this name is derived from Old High German bald "bold, brave."

King of Scotland, first named by Geoffrey of Monmouth.The numerous variations of his name may include Anguish of Ireland. Geoffrey tells us that he was the brother of Uriens and Lot, but the Vulgate Merlin calls him the son of King Caradoc and one of Arthur’s unnamed half-sisters (and therefore Arthur’s nephew). In a Welsh adaptation of Geoffrey, his counterpart is Arawn. His name suggests the common Scottish Angus, which belonged to an earl of Moray in the early twelfth century.In Geoffrey’s version, Arthur restores him to his position as king of Scotland after the country was reclaimed from the Saxons. In later works, however, he is portrayed as an early enemy of Arthur. He was one of the kings who rebelled against Arthur’s ascension to the throne. Arthur defeated the confederation at the battle of Bedegraine, after which the Saxons invaded Scotland, and Angusel had to return to fortify his city of Caranges. Joined by Kings Urien and Nentres, he successfully fought off the invaders, led by King Oriel. Eventually, Angusel and the other rebelling kings reached a truce with Arthur and together crushed the Saxons at Clarence. He later joined Arthur’s wars against Rome, Galehaut, and Claudas.

In certain myths he is considered the creator deity and supreme being. The meaning of his name is said to refer to his mutilation of his daughter Sedna, an act which ultimately resulted in her becoming the goddess of the sea.

This was the name of a god of war and hunting in Egyptian mythology. He was the husband of Menhit, his female counterpart, and possibly derived his name from his role of bringing her to Egypt from Nubia. He was typically depicted as a bearded man wearing a robe or kilt and a headdress with four feathers, while holding a spear or lance, and occasionally with a lion's head, like his wife.

Transferred use of the surname Aniston.The first is that it is an obscure English locational surname, which is said to mean "town of Anis". Anis is a medieval English form of Agnes, which is also found spelled as Annice, Annise, Annis and Annys. Interestingly, there is no town in the modern-day United Kingdom that is called Aniston or a variant spelling thereof. It seems that over time, the original town must either have perished or been renamed. Perhaps we could even go so far as to say that such a town never existed in the first place, in that Aniston might have originated as a nickname for any town (with a different name) that had a church that was devoted to Saint Agnes.The second possibility is that the surname is an anglicization of the Gaelic surname McAniston, which in turn is a variant spelling of McAnistan. The meaning of the surname as a whole is uncertain, but we can at least say that it is a patronymic surname, as Mc means "son of".The third possibility is that the surname is a variant spelling of the rare English surname Aneston, which itself may be a variant form of the surname Haneston (also found spelled as Haniston, Heneston and Heniston). The meaning of these surnames is uncertain.The fourth and final possibility is that the surname Aniston is an anglicization of Greek surnames starting with Anastas-, such as Anastasides. A famous example of this is the Greek-American actor John Aniston (b. 1933), who is best known for his role as Victor Kiriakis on the NBC daytime drama "Days of our Lives" (1965-present). His father anglicized the family's surname of Anastasakis to Aniston, sometime after the family had emigrated to the United States. The family's original surname meant "little Anastasius" in Greek. John Aniston's daughter Jennifer (b. 1969) went on to become an actress in her own right, her fame eventually surpassing that of her father's. Due to her iconic role as Rachel Green in the television sitcom "Friends" (1994-2004), her popularity became such that it can be argued that most parents naming their child Aniston were probably inspired (to do so) by her in one way or the other.Finally, as a given name, Aniston can be a variant spelling of Anniston in some cases, which has an entirely different etymology.

The toponym Annecy was first recorded in 1107, while in the 9th century it was recorded under its Latin name Anericiacum, which is ultimately derived from a Germanic given name Anerīk or Annarigus and the Gaulish suffix -acum which used to denote property.

Combination of Anne 1 and the Old Swedish name element vī "temple, sanctuary" (ultimately from the Old Norse name element vé "home; temple, sanctuary; devoted, dedicated").
Altered form of Arnfrid, first documented in Norway c.1500 (Arnfrid: 1888).
Combination of Anna and the name element Fried. Since names ensing in Fried are usually masculine makes this an interesting variation.

Derived from Greenlandic anngak meaning "her brother's child" combined with the suffix -nguujuk meaning "sweet little". (Also compare the Greenlandic kinship terms qangiak/qangiaq "his brother's child" and nuaraluaq and ujoruk, both of which mean "sister's child".) This is the name of a character in a Greenlandic legend which is popular among children.
From Sino-Vietnamese 安閒 (an nhàn) meaning "peaceful, leisurely, carefree".
From Sino-Vietnamese 安然 (an nhiên) meaning "peaceful, safe, leisurely".
Younger form of Arnhild or new combination of Ann and Hild.
Feminine form of Annius. Annia Aurelia Faustina (c. 201 AD – c. 222 AD) was an Anatolian Roman noblewoman. She was an Empress of Rome and third wife of the Roman emperor Elagabalus briefly in 221.
Diminutive of Anna. In some cases it may also be a short form of Giuannica.
Archaic diminutive of Anna (compare Annika, Anneke, Annike), in use between the 1500s and 1700s.
Variant of Anabel or a combination of Annie and Belle.
A combination of Annie and Kate.
A combination of Annie and Kay 1.
A combination of Annie and Mae.
Perhaps a variant of Agnès, reflecting the French pronunciation.
Variant of Annefrid. A famous bearer of this name is Anni-Frid "Frida" Lyngstad (1945-), a founding member of the Swedish pop band ABBA.

Variant of Aningan. In Greenlandic mythology Anningan is the god of the moon and the brother of Malîna, the sun goddess. He chases his sister across the sky. The Greenlandic people explained the phases of the moon by saying Anningan forgets to eat while chasing her and becomes thinner and thinner, then leaves for three days to find food before returning to chase his sister again.
Possibly the masculine form of Annina.
Elaboration of Anna, formed from the popular name suffix qua- (see also Annika, Anika 1, Shaniqua and Janiqua).
Son of Pradyummna, and grandson to Lord Krishna

Derived from the name of the city of Anniston in the state of Alabama. The city was founded in the late 19th century by Samuel Noble and Daniel Tyler, who named the city after the latter's daughter-in-law, Annie Tyler. As a result, the meaning of the name is literally "Annie's town".In some cases, Anniston as a given name can also be a variant spelling of Aniston.A known bearer of this name is the youngest daughter of American actress Chyler Leigh (b. 1982) and her husband Nathan West (b. 1978).
Annit was a northern Babylonian moon goddess who was later replaced by Ishtar.
Either a diminutive of Anna or a Greek form of Anita 1.
A variant of Anita 1 or Annetta.
Marcus Annius Verus (died 124 AD) was a distinguished Roman politician who lived in the 2nd century, served as a praetor and was the father of the Emperor Marcus Aurelius.
Of uncertain etymology. Name borne by the mother of an augur, known from a text detailing a fertility ritual involving burying clay birds on the steppe.
Swedish and German combination of Anne 1 and Katrin.
Combination of Ann and Lynn, also a variant of Annlyn.
Swedish, Finnish, Norwegian form of Annmarie.
In Roman Mythology, Annona is the divine personification of the grain supply to the city of Rome. The name itself is derived from Latin annona "yearly produce; corn, grain".

Means "she who supplies corn" in Latin, derived from annona "yearly produce", "crop, harvest" or "corn, grain" (also the name of a Roman goddess who personified the year), which was ultimately from annus "year". This was an epithet of the goddess Fortuna, protector of the corn supplies.
French form of Annunziata. Also compare Annonciation.
Means "sea, ocean" in Thai, ultimately from Sanskrit अर्णव (arṇava).

Queen of Averre in Wolfram’s Parzival.She was loved by Galoes of Anjou (Perceval’s uncle), who died in her service.Der Pleier adds that she was married to King Avenis and had two daughters named Laudamie (Laudame) and Anfole.

Medieval diminutive of Ann a short form of Annes (see Annis), Annora, and Alianora. It was used by Sir Walter Scott for a character in his short novel 'A Legend of Montrose' (1819). This name was a precursor to Annette.

According to Malory, she was a great sorceress who fell in love with Arthur and entinced him to her tower in the Forest Perilous (Perilous Forest). When she could not get him to make love to her, she plotted his death.
Alternate transcription of Hindi अन्नपूर्णा (see Annapurna).
A combination of names Ann and Rika.
A blend of Anne and a name ending in -traud, e.g., Waltraud.
Diminutive of Anna and other names beginning an.
Dialectal variant of Arnulf, no longer in use.
Dialectal variant of Arnulf, no longer in use.
Means "the skirmisher" or "the martial one". This was an epithet of Ishtar in her capacity as a war goddess. Later in the Sargonic period, Annunitum became a distinct deity in her own right.

From Italian annunzio, a variant of annuncio meaning "announcement", likely after the yearly Catholic event of the announcement of Easter Day (annuncio del giorno di Pasqua).Annunzio Paolo Mantovani, known mononymously as Mantovani (1905-1980), was an Italian British conductor, composer and light orchestra-styled entertainer with a cascading strings musical signature.
Russian diminutive of Anna. Also compare Annushka and Annusya.
Ukrainian diminutive of Anna also used in Russia. Also compare Annusha and Annushka.
Variant of Arnveig as well as a younger combination of Anna and veig "power; strength".
Breton cognate of Anwen. It is also regarded as a combination of Anne 1 and Gwenn.
From the Welsh word annwyl, which means "dear". The word annwyl is comprised of an, an intensive prefix and gŵyl “mild, gentle, graceful; bashful, modest”.
Icelandic and Faroese form of Annie.

column3: انو(Pashto)|あの(Japanese Hiragana)|亜乃, 愛乃, 綾乃, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: Older form of Anu 1, rare today.
From Japanese 亜 (a) meaning "second, Asia", 乃 (no), a possessive particle combined with 亜 (a) meaning "second, Asia". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Derived from ano meaning "desolate" and arii meaning "king, chief".

"Ascent" or "Upward Progress" from the Greek οδος with the prefix αν. Used by Plato to refer to enlightenment. Anodos is the central character in the George Macdonald novel "Phantastes". The name was also used as a pseudonym by author and poet Mary Elizabeth Coleridge.
From Latin "anōdynos", meaning “stilling or relieving pain”, from Ancient Greek "ἀνώδυνος", meaning “free from pain”), from "ἀν-", meaning “without” plus "ὀδύνη", meaning “pain”.
Means " ripe fruit" or "exceptionally lovely" in Hindi.
Variant of Anuschka. This is borne by Namibian author Anoeschka von Meck (1967-).
Meaning "one who is happy or joyous".
Borne by a king of the island of El Hierro.
Means "pleasured" in Hebrew, a poetic verbal of Oneg.
Uzbek and Tajik form of Anahita.
The name Anokhi is a feminine name that means unique. Its very commonly used in the language hindi. But its not a common name.
From ano meaning "awestruck, lost in thought" and lani meaning "heaven".

column12: Means "joy, delight, pleasure" in Thai, ultimately from Sanskrit आनन्द (ānanda).

column12: From Thai อนงค์ (anong) meaning "beautiful woman" and ลักษณ์ (lak) meaning "characteristic, quality".

column12: Alternate transcription of Thai อนงค์ลักษณ์ (see Anonglak).

From Thai อนงค์ (anong) meaning "beautiful woman" and นาฏ (nat) meaning "woman, beautiful woman".
From Thai อนงค์ (anong) meaning "beautiful woman" and พร (phon) meaning "blessing".
Alternate transcription of Thai อนงค์พร (see Anongphon).

column12: From Thai อนงค์ (anong) meaning "beautiful woman" and รัตน์ (rat) meaning "gem, jewel".
From Thai อนงค์ (anong) meaning "beautiful woman" and วรรณ (wan) meaning "colour, tint".
From ʻānoni meaning "to mix, interweave, intertwine, mixed".
Alternate transcription of Thai อานนท์ (see Anon).
Alternate transcription of อนุรักษ์ (see Anurak).
Alternate transcription of Persian انوشه‎ (see Anousheh).
Alternate transcription of Persian انوشه (see Anousheh).
