Alternate transcription of Thai อรรณพ (see Annop).
Possibly a variant of Anara or Anora 2.
Maybe a combination of Anore and -nnguaq "sweet, dear".
Old spelling of Anori (as per the Greenlandic spelling reform of 1973).
Mycenaean Greek form of Andromedes, derived from ἀνήρ (aner) meaning "man" and μήδομαι (medomai) meaning "to plan, plot, intend".
East Prussian German contraction of Anna-Dorothea.

Means "immortal soul", derived from Middle Persian anōš (also anōsh) meaning "immortal" combined with Middle Persian ruwān meaning "soul". This was an epithet of Khosrau I, a popular 6th-century emperor of the Sassanid Persian Empire.
Alternate transcription of Thai อโณทัย (see Anothai).
Means "rising sun" in Thai, ultimately from Sanskrit अरुणोदय (arunodaya).
Alternate transcription of Arabic أنور (see Anwar) chiefly used in North Africa.
Alternate transcription of Arabic أنور (see Anwar) chiefly used in Tunisia.

Possibly a variant of Anuket, as she is depicted in an almost identical way, or even Neith, and perhaps the inspiration for the Greek Goddess Hestia as they are thought to have shared similar duties. She was worshiped in Nubia as well.
Variant transcription of Anuki. A known bearer of this name is the Georgian fashion designer Anuki Areshidze (b. 1989), who goes by the mononym Anouki.
Derived from Persian انوشه (anuše) meaning "immortal", ultimately from Old Persian *anauša- and Avestan anaoša.
Alternate transcription of Armenian Անուշավան (see Anushavan).
Alternate transcription of Persian انوشیروان (see Anushirvan).
my name is from the mom and dad and this name is come from CBRN Reseresky and this Names are important because they help us connect
From Lao ອະ​ນຸ​ (anou) meaning "small" and ສອນ (sone) meaning "arrow, weapon".
Greek form of the Italian name Annunziata.
From Egyptian inpw-m-sA.f meaning "Anubis is his protection" derived from the name of the god Anubis and combined with m "in, in the role of", zꜣ "protection", and the suffix .f "he, him, his".
Means "Anubis is content", from Egyptian Anpu, a variant form of Anubis, and ḥtp "peace, satisfaction".
This name combines 安 (ān) meaning "peaceful, tranquil, quiet" and 琪 (qí) meaning "type of jade."In most cases, it can be translated as Angie.
From the Chinese 安 (ān) meaning "quiet, calm, peaceful, tranquil" and 强 (qiáng) meaning "strong, powerful, energetic".
From the Chinese 安 (ān) meaning "quiet, calm, peaceful, tranquil" and 晴 (qíng) meaning "fine weather".
From the Chinese characters 岸 (àn) meaning "bank, shore; beach, coast" and 琼 (qióng) meaning "jade; rare, precious; elegant;".
Derived from anqo meaning "anqa (a mythological bird" and gul meaning "flower, rose".
Portuguese and Spanish form of Anchinoë.

column3: 杏里, 杏理, 安吏, 安莉, 杏莉, 杏吏, 杏梨, 杏璃, 安李, 安梨, 安理, 安璃, 安里(Japanese Kanji)|あんり(Japanese Hiragana)|アンリ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: As a unisex name, this name can be used as 杏里, 杏理, 安吏, 安莉 with 杏 (an, kyou, kou, anzu) meaning "apricot," 安 (an, yasu, yasu.i, yasu.maru, yasu.raka) meaning "cheap, low, peaceful, rested," 里 (ri, sato) meaning "parent's home, ri (unit of distance - equal to 3.927 km), village," 理 (ri, kotowari) meaning "justice, logic, reason, truth," 吏 (ri) meaning "an official, officer" and 莉 (rai, ri, rei), part of 茉莉 (matsuri) meaning "jasmine."As a feminine name, it can be used as 杏莉, 杏吏, 杏梨, 杏璃, 安李, 安梨, 安理, 安璃, 安里 with 梨 (ri, nashi) meaning "pear tree," 璃 (ri) meaning "glassy, gem" and 李 (ri, sumomo) meaning "plum."One bearer of this name is J-Pop singer/songwriter Anri (杏里), born Eiko Kawashima (川嶋 栄子) (1961-).Usage of this name, for males, is likely influenced by the phonetic similarity to Henri.
Hungarian borrowing of Henriette, reflecting the French pronunciation.
From Japanese 安 (an) meaning "peace", 里 (ri) meaning "village" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Possibly a Esperanto form of Henry.
From Chinese 安 (ān) meaning "peace", 睿 (ruì) meaning "astute", and 雅 (yǎ) meaning "elegant, graceful, refined".
Medieval Portuguese and Medieval Galician form of Henrique.
From the Chinese 安 (ān) meaning "quiet, calm, peaceful, tranquil" and 孺 (rú) meaning "child; affection".

Meaning unknown. This was the name of I (also transliterated Yi, Lee and Ri) An-sa (d. 1274), an ancestor of the Joseon dynasty. Over a hundred years after his death his great-great-grandson King Taejo granted him a royal title and posthumously declared him King Mokjo of Joseon.

column3: 杏沙, 杏紗, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: In Hindu myth, one of the Adityas, the guardian deities of the months. A minor sun god.
Alternate transcription of Arabic أنصار or Urdu انصار (see Ansar).
Italian and Spanish form of Ansanus.
Of uncertain origin: it may be derived from Germanic ans ("God"), from a Latin nickname denoting a person with big ears, or from the name Antianus.
Derived from Ansari, a Muslim surname found in the Middle East and South Asia.
East Prussian German form of Hans.
Means "brave god", derived from Old High German ans "god" combined with Old High German bald "bold, brave."
Italian and Spanish form of Ansbert.
Derived from Old High German ans "god" combined with Old Norse brand "sword."
Italian form of Ansgar via Latinized form Anscharius and variant of Ansgario.
French form of Ansgar via Latinized form Anscharius.

Derived from the Old High German elements asc meaning "ash tree; spear" and wolf meaning "wolf", or possibly a variant form of the Old English name Æscwulf; the first element was altered due to the influence of Old High German ansi meaning "god, deity". A known bearer was the 11th-century Norman baron Ansculf de Picquigny, who followed William the Conqueror to England.
Derived from Old High German ansi meaning "god, deity" and Proto-Germanic *geldą meaning "reward, gift, money".
Latinized form of Ansegis, derived from Old High German anse "God" and gis, either "spear" or "pledge". This was the name of a 9th-century saint and Benedictine monk.
A knight from Sorelois who fought in the tournament at Sorelois.

Latinized form of the Old German name Ansila, a derivative of Old High German ansi "a god". This was often confused with the similar name Anselm. Ansellus of Laon (died 1117), also known as Anselmus, was a medieval French theologian.
Languedocian and Gascon form of Anselm.

Medieval Italian diminutive of Anselmo, as -uccio is an Italian masculine diminutive suffix.A known bearer of this name was Anselmo "Anselmuccio" della Gherardesca (c. 1274-1289), who was immured and starved to death in the Muda Tower in Pisa together with his father and grandfather. His tragic fate was covered by Dante Alighieri in his Divine Comedy (1320).
Derived from Old High German ans "god" combined with flâdi "beauty, respectability."
Variant spelling of Ansfleda. Ansflede was the wife of Waratton, a 7th-century mayor of the palace of Neustria and Burgundy.
Means "peaceful god", derived from Old High German ans "god" combined with Old High German fridu "peace."
Italian and Spanish form of Ansfrid via Latinized form Ansfridus.
Dutch and German form of Ansfrid.
Derived from the Germanic elements ans "god" and gard "enclosure". This name was borne by Ansgarde of Burgundy, a French queen of Aquitaine who lived during the 9th century.
Portuguese form of Ansgar via the form Ansgarius.
Italian form of Ansgar via the form Ansgarius.
Derived from Old High German ans "god" combined with gisel "hostage" or "pledge."

Derived from the Old High German elements ansi "god, deity" and got "god, deity", or possibly a Norman form of Old Norse Ásgautr (compare Old Swedish Asgot) in which the second element is the tribal name gautr.

Means "whole heaven", deriving from the Sumerian elements šar ("totality, all"), and an ("sky, heaven"). Name borne by a primordial god of creation, who was viewed as the father of the sky god Anu. His consort was the earth goddess Kishar.
Combination of 安 and 生, meaning quiet, peaceful.

From Chinese 安 (ān) meaning "peace, quiet" combined with 石 (shí) meaning "stone". Other hanzi combinations are possible. A notable bearer was Wang Anshi (1021-1086), Chinese economist, philosopher, poet, and politician during the Song dynasty.
This name means "unique" or "no one is like you". It can also mean "one whos fame is pearless".
From Sanskrit अंशु (aṃśu) meaning "stalk, thread, ray, beam of light".
From Sanskrit अंशुमान (aṃśumān) meaning "sun". In the Hindu epic the Mahabharata this is the name of a king of the Solar dynasty (Suryavamsha).
From Sanskrit अंश (aṃśa) meaning "part, portion" and वीर (vīra) meaning "hero, man, brave" (possibly in the sense "part of God").
Derived from Old High German *ans, ans-, ansi- meaning "god, deity" and Old High German hiltja meaning "battle".
Possibly a feminine form of Ansilo.
Old High German name related to the name element as ('god')
Allegedly taken from the name of a mountain in the Argentinian Andes.
Of uncertain origin and meaning. Theories include a Provençal form of Ansgar.
Means "to live in peace" or "welfare", from Sino-Vietnamese 安 (an) meaning "peace, security" and 生 (sinh) meaning "to be born".

He was called “the Pilgrim” because of his passion for going on pilgrimage, "for every third year he would be at Jerusalem" He passed his nickname on to his daughter, Alice le Beale Pilgrim. Ansirus was of Lancelot’s kin, apparently in the British branch of the family. His daughter and her knight, Alisander le Orphelin, settled in “their country of Benoye,” which presumably was Ansirus’ dukedom.
Latvian adaption of Hans (compare East Prussian Ansas).
Finnish diminutive of names beginning with Ans- and An-.
Norman form of Ásketill, altered due to the influence of Old High German ansi "god, deity".
Diminutive of Anna and other names beginning an.

This was the name of Latvian writer, journalist and painter Anšlavs Eglītis who became a war refugee in 1944. He had prolific career as a novelist, and his later work often examined aspects of exile life.
Transferred use of the surname Anslow.
Transferred use of the surname Anslyn.
Derived from Old High German ans "god" combined with Old High German mâri "famous."
Derived from Old High German ans "god" combined with Old High German mund "protection."
From the Chinese 岸 (àn) meaning "beach, shore" and 松 (sōng) meaning "pine, fir".

Ansotica was a Liburnian goddess who was worshipped in what is now Croatia. Seeing as she was equated with the Roman goddess Venus, it has been speculated that she might have been a goddess of love. The origin and meaning of her name are unknown, as it is impossible to determine whether her name is of Celtic or Illyrian origin.
Italian form of Answin via Ansovinus and variant of Ansuino.
Variant spelling of Ansbrand. Ansprand was the name of an 8th-century king of the Lombards.
Variant of Anstice recorded in late medieval Ireland on women born into English and Anglo-Norman families.
Transferred use of the surname Anstice, which was derived from the medieval given name Anastase or Anastayse (from Latin Anastasius), or from its feminine equivalent Anastasie (from Latin Anastasia).
Derived from Old High German ans "god" combined with þruþ "strength."

Unclear etymology; possibly a combination of the Germanic roots ansi "god" and war "aware", a cognate of Assar or of Celtic origin. This is the name of a Galician saint who was bishop of Ourense in the 10 century AD.
Derived from Old High German ans "god" combined with Gothic valdan "to reign."
Derived from Old High German ans "god" combined with Old High German wini "friend."

Means "endless food" from Sanskrit अनन्त (ananta) meaning "infinite, endless" combined with भोग (bhoga) meaning "enjoyment, pleasure, delight, food". In Javanese, Sundanese and Balinese mythology this is the name of a serpent deity who created the world.

Latinized form of Greek Ἀνταῖος (Antaios), which is derived from Greek ἀνταῖος (antaios) meaning "(right) opposite, opposed to, set over against". In turn, it is ultimately derived from the Greek verb ἀντάω (antaō) meaning "to come opposite (to), to meet face to face, to meet (with)". Also compare Greek ἄντα (anta) meaning "over against, face to face". In Greek mythology, Antaeus was the son of Gaia and Poseidon.
Possibly meaning "flower" and deriving from the Greek ἄνθος (anthos).
Latinized form of Antalkidas. This was the name of a Spartan soldier and diplomat from the 4th century BC.

Means "son of Antalkes" in Greek, derived from the name Antalkes combined with ίδας (idas), which is the Aeolic and Doric Greek form of the patronymic suffix ἴδης (ides).This was the name of a Spartan soldier and diplomat from the 4th century BC. He is better known under the latinized form of his name, which is Antalcidas.
Latinized form of Antandros. This name was borne by Antander of Syracuse (4th century BC), who was the brother of the tyrant Agathocles of Syracuse.

Derived from Ancient Greek ἄντανδρος (antandros) meaning "instead of a man, substitute", composed of ἀντί (anti) "against, compared to, like" and ἀνδρός (andros) "of a man" (compare Antenor). Antandre was an Amazon warrior in Greek mythology, one of Penthesilea's twelve companions at Troy.
Italian and Spanish form of Antander.

Means "opposing men" or "equal to men", derived from Ancient Greek ἀντί (anti) meaning "against, opposed, compared to, like" and ἀνδρός (andros) meaning "of a man". Also compare the adjective ἄντανδρος (antandros) meaning "instead of a man, as a substitute".Also compare the Greek name Antenor, which is closely related and essentially means the same.
Feminine form of Antanas. In other words, this name is the Lithuanian equivalent of Antonia.
Konkani form of Anthony, borrowed from Portuguese Antão. Used by Konkani Catholics.

Portuguese form of Antonius.In Portuguese, Santo Antão is the common name of Saint Anthony the Great, or Saint Anthony of Egypt. In turn, the medieval Saint Anthony of Padua (born in Portugal, and who took his religious name after that Saint) is known as Santo António. The popularity of the latter saint in Portugal and in other countries means that this form of the name has been eclipsed by António.

Borne by the pre-Islamic Arab knight and poet Antar ibn Shaddad al-ʿAbsī (525-608), famous for both his poetry and his adventurous life. His name is now used to mean "brave, bold, champion" in Arabic.
Means "within, in the middle, between" in Sanskrit.

From the continent of Antarctica, which is a romanized version of the Greek compound word ἀνταρκτική (antarktiké), feminine of ἀνταρκτικός (antarktikós), meaning "opposite to the Arctic, opposite to the north".

Perhaps derived from Greek ἀντί (anti) meaning "against, opposed, compared to, like" and αὔρα (aura) meaning "breeze". This is the name of a Greek demon of migraine headaches, who rises up out of the sea, moves like the wind, and enters into people's heads to cause intense pain. In a 3rd-century AD amulet inscription from Roman Carnuntum, Antaura is thwarted by the goddess Artemis, who diverts Antaura into the head of a bull in the mountains. Modern-day academics speculate that the demon Antaura developed from Abyzou, a Sumerian demon who kills children.
Means "colour of the clouds at sunset" in Aymara.
Diminutive of Andreas, Anders and Anton.
Form of Anthea used in various languages.
According to Homer and other early writers, this was the name of the consort of Proetus. The tragic poets gave the name of the consort of Proetus as Stheneboea.
Polish and Silesian diminutive of Antoni.

An earl in the service of the Duke of Lorraine in the Alliterative Morte Arthure.With his brother Algere, he fought in a battle against Gawain during the Roman War.Malory includes this character but re-names him Ethelwold.
From the Chinese 安 (ān) meaning "quiet, calm, peaceful, tranquil" and 腾 (téng) meaning "fly, gallop, run, rise".
Czech variant and Slovak form of Antenor.
Elaborated form of Ante 1, possibly influenced by Mateo.
French form of Anteros via Anterus.
Catalan and Portuguese form of both Antaeus and Antheus.
Meaning uncertain. This was another name for the goddess Prorsa. It is also an alternative name for Gamma Virginis, a binary star system in the constellation of Virgo.
Bulgarian, Russian and Ukrainian form of Antaeus.
Diminutive of any name ending in -antha.

Means "full bloom; blossom, bloom" in Ancient Greek, from ἄνθος (anthos) "flower". In Greek mythology, Anthe was one of the Alcyonides, nymphs of fair weather. After the death of their father Alcyoneus at the hands of Heracles, they threw themselves into the sea in their grief and were transformed into kingfishers. A moon of Saturn was named after her.

Means "opposite the sun, looking east" or "reflecting the sun", derived from Ancient Greek ἀντί (anti) meaning "against, opposed, compared to, like" and ἥλιος (helios) meaning "sun". In Greek mythology, Anthelia was one of the fifty daughters of Danaus, murdering her husband, Cisseus, on their wedding night.
From the English word anthem, "a rousing or uplifting song", ultimately from the Greek ἀντίφωνα (antíphōna), a call and response style of singing.
Derived from Ancient Greek ἄνθεμον (anthemon) meaning "flower" (see ἄνθος (anthos)). Also compare the Late Greek given name Anthimos.
Likely a latinized form of Greek Anthemios.Procopius Anthemius was the Western Roman emperor from 467 to 472.

Derived from Ancient Greek ἀνθέω (antheo) meaning "to blossom, to bloom", ultimately from ἄνθος (anthos) meaning "flower, blossom" (compare Anthea). This was the name of several characters in Greek mythology, including a soldier of Dionysus, a son of Antenor accidentally killed by Paris during a game, and a youth murdered by Queen Cleoboea for rejecting her advances.

Possibly a variant of Anthea. This name was borne by a 2nd-century Illyrian saint who was martyred with her son Eleutherius during the persecutions of the Roman emperor Hadrian. It was also used by Xenophon of Ephesus for the lover of Habrocomes in his 2nd-century novel An Ephesian Tale (one of the sources for Shakespeare's äRomeo and Juliet).
Means "evening, dusk" in Thai, ultimately from Sanskrit अन्धिका (andhikā).
Meaning uncertain. It could perhaps come from the Greek name Anthimos, but I don't know how likely it generally is for Greek names to be used in India.
French form of Anthimos via Anthimus.
Latinized form of Anthimos. This name was borne by several patriarchs of Constantinople.
Feminine form of Anthippos. In Greek mythology, Anthippe is one of the fifty daughters of king Thespius. She had a son named Hippodromus with Heracles.

Derived from Ancient Greek ἀντί (anti) meaning "against, opposed, compared to, like" combined with ἵππος (hippos) meaning "horse". Compare ἀνθιππεύω (anthippeuo) meaning "to ride against, to charge on horseback against someone".
Latinized form of Anthippos. This was the name of an ancient Greek comic poet, of whom it is not (yet) certain whether he really existed.
Variant of Antoine. This name is borne by French race car driver Anthoine Hubert (1996-2019) and French hockey player Anthoine Lussier (1983-).
Probably Antonia with a pseudo Russian diminutive suffix.
A variant of the name Anthony. This is the name of a character from the Webcomic Marionetta
Diminutive of names containing the Greek element ἄνθος (anthos) meaning "flower, blossom", such as Kleanthis.
Means "embers, burning charcoal" in Greek. In Greek myth this name belonged to one of the nurses of the infant Zeus.

From Ancient Greek ἄνθος (anthos) meaning "flower, blossom, bloom". This was also the name of a kind of small bird, according to legend named after the mythical character Anthus, a son of Hippodameia and Autonous who was eaten by his father’s starving horses when he denied them pasture and turned into a bird by the gods out of pity for his family.
Latinized form of Anthousa. Used by various saints.
French form of Anthousa via Anthusa.
Alternate transcription of Greek Ανθή (see Anthi).
Derived from Ancient Greek ἄνθος (anthos) meaning "blossom, flower, brightness". Anthylla was a sacrificed victim of the Minotaur in Greek mythology.
Lule Sámi form of Ánte, a diminutive of Andreas.
Latinized form of Antialkidas. This was the name of an Indo-Greek king from the 2nd century BC.
Derived from Greek ἀντί (anti) meaning "against, compared to, like" combined with the Greek noun ἀλκή (alke) meaning "strength".
Means "son of Antialkes" in Greek, derived from the name Antialkes combined with ίδας (idas), which is the Aeolic and Doric Greek form of the patronymic suffix ἴδης (ides).

Derived from Greek ἀντιάνειρα (antianeira) meaning "a match for men", itself from ἀντί (anti) "against, compared to, like" and ἀνήρ (aner) "man". In Homer's Iliad ἀντιάνειραι (antianeirai) was an epithet of the Amazons. This was the name of several characters in Greek mythology.
Latinized form of Antianeira, as well as the Italian, Portuguese and Spanish form of this name.

Means "equal to man", from Greek ἀντί (anti) meaning "against, compared to, like" combined with βροτός (brotos), a poetic term meaning "mortal man". This was the name of an Amazon warrior in Greek mythology.
Latinized form of Antikles. A known bearer of this name was Anticles of Messenia, an ancient Greek athlete from the 8th century BC.
Latinized form of Antikleides. A known bearer of this name was the Greek writer Anticlides of Athens (3rd or 4th century BC).

The seneschal of King Brandon the Saxon. He participated in the Saxon invasion of Britain in the early days of Arthur’s reign. He was killed at the siege of Clarence by Arthur’s Sir Eliezer (Eliezier).
Means "return-gift, recompense; present offered in exchange", derived from Greek ἀντί (anti) meaning "against, opposite" or "instead of, in exchange for" combined with δῶρον (doron) meaning "gift".

This given name originated in medieval times as a variant spelling (or even a misspelling) of Antjen, as the letter 'j' was regularly written as an 'i' in medieval records. The name Antien has since gone on to become a name of its own, in that this particular spelling took hold and also became pronounced just as it was written (i.e. the 'j' was no longer an 'i' in just writing, but also in pronunciation), thus truly making it independent from Antjen.The name is still in use in the Netherlands to this day, but it is considered rare, as in 2014 there were a little over 60 living bearers (of all ages) in the entire country.
Variant of Antoni, traditionally found in the Surselva region and in central Grisons.
Italian, Spanish and Portuguese form of Antiphon.
Form of Əntiqə used outside of Azerbaijan.

Derived from Greek ἀντί (anti) meaning "against, opposed, compared to, like" and γενής (genes) meaning "born". This name was borne by a general of Alexander the Great, who lived in the 4th century BC.
Catalan form of Antigonos via it's Latinized form Antigonus.
Spanish and Portuguese form of Antigone.
Albanian and Croatian form of Antigone.
French form of Antigonos via its Latinized form Antigonus.
Portuguese, Spanish, and Galician form of Antigonos via it's Latinized form Antigonus.
Italian form of Antigonos (via it's Latinized form Antigonus).

From a title of Virgin Mary, which came to be in Seville Cathedral's Virgen de la Antigua chapel. The word antigua "old, ancient" referred to a fresco depicting Virgin Mary, which was sculpted on the wall of an ancient mosque which served as the basis for the new cathedral. The veneration of the aforementioned depiction of Mary (or other similar images) came to be associated with the Virgen de la Antigua title and later spread all over Spain and Latin America.Another theory posits that Pope Sylvester I created the Antigua title in the 4th Century because Mary represented the fulfillment of the prophecies within the Old Testament.
Alternate transcription of Thai อันธิกา (see Anthika).
Means "son of Antikles" in Greek, derived from the name Antikles combined with the patronymic suffix ἴδης (ides).

Medieval German variant of Antigone. In Arthurian legend, she is the sister of King Vergulaht of Ascalun who became infatuated with Gawain during one of his visits. This caused her brother to attack Gawain. She later married King Dulcemar of Tandernas and gave birth to Tandareis, who became one of Arthur’s knights. She is mentioned in both Der Pleier's Tandareis and Flordibel and Wolfram von Eschenbach's Parzival.
Derived from Greek ἀντί (anti) meaning "against" and κράτος (kratos) meaning "power, strength".

Means "lion-like, leonine" in Ancient Greek, from ἀντί (anti) meaning "like, equal to" and λέων (leon) meaning "lion". This was the name of one of the fifty (or fifty-one) grandsons of Thespius fathered by Heracles in Greek mythology, his mother being Procris and his twin brother Hippeus. It was also the name of an Ancient Greek author.

Derived from Greek ἀντί (anti) meaning "against, compared to, like" combined with the Greek noun λόχος (lochos) meaning "ambush", a word that later came to signify a tactical sub unit of the ancient Greek army. The word is ultimately derived from the Greek verb λοχάω (lochao) meaning "to lie in wait for, to waylay" as well as "to snare".
Latinized form of Antilochos. This was the name of an ancient Greek historian.In Greek mythology, Antilochus was the son of king Nestor of Pylos, who fought in the Trojan War as one of the Achaeans.
Bulgarian and Romanian form of Anthimos.

Derived from the Greek adjective ἀντίμαχος (antimachos) meaning "capable of meeting in war", which consists of Greek ἀντί (anti) meaning "against, compared to, like" combined with the Greek noun μάχη (mache) meaning "battle".Also compare the Greek verbs ἀντιμαχέω (antimacheo) meaning "to resist by force of arms" and ἀντιμάχομαι (antimachomai) meaning "to fight against".

Latinized form of Antimachos. Bearers of this name include two Greek poets and two Graeco-Bactrian kings.Antimachus is also the name of several characters from Greek mythology, one of which is a suitor of Penelope.
Antimony was named after the Greek words anti and monos to mean “a metal not found alone.” The chemical symbol, Sb, comes from the element's historical name, stibium.
Ukrainian variant or folk/older form of Anton. A notable bearer was Antin Holovatyi, Zaporozhian Cossack otaman who was one of the creators and a commander of the Black Sea cossack army.
Short form of Gosantine. Antine Nivola (1911-1988) was a Sardinian sculptor, architectural sculptor, muralist, designer and teacher.

Created by Pierre Benoit in his novel L'Atlantide (1919) for Queen Antinéa. The name is inspired by Tinhinan, a 4th-century Tuareg queen with a legendary story. Tinhinan means "woman of the tents" but may be metaphorically translated as "mother of us all".
Spanish and Italian form of Antinéa.

Feminine form of Antinoos. This was the name of several princesses in Greek mythology, including one of the Peliades (the daughters of King Pelias of Iolcus and sisters to Alcestis, who were tricked by the sorceress Medea into killing their own father).
Means "against the mind", derived from Greek ἀντί (anti) meaning "against" and νόος (noos) meaning "mind, thought".
Latinized form of Antinoos. This name was borne by the favourite and lover of the Roman Emperor Hadrian (2nd century AD).

English form of Antiochus. The capital city of Syria bore this name, an important centre in early Christianity (founded c.300 BC by Seleucus I Nictor and named for his father, Antiochus). The name was used by J. K. Rowling in her 'Harry Potter' series of books, where it belongs a minor character.

French form of Antiochus (masculine), as well as an ancient Greek feminine form of Antiochos (note, the usual feminine form was Antiochis). In Greek mythology Antioche, also called Antiope, was a daughter of Pylon and wife of Eurytus, by whom she became the mother of the Argonauts Iphitus and Clytius.

Means "son of Antiochos" in Greek, derived from the name Antiochos combined with the patronymic suffix ἴδης (ides).This name was borne by an eponymous archon of Athens, who lived in the 5th century BC.
Feminine form of Antiochos. This name was borne by multiple Hellenistic princesses from the Seleucid dynasty.
Spanish, Galician and Portuguese form of Antiochus.
Feminine form of Antiogu. It was used for a character in the Sardinian-language play Ziu Paddori (1918) by Efisio Vincenzo Melis.
Lamanite king of land of Middoni.
Perhaps an erroneous spelling of Antoine.
Russian and Romanian form of Antipas. It was borne by the early saint Antipas of Pergamum. The name is sometimes adopted by monks.
Derived from Greek ἀντί (anti) "against, in return" and φανής (phanes) "appearing". This was the name of a 4th-century BCE comic playwright of Middle Comedy.
Derived from Ancient Greek ἀντί (anti) meaning "against, opposite" or "compared to, like" combined with φίλος (philos) meaning "friend, lover".
Latinized form of Antiphilos. This name was borne by a Greek painter from the 4th century BC.

Possibly a variant of Antiphilus. The first element of this name is Greek αντι (anti) "against, compared to, like"; the second element is less certain, perhaps derived from Greek φωλεός (phôleos) "den, lair" (the source of the mythological name Pholus) or from Latin folium "a leaf; a sheet of paper; trifle, thing of no consequence". This name belongs to two characters in William Shakespeare's play 'The Comedy of Errors' (1592): the twin brothers Antipholus of Ephesus and Antipholus of Syracuse.

Derived from Greek ἀντί (anti) meaning "against, opposite, in return" combined with φωνή (phone) meaning "voice". This was the name of several historical Ancient Greek figures, including Antiphon the Sophist, who lived in the 5th century BC. It was also the name of a comrade of Odysseus in the Odyssey. In English, an antiphon is a kind of music sung responsively, usually a devotional chant, ultimately derived from the same Greek elements as the given name.

Latinized form of Greek Ἀντίφονόν (Antiphonon), derived from ἀντίφονος (antiphonos) meaning "in return for slaughter" or "in revenge for blood", from ἀντί (anti) "in return for; for the sake of, for" and φόνος (phonos) "murder, slaughter; blood shed in murder, gore". In Greek legend Antiphonus was one of the sons of the Trojan king Priam.

Means "bright one, one who sheds light before him", derived from Ancient Greek ἀντί (anti) meaning "against" or "compared to, like" combined with φῶς (phos) meaning "light". This was the name of several figures in Greek mythology, including one of the fifty sons of King Priam, and one of the fifty (or fifty-one) grandsons of Thespius fathered by Heracles in Greek mythology, his mother being Laothoe.
Taken from the title of the Virgin Mary Our Lady of Antipolo, also known as Our Lady of Peace and Good Voyage.
Nephite commander in city of Judea.(c. 65 BC)
Means "ancient" in Uzbek but also figuratively "amazing, wonderful".
From the place name Antissa, a city on the island of Lesvos.
Derived from Greek ἀντί (anti) meaning "against" and σθένος (sthenos) meaning "vigour, strength." This name was borne by a Greek philosopher from the 4th century BC.

This name is a variant of Anna, where the diminutive suffix -tjen has been added to the name. Since -tjen is a diminutive suffix that was primarily used in the Middle Ages and has since been replaced by the more modern -tje, we can actually say that Antjen is the medieval Dutch form of Antje.The name Antjen has survived to modern times, but barely so, as it is extremely rare in the Netherlands these days: in 2014, there were less than 50 living bearers (of all ages) in the entire country. Most living bearers are elderly as well, so the name is set to become even rarer in the future.
Variant of Antoine influenced by Juan 1.

From Greek ἀντλία (antlia) meaning "hold of a ship". Antlia is one of the constellations created by the French astronomer Nicolas Louis de Lacaille in the 18th century. He originally named it Antlia Pneumatica, or Machine Pneumatique in French, in honour of French physicist Denis Papin’s invention, the air pump.
Means "posthumous child" in Fante. It is typically given to a child whose father died before they were born.
Feminine form of Antoenne and cognate of Antoinette.
Variant of Antonella and feminine form of Antoine.
A variant of Antonio likely based on Antoine.
Feminine form of Antoine using the fashionable suffix -iece.
Feminization of Antoine by using the fashionable suffix -ique
Diminutive of Antonia. Perhaps most famously borne by author Anaïs Nin, whose full birth name was Angela Anaïs Juana Antolina Rosa Edelmira Nin y Culmell.
Diminutive of Antonio. In other words, this is the masculine form of Antolina.
Sardinian form and Galician variant of Antonia.

Modern Greek diminutive of Antonios and Antonis, as it contains the modern Greek diminutive suffix -άκης (-akis). This name is typically only used informally, meaning: it does not appear on birth certificates.
Corsican and Ladin form and English variant of Anthony.
Croatian and Albanian form of Antoinette.
Occitan, Piedmontese, Milanese Lombard and Emilian-Romagnol form of Anthony.
Form of Anton with the nominative suffix, used in Georgian when the name is written stand-alone.
Used in 'My Ántonia', as the name of a Bohemian (Czech) protagonist. A form of the name Antonia, different than the usual Czech form Antonie 1.
Catalan, Piedmontese and Sardinian form of Antonia.
Could be a form of Anthony/Antonio?
Ukrainian folk form of Antonina and Russian variant.
Czech feminine form of Antoninus (see Antonino).

Diminutive of Antonio, as -otto is an Italian masculine diminutive suffix. A known bearer of this name was the Genoese trader and explorer Antoniotto Usodimare (1416-1462). The name has also been borne by several doges of the Republic of Genoa.
Medieval Italian diminutive of Antonia, as -uccia is an Italian feminine diminutive suffix.
Medieval Italian diminutive of Antonio, as -uccio is an Italian masculine diminutive suffix.
The father of Vyolette, a maiden saved from two giants by Guinglain (Gawaine’s son). In reward for his heroism, Antore gave Guinglain a fine suit of armor.
A knight in the service of King Claudas (Lancelot’s enemy), killed by Gawaine in the battle of Trebe (Trebes).
Old Hungarian short form of Antal.
Essentially a combination of Anathoth with yah "Yahweh", thus the meaning is effectively "prayers answered by Yahweh". In the bible, this was the name of a member of the tribe of Benjamin.
Alternate transcription of Arabic أنطون (see Antun).
Of uncertain origin and meaning. Theories include a variant of Andra 1 and a contracted form of Anitra.
A modern invented name of unknown meaning.

Medieval feminine form of masculine Antso.Back in the day, this name was usually prefixed by Andre, meaning it was more often than not found as a compound name Andreantsa.Andre is a Basque word meaning "lady" that at some point had become a very productive name element in feminine names.
Coined by Sabino Arana Goiri and Koldo Elizalde as a Basque equivalent of Anselma.
Coined by Sabino Arana Goiri and Koldo Elizalde as a Basque equivalent of Anselma.
Medieval Basque form of Sanctius and Sancho.
Basque diminutive of Antonia (see also Antton).

She evolved from the Sumerian goddess Ki.In Akkadian and Babylonia mythology she was the first consort of Anu. Eventually she was replaced by Ishtar. She is likely the influence for the Greek goddess Hera, and was perhaps related to Anat. Her name possibly derives from the Sumerian element an, meaning "heaven, sky".
From Mapudungun antü (also antv and anty) meaning "sun, day."
Spanish version of Antoine reflecting French pronunciation.
Sicilian diminutive of Antuni and Corsican diminutive of Antonu.
From a title used by Banjar men and women of noble descent, typically placed before the given name.
Sicilian and Corsican form of Antoninus.
Possibly from the Awajún ántut meaning "hear, understand, obey".
Romanian and Polish form of Anthousa.
Latinization of Antwanette. This is borne by a young female basketball player Antwanetta Boswell. Also, see Antoinetta.
Variant of Antoinette influenced by Antwan.
Polish form of Antigonos via it's Latinized form Antigonus.
Polish and Ukrainian form of Anthimos (see Anthimus).
Greek form of the English name Angie, used as a diminutive of Angeliki or Angela. This is borne by Greek singer Angeliki 'Antzy' Samiou (1960-).

Proto-Celtic theonym *Φanon- "mother", Anu is an Irish goddess with uncertain functions and often conflated with other figures of Irish mythology and folklore, like Danu. In the Lebor Gabála Érenn, 'Anand' is given as an alternate name for Morrígu. While an Irish goddess, in parts of Britain a similar figure is referred to as 'Gentle Annie', in an effort to avoid offence, a tactic which is similar to referring to the fairies as “The Good People”.
Malay, Kazakh, Indonesian and Spanish form of Anwar.
Combination of Anuar and the Turkish military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".

Borne by the Blessed Marie-Clémentine Anuarite Nengapeta (1939-1964), a beatified Congolese nun who was killed at age 24 during the Congo Crisis. According to the Dictionary of African Christian Biography, she belonged to the Wabudu tribe and her name means "one who laughs at war".
Derived from Sanskrit अनुभव (anubhava) meaning "perception, understanding".
Alternate transcription of Hindi अनुभूति (see Anubhuti).
From Sanskrit अनुभूति (anubhūti) meaning "perception, sensation, experience".
Italian form of Anubis as well as the Georgian form of Anubius.

Latinized form of Ἀνουβιος or Ἀνούβιος (Anoubios), which is a Late Greek variant of Anoubis (ultimately of Egyptian origin).The best known bearer of this name is the Egyptian saint Anoub of Scetis (5th century), who is alternatively known as An(o)ubios and Anubius.
Means "younger brother" in Thai, ultimately from Sanskrit अनुज (anuja).
From Thai อนุ (anu) meaning "small, often" and ชัย (chai) meaning "victory".
Alternate transcription of Thai อนุชาติ (see Anuchat).
From Thai อนุ (anu) meaning "small, often" and ชาติ (chat) meaning "life, birth, origin, existence".
Means "to win repeatedly, to always win" in Thai.
Etymology uncertain. Probably derived from Ana Dara, an alternate name for Queen Anu.

From the Sanskrit word अनुदेय (anudeya) meaning "gift", from अनु (anu) "away, after" and दा (dā) "to give" (i.e. "to give back" or "to give in turn"). This was used as a 'sannyas' name by followers of the controversial Indian spiritual teacher Bhagwan Shree Rajneesh (1931-1990), also known as Osho. It was customary for new followers, or sannyasins, to receive a new name from Osho during initiation ceremonies.
Alternate transcription of Thai อนุสรา (see Anutsara).
Originally conceived as a short form of Emmanuel, this is the stage name of Puerto Rican singer Anuel AA.
Russian and Ukrainian variant of Onufriy.
From Sanskrit अनुग्रह (anugraha) meaning "favour, kindness". It is sometimes used as a feminine name in Indonesia.
Means "cool, soft fragrance," from anu meaning "cool(ness)" and hea meaning "mist".
Georgian diminutive of Ana. Notable Georgian bearers of this name include the queen consort Anuka Abashidze of Imereti (died in 1721) and princess Ana "Anuka" of Kartli (1698-1746).
Alternate transcription of Thai อนุกูล (see Anukun).
Alternate transcription of Thai อนุกูล (see Anukun).
From the Sanskrit अनुकृति (anukṛti), meaning "imitation, replica".
Alternate transcription of Thai อนุกูล (see Anukun).
Means "to help, to support, to assist" in Thai, ultimately from Sanskrit अनुकूल (anukula).
Kashubian diminutive of Ana and Polish diminutive of Anna.
A famous bearer would be famous thai pop singer whose real name is Benjawan Pohkasap.
Possibly from Arabic أنعم (ʼanʿum) meaning "blessings, favours" (plural form of نعمة (niʿma) "blessing, favour, grace"), a word mentioned in the Quran in verse 16:112, or possibly a variant of Anam.
Anumati is the Hindu godess of the moon. The meaning of the name is moon.
Diminutive of Ana, as it contains the Georgian diminutive suffix -უნა (-una).
Means "excellent, superb, extraordinary (of a child)" in Javanese.
Alternate transcription of Thai อนัญญา (see Ananya).
Means "God's mercy is plenty" in Yoruba.
Alternate transcription of Thai อนุพันธ์ (see Anuphan).
Alternate transcription of Thai อนุภาพ (see Anuphap).
Means "related, connected to" in Thai, ultimately from Sanskrit अनुबन्ध (anubandha).
From Thai อนุ (anu) meaning "small, often" and ภาพ (phap) meaning "picture, image, vision".

MEANING - accomplished, worship, happiness, born under the asterism 'Anuradha', Seventeenth of twenty -eight lunar mansionsOrigin - Sanskrit
Means "to conserve, to maintain, to protect" in Thai, ultimately from Sanskrit अनुरक्ष् (anurakṣ).
From Thai อนุ (anu) meaning "small" and รัตน์ (rat) meaning "gem, jewel".
Means "pacified, soothed" in Sanskrit. This was the name a disciple and cousin of the Buddha.
Alternate transcription of Thai อนุรักษ์ (see Anurak).
From Sanskrit अनुरूप (anurūpa) meaning "suitable, fit, worthy".
From Thai อนุ (anu) meaning "small, often" and ศักดิ์ (sak) meaning "power".
Alternate transcription of Thai อนุสรา (see Anutsara).

Mandaic form of Enosh. This is the name of an uthra (a celestial being) who is one of the three sons of Adam in Mandaean tradition. He helped to reveal Mandaean teachings to John the Baptist and is considered an equivalent of the biblical Enosh.
Derived from Sanskrit, this name means "beautiful morning". It is also the name of a star.Anusha Rizvi (born 1978) is an Indian film director and screenwriter.

Means "sweet town" from Armenian անուշ (anuš) meaning "sweet" combined with ավան (avan) "town, village". Originally, it was formed from Avestan anaoša meaning "immortal" and urvan "soul", though it was also interpreted as meaning "slogan" or "adoring, loyal" or derived from a word meaning "coconut".
From the Middle Persian 𐭠𐭭𐭥𐭱𐭪𐭩 𐭫𐭥𐭡𐭠𐭭 (ʾnʿšky lʿbʾn /⁠anōšag ruwān⁠) meaning "immortal soul". This was an epithet of Khosrow I.

From Middle Persian 𐭠𐭭𐭥𐭱𐭪𐭩 𐭫𐭥𐭡𐭠𐭭 (anōšag ruwān) meaning "immortal soul", derived from 𐭠𐭭𐭥𐭱𐭪𐭩 (anōšag⁠) meaning "immortal" and 𐭫𐭥𐭡𐭠𐭭 (ruwān) meaning "soul". This was an epithet of Khosrau I, a popular 6th-century emperor of the Sassanid Persian Empire.

From Persian anush meaning "undying" and Turkic tegin meaning "prince".
From Sanskrit अनुष्ठा (anuṣṭhā) meaning "to follow, to practise, to perform".
Croatian, Czech, Slovak and Slovene form of Anushka.
Means "memory, remembrance" in Thai, ultimately from Sanskrit अनुस्मरण (anusmaraṇa).

From Thai อนุ (anu) meaning "small, often" and เทพ (thep) meaning "god, deity, angel".
From Thai อนุ (anu) meaning "small" and ธิดา (thida) meaning "daughter, girl".

From Thai อนุสร (anuson) meaning "to remember, to think of".
Means "incomparably great, best" in Sanskrit. This is one of the thousand names of Vishnu.
Combination of Anu, the name of a 17th century Mongolian queen consort, and the early Mongolian suffix üjin meaning "lady, princess, queen".
Alternate transcription of Thai อนุวัฒน์ (see Anuwat).
Russian and Ukrainian form of Anubius.
From Sanskrit अनुव्रत (anuvrata) meaning "devoted, faithful, devout".
Bengali and Malay form of Anwar.
From Thai อนุวัต (anuwat) meaning "to follow, to comply with, to act according to, to observe", ultimately from Sanskrit अनुवृत् (anuvṛt).
MEANING - (to go after or alongside, to follow ;to seek ; to be guided by; to fall to one's share.) Usage : Sanskrit, Indian, Tamil, Telugu, Nepali, Sinhala, Hindi, Sikh, Buddhist

Means "lights" in Arabic, the plural of نُور (nūr) meaning "light". It is used as a masculine name in Pakistan while it is typically feminine in Arabic-speaking countries.
Means "rays of light" in Arabic. From the same root as masculine Anwar.
Means "light of the faith", from Arabic أَنْوَار (anwār) meaning "light, illuminous" and دِين (dīn) meaning "faith, religion".
Means "lights of the truth" from Arabic أنوار (ʾanwār) meaning "lights" (the plural of نور (nūr) meaning "light") combined with حقّ (ḥaqq) meaning "truth".
First part of compound Arabic names beginning with أنوار ال (ʾAnwār al) meaning "lights of the" (such as أنوار الحق (ʾAnwār al-Ḥaqq) meaning "lights of the truth").
From Sanskrit अन्वेष (anveṣa) meaning "searching for, seeking, investigating".
Alternative form of Annwyl, derived from the Welsh word annwyl meaning "dear, darling".
From the Welsh word annwyl, which means "dear" or "darling".
Directly taken from Welsh anwylyd "beloved; dear".
Diminutive form of Annwyl or Anwyl, with the diminutive suffix -yn.

column3: 岸翔, 安翔, 岸祥, 安祥, 岸响, 安响, etc.(Chinese)|岸響, 安響, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 岸 (àn) meaning "beach, shore, bank" or 安 (ān) meaning "peace, quiet" combined with 翔 (xiáng) meaning "soar, glide" or 祥 (xiáng) meaning "good luck, good omen" or 响 (xiǎng) meaning "sound, echo". Other hanzi combinations are posisble.
Derived from Galician anxos, the plural form of anxo "angel" and thus a cognate of Ángeles.
From the Chinese 岸 (àn) meaning "bank, shore; beach, coast" and 萱 (xuān) meaning "day-lily".

column3: 安雅, etc.(Chinese)|Аня(Mongolian Cyrillic)|ᠠᠨᠶᠠ(Traditional Mongolian)|อัญญา(Thai)

column12: Variant of Aniyah, or a combination of Nyah with a phonetic prefix.
Alternate transcription of Thai อัญมณี (see Anyamani).
Means "jewel, gem" in Thai, ultimately derived from Sanskrit अन्य (anya) meaning "other, different" and मणि (maṇi) meaning "jewel, gem".
Meaning born in the mid morning
its a name that is given to the step herbs.
Name of a vengeance demon, Anyanka "Anya" Jenkins, from the American TV-series 'Buffy the Vampire Slayer' (1997-2003).
From the Chinese 安 (ān) meaning "quiet, calm, peaceful" and 瑶 (yáo) meaning "precious jade".

column3: 安逸, 安忆, 安怡, etc.(Chinese)
column12: Spanish form of Angie reflecting the English pronunciation.
A notable bearer is Anyim Pius Anyim, a Nigerian politician.
From the Chinese 安 (ān) meaning "quiet, calm, peaceful, tranquil, satisfied" and 英 (yīng) meaning "hero, brave" or "flower, leaf, petal".
Means "the one who sweetens me" in Bette Obudu.
Variant of Anylah, derived from the masculine name, Anil.When used as an English name, it may be an invented name based of Nyla.
Variant of Anila 1, Aniela, or Anela.
Possibly a diminutive of Angel and/or Ayan. A known bearer of this name was the Bulgarian soccer player Ayan "Anyo" Sadakov (1961-2017).

From Ancient Greek ἄνυσις (anusis) "fulfillment, accomplishment", ultimately from άνύω (anúō) ("to accomplish, to cause"). Saint Anysia of Salonika was a Christian virgin and martyr of the 4th century.
Feminine form of Anytos. Anyte of Tegea was a 3rd-century BC Arcadian poet, admired by her contemporaries and later generations for her charming epigrams and epitaphs.

Derived from Ancient Greek ἁνύτω (anyto), the Attic form of ἀνύω (anyo), meaning "to effect, achieve, accomplish, complete". This was the name of a titan in Greek mythology, said to have raised the goddess Despoine.

An acronym, given in honour of the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps; originally those who served at Gallipoli during World War I, but now all who have served and died for Australia and New Zealand during military operations.
Originates from the Arabic language.Anzar name meaning in English is Pure Gold, Silver.
From Japanese 杏 (an) meaning "apricot" combined with 世 (ze) meaning "generations". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Sardinian form of Angela as well as a quasi-adoption of the Sardinian word ànzelu "angel".
Latvian form of Angela and Estonian transcription of Анжела (see Anzhela). Belarusian łacinka form of Anzhela.
Polish transcription of Анжела (see Anzhela) as well as variant of Angela influenced by Anzhela. (See also Andżela, Anżelika).

Polish transcription of Анжелика or Анжеліка (see Anzhelika. Rarely used as a Polish alternate form of Angelika, possibly influenced by the word "anżelika", which refers to candied Angelica, or to the plant Angelica in general.
Polish and Hungarian form of Anselm.
Polish, Hungarian, Croatian and Lithuanian feminine form of Anselm.
Variant of Ànghelu. The name coincides with Sardinian ànzelu "angel".
From the Chinese 岸 (àn) meaning "beach, shore" and 峥 (zhēng) meaning "high, lofty, noble" or 正 (zhèng) meaning "correct, right, proper".

column3: 安治, 安志, 安智, etc.(Chinese)
column12: Combination of the names An 1 and Zhi, can also be a form of Angie or Angi.
From the Chinese 岸 (àn) meaning "beach, shore" and 钟 (zhōng) meaning "clock, bell".

A murderer who figures into Tristan’s ancestry. He was born the son of King Clodoveus. His sister was named Cressile or Trasfilas.He slew Apollo, the first King of Lyoness (Lyonesse) (and Tristan’s great-great-great-grandfather), for which his father executed him.Appearing in the Prose Tristan and La Tavola Ritonda, he is unnamed in the former.
Form of Anzor with the nominative suffix, used in Georgian when the name is written stand-alone.

column3: 杏, 杏子, 杏珠(Japanese Kanji)|あんず(Japanese Hiragana)|アンズ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From 杏 or 杏子 (anzu), referring to a type of apricot known as Prunus armeniaca (also called the ansu, Siberian or Tibetan apricot).The second kanji can be substituted with one that can be read as zu, like 珠 meaning "gem, jewel."One bearer of this name is actress Anzu Nagai (永井 杏) (1992-).
Possibly means "heavenly eagle". Name borne by a Mesopotamian demon, who was drawn in the form of a huge fire and water breathing bird, or a lion-headed eagle.
From Japanese 杏 (anzu) meaning "apricot" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Chinese 骜 (áo or ào) meaning "a steed, an uncontrollable wild horse, a good horse" or 傲 (ào) meaning "proud, arrogant". Other hanzi can also form this name.
Name of the Guaraní god of fertility, whose offspring served as the protectors of the hills and mountains. The name is derived from the sound the creature is said to make when pursuing victims.

column3: 青葉, 蒼葉, 蒼波, 蒼羽, 青波, 青羽, 碧葉, 碧波, 碧羽, 葵葉, 葵波, 葵羽(Japanese Kanji)|あお葉(Kanji/Hiragana)|あおば(Japanese Hiragana)|アオバ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Derived from the Japanese kanji 青葉 (aoba) referred to "fresh, green/blue leaves". For a long time, the distinction between "blue" and "green" in Japanese was not made. This name can be also written 蒼 / 碧 (ao) meaning "green, blue" as well or 葵 (ao) meaning "hollyhock, mallow" combined with 葉 (ba) meaning "leaf, blade, needle" or 波 (ba) meaning "wave, billow, ripple" or 羽 (ba) meaning "feather, wing". This name is more often used as surname or given name for fictional characters.Other kanji combinations are also possible.
From the Chinese 奥 (ào) meaning "mysterious, obscure, profound" and 柏 (bǎi) meaning "cypress, cedar".
From Japanese 翠 (ao) meaning "green", 巴 (ba) meaning "tomoe" combined with 子 (ko) "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From the Chinese 奥 (ào) meaning "mysterious, obscure, profound" and 兵 (bīng) meaning "soldier".

column3: 骜博, 奥博, 奥帛, 傲博(Chinese)
column12: From the Chinese 骜 (ào) meaning "wild horse", 奥 (ào) meaning "mysterious, obscure, profound" or 傲 (ào) meaning "proud, haughty" and 博 (bó) meaning "rich" or "win, gamble, play games" or 帛 (bó) meaning "silks, wealth, property".

column3: 翱倡, 翱畅, 奥昌, 傲昌(Chinese)
column12: From the Chinese 翱 (áo) meaning "soar, roam", 奥 (ào) meaning "mysterious, obscure, profound" or 傲 (ào) meaning "proud, haughty" and 倡 (chàng) meaning "guide, leader; lead", 畅 (chàng) meaning "free, smooth" or 昌 (chāng) meaning "light of sun; good, proper".

column3: 翱成, 翱诚, 奥丞, 傲丞(Chinese)
column12: From the Chinese 翱 (áo) meaning "soar, roam", 奥 (ào) meaning "mysterious, obscure, profound" or 傲 (ào) meaning "proud, haughty" and 成 (chéng) meaning "become, succeed" or "completed, finished", 诚 (chéng) meaning "sincere, honest, real" or 丞 (chéng) meaning "assist, aid, rescue".
Means "good for nothing" or "null" in Nahuatl, derived from aoc "no longer, not anymore" and nelli "true, truth".
From the Chinese 奥 (ào) meaning "mysterious, obscure, profound" and 聪 (cōng) meaning "intelligent, bright".
Meaning uncertain, possibly means "no more time" or "not yet time" in Nahuatl, from aoc "no longer, not anymore; not yet" and queman "sometimes; at what time, when?".
Possibly means "he says nothing", from Nahuatl aoctle "nothing, no more, nothing left" and the directional form of itoa "to say, to speak".
Possibly means "nameless" in Nahuatl, from aoctle "nothing, no more, nothing more" and itoca "name".

Feminization of Aodh, which is derived from Old Irish Áed meaning "fire". This seems to be a modern Irish name and it's sometimes incorrectly pronounced like Ada (AY-da), however in Irish the H would lead to the D not being pronounced.
Compound name composed of Aodh "fire" and Fionn "white".

This is a modern Irish name based on the Irish Aodh stemming from áed which means "fire" combined with the popular modern suffix of la. It was likely also inspired by names with popular sounds such as Ayla. It's not a traditional Irish name. Contrary to popular belief, this is not a form of Isla. Aodh can only sound like AY or EE in Irish, never like EYE.
Feminine diminuitive of Aodh. This was 'the name of an Irish saint whose feast was kept on 9 November'.
From the Chinese 奥 (ào) meaning "mysterious, obscure, profound" and 东 (dōng) meaning "east, eastern".

Derived from Old Breton alt "high; elevated" and either Old Breton roen "royal" or Old Breton roen / roin "lineage of a king". In recent times, folk etymology likes to associate this name with Modern Breton aod "coast, shore, waterside".

column3: 青恵, 青江, 青絵, 青枝, 蒼絵, 蒼恵, 蒼江, 蒼枝, 碧絵, 碧恵, 碧江, 碧枝, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 青 (ao) meaning "blue", 蒼 (ao) meaning "blue, green" or 碧 (ao) meaning "jade" combined with 恵 (e) meaning "favour, benefit", 江 (e) meaning "creek, bay", 絵 (e) meaning "picture, painting, drawing, sketch" or 枝 (e) meaning "branch". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From the Chinese 奥 (ào) meaning "mysterious, obscure, profound" and 芳 (fāng) meaning "fragrant".
From the Chinese 奥 (ào) meaning "mysterious, obscure, profound" or 傲 (ào) meaning "proud, haughty" and 峰 (fēng) meaning "peak, summit".
From the Chinese 奥 (ào) meaning "mysterious, obscure, profound" and 耿 (gěng) meaning "bright, shining".

column3: 仰(Japanese Kanji)|あおぎ(Japanese Hiragana)|アオギ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From 仰ぎ (aogi) meaning "respect, reverance" (compare Aogu).This name is very rarely used.

column3: 仰(Japanese Kanji)|あおぐ(Japanese Hiragana)|アオグ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From verb 仰ぐ (aogu) meaning "to look up to, respect, revere; to seek; to depend/rely on" (compare Aogi).This name is rarely used.

column3: 葵葉, 葵波, 葵羽, 蒼羽, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 葵 (ao) meaning "hollyhock" combined with 葉 (ha) meaning "leaf". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Aohei comes from Japanese 青兵 which consists of 青 (ao) meaning “blue, green” and兵 (hei) meaning “soldier, warrior.”
From Japanese 青 (ao) meaning "blue" combined with 姫 (hime) meaning "princess". Other kanji combinations are also possible.

column3: 青人, 蒼一, 葵仁, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 青 or 蒼 (ao) meaning "blue" combined with 人 (hito) meaning "person". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From the Chinese 奥 (ào) meaning "mysterious, obscure, profound" and 欢 (huān) meaning "joyous, merry, happy".
From the Chinese 翱 (áo) meaning "soar, roam" and 珲 (huī) meaning "bright, glorious, splendid".
Aoibh - an old Irish girls name of Celtic origin meaning “Beautiful” “radiant” “Pleasant”
Derived from the Irish word "aoibh", meaning beauty. Numerous bearers can be seen on social media.
Variant of Aoibheann.Irish meaning "Fairy Queen". She was queen of the fairies in Irish Gaelic Mythology.

Probably from Old Irish óibell "spark, fire". In Irish legend this is the name of a banshee or goddess who appeared to the Irish king Brian Boru on the eve of the Battle of Clontarf (1014). She is still said to dwell in the fairy mound of Craig Liath in County Clare.

Derived from Irish aoibh "smile, pleasant expression" and grian "sun". This name belonged to the daughter of Deirdre and Naoise in Longas Mac nUislenn (The Exile of the Sons of Uisnech), a story of the Ulster Cycle of Irish mythology. She was thought to marry Rinn, king of the Otherworld.
Irish form of Evie or a diminutive of Aoibheann.
From Japanese 青 (ao) meaning "blue" combined with 一 (ichi) meaning "one". Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.

column3: 碧伽, 碧夏, 碧架, 碧花, 碧華, 碧香, 葵加, 葵可, 葵架, 葵香, 蒼佳, 蒼加, 蒼可, 蒼夏, 蒼果, 蒼華, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 碧 (aoi) meaning "blue, green", 葵 (aoi) meaning "hollyhock" or 蒼 (aoi) meaning "blue" combined with 伽 (ka) meaning "nursing, attending, entertainer", 夏 (ka) meaning "summer", 架 (ka) meaning "erect, frame, mount, support, shelf, construct", 花 (ka) or 華 (ka) both meaning "flower", 香 (ka) meaning "fragrance", 加 (ka) meaning "add, addition, increase, join, include, Canada", 可 (ka) meaning "can, passable, mustn't, should not, do not", 佳 (ka) meaning "excellent, beautiful, good, pleasing, skilled" or 果 (ka) meaning "fruit, reward, carry out, achieve, complete, end, finish, succeed". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 葵子(Japanese Kanji)|あおいこ(Japanese Hiragana)|アオイコ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Aoi combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child."This name is very rarely used.
From Irish faoileann meaning "fair maiden" or "seagull".
From Irish aoine meaning "Friday", derived from Latin ieiunum. Aoine has only been used as a given name in Ireland in recent times.
Derived from aois meaning "age, era" in Irish.
From the Chinese 奥 (ào) meaning "mysterious, obscure, profound" or 傲 (ào) meaning "proud, haughty" and 捷 (jié) meaning "win, victory, triumph" or 杰 (jié) meaning "hero; heroic, outstanding".

column3: 葵花, 葵華, 葵香, 蒼花, 碧花, 藍華, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 葵 (ao) meaning "hollyhock" combined with 花 (ka) or 華 (ka) which both mean "flower" or 香 (ka) meaning "fragrance". Other kanji combinations are possible.

From Japanese 青 (ao), meaning “blue”, and 木 (ki), meaning “tree”. 青木 (although commonly アオキ) is the Japanese word for the Aucuba japonica, or the spotted laurel plant. In the language of flowers, the Aucuba japonica symbolizes the idiom 初志貫徹, meaning to carry out your first plan, or to follow through on your original intentions.

column3: アオコ(Japanese Katakana)|青子, 蒼子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 青 (ao) "blue, green" combined with 子 (ko) "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 碧玖, 藍久, 青空, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 碧 (ao) meaning "blue, green", 藍 (ao) meaning "indigo" or 青 (ao) meaning "blue" combined with 玖 (ku) meaning "beautiful black jewel, nine", 久 (ku) meaning "long time" or 空 (ku) meaning "sky". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Derived from Hawaiian ao "cloud" and lani "sky, heaven".

column3: 傲磊, 傲雷, 傲蕾, 奥磊, 奥雷, etc.(Chinese)|奧磊, 奧雷, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 奥 (aò) meaning "difficult to understand" or 傲 (ào) meaning "to defy, to refuse to yield to" combined with 雷 (léi) meaning "thunder", 磊 (lěi) meaning "pile of stones, open, upright", or 蕾 (lěi) meaning "bud". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From the Chinese 奥 (ào) meaning "mysterious, obscure, profound" and 翎 (líng) meaning "feather, wing".

A combination honoring Irish deities Aodh and Lugh. Aodh is often referred to as a "god of the underworld," although this is likely influenced by Christian interpretation. He and his siblings were turned into swans by their stepmother, Aoife. Lugh was a deity famed for being skilled in many disciplines, including being a poet, smith, swordsman, harpist, historian, craftsman, historian, and warrior. He is known by the epithets Lámfada ("of the long arm"), Ildánach ("skilled in many arts"), Macnia ("youthful hero"), and Lonnbéimnech "fierce striker"), among others.

column3: 青芽, 青女, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 青 (ao) meaning "blue" combined with 芽 (me) meaning "bud, sprout, shoot" or 女 (me) meaning "female, woman, wife". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: あおみ(Japanese Hiragana)|葵海, 葵巳, 翠美, 青海, 青実, 青水, 青美, 蒼海, 蒼実, 蒼深, 蒼美, 蒼望, 蒼未, 蒼魅, 蒼巳, 蒼弥, 碧海, 碧実, 碧水, 碧美, 碧魅, 碧巳, 碧洋, 明歩, 藍海, 藍美, 碧深, 明緒実, 明百美, 粟生実, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 葵 (ao) meaning "hollyhock, althea", 翠 (ao) meaning "green, kingfisher", 青 or 蒼 (ao) meaning "blue", 碧 (ao) meaning "blue, green", 明 (ao, a) meaning "bright", 藍 (ao) meaning "indigo", 粟 (a) meaning "millet", 緒 (o) meaning "cord, strap", 百 (o) meaning "hundred" or 生 (o) meaning "live" combined with 海 (mi) meaning "sea, ocean", 巳 (mi), referring to the Snake, the sixth of the twelve Earthly Branches, 美 (mi) meaning "beautiful", 水 (mi) meaning "water", 実 (mi) meaning "fruit, good result, truth", 深 (mi) meaning "deep, heighten, intensify, strengthen", 望 (mi) meaning "ambition, full moon, hope, desire, aspire to, expect", 未 (mi) referring to the Sheep, the eighth of the twelve Earthly Branches, 魅 (mi) meaning "fascination, charm", 弥 (mi) meaning "all the more, increasingly", 洋 (mi) meaning "ocean" or 歩 (mi) meaning "walk". Other kanji combinations are also possible.This name is most of the time given for females, but rarely given to males, if given at all.
A famous bearer would be famous thai pop singer, Aommy, whose real name is Plernsin Ketkaew.

column3: 亜音, 空音, 蒼音, 碧音, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 亜 (a) meaning "second, Asia", 空 (a) meaning "sky", 蒼 (a) meaning "blue, green" or 碧 (a) meaning "jade, green, blue" combined with 音 (on) meaning "sound". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 彩桜那, 青奈, 蒼菜, 碧那, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
青音, 葵音, 蒼音, 碧音, 藍音, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 青 (ao) meaning "blue", 葵 (ao) meaning "hollyhock", 蒼 (ao) meaning "blue, green", 碧 (ao) meaning "green, blue" or 藍 (ao) meaning "indigo" combined with 音 (ne) meaning "sound". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 青乃, 蒼乃, 碧野, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 青 (ao) "blue", 蒼 (ao) meaning "blue, green", or 碧 (ao) meaning "green, blue" combined with 乃 (no), a possessive particle or 野 (no) meaning "plain, wilderness, field". Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.
From the Chinese 翱 (áo) meaning "soar, roam" and 鹏 (péng), the name of a mythological bird or 怦 (pēng) meaning "eager, ardent".
From the Chinese 奥 (ào) meaning "mysterious, obscure, profound" or 傲 (ào) meaning "proud, haughty" and 琴 (qín), a type of Chinese lute or 钦 (qīn) meaning "respect, admire; respectful".
From the Chinese 翱 (áo) meaning "soar, roam" and 泉 (quán) meaning "spring, fountain" or "wealth, money".

Probably derived from Ancient Greek ἄωρος (aoros) meaning "unripe, premature, untimely", composed of the negative prefix ἀ (a) and ὥρα (hora) meaning "season, time period". This was the name of a nymph in Greek mythology, namesake of the ancient town Aoros in Crete, later renamed Eleutherna. Local aristocrats claimed to be descended from Aora and her husband Eleuther, one of the Kouretes.
Means "cloud in the sky" in Māori. Aoraki/Mt Cook is New Zealand's highest mountain. Variant of Aorangi referring to the clouds surrounding the mountain.
From the Chinese 奥 (ào) meaning "mysterious, obscure, profound" or 傲 (ào) meaning "proud, haughty" and 然 (rán) meaning "yes, certainly; pledge, promise".
Means "bright sky" or "cloud in the sky" in Māori from ao "world, bright, cloud" and rangi "sky". Aorangi is also the Māori word for "planet".
From the Chinese 奥 (ào) meaning "mysterious, obscure, profound" and 人 (rén) meaning "man, person; mankind".

column3: 青梨, 青理, 翠麗, 翠璃, 翠梨, 青里, 蒼利, 蒼李, 翠利, 華百, 愛織, 亜緒梨, 亜王理, 亜王吏, 蒼理, 蒼麗, 碧生理, 碧李, 碧麗, 藍梨, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|あおり(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: From Japanese 青 (ao) meaning "blue" combined with 梨 (ri) meaning "pear". Other kanji combinations are possible.

Meaning uncertain, perhaps from Greek ἄορ (aor) meaning "sword hung in a belt". In Greek legend this name belonged to a son of Aras, an autochthon who was believed to have built Arantea, the most ancient town in Phliasia. When his sister Araethyrea died, Aoris renamed the country of Phliasia 'Araethyrea' after her.

column3: 碧冴, 碧砂, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 碧 (ao) meaning "green, blue" and 冴⁠ (sa.eru) "be clear, serene, cold, skillful”. Other kanji combinations can be used.
From the Chinese 奥 (ào) meaning "mysterious, obscure, profound" and 森 (sēn) meaning "forest".
From the Chinese 傲 (ào) meaning "proud, haughty" and 松 (sōng) meaning "pine, fir".
Means "white cloud" in Māori. Aotearoa is the Māori name of New Zealand
From the Chinese 奥 (ào) meaning "mysterious, obscure, profound" and 天 (tiān) meaning "sky, heaven".
Variant of Awa. A notable bearer was Malian independence activist Aoua Kéita (1912-1980).
Alternate transcription of Arabic عواطف (see Awatif) chiefly used in North Africa.
Alternate transcription of Arabic عواطف (see Awatif) chiefly used in North Africa.
This is the name of a Parsi Princess in Jules Verne's novel 'Around The World In Eighty Days'.
The name of a minor Breton saint of whom nothing else is known.
Likely derived from the five vowels of the English language.

Breton name, in which the first element is aour meaning "gold" (ultimately from Latin aurum). The second element may be Breton gen "cheek, face" or gwenn "shining, holy". This was the name of a Breton saint.
Derived from Breton aour "gold", this name is generally considered the Breton form of Aurelia.
Derived from Breton aour "gold" and Old Breton ken "fair; beautiful; splendid" (kaer and koant in Modern Breton), this name is the Breton cognate of Welsh Eurgain.

column12: From 青空 (aozora) meaning "blue sky."It can also be written as 蒼空 or 碧空. The first kanji can be changed to 葵, normally read as aoi, which refers to a mallow plant. The second kanji can be substituted with one that has the same or similar meaning(s) to 空, like 天.Nowadays, excluding 葵空, the kanji combinations used for this name are most commonly read as Sora.
Short form of Albert and Albertus (probably via the medieval variants Alpert and Alpertus). Also compare Ab.
From Yavapai, 'epache, "people" and sometimes derived from Zuni apachu, "enemy."
Derived from Basque apal "humble".The form Apala was first recorded in 1145, however the elaborated form Andreapala was recorded several times before Apala made her first appearance.

Meaning uncertain, probably related to Avestan apama- "the latest", hence "the youngest (child), nestling". This was the name of Apama, the first Queen of the Seleucid Empire, and wife of Seleucus I Nicator. She was sometimes known as Apama I or Apame I. Several towns were named Apamea after Apama I. Other bearers of this name include Apama II, a Seleucid Princess, and her niece Apama III.
A variant of Apama. A bearer of this name is Apame, a concubine of King Darius I.

Probably derived from Coptic apa Amoun, where apa means "father" and Amoun is the Coptic form of Amon. The name thus essentially means "father Amon". However, it may also be possible that the name is a more extended form of Pamoun.
Altai and Belarusian form of Afanasiy.
From the Blackfoot word apaniiwa "butterfly", with the animate noun suffix -wa omitted.
Derived from the Ottoman Turkish title افندي (efendi) meaning "lord, master".

Probably derived from Coptic apa Anoub, where apa means "father" and Anoub is the Coptic form of Anubis. The name thus essentially means "father Anubis". However, it may also be possible that the name is a more extended form of Panoub.
In Inuit mythology, Apanuugak is a culture hero who was sometimes depicted as an error-prone warrior who lives to old age and sometimes as a dastardly villain.
Alternate transcription of Thai อาภาพร (see Aphaphon).
Derived from Georgian აპარეკა (Apareka), which is the name of a famous folk song from Khevsureti, the mountain region of Georgia. In the song itself, Apareka is the name of a young man.

Latinized form of Apellikon. A known bearer of this name was Apellicon of Teos, a famous book collector from the 1st century BC.
Derived the name of the god Apollo combined with Ancient Greek ἱκέτης (iketes) meaning "suppliant, one who comes looking for aid or protection", ultimately from ἵκω (iko) "to come, to reach out".
Derived from the Greek adjective ἀπήμαντος (apemantos) meaning "unharmed, unhurt".
Latinized form of Apemantos. This is the name of a cynical and misanthropic philosopher in the play Timon of Athens by William Shakespeare.
Means "rising fire sparks woman" or "rising cinder sparks woman" in Ainu. It is the full name of the goddess Kamuy-huci.

Means "freedom from harm, safety" or "harmlessness, innocence" in Ancient Greek. This was the name of a daughter of King Catreus in Greek mythology. She was able to outrun the god Hermes when he pursued her, though he eventually caught her by laying a trap in her path.
Apep is the Egyptian personification of darkness and disorder, often depicted as a giant serpent or snake. He was the main enemy of the sun god Ra.

A Roman cognomen of uncertain meaning. It is possibly derived from the Latin word aper meaning "boar" or apro meaning "wild boar". This was the cognomen of 4 people in the Severan family tree including a Roman aristocrat, Gaius Septimius Severus Aper.
Means "fearlessness, absence of danger" or "forgiveness, pardon" in Thai.

Possibly derived from Ancient Greek ἀφανής (aphanes) meaning "unseen, invisible, disappearing, secret" (see a and phanes). Aphaia was a Greek goddess who was worshipped almost exclusively at a single sanctuary on the island of Aegina in the Saronic Gulf. She originated as early as the 14th century BCE as a local deity associated with fertility and the agricultural cycle, but later came to be identified with the goddesses Athena and Artemis and with the nymph Britomartis.
From Thai อาภา (apha) meaning "light, brightness" and พร (phon) meaning "blessing".
Alternate transcription of Thai อาภาพร (see Aphaphon).

Uncertain etymology, possibly derived from Ancient Greek ἄφαρ (aphar) meaning "quickly, suddenly", or perhaps the toponym Φαραί (Pharai). Other possibilities are ἀφαρής (aphares) meaning "without" and ἄφαρος (apharos), which can mean "unploughed, untilled" as well as "unclad, naked". The latter possibility is ultimately derived from the Greek negative prefix ἄ- (a) combined with Greek φάρος (pharos), which can mean "plough" as well as "a large pierce of cloth, web". This was the name of several figures in Greek mythology, including a king of Messenia and a centaur. Aphareus was also the name of an ancient Greek tragedian and orator from the 4th century BC.
From Thai อาภัสระ (aphatsara) meaning "bright, clear, shining", ultimately from Sanskrit आभास्वर (abhasvara). This is also the name of a heavenly realm in Buddhist tradiiton.

Means "unsparing, not miserly" in Greek, derived from the Greek negative prefix ἀ (a) combined with the Greek adjective φειδός (pheidos) meaning "sparing, thrifty".This is the name of several characters from Greek mythology.
From the Greek goddess “Apheleia”, the goddess of ease, simplicity and good primitivity.
Means "complete, whole, all present" in Xhosa and Zulu. Often given to the last child to be born in a family.
Means "I will make to breathe", from Hebrew פּוּחַ (púakh) "to breathe, to blow". Aphiah, of the tribe of Benjamin, was an ancestor of King Saul.
Means "protect, guard, look after" in Thai, ultimately from Sanskrit अभिपाल (abhipāla).

Notable bearers of this name include the Greek sophist and rhetorician Aphthonius of Antioch (4th century AD) and the Roman writer Aelius Festus Aphthonius (4th century AD). Derived from either the Greek noun ἀποδημία (apodemia) meaning "going/being abroad, journey abroad" or from the Greek adjective ἀπόδημος (apodemos) meaning "away from one's country, abroad".Both words are ultimately derived from the Greek preposition ἀπό (apo) meaning "from, away from" and the Greek noun δῆμος (demos) meaning "people" as well as "country, land".
Latinized form of Apodemios. This was the name of a Roman officer from the 4th century AD, who worked as a secret agent of sorts for the Roman emperor Constantius II.

Means "giant lord" from the Tagalog title apo meaning "lord, master" and laki meaning "big, large". In Tagalog mythology Apolaki was the god of the sun and war and the brother of Mayari. After a war with his sister, which resulted in Mayari losing an eye, he came to rule the world during the day.
A greek word meaning destruction, ruin, and loss.
Spanish and Polish feminine form of Apollinaris and Romanian form of Apollinaria. This is also attested as an ancient Greek name.
Portuguese and Louisiana Spanish form of Apollinaris.
Feminine form of Apollo. It was used in the "Twitches" novel series by H. B. Gilmour and Randi Reisfeld.
Languedocian and Provençal form of Apollinaris.
Russian variant transcription of Apollinariy and Sicilian form of Apollinaris.
Russian feminine form of Apollinaris. According to Orthodox Christian ecclesiastical traditions, Apollinaria is venerated as a Virgin-Martyr alongside Saint Drosis.
Russian and Ukrainian form of Apollinaris.

Variant of Apollonius used by John Gower for the hero of his 1,737-line Middle English narrative 'The Tale of Apollinus' (in the 'Confessio amantis'), his version of the classical romance 'Apollonius of Tyre', widely popular in the Middle Ages.

Means "born of Apollo" from the name of the god Apollo combined with Ancient Greek γενής (genes) meaning "born". This name was borne by an eponymous archon of Athens, who lived in the 1st century BC.
Means "glory of Apollo" from the name of the god Apollo combined with Greek κλέος (kleos) meaning "glory".
