From the Uzbek bibi meaning "mother, learned woman, authoritative woman" and the given name Saida.
From the Uzbek bibi meaning "mother, learned woman, authoritative woman" and sanam meaning "idol, beautiful woman".
From the Uzbek bibi meaning "mother, learned woman, authoritative woman" and san'at meaning "art, craft".
From Kazakh бибі (bibı) meaning “matron, hostess” combined with the given name Sara.
From the Uzbek bibi meaning "mother, learned woman, authoritative woman" and shahar meaning "city, large town".
From the Uzbek bibi meaning "mother, learned woman, authoritative woman" and shakar meaning "sugar, sweet".
From the Uzbek bibi meaning "mother, learned woman, authoritative woman" and shamsiya meaning "parasol".
From the Uzbek bibi meaning "mother, learned woman, authoritative woman" and sohiba meaning "owner, possessor (fem.)".
From Persian بی‌بی (bibi) meaning "madam, lady, matron" and سارا (sara) meaning "clean, pure".
From the Uzbek bibi meaning "mother, learned woman, authoritative woman" and sulu(v) meaning "beautiful".
From the Uzbek bibi meaning "mother, learned woman, authoritative woman" and suman meaning "jasmine".
Means "origin, source, offspring, seed" in Javanese.
From the Uzbek bibi meaning "mother, learned woman, authoritative woman" and toj meaning "crown".
From the Uzbek bibi meaning "mother, learned woman, authoritative woman" and zar meaning "gold, wealth".
From the Uzbek bibi meaning "mother, learned woman, authoritative woman" and the given name Zaynab.
From the Uzbek bibi meaning "mother, learned woman, authoritative woman" and zilol meaning "crystal-clear, limpid, unclouded".
From the Uzbek bibi meaning "mother, learned woman, authoritative woman" and zor meaning "entreaty, need, desire".
Probably from the word bible, the central religious text of Christianity, or from the surname Bible.
Derived from the English word bible.
Old Hungarian name originally meaning "flax tissue", nowadays it is associated with Hungarian word "purple". Its more popular diminutive is Bíborka.

Roman cognomen which was derived from the Latin adjective bibulus, which can mean "fond of drinking, drinking readily or freely, ever thirsty" (mostly in relation to alcoholic beverages), as well as "absorbent, porous". A bearer of this name was Marcus Calpurnius Bibulus, a Roman politician from the 1st century BC.
Vietnamese form of Vijaya, referring to Maha Vijaya, a king of Champa from 1441 or 1442 to 1446.
Possibly derived from Old English becca "pickaxe, spade" or bica "beak, point; pointed ridge".
Cremish Lombard short form of Beatrice.

column3: 笔畅, 必畅, 笔昌, 必昌, etc.(Chinese)|筆暢, 必暢, 筆昌, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 笔 (bǐ) meaning "writing brush, pencil" or 必 (bì) meaning "surely, most certainly" combined with 畅 (chàng) meaning "smooth, free, unrestraind" or 昌 (chāng) meaning "flourish, prosper, good, sunlight". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Derived from the Georgian noun ბიჭი (bichi) meaning "boy, lad" as well as "son".
Meaning unknown. It is possibly used in honor of the French saint, St Joan Elizabeth Bichier des Âges, who is commonly referred as Elizabeth Bichier.
Diminutive of Bichia, which has by now become an independent name in Georgia. Interestingly, in this case the diminutive (Bichiko) is much more common in Georgia than the main form (Bichia).
From Sino-Vietnamese 碧玉 (bích ngọc) meaning "jasper" or inverted variant of Ngọc Bích. This is also a kind of orchid, Cymbidium dayanum.

Rare Dutch given name, which is probably derived from (or related to) the Dutch word bikkel, which is an informal (or slang) word for a tough, no-nonsense man. In that regard, the name is somewhat comparable with English masculine names such as Brick and Rock, as those are also meant to convey a certain sense of rugged masculinity. Also compare the Dutch given name Bink.A known Dutch bearer of this name is the aspiring actor Bickel Krabbé (b. 2000), the eldest son of the Dutch radio and television presenter Martijn Krabbé (b. 1968) and his ex-wife Amanda Beekman. Martijn is a son of the Dutch actor Jeroen Krabbé (b. 1944), so Bickel comes from a well-established Dutch show business family.
Variant of Victoria reflecting the Spanish pronunciation.
Transferred use of the surname Biden.
From Sanskrit विधान (vidhāna) meaning "order, arrangement, rule, regulation".
Bidkar was an officer of the Israelite king Jehu. Jehu ordered Bidkar to throw the body of the king he usurped, Jehoram, into the field of Naboth, fulfilling prophecy. II Kings 9:25
Bengali, Assamese, Odia and Nepali form of Vidya.
Bengali, Odia and Assamese form of Vidyut.
Diminutive of Benigna, Benedykta and Beata.
Diminutive of Beatrijs/Beatrix and Sabina/Sabine as well as Gabrielle (via its short forms Gabi and Gabie).
Short form of Sibilla, likely via the French form Sibylle or Sybille.
Belarusian form of Snow White, from Belarusian белы (biely) "white" and снег (snieh) "snow".
Variant of Beylke. Jerry Bock used this for the name of Tevye's fifth daughter in his musical 'Fiddler on the Roof' (1964).

Meaning unknown, as the name is a distortion that originated from nursery speech, which makes it difficult to retrace the original name.A notable bearer of this name is the Dutch news presenter Biem Buijs (b. 1981).
From Sino-Vietnamese 變 (biến) meaning "to change into, transform, become".
Possibly from Sino-Vietnamese 駢 (biền) meaning "side by side, parallel".
Possibly from Sino-Vietnamese 辦 (biện) meaning "to handle, prepare, measure" or 辯 (biện) meaning "to debate, discuss".
Variant of Benvenida, possibly via Benvenuta.
From Sino-Vietnamese 邊疆 (biên cương) meaning "border, frontier", composed of 邊 (biên) meaning "border" and 疆 (cương) meaning "boundary".
Means "welcome the good" derived from Bien meaning "good", li meaning "the" and Viengue meaning "to come" from Latin venire.
In the case of French swimmer Bienna Pélégry (1899-1989), it is a short form of one of her names, Bibiena.
Variant of Bianor. This is the name of several characters from Greek mythology, one of which is a centaur.
From Sino-Vietnamese 邊陲 (biên thùy) meaning "border, frontier", composed of 邊 (biên) meaning "border" and 陲 (thùy) meaning "frontier".
Meaning unknown, possibly of West Frisian origin.A notable bearer of this name is the Dutch children's book author Bies van Ede (b. 1957), whose birth name is Willem Johannes Franciscus van Ede.
Possible diminutive of Beitris. See also Beatie.

Perhaps from Bietta, the Romansch form of Beata.The medieval French woman Biette de Cassinel (c.1340–c.1380) was the chief mistress of King Charles V of France. She is occasionally referred to as Biota. Biette could conceivably be a francization of Bettina; her Italian great-grandfather was Bettino Cassinelli.
Feminized form of "Biff". Possible variant of "Tiffany".
Derived from Old Norse bifa "story" and lind "lime-tree" or bif "movement; air; water" and lind. This is another name for Odin.
Combination of bif 'movement', 'air', 'water' and liði 'one who goes', 'one who fares'. Bifliði is a name for Óðinn.

Derived from Latin bifrons meaning "having two faces, two-faced". This is an epithet of the Roman god Janus, who is often depicted with two faces looking in opposite directions. It is also the name of a demon who appears in several works on demonology, including the 17th-century grimoire The Lesser Key of Solomon (author unknown) and the Pseudomonarchia Daemonum (1563) by Dutch physician Johann Weyer.
The name of a dwarf in The Hobbit by J.R.R. Tolkien.Tolkien took the name from the Catalogue of dwarves (Dwergatal) in the Völuspá, a part of the poetic Edda.
Possibly derived from German biber or bever both meaning "beaver", or an Old Norse name meaning "the quaking one". In Norse mythology this is the name of a dwarf.
Sami variant of Biggi and Swedish diminutive of Birger.
Pet form of Brigitte, Birgit and their variants.
From Tagalog bighani meaning "allurement, fascination, charming".
Logudorese and Sassarese form of Iulianus (see Julian).
Romansh form of Barbara as well as a variant of Bina. This name is traditionally found in the Engadine valley.
Bigtha is one of the eunuchs who served King Xerxes in Esther 1:10.

From the Persian name meaning "God's gift". In the Old Testament this is the name of an eunuch in service of the Persian king Xerxes. Mordecai rested in the courtyard one day and overheard Bigthan, along with Teresh, plotting to kill the king. He went on to inform the king through Esther, thus thwarting the plot.
In the Book of Esther, one of the two chamberlains or eunuchs of Xerxes who conspired against the king's life
From the Chinese 碧 (bì) meaning "jade, green, blue" and 翮 (hé) meaning "quill".

column3: 必虹, 碧鸿, 碧虹(Chinese)
column12: From the Chinese 必 (bì) meaning "surely, most certainly" or 碧 (bì) meaning "jade, green, blue" and 虹 (hóng) meaning "rainbow" or 鸿 (hóng) meaning "wild swan".
Derived from Basque bihotz "heart; spirit; (by extension) courage; (term of endearment) dear, darling".
Coined by Sabino Arana Goiri and Koldo Elizalde as a variant of Bihotza.
Mandaic form of Vərəthraghna (see Bahram). In Mandaean tradition this is the name of an uthra (a celestial being) who presides over baptisms.
From the Chinese characters 碧 (bì) meaning "jade; green, blue" and 焕 (huàn) meaning "shining".
From the Chinese 必 (bì) meaning "surely, most certainly" and 惠 (huì) meaning "benefit, favour, kindness".

Loosely translated from Anishinaabemowin (the Ojibwe language) it is a name meaning "daybreak," "the approach of dawn," "dawn is coming." In experience, it is given as a--or part of an--Ojibwe/Indian name and most likely is not someone's legal name.
Sami form of Pia and variant of Birrá.
Means "wise, clever, reasonable" in Indonesian, ultimately from Sanskrit विचक्षण (vicakṣaṇa).
bijal means the richel,sine.the sanskrit mining is bijali,the hindi mining is roshni,prakash.
Modern form of Bizhan. In literature, Bijan is the name of a character in the 10th-century epic poem Shahnameh written by the Persian poet Ferdowsi.
Derived from Kurdish bijare meaning "elite, the best".
Odia and Nepali form of Vijaya.

column3: 実人, 美人, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|碧锦(Chinese)
column12: From Japanese 実 (bi) meaning "fruit, good result, truth" or 美 (bi) meaning "beautiful" combined with 人 (jin) meaning "person". Other kanji combinations are possible.As a word, Bijin (美人) means a beautiful woman, a beauty, a belle or a handsome man.
From the Chinese 馝 (bì) meaning "fragrance" and 久 (jiǔ) meaning "a long time ago".
Plural of the French word bijou, meaning "jewel". It is not used as a given name in France.
From the Chinese characters 碧 (bì) meaning "jade; green, blue" and 涓 (juān) meaning "brook, stream; select; pure".
From Turkic bika meaning "lady" (feminine form of beg meaning "chieftain, master").
Bengali, Odia, Assamese and Nepali form of Vikas.
Derived from Bashkir бик (bik) meaning "strong, hard" and from Persian پولاد (pulâd) meaning “steel”.
Meaning "Frog" in Ainu. Name of Ainu artist and activist Bikki Sunazawa, who designed the Ainu flag in 1973.
Alternate transcription of Punjabi Gurmukhi ਬਿਕਰਮਜੀਤ (see Bikramjit).

Late Greek form of Victor, as well as the original Georgian form of Victor. Biktor is considered an old and rare name in both Georgia and Greece. In Georgia, this is because Viktor has become the dominant form there, probably due to the influence that Russia has had on the country. As for Greece: Viktor (written as Βίκτωρ) is also the dominant form there now, but for a different reason. The pronunciation of the first letter of the name (the beta) has changed over time: it was a 'b' in ancient Greek, but it is a 'v' in modern Greek. As such, Βίκτωρ was Biktor in older times, but it is Viktor in modern times.

Means "open space, interval; moment, instant" in Icelandic and Old Norse. In the Poetic Edda, Bil and her brother Hjúki follow Máni, the personification of the moon, across the heavens. Her name was sometimes used as a kenning for "woman".
Hebrew transcription of Pippi, used in the Hebrew translation of 'The Adventures of Pippi Longstocking'.
Etymology unknown. Bildad the Shuhite was one of Job's three friends. Also used for one of the characters in Moby Dick
Derived from Basque bildots "lamb" and the Basque feminine suffix -ne. It is used as a Basque equivalent of Inés.
Derived from Old Norse bíldr, a knife for blood-letting. This is the name of a dwarf in Norse mythology.
From Mongolian билэг (bileg) meaning "gift, talent" and сайхан (saikhan) meaning "nice, beautiful, handsome".
Alternate transcription of Arabic بلال (see Bilal) chiefly used in North Africa.
Variant of Billfrith, derived from Old English Bilfrið.
Derived from the Old English elements bil "sword" and friþ "peace". A notable bearer of this name was an obscure Northumbrian saint dubbed "St Billfrith the Anchorite".
From the Turkish bilge meaning "wise, profound".
Means "scholar, pundit, learned person" in Turkish.
Combination of Bilgin and Persian ناز (nāz) meaning "delight, comfort".
Means "wise moon", from Bilgüün meaning "wise" and саран (saran) meaning "moon".
Derived from the Old English elements bil "sword" and heard "firm, hardy, brave".
Latinised form of Bilihild.Sometimes used as a monastic name for nuns.
From the Chinese 碧 (bì) meaning "jade, green, blue" and 莲 (lián) meaning "lotus, water lily".
From the Chinese 碧 (bì) meaning "jade, blue, green" and 良 (liáng) meaning "good, virtuous, respectable".
Gallurese variant form of Iulianus (see Julian).
Variant spelling of Bilihild. Bilichild was the wife of Childeric II, a 7th-century Frankish king.
Derived from the Germanic element bili "gentleness" combined with Old High German fridu "peace."

The first element of this name is derived from the Germanic element bili "gentleness." The second element is derived from gardan "to hedge in, to enclose, to fence in" or from Gothic gards "house, garden, (court)yard."

The first element of this Germanic name comes from bili "gentleness." The meaning and origin of the second element is rather uncertain: we know that it comes from gis (the original form was possibly gîs), but we don't exactly know where gis itself comes from. But there are a few possibilities. It might come from Gallo-Celtic gaiso "spear" (see Gaiseric) or it might be a short form of gisel, which means "hostage" or "pledge" (see Giselle).

The meaning of the first element of this name is uncertain. Some sources theorise that it is derived from a Germanic (possibly Saxon) word that meant "gentleness". Compare Proto-Germanic *biliz meaning "gentle, kind" as well as "fair, decent".Other sources connect the first element to Old High German bîl meaning "axe, hatchet". Also compare modern Dutch bijl and modern German Beil meaning "axe, hatchet".Finally, one source states that this element might possibly be Celtic in origin, in which case it might come from bilo meaning "safe, secure" as well as "good, fortunate".The second element of this name is derived from Old High German grimo meaning "mask".
Derived from the Germanic element bili "gentleness" combined with Old High German gund "war."
Derived from the Germanic element bili "gentleness" combined with Old High German helm "helmet, protection."
Derived from the Germanic element bili "gentleness" combined with Old Norse hildr "battle."
Possibly a shortened form of Hurichabilike, or simply a sinicized form of a Mongolian name.
Derived from the Germanic element bili "gentleness" combined with Old High German mâri "famous."
Derived from the Germanic element bili "gentleness" combined with Old High German mund "protection."

column3: 必琳, 馝凛, 碧粼(Chinese)
column12: From the Chinese 必 (bì) meaning "surely, most certainly", 馝 (bì) meaning fragrance" or 碧 (bì) meaning "jade, blue, green" and 琳 (lín) meaning "beautiful jade, gem", 凛 (lǐn) meaning "cold, severe, strict" or 粼 (lín) meaning "clear".
Probably rarely used alternate spelling of Belinda. Mostly known because of Bilinda Butcher, who is guitarist/singer of My Bloody Valentine.
From the Chinese 必 (bì) meaning "surely, most certainly" and 玲 (líng) meaning "tinkling of jade".
Derived from the Germanic element bili "gentleness" combined with hraban or hramn "raven."

Perhaps a Macedonian dialectical form of Philistiche, or a Hellenized form of a non-Greek name. This was borne by a 3rd-century BC hetaira (courtesan or prostitute of ancient Greece) of uncertain origin. According to Pausanias, she was a Macedonian; according to Athenaeus, an Argive; according to Plutarch, a foreign slave bought from the marketplace. She won the tethrippon and synoris horse races in the 264 BC Olympic Games. She became a mistress of Ptolemy II Philadelphus and was deified by him as Aphrodite Bilistiche.
Derived from the Germanic element bili "gentleness" combined with þruþ "strength."
Masculine form of Biljana. Biljan Stojanovski is a Macedonian singer.
Low German diminutive of Names starting in Bil- (from the Germanic name element BILI "gentleness").
Dutch, Limburgish and Romansh short form of Sibilla.
Bengali form of Bilal, as well as an Arabic alternate transcription chiefly used in North Africa.
Transferred use of the surname Billard.
Perhaps originally a diminutive of Birger.
From Hindi बिल्ली (billee) meaning "cat". It is also used as variant of the name BILLY, BILLIE, or BILLI.
Alternate spelling of Billie with -eigh ending.
Alternate transcription of Arabic بلال (see Bilal) chiefly used in Algeria.
Anglicised form of Anglo-Saxon Bilfrið. Saint Billfrith is a famous bearer.
Variant of William, incorporating the diminutive Bill.
Possibly a feminine elaboration of Billie.
Strictly feminine version of Billie, or a combination of Billy and Anne 1.
Combination of Billie and Jean 2. This is also popularized by the title of the song by Michael Jackson named "Billie Jean" released on January 22nd 1983.
Combination of Billie and Jo. Also, see its male counterpart: Billyjoe.
Character from a novel in the Oz series.

Derived from Old Norse billingr "twin" or from Ancient Germanic bhi- "two-, double-" and -ingr, a suffix denoting "belonging to" or "descended from". In Norse mythology this is the name of both a dwarf and a giant, the latter of whom is the father of a girl Odin wants to seduce.
Transferred use of the surname Billson.
Means "crystal" in Turkish, ultimately from Persian بلور (bolur).
Derived from the Uzbek billur meaning "crystal".
Variant of Bilis influenced by the unrelated English name Billy.
Combination of Billy and Joe. It's feminine counterpart is Billiejo.
Tajik and Uzbek form of Bilal.
Ukrainian form of Snow White, from Ukrainian білий (bilyy) "white" and сніг (snih) "snow".
Chechen name of Turkic origin from Proto-Turkic *bạl meaning "honey" combined with *kɨ̄ŕ "girl, woman".
Alternate transcription of Urdu بلقیس (see Bilquis).
Transferred use of the surname Bilson. A famous bearer of the surname is American actress Rachel Bilson (1981-).
Variant of Biltrud. Biltrude was the wife of Grimoald, an 8th-century duke of Bavaria.
Circassian and Crimean form of Bilal.
Diminutive of names like Birgitta and Britt-Marie.
Means "make achieve, make succeed" in Shipibo.
Bengali, Assamese, Odia and Nepali form of Vimal.
Means "Milky Way" in Indonesian, from the name of the Hindu god Bhima and Sanskrit शक्ति (śakti) meaning "power".
From the Chinese 必 (bì) meaning "surely, most certainly" or 碧 (bì) meaning "jade, green, blue" and 梦 (mèng) meaning "dream".
From the Chinese 馝 (bì) meaning "fragrance" or 碧 (bì) meaning "green, blue" and 旻 (mín) meaning "heaven".
From Chinese 碧 (bì) meaning "jade, green, blue, cyan" combined with 明 (míng) meaning "bright, light, clear". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Means “two islands” in the Lucayan language of the Bahamas.
Means "one who is gorgeous and beautiful" in Yoruba.

Yiddish name derived from בין (bin) "bee", which was originally used as a translation of the Hebrew name Deborah, though it has since become associated with modern Hebrew בִּינָה (academic bînāh, otherwise biná) "understanding, insight; intelligence".Allegedly it is sometimes used as a Hebrew form of Sophia, and is also the Yiddish form of the Judeo-Spanish name Buena.
Means "violet flower" in Uzbek, from Persian بنفشه‎ (banafše). Also see Banafsheh.
From Arabic بن على (bin 'ali), meaning "son of Ali 1".
From the Shipibo bina meaning "wasp" and the genitive suffix -n.
From Sanskrit वीणापाणि (vīṇāpāṇi) meaning "lute-hand", derived from वीणा (vīṇā) meaning "lute" and पाणि (pāṇi) meaning "hand".
Meaning uncertain. This was the name of a 14th-century king of Champa.

Diminutive of Jakobina, Jakobine, Sabina, Sabine and sometimes Sabrina, as it contains the German diminutive suffix -chen. It is a homophone to the German word Bienchen, a diminutive of Biene "bee".This name is typically only used informally, meaning: it is rarely (if ever) used as an official name on birth certificates.
Transferred use of surname Bincley meaning "Binca's clearing".
Derives from Bindal an ethnic name. This Aboriginal people live in Burdakin Shire, Queensland.

Means "butterfly" from the word bindi-bindi in Nyungar, spoken in Western Australian near Perth.It could also mean "little girl" in other southern Australian languages.Bindi Cole (1975-) is a new media artist and writer while Bindi Sue Irwin is the daughter of Steve Irwin (1962-2006) known as "The Crocodile Hunter".Bindi is also the informal name of Soliva sessilis, a weedy plant known for its tiny sharp-needled seeds originate from Southern Australia.
Medieval name of unknown origin. It was very popular in Florence in the age of Dante Alighieri (late 13th - early 14th centuries). It is no more in use but it has originated the common surname Bindi.
Hindi feminine name meaning "who wears garlands of pearls".
Biblical boy's name meaning "Son of the Lord"
Diminutive of Bine 1, as it contains the Dutch diminutive suffix -ke.This name is rarely used as an official given name on birth certificates.
Diminutive of Bine 1 with the originally Spanish or Portuguese ending -eta.
Means "they have enlightened us" in Dagbani.
Either transferred use of the surname Bing or from a nickname, as was the case for American singer and actor Bing Crosby (1903-1977), who was originally called Bingo.
Reduplication of Chinese 冰 (bīng) meaning "ice". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

From Chinese 炳 (bǐng) meaning " bright, luminous, glorious" or 丙 (bǐng), refering to the third of the ten Heavenly Stems combined with 才 (cái) meaning "talent, ability". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From the Chinese 炳 (bǐng) meaning "bright, luminous, glorious" and 嫦 (cháng), from the name of a moon goddess.

This name can be combined with 冰 (bing) meaning "cold, ice", combined with and 春 (chun) meaning "season of springtime", or 纯 (chun) meaning "purity, pure, unmixed, skillful, genuine, simple, practiced". Other combinations are possible.
From the Chinese characters 炳 (bǐng) meaning "bright, luminous; glorious" and 娥 (é) meaning "be beautiful; good".
Coined by Sabino Arana Goiri and Koldo Elizalde as a Basque equivalent of Vicenta.
From the Chinese 冰 (bīng) meaning "ice" and 霏 (fēi) meaning "falling of snow and rain".
From the Chinese characters 冰 (bīng) meaning "ice; ice-cold" and 芬 (fēn) meaning "fragrance, aroma; perfume".
From Chinese 冰 (bīng) meaning "ice, cold" combined with 福 (fú) meaning "happiness, good fortune, blessing". Other character combinations are possible.
Transferred use of the surname Bingham.
From the Chinese 冰 (bīng) meaning "ice" and 寒 (hán) meaning "cold, wintry" or 菡 (hàn) meaning "bud".
From the Chinese 炳 (bǐng) meaning "bright, luminous, glorious" and 贺 (hè) meaning "congratulate, send present".
From the Chinese 炳 (bǐng) meaning "bright, luminous, glorious" and 虹 (hóng) meaning "rainbow" or 宏 (hóng) meaning "great, grand, vast".

column3: 炳华, 秉华, etc.(Chinese)|炳華, 秉華, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 炳 (bǐng) meaning "bright, luminous, glorious" or 秉 (bǐng) meaning "grasp, hold, preserve, persist" combined with 华 (huá) meaning "splendid, illustrious, flowery, Chinese". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
From the Chinese 炳 (bǐng) meaning "bright, luminous, glorious" and 寰 (huán) meaning "great domain, country, world".

column3: 炳辉, 秉辉, etc.(Chinese)|炳輝, 秉輝, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 炳 (bǐng) meaning "bright, luminous, glorious" or 秉 (bǐng) meaning "grasp, hold, preserve, persist" combined with 辉 (huī) meaning "brightness". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 冰娇, 冰嬌, 炳骄, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 冰 (bīng) meaning "ice" combined with 娇 (jiāo) meaning "tender, lovely, charming". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 冰洁, etc.(Chinese)|冰潔, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 冰 (bīng) meaning "ice" combined with 洁 (jié) meaning "clean, pure". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
From the Chinese 炳 (bǐng) meaning "bright, luminous, glorious" and 娟 (juān) meaning "beautiful, graceful".

column3: 炳军, 秉钧, 秉均, etc.(Chinese)|炳軍, 秉鈞, 秉均, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 炳 (bǐng) meaning "bright, luminous, glorious" or 秉 (bǐng) meaning "grasp, hold, preserve, persist" combined with 军 (jūn) meaning "army", 钧 (jūn) referring to an ancient unit of measurement (equivalent to about 15 kilograms) or 均 (jūn) meaning "equal, uniform, fair". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 炳焜, 炳昆, 炳锟, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From the Chinese 炳 (bǐng) meaning "bright, luminous, glorious" and 昆 (kūn) meaning "elder brother" or 锟 (kūn) meaning "ancient sword".
From the Chinese characters 冰 (bīng) meaning "ice; ice-cold" and 岚 (lán) meaning "mountain mist, mountain haze".
From the Chinese 炳 (bǐng) meaning "bright, luminous, glorious" and 丽 (lì) meaning "beautiful".
From the Chinese 炳 (bǐng) meaning "bright, luminous, glorious" and 莲 (lián) meaning "lotus, water lily".
This name can be made up of 冰 (bing) meaning "ice, cold" and 梁 (liang) meaning "beam, elevation, bridge, mast". Other character combinations are possible.

column3: 冰铃, 冰灵, 冰凌, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From 冰 (bing) meaning "ice, cold" combined with 灵 (ling) meaning "soul, spirit" or 铃 (ling) meaning "chime, bell". Other character combinations can be used.

column3: 冰柳, 冰榴, 冰瑠, 冰流, 冰刘, 冰六(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 冰 (bīng) meaning "ice" combined with 柳 (liǔ) meaning "willow", 榴 (liú) meaning "pomegranate", 瑠 (liú) meaning "lapis lazuli", 流 (liú) meaning "flow, stream, current", 刘 (liú) meaning "kill, destroy", or 六 (liù) meaning "six". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
From the Chinese 冰 (bīng) meaning "ice" and 鸾 (luán), a mythological bird.
From the Chinese 炳 (bǐng) meaning "bright, luminous, glorious" and 梅 (méi) meaning "plum".
From an alternative form of bing, suggesting a ringing sound. As an exclamation of surprise or sudden realization, bingo! is attested from 1923.
From the Chinese characters 炳 (bǐng) meaning "bright, luminous; glorious" and 倩 (qiàn) meaning "beautiful, lovely" or 茜 (qiàn) meaning "madder, reeds".
From the Chinese 炳 (bǐng) meaning "bright, luminous, glorious" and 琴 (qín), a type of Chinese lute.
From the Chinese 冰 (bīng) meaning "ice" or 炳 (bǐng) meaning "bright, luminous, glorious" and 泉 (quán) meaning "spring, fountain, wealth" or 权 (quán) meaning "power, right, authority".
From the Chinese characters 冰 (bīng) meaning "ice; ice-cold" and 娆 (ráo) meaning "graceful, charming".
From the Chinese 冰 (bīng) meaning "ice" and 仁 (rén) meaning "humaneness, benevolence, kindness".
From the Chinese 炳 (bǐng) meaning "bright, luminous, glorious" and 蓉 (róng) meaning "hibiscus".
From the Chinese 炳 (bǐng) meaning "bright, luminous, glorious" and 蕊 (ruǐ) meaning "flower buds, unopened flowers".
From the Chinese 炳 (bǐng) meaning "bright, luminous, glorious" and 生 (shēng) meaning "life".
From the Chinese 炳 (bǐng) meaning "bright, luminous, glorious" and 淑 (shū) meaning "kind and gentle".

Birkal is a beautiful, commanding imperative name formed by the Turkish numeral/adjective bir meaning "one", "unified", or "completely unique", and the verb stem kal meaning "to stay" or "remain". It translates literally to "Stay as One", "Remain Unique", or "Preserve Your Unity".Birkal is a deeply moving and spiritually profound name that carries the weight of a sacred, parental blessing. Historically used by parents as a heartfelt wish for their child to always remain true to their roots, uncorrupted by the world, and unique in their character. Symbolically, it praises an individual who serves as a great unifier—someone who brings people together, heals divisions, and stands as a solid pillar of loyalty, integrity, and timeless harmony. It represents a soul that is inherently complete within itself, a person who values deep bonds, and someone whose life is a beautiful testament to staying true to oneself. It is a powerful praise of strength, community spirit, and an unchanging inner purity.

German name of debated origin and meaning. Current theories include an old and obscure feminine form of Birk, which itself is an Alemannic short form of names containing the element Burk- (the name element being derived from Old High German burg "protection; shelter", compare Burkhard), an early 20th-century coinage based on Indogermanic bircha "glowing", an early 20th-century coinage based on Middle Low German berke "birch tree" and an early 20th-century coinage based on the modern German word Birke "birch tree" and thus making it a botanical word name.Whatever theory might be true, the general public usually considers Birke a word name nowadays.

The latter is perhaps in reference to disappearing snow (byrančiu sniegu, which literally means "crumbling snow") in weather that is too warm for snow to remain in. The second element of this name is either derived from Lithuanian mantus meaning "intelligent" (see Daumantas) or from Lithuanian manta meaning "property, estate" as well as "wealth, riches, fortune".
