column3: จันทร์เพ็ญ(Thai)
column12: Means "full moon" from Thai จันทร์ (chan) meaning "moon" and เพ็ญ (phen) meaning "full".
Means "upright, proper", from Sino-Vietnamese 真 (chân) meaning "true" and 方 (phương) meaning "square, upright".
From Thai ชาญ (chan) meaning "expert, skilled" and ศักดิ์ (sak) meaning "power".
From Sino-Korean 燦 "vivid, illuminating; bright" and 盛 "abundant, flourishing".
Unknown. Also a locality in Ghana
From Thai ชาญ (chan) meaning "expert, skilled" and สิทธิ์ (sit) meaning "right, authority, privilege".
From a combination of the present determiner form of verb 차다 (chada) meaning "to fill" and Sol.
From the Lao ຈັນ (chan) meaning "moon" and ໂສມ (som) meaning "form, appearance" or "pretty".
Possibly an invented name based on Chance and the popular suffix son. It coincides with the French word chanson ("song").
Most likely derived from French chanson meaning "song" combined with the feminine suffix etta. This name was borne by Chansonetta Stanley Emmons (1858-1937), an American photographer.
This is a feminine name of Thai origin. It means "moon water".
Possibly the feminine version of Channing combined with the name Tess.
From Lao ຈັນທະ (chantha) meaning "moon" and ບຸນ (boun) meaning "happiness, prosperity, goodness".

column3: ฉันทนา(Thai)|จันทนา(Thai)
column12: From Thai ฉันท์ (chǎn) meaning "satisfaction, pleasure, love".

column3: จันทร์ธารา(Thai)
column12: From Thai จันทร์ (chan) meaning "moon" and ธารา (thara) meaning "water, stream".
Etymology uncertain, perhaps from Lao ຈັນ (chan) meaning "moon" and ທີ (thi) meaning "time".
Means "the moon" in Thai (a poetic word), ultimately from Sanskrit चन्द्र (candra).
Chanthu means flower in Khmer and has been used to name 4 tropical cyclones
The name of the rooster in 'Chanticleer and the Fox' and 'Reynard,' medieval fables.

Derived from Nahuatl chantli "home" and the suffix -co, meaning "in the home" or "she makes the home". This was the name of an Aztec fire deity. While usually interpreted as female, several historical writings use ambiguous pronouns.
From the name of a town in France. The town's name is derived from the Gallo-Roman name Cantilius. It can also be given in reference to Chantilly lace, which is named after the town.
Variant of Chantrea. Meaning - moon, moonlight.

From an English surname, meaning "singer in a chantry chapel" or "one who lives by a chantry chapel", derived from Old French chanterie, which derives from French chanter "to sing". This name was used for the main character in the movie What if?, starring Daniel Radcliffe and Zoe Kazan, released in 2013.
From Sino-Korean 燦 (chan) "vivid, illuminating; bright" and 佑 (u) "help, protect, bless".
Alternate transcription of Thai ชาญวิทย์ (see Chanwit).
Alternate transcription of Thai ชาญวุฒิ (see Chanwut).
From Thai ชาญ (chan) meaning "expert, skilled" and วิทย์ (wit) meaning "knowledge, science".
From Sino-Korean 燦 "vivid, illuminating; bright" and 祐 "divine intervention, protection" or 玉 "jade, precious stone, gem" (u).
From the Chinese 澶 (chán) meaning "still water, tranquil" and 妩 (wǔ) meaning "charming, enchanting".
From Thai ชาญ (chan) meaning "expert, skilled" and วุฒิ (wut) meaning "prosperity, wisdom, knowledge".
From the Chinese 婵 (chán) meaning "beautiful, lovely, pretty" and 贤 (xián) meaning "virtuous, worthy, good".
Means "morality, ethics, good behaviour" in Thai, ultimately from Sanskrit चर्या (caryā).
Derived from the Chinese 婵 (chán) meaning "beautiful, graceful, lovely" and 烨 (yè) meaning "bright, glorious" or "firelight, flame".
From Sino-Korean 燦 (chan) "vivid, illuminating; bright" and 烈 (yeol) "fiery, violent, vehement, ardent". A famous bearer is South Korean singer Park Chan-yeol (1992-).

column3: 찬영(Korean Hangul)|撰英, 纂英, 粲英, 撰榮, 纂榮, 粲榮, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 撰 (chan) meaning "write, compose" or 纂 (chan) meaning "edit, compile" or 粲 (chan) meaning "bright, radiant" combined with 英 (yeong) meaning "flower, petal, brave, hero" or 榮 (yeong) meaning "glory, honour, flourish, prosper". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
Alternate transcription of Thai ชาญยุทธ (see Chanyut).

From 찬(chan) meaning "cold, filled" or 燦(chan) meaning "vivid, illuminating, bright" combined with 英(young) meaning "superior, hero, bloom" or 榮(young) meaning "glory, flourishing" or 瑛(young) meaning "crystal, luster of jade". Other hanja combinations can also form this name.
From the Chinese 婵 (chán) meaning "beautiful, lovely, pretty" and 玉 (yù) meaning "jade".
From the Chinese 婵 (chán) meaning "beautiful, graceful, lovely" and 媛 (yuán) meaning "beautiful woman".
From Thai ชาญ (chan) meaning "skilled, proficient" and ยุทธ (yut) meaning "war, battle".

Means "in the wilderness" or "among the trees" in the Lakota language, referring to someone at one with nature.A noted bearer is War Chief Crazy Horse (c.1840 - 1877), born Cha-o-ha, of the Oglala Lakota. He took up arms against the U.S. Federal government to fight against encroachments on the territories and way of life of the Lakota people, including leading a war party to victory at the Battle of the Little Bighorn in June 1876.
From 朝 (chāo) meaning "morning" and 鸿 (hóng) meaning "swan".

From Chinese 朝 (cháo) meaning "dynasty, imperial court, morning" combined with 晖 (huī) meaning "bright, light, radiant" or 辉 meaning (huī) meaning "brightness". Other hanzi combinations can form this name as well.
From the Chinese 朝 (cháo) meaning "dynasty, morning" and 玲 (líng) meaning "tinkling of jade".
From the Chinese 焯 (chāo) meaning "clear and thorough" and 露 (lù) meaning "dew".
Means “Emperor” and more literally “Great Lord”. It is very typically an honorific title for Shan Emperors, not a name.
From Chinese 朝 (cháo) meaning "towards, morning" combined with 美 (měi) meaning "beauty". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
From the Chinese 超 (chāo) meaning "jump over, surpass" and 囡 (nān) meaning "daughter".
From 超 (chāo) meaning "to jump, to leap over" and 攀 (pān) meaning "to climb upwards, to clamber".
From the Chinese 朝 (cháo) meaning "morning" and 晴 (qíng) meaning "fine weather".
From Chinese 超 (chāo) meaning "surpass, leap over" and 然 (rán) meaning "correct, right". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
From the verbal noun of verb 차오르다 (chaoreuda) meaning "to rise, fill up," effectively a combination of the stem of verb 차다 (chada) meaning "to fill" and verb 오르다 (oreuda) meaning "to go up."

From the English word meaning "gaping void," ultimately from the Greek khaos "abyss, that which gapes wide open, is vast and empty." In Hesiod's 'Theogeny,' Chaos is the primeval emptiness of the Universe, who gave birth to Gaea (Mother Earth), Tartarus (embodiment of the underworld), Eros (god of love), Erebus (embodiment of silence), and Nyx (embodiment of night).
From the Chinese 晁 (cháo) meaning "morning, dawn" and 珊 (shān) meaning "coral".
Wade Giles romanization of Zhaoxuan used in Taiwan.
Alternate transcription of Arabic شوقي (see Shawqi) chiefly used in North Africa.

column3: เชาว์วัฒน์(Thai)
column12: From Thai เชาว์ (chao) meaning "fast, quick-witted, intelligent" and วัฒน์ (wat) meaning "prosperity, culture, development".
From Chinese 朝 (cháo) meaning "court, government; dynasty; (v.) face, look; (prep.) to, towards" combined with 伟 (wěi) meaning "big, great, mighty". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 潮霞, 朝霞, 潮夏, 朝夏, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 潮 (cháo) meaning "tide, flow, damp" or 朝 (cháo) meaning "dynasty, imperial court" combined with or 霞 (xiá) meaning "rosy clouds, mist" or 夏 (xià) meaning "summer, great, grand". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
“Chao” (朝) typically means “morning” or “dynasty,” and “xiang” (香) means “fragrance” or “aroma.”

column3: 超阳, 朝阳, etc.(Chinese)|超陽, 朝陽, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 超 (chāo) meaning "surpass, leap over" or 朝 (cháo) meaning "imperial court, government, dynasty" combined with 阳 (yáng) meaning "light, sun, male". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
From 超 (chāo) meaning "to jump, to leap over" and 怡 (yí) meaning "cheerful, happy, joyous".
From Chinese 超 (chāo) meaning "surpass, leap over" combined with 英 (yīng) meaning "flower, petal". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
From the Chinese 焯 (chāo) meaning "clear and thorough" and 媛 (yuàn) meaning "beauty, beautiful woman".
From Sino-Vietnamese 執 (chấp) meaning "to manage, execute".
Means "of the road, of the journey" in Chewa.
Means "earth, dirt, belongs to earth" in Tumbuka, often given after other children in the family have died.

Transferred use of the surname Chapel and a "subordinate place of worship added to or forming part of a large church or cathedral, separately dedicated and devoted to special services," from Old French chapele (12c., Modern French chapelle), from Medieval Latin capella, cappella "chapel, sanctuary for relics," literally "little cape," diminutive of Late Latin cappa "cape."
Transferred use of the surname Chapin.
Either transferred use of the surname Chaplain or from the word chaplain.
Transferred use of the surname Chaplin.
Transferred use of the surname Chapman.
Derived from Nahuatl chapopotli, meaning "tar, asphalt".
Transferred use of the surname Chappell. A notable bearer is singer Chappell Roan (1998- ), born Kayleigh Rose Amstutz, who chose her stage name from her grandfather's surname.
Derived from chaqa meaning "brass or copper coin, money" or "child" and boy meaning "rich, wealthy".
Derived from chaqir- meaning "to call, summon, invite" and boy meaning "rich, wealthy".
Means "to be adept, quick" in Uzbek.
Short form of names beginning with Char, such as Charles or Charlotte.
Alternate transcription of شرف الدين (see Sharaf ad-Din) chiefly used in Morocco and Algeria.
Means lamp of the religion in Persian. The word "charaagh" means lamp and "deen" means religion.
Means "polished" or "polished, cut stone or gem" in Khmer.
From Sanskrit चरण (caraṇa) meaning "foot, pillar, support" and जिति (jiti) meaning "victory, conquering".
Alternate transcription of Punjabi Gurmukhi ਚਰਨਜੀਤ (see Charanjeet).

This name is most likely a form of Hariric - however, this is not completely certain. The first element in the name might also be derived from (or is a blend with) garva "ready, prepared", Gothic gairu "spear" or from Old High German wachar "vigilant." Chararic was a 5th-century king of the Salian Franks.
Alternate transcription of Thai จรัส (see Charat).
Name of a Scythian King meaning Black Horse.Scythian transcription of Siyavash
Charaton is the name of a Hunnic King ca 350 AD meaning Black Mantel
French form of the name Charaxus.

Possibly derived from Greek χάραξ (charax) meaning "vine prop, pointed stake, pole", as well as "bandage" and "bream (fish)". Alternatively, it could derive from χαράσσω (charasso) meaning "to sharpen; to engrave, carve, write". This was the name of one of the brothers of Sappho.
French and Portuguese transliteration of شربل‎ (see Sharbel).
Transferred use of the surname Charbonnel.
Charcandrick West- running back for the Kansas City Chiefs in the NFL.

Combination of any name starting with Char- (such as Charlotte and Charmaine) with a name ending in -cilia (such as Cecilia and Lucilia).A known bearer of this name is the American singer Freda Payne (b. 1942), who carries the name as a middle name.

Chardente Saya Ndoulou (also spelt Saya-Ndoulou) born 15 August 1990, is a Congolese women's footballer who played as a forward. Saya Ndoulou is from Zanaga, Republic of the Congo and is the sister of Congolese footballer Laure Koléla.
Transferred use of the surname of Chardin or Chardine.

After the village of Chardonnay, France, itself from Late Latin Cardonnacum, ultimately from Latin carduus "thistle". This is the name of a green-skinned grape variety used to make a white wine and, by extension, the name of the wines produced from them.
Alternate transcription of Arabic شرف الدين (see Sharaf ad-Din), used chiefly in Tunisia. Also see Charafeddine.
French form of Chariclea which was used on one of the titular characters of Henri Desmarets's opera Théagène et Chariclée (1695).
Latinized form of Charikles. This was the name of an Athenian politician who was part of the Thirty Tyrants.
Latinized form of Chariklo. It is the name of two nymphs in Greek mythology.

The first element of this name is either derived from Greek χαρά (chara) "happiness" or from Greek χάρις (charis) meaning "grace, kindness". The second element is derived from Greek δῆμος (demos) "the people"
Latinized form of Charidemos. This name was borne by a Greek mercenary leader from the 4th century BC, who was put to death by Darius III of Persia.
Alternate transcription of شريف (see Sharif), chiefly used in Northern Africa.
Derived from Ancient Greek χάρις (charis) meaning "grace, kindness" and κλέος (kleos) meaning "glory".

Derived from Greek χάρις (charis) meaning "grace, kindness" combined with either κλέος (kleos) meaning "glory" (compare Chariclea) or κλώθω (klotho) meaning "to spin, to twist by spinning". This was the name of two different nymphs in Greek mythology, one a close friend of the goddess Athena and mother of the blind seer Teiresias, the other a nymph of Mount Pelion and wife of the centaur Chiron.
Latinized form of Charilaos. This was the name of the Spartan king who embraced the Minoan legislation for Sparta in the 8th century BC.
Derived from Sanskrit चारिणी (charini) meaning "one who behaves", itself from चर्या (charya) meaning "behaviour, conduct".
A character in 'Pseudolus', a play by the ancient Roman playwright Titus Maccius Plautus, one of the earliest examples of Roman literature.
Chariomerus is the last recorded chieftain of the Germanic Cherusci tribe.
Diminutive of Zacharias and names containing the Greek element χάρις (charis) meaning "grace, kindness".
Latinized form of Charisandros. This name was borne by an archon of Athens.
Derived from Ancient Greek χάρις (charis) meaning "grace, kindness, beauty" and ἀνδρός (andros) meaning "of a man".
Derived from Greek χάρις (charis) meaning "grace, kindness".
Variant of Charity. Notable bearer is Charitie Lees Smith, a hymn-writer in the 19th century.

Latinized form of Charitine. Saint Charitina of Amisus (also known as Charitina of Rome) was a virgin martyr from Asia Minor, distinguished by strict chastity and piety, while Charitina of Lithuania (died 1281) is a saint in the Eastern Orthodox Church.

Derived from Greek χαρις (charis) meaning "grace, kindness". This name can be viewed as a feminine equivalent of Chariton. This was the name of an early Christian martyr from Amisus, a city in Pontus in modern-day Turkey, also known as Saint Charitina.

Frankish form of Hariulf. Also compare the similar-looking names Garulf and Gerulf, which can easily get confused with this name and vice versa.This name was borne by a 6th-century Frankish nobleman as well as by an obscure saint, who was one of the disciples of the Frankish missionary and saint Marculf (c. 490-558). The disciple in question is better known under the French names Cariulphe and Criou.

Chariveus was a Merovingian-era nobleman who served as Count of Laon in the late 7th century, living from approximately 660 to 692 AD. He is recognized in genealogy as the husband of Saint Irmina of Oeren and the maternal grandfather of Charlemagne's mother, Bertrada of Laon.

The first element of this name is derived from either the Greek noun χαρά (chara) meaning "joy, delight, happiness" or the Greek noun χάρις (charis) meaning "grace, kindness" (see Chares). The second element consists of Greek ξένος (xenos) meaning "foreign, strange" as well as "foreigner, guest".
Means "conduct, behaviour, morals" in Thai, ultimately from Sanskrit चर्या (carya).
Gallo and Afrikaans form of Charles.
French form of Charalampos via Charalampus.
Rare variant of Charlene and Charlaine.
Combination of Charlene and the popular suffix andra.
Variant of Charlaine.A notable bearer is the actress Charlayne Woodard.
Cotentinais Norman, Gallo, Walloon and Afrikaans form of Charles.
Either a variant of Charlie or an elaboration of Charla.
Most likely a variant of Charlemagne in the style of Charmaine.
Variant form of Charlie or Charlene/Charlyn (See also Carlin/Carlen). While a feminine name in other countries, in Brazil, it's exclusively masculine.
Feminine form of Charles, possibly via Charlet.

column5: shahr-LEES(African American, American English)|shahr-LEEZ(African American, American English)

column12: A combination of Charles and John.
Transferred use of the surname Charleson.
Combination of Charles and the ending -tavious.
Rare feminine form of Charles or Charleston
Transferred use of the surname Charleston.
French feminine diminutive of Charles, as it contains the French feminine diminutive suffix -ette.
An elaboration of Charlie and Charla in the style of Julia.
Elaboration of Charlia (a double elaboration of Charla) or a blend of Charline and Juliana.
Combination of Charlotte/Charlene with the suffix -icia found in Alicia and Felicia.
Dutch and Flemish form of Charline.
Variant of Charlize, influenced by Liese.
Feminine elaboration of Charles using Lisha. See also Charlesia.
Combination of Charles and the feminine suffix -issa.
Presumably, an elaboration of Charlize. (See also Charlisa).
Gallo form of Charlotte and Walloon variant of Tchårlote.
Gallo form and Swedish, Norwegian and German variant of Charlotte reflecting the French pronunciation as well as an English variant of this name.

It may perhaps be a diminutive form of Charlotte that spun off as an independent name or an attempt to feminize Charles.It appears to be in common use in the American South in the late 19th-century up until the early 20th-century.
Transferred use of the surname Charlson.
Variant of Charlyn, which is a variant of Charlene using the popular name element lyn.

From the English word charm meaning "the power or quality of giving delight or arousing admiration". This name was used by Australian Olympic swimmer and YouTuber Justin Norris for his daughter born 2019.
Variant of Charmaine in the style of Charlemagne.
Derived from either Ancient Greek χάρμα (charma) meaning "joy, delight" or the related χάρμη (charme) meaning "joy of battle, eagerness for combat" combined with ἀνδρός (andros) meaning "of a man".
Rare combination of the prefix char-, May and Anne 1 to make a variant of Charmaine
Derived from the English-speaking word charmer, which is a person with an attractive and engaging personality. Typically one who uses this to impress or manipulate others.
The meaning of Charmi is : Charming, Lovely, Lovely, a lovely girl

Aeolic and Doric Greek form of Charmides, because it contains ίδας (idas), which is the Aeolic and Doric Greek form of the patronymic suffix ἴδης (ides).In Greek mythology, this is the name of a distinguished Spartan. He was sent to the island of Crete by king Alcamenes, who wanted him to quell the civil unrest there.
Means "son of Charmos" in Greek, derived from the name Charmos combined with the patronymic suffix ἴδης (ides).This was the name of an Athenian statesman from the 5th century BC.
Appalachian, seen as a double name (Charmie Mae)
Used in the book 'Ella Enchanted', the character Prince Charmont. Formed from Prince Charming.
Derived from either the Greek noun χάρμα (charma) meaning "joy, delight" or the related Greek noun χάρμη (charme) meaning "joy of battle, eagerness for combat".
Latinized form of Charmos. A known bearer of this name was the Athenian polemarch Charmus of Kolyttus (6th century BC).
Derived from the English word charm.

column3: ชาญชัย, ชาญชาย(Thai)
column12: Alternate transcription of Thai ชาญชัย or ชาญชาย (see Chanchai).
Probably an invented name. Compare Charnette.
Presumably, an invented name similar to names like Charnette, Charmaine and Chanelle. It's most likely a variant of Sharnell or Charnele.
Alternate transcription of Thai ชาญณรงค์ (see Channarong).
Alternate transcription of Thai ชาญศักดิ์ (see Chansak).
Alternate transcription of Thai ชาญสิทธิ์ (see Chansit).
Alternate transcription of Thai ชาญวิทย์ (see Chanwit).
Alternate transcription of Thai ชาญวิทย์ (see Chanwit).
Alternate transcription of Thai ชาญวุฒิ (see Chanwut).
Means "to grow, to increase, to flourish, to prosper" in Thai.
From Thai เจริญ (charoen) meaning "to grow, to increase, to flourish, to prosper" and ชัย (chai) meaning "victory".

column3: เจริญรัศมี(Thai)
column12: From Thai เจริญ (charoen) meaning "prosper, grow, deevelop" and รัศมี (ratsami) meaning "ray of light".

column3: เจริญศักดิ์(Thai)
column12: From Thai เจริญ (charoen) meaning "prosper, flourish, grow" and ศักดิ์ (sak) meaning "power".
Variant of Cheryl with the spelling influenced by Carol 1.
Variant of Charlotte. May also be used as a phonetic variant of Sherylette.
Means "of Charon", using the Boeotian patronymic suffix ώνδας (ondas). This was the name of a celebrated lawgiver of Catania in Sicily.
Alternate transcription of Thai จรูญ (see Charun).

Probably derived from Greek χαρωπός (charopós) meaning "bright-eyed" or "fierce gaze", the second element being οψ (ops) meaning "face, eye". This was the name of an Amazon warrior in Ancient Greek mythology.
The name is associated with the Greek word charopos (χαρωπός), which generally means "bright-eyed," "joyous," or "gladsome,".
From an Uzbek word for a variety of dark grapes, often reffering to dark coloured eyes.
In French Charri is associated with “charm” and “grace”. Having French, English, Irish, and Greek origins
Meaning uncertain, most likely a variant of Charon, Karen 1, Caron and Sharon.
Form of Carshena used in the Vulgate (Latin Bible) as well as at least one English Bible: the Douay-Rheims Bible (1582-1610).

column3: ฉัตรชัย, ชาติชัย, ชาติชาย, ชาติชัย(Thai)
column12: Alternate transcription of Thai ฉัตรชัย, ชาติชัย, ชาติชาย or ชาติชัย (see Chatchai).
Means Beauty (One of the names shri ram) (Charuchandraji)
Feminine form of Charuhas or Charuhaas.
Hindi feminine name meaning "with beautiful hair".
Means "radiant, brilliant, prosperous, beautiful" in Thai.
Alternate transcription of Thai จารุณี (see Charuni).
From Thai จารุ (charu) meaning "beautiful, lovely" and เนตร (net) meaning "eyes".
Hindi feminine name meaning "with beautiful eyes".
Derived from Thai จารุ (charu) meaning "beautiful, lovely".

column3: จารุญลักษณ์(Thai)
column12: From Thai จารุ (charu) meaning "beautiful, lovely" and ลักษณ์ (lak) meaning "characteristics, appearance".
Alternate transcription of Thai จารุวรรณ (see Charuwan).
From Thai จารุ (charu) meaning "beautiful, lovely" and วรรณ (wan) meaning "colour, tint".
From Thai จารุ (charu) meaning "beautiful, lovely" and วัฒน์ (wat) meaning "prosperity, culture, development".
MEANING : One who speaks nicely or sweetly, a philosopher

Means "beautiful-bodied" in Sanskrit (from चारु (cāru) "beautiful, lovely" and अङ्ग (aṅga) "a limb of the body; the body"), a word used in the Shiva Purana to describe the goddess Kali (called 'Kālī of exquisite body (i.e., cārvaṅgī) and comely appearance').

Uncertain etymology, possibly derived in part from Ancient Greek ῥοῖβδος (rhoibdos) meaning "rushing noise, rushing motion". In Greek mythology, this was the name of a sea monster that resided on one side of a narrow strait, opposite to Scylla, sucking in and spitting out a massive whirlpool three times a day and consuming any ships that strayed too close. In some accounts she was a daughter of Gaia and either Pontus or Poseidon; in others she was simply a massive whirlpool.
Polish form of Charitina and Ukrainian variant transliteration of Харитина (see Kharitina).
Apparently a modern respelling of Jason via the nickname Chase, though it may also be transferred from the surname Chasen.
Combination of Chase with the popular suffix -ton.
From the Korean symbols "차" meaning "tea" and "승" meaning "win".
Possibly derived from Persian چشمه (češme) meaning "fountain, spring".

In Incan mythology, Ch'aska ("Venus") or Ch'aska Quyllur ("Venus star") was the goddess of dawn and twilight, the planet Venus, flowers, maidens, and sex. She protected virgin girls. This name is of a separate etmology, with the Quechua ch'aska referring to what they thought was the brightest star but was the planet Venus. The Quechue quyllur means 'star'.
Means "junior" or "firstborn son" in Dakota. See also Chaska.
Variant of Jasmine, possibly influenced by Chasity.
Romansh form of Caspar, traditionally found in the Engadine valley.
Romansh form of Caspar, traditionally found in Val Müstair.
A variant of Chasity possibly influenced by the spelling of Cassidy. Depending on pronunciation, it could also be used as a variant of Cassidy.

Possibly derived from a surname which was itself derived from Old French chastelain meaning "castle-keeper, castellan", either an occupational or status name for the governor or constable of a castle. This name was brought to some public attention in 2009 by Chastelyn Rodriguez, who was a contestant on the third season of the reality television series Nuestra Belleza Latina. She was born to Puerto Rican immigrants.
Transferred use of the surname Chasten.
Transferred use of the surname Chaston. May also be a variant of Chaseton.
From Sino-Vietnamese 質 (chất) meaning "substance, matter, quality".
F, Bajju name from nigeria; it means, love or like
From Japanese 茶 (cha) meaning "tea" combined with 太 (ta) meaning "thick, big". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Alternate transcription of Thai จุฑารัตน์ (see Chutharat).

column3: ฉัตรชัย, ชาติชัย, ชาติชาย, ชาติชัย(Thai)
column12: From Thai ฉัตร (chat) meaning "tiered umbrella, parasol" or ชาติ (chat) meaning "nation, country, life, birth" and ชัย (chai) meaning "victory" or ชาย (chai) meaning "man".
Alternate transcription of Thai ชัชวาลย์ (see Chatchawan).
Alternate transcription of Thai ชัชวาลย์ (see Chatchawan).
From Thai ชัชวาล (chatchawan) meaning "bright, brilliant".
Means "clear, explicit, easy to comprehend". From Thai ชัด (chat) meaning "sharp, concise" and เจน (chen) meaning "familiar, experienced, skilled".
From Thai ฉัตร (chat), the name of the constellation Ardra in Hindu astronomy, and ดาว (dao) meaning "star, celestial body".
Transferred use of the surname Chatham.
Means "clever, astute, skillful, nimble" in Sinhalese, ultimately from Sanskrit चतुर (chatura).
Means "chess (the game)" in Sinhala, ultimately from Sanskrit चतुरङ्ग (caturaṅga) literally meaning "(an army) consisting of four parts".
From Thai ชาติ (chat) meaning "nation, country" or "life, birth" and ชาย (chai) meaning "man".
From Sino-Vietnamese 質量 (chất lượng) meaning "quality", composed of 質 (chất) meaning "quality" and 量 (lượng) meaning "quantity".
Alternate transcription of Thai ชาตรี (see Chatri).
Romansh form of Katherine, traditionally found in the Engadine valley in southeast Switzerland.
From Thai ฉัตร (chat) meaning "tiered umbrella, parasol" and สุดา (suda) meaning "woman, lady, daughter".
Diminutive of Charlotte and sometimes Catherine, possibly because "chatty" rhymes with Cathy.
Alternate transcription of Thai จตุภัทร์ (see Chatuphat).
From Thai จตุ (chatu) meaning "four" and ภัทร (phat) meaning "good, prosperous, excellent".
Alternate transcription of Thai จตุพล (see Chatuphon).

column3: จตุพล, จตุพร(Thai)
column12: From Thai จตุ (chatu) meaning "four" and พล (phon) meaning "strength, power" or พร (phon) meaning "blessing". The spelling จตุพล is masculine while จตุพร is feminine.
Alternate transcription of Thai จตุพล (see Chatuphon).

column3: จตุพล, จตุพร(Thai)
column12: Alternate transcription of Thai จตุพล or จตุพร (see Chatuphon).
Alternate transcription of Thai จตุพร (see Chatuphon).
Alternate transcription of Sinhala චතුර (see Chathura).
Alternate transcription of Sinhala චතුරංග (see Chathuranga).

column3: จตุรงค์, จาตุรงค์(Thai)
column12: Means "four parts, four groups" in Thai, from Sanskrit चतुरङ्ग (caturaṅga). This is the Thai name for chaturanga, an ancient Indian strategy game similar to chess.

Means "(thing) which is known by four ears" (i.e., only two people), derived from an alternative form of Sanskrit चतुर् (catúr) meaning "four" and कर्ण (karna) meaning "ear" (also compare Karna). In the Hindu epic the Mahabharata this name is listed as belonging to an attendant of the god Skanda.
Transferred use of a surname which was a variant of Chatwin.
Means "Asia", from Sino-Vietnamese 洲 (châu) meaning "continent" and 亞 (Á) meaning "Asia".

Possibly means "praise Yahweh", derived from Hebrew שָׁבַח (shavaḥ) meaning "praise, commend" combined with יָהּ (yah) referring to the Hebrew God. This is the name of an angel belonging to the order of the Powers. He is one of the 72 angels bearing the explicit name of God (the Shem HaMephorash), as interpreted by some Christian Kabbalists.
Means "Europe", from Sino-Vietnamese 洲 (châu) meaning "continent" and 歐 (Âu) meaning "Europe".
Transferred use of the surname Chaucer.

Meaning uncertain. May derive from Nahuatl chahuatl "concubine" or chahuati "to be envious, jealous, suspicious", combined with yohua "to become night, to grow dark", or -yoh "made of, full of, with the quality of" and -huan "with, together with".
Short form of Chauncey or variant of Chance.
Probably a combination of Chanté with the suffix tasia (from names such as Anastasia or Fantasia).
Probably a variant of Chantelle. Notably used by Chauntelle DuPree, the lead guitarist of the American rock band Eisley.
Means "Africa", from Sino-Vietnamese 洲 (châu) meaning "continent" and 非 (Phi) meaning "Africa".
Variant of Charisse, this name is used for the deuteragonist of "Silver Sparrow" by Tayari Jones.
Chavah (Ha-va) is the Hebrew translation for the Biblical name Eve, which means "Mother of all living" or "Life". Eve was the first woman in the Bible, the wife of Adam.
Diminutive of Chava. Chavaleh is a song in the musical Fiddler on the Roof, sung by Tevye about his daughter Chava.
Alternate transcription of Thai ชวลิต (see Chawalit).

Means "lily" in Hebrew, presumably taken from the phrase חבצלת השרון (Chavatzelet HaSharon) "rose of Sharon" found in the Old Testament book the Song of Solomon. (In Israel, Solomon's "rose of Sharon" is popularly accepted to have been the sand lily, which grows in the Sharon plain in coastal sands, though technically the flower has not been identified.)
Name of Hebrew and Yiddish origin. In musical Fiddler On The Roof, used as alternative name for Chava. Meaning of Chava is "life" so Chaveleh must have a similar meaning.
Means "pleasant, beloved, darling" in Hebrew, making it a cognate of Habiba.
From Spanish chavo meaning ''boy, kid'', used as a nickname.
Means "prosperous, bright, shining, glorious" in Thai, ultimately from Sanskrit ज्वलित (jvalita).
From Thai ฉวี (chawi) meaning "complexion, skin" and วรรณ (wan) meaning "colour, tint".
Alternate transcription of Arabic شوقي (see Shawqi) chiefly used in North Africa.
From 차 meaning "beleza" "bondade" and and 雄 "male of species; hero; manly".

Derived from Guanche *ta-ahghər-ahəgh(i), meaning "she who sustains the firmament". This is the name of the mother goddess in Guanche mythology. After the conquest of the Canary Islands and their subsequent Christianization, Chaxiraxi became identified with the Virgin of Candelaria, an alleged appearance of the Virgin Mary on the island of Tenerife.

Diminutive of Charles. 'Appeared in 1975 when the British yachtsman Chay Blyth was receiving a great deal of publicity. Further used since then. In the case of Mr Blyth, the name is a pet form of Charles.'

Derived from the Russian noun чаяние (chayanie) meaning "expectation" as well as "hope, dream, aspiration", which is ultimately derived from the archaic Russian verb чаять (chayat') meaning "to expect, to hope".This name is also encountered as a Khakas, Tatar and Tuvan variant transcription of Çayan.
Feminine form of Chayan as well as a Tatar and Tuvan variant transcription of Çayana.

column5: shie-AN(Hispanic American)|cha-YAN(Hispanic American, Latin American Spanish)|sha-YAN(Brazilian Portuguese)
column12: Variant of Cheyenne. This name was popularized by Puerto Rican singer Chayanne (1968-) (real name Elmer Figueroa Arce).
From Sino-Korean 茶 (cha) meaning "tea" and 年 (yeon) meaning "year".

Diminutive of Chayo. In other words, this is a double diminutive of Rosario. A known bearer of this name was the Mexican-born American folk singer and actress María del Rosario "Chayito" Valdez (1945-2016).
Combination of Chay and the popular suffix -la in the style of Kayla and Jayla
Alternate transcription of Arabic شيماء (see Shaima) chiefly used in North Africa.
Alternate transcription of Arabic شيماء (see Shaima) chiefly used in North Africa.
Alternate transcription of Arabic شيماء (see Shaima) chiefly used in Morocco.
Means "siskin" in Quechua. A siskin is a type of bird in the finch family.
MEANING - "showing awe, showing respect"Origin - Sanskrit, Indian, Tamil, Telugu, Nepali, Sinhala, Sikh, Buddhist
From Guanche *ta-jiwəg-ah, meaning "flowering". This was the name of a goddess venerated in Tenerife.
This is the name of the 8th Watcher of the 20 leaders of the 200 fallen angels that are mentioned in an ancient work called The Book of Enoch. The name means "cloud of God".
Form of Chadwick with a "z" instead of a d.
Australian diminutive of Charlotte and Charles (compare Chazz and Chazzie).
Uncommon diminutive of Chaz, Charlie or Charles.
Variant of Trà, from a non-Sino-Vietnamese reading of Chinese 茶 (chè).
Means "born" in Khmer, ultimately from Sanskrit जात (jata).
Means "birth" in Khmer, ultimately from Sanskrit जात (jāta).
Italian feminine form of Checco and Venetian variant of Checa.

Diminutive of Francesco. One notable bearer was Checco Orsi who, together with his brother Ludovico, assassinated Girolamo Riario, Lord of Imola and Forlì, the last survivor of the Pazzi Conspiracy (15th century).
Of uncertain etymology. Name borne by a daughter of Genghis Khan and his first wife Börte.
Derived from Tuvan Чечен (Chechen) meaning "eloquent, elegant" or perhaps "Chechen (person)" combined with оол (ool) "son, boy".

Variant of Chad (chiefly used in the United States), a short form of names beginning with Ched- (e.g. Chedomir) or a diminutive of Charles paired with a middle name that starts with Ed- (e.g. Edward and Edwin) or D-.
From the English word cheddar meaning "deep hole or cavity", used for a type of cheese.
Variant transliteration of Чедо (see Čedo) as well as a short form of Chedomir.
Means "a handful of sheaves." He is a king of Elam in the book of Genesis.
Alternate transcription of Thai เจษฎา (see Chetsada).
Alternate transcription of Hebrew חדוה (see Hedva).
Chee means "Shine or Shining" in Hmong.

Short form of various names, chiefly Frank among men of Italian American descent (via Ciccio). In the case of American actor Cheech Marin, it comes from the Spanish word chicharrón meaning "fried pork rind".
From the English word cheer, referring to a feeling of happiness, or a shout of joy or encouragement. Ultimately derived via Old French chiere from Late Latin cara "head".

column3: จิรนันท์, จีรนันท์(Thai)
column12: Alternate transcription of Thai จิรนันท์ or จีรนันท์ (see Chiranan).

column12: Alternate transcription of Thai จิรนันท์ or จีรนันท์ (see Chiranan).

column12: Alternate transcription of Thai จิรวัฒน์ (see Chirawat).
Alternate transcription of Thai จิรวรรณ (see Chirawan).
Alternate transcription of Thai จิรวัฒน์ (see Chirawat).
Alternate transcription of Thai จิรวุฒิ (see Chirawut).
From the English word cheerful meaning "feeling or showing happiness".
The name of a humanoid cheetah in the animated television series ThunderCats (1985-1989). It is an elaboration of English cheetah, a word ultimately derived from Sanskrit.
From 志 which means willpower, ambition and 英 hero, excellence (Zhì Yīng / Chee-Yin).
Possibly a combination of Che and Gianna. This name is borne by a daughter of American poet and musician Gil Scott-Heron (1949-2011).
From Persian چهره (čehre) meaning "face, visage" combined with gul meaning "flower".
Variant form of Cheiene. Also compare Cheyanne.

Derived from Portuguese cheiene meaning "Cheyenne" (singular). So, in other words, you could say that this name is the Portuguese cognate of Cheyenne.With that said, the name Cheiene is pretty rare in Brazil, even more so when compared to its variants Chaiane and Chaiene, which are common there.
Western African and Maghrebi variant of Sheikh.
Feminine form of Sheikh (chiefly Algerian and Mauritanian).
Diminutive of Chaje and variant of Cheiche.
Variant transcription of Shaima chiefly used in North Africa.
Means "to weigh, to consider" or "to aim for, to aspire to" in Burmese.
Galician diminutive of Xosé and José by an elaboration of Che.

Latinized form of the Greek name Χειρίσοφος (Cheirisophos) meaning "skilled with the hands", or perhaps "cunning in his handicraft", derived from χείρ (cheir) meaning "hand" and σοφός (sophos) meaning "skilled, clever". This was the name of a Spartan general who participated in Cyrus the Younger's failed march against his brother Artaxerxes II in 401 BC.
Possibly derived from the Swahili verb -chekesha meaning "to joke, to kid, to make laugh" (the causative form of -cheka "to laugh").
Derived from chek meaning "end, limit" or "lot, potion" and Mirza or mirza meaning "scribe, scholar".

Short form of Michel (masculine) and Rachel (feminine). Also compare the related names Chiel and Sjel (both masculine).This name is unisex in Dutch, but strictly masculine in Limburgish.A known bearer of this name is the Limburgian singer-songwriter Michel "Chel" Savelkoul (1924-2003). He is considered to be among the five greatest and most influential artists of Limburg.
Greek form of Chilion, as it first appeared in the Septuagint.
He is mentioned in the Bible as being one of the sons of Pahath-Moab.
From the name of a lake and city in the American state of Washington, which is derived from the Salish Indian word Tsi-Laan meaning "deep water".
Combination of the prefix che and Layna.
Variant transcription of Heled.This transcription is used in the Orthodox Jewish Bible.
Variant of Celidoine, king of Scotland, son of the first Nascien and Flegentine, and ancestor of Lancelot and Galahad.
Derived from the Greek noun χελιδών (chelidon) meaning "swallow" (as in, the bird).This was the name of a Roman courtesan from the 1st century BC, who was a freedwoman by origin.
Italian name derived from the Greek word chelidon meaning "swallow". This name was borne by a 12th-century Italian saint.
Derived from the Greek adjective χελιδόνιος (chelidonios) meaning "of the swallow", which is ultimately derived from the Greek noun χελιδών (chelidon) meaning "swallow" (see Chelidon).
A variant of Chalice or Chelsea.Used in a book by Christian Fiction author, Ted Dekker and, is also the name of his daughter.
Likely an invented name, possibly a combination of Chelsea and Melissa or an elaborated variant of Chelise
Variant of Chelle. Chell is the name of the main protagonist in Valve game studio's 'Portal' video game series.
From Sanskrit ceta meaning "servant, slave (to God)".

Diminutive of feminine names that end in -chel (such as Rachel) and -chelle (such as Michelle and Rochelle). It is also possible that there are cases where this name is an alternate spelling of Shelley.A notable bearer of this name is the American politician Chellie Pingree (1955-), whose birth name is Rochelle Marie Johnson.
It's a variation of the name Chelsea.

Means "tortoise, sea turtle" in Ancient Greek. In Greek mythology, Chelone was a nymph who refused to attend the wedding of Hera and Zeus, telling the messenger god Hermes that she preferred her own home. Hermes then cursed her to carry her home with her everywhere, turning her into a tortoise.
Means "meadow" in Turkish, ultimately from Persian چمن‎ (čaman).
Son of Omni, Nephite record keeper.
Diminutive of Chema, which in turn is a diminutive of José María or José Manuel.
Variant transcription of شمس (see Shams), chiefly used in Northern Africa.
Alternate transcription of شمس الدين (see Shams ad-Din) chiefly used in Northern Africa.

Derives from the East African tribe, the Kalenjins. Like many other Kalenjin names, the first part of the name relates to the gender of the person and the second part is how, when, or where they were born. The 'Che' is feminine and '-mutai' means born near dawn.
From Chenab river in Pakistan. The name stands for "river in the moonlight". This name originated from old Indus civilization.
Likely derived from Chennai, an Indian city of 10 million.
From the Chinese 晨 (chén) meaning "early morning, daybreak" and 炳 (bǐng) meaning "bright, luminous, glorious".

column3: 晨晨, 辰辰, 宸宸, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From a repetition of Chinese 晨 (chén) meaning "early morning, daybreak" or 辰 (chén) meaning "early morning" and also referring to the fifth Earthly Branch (7 AM to 9 AM), which is itself associated with the dragon of the Chinese zodiac, or 宸 (chén) meaning "mansion palace". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From the Chinese 晨 (chén) meaning "early morning, daybreak" and 聪 (cōng) meaning "intelligent, clever, bright".
From Chenda and មណី (mony) meaning "precious stone, diamond".
From the Chinese 晨 (chén) meaning "early morning, daybreak" and 旦 (dàn) meaning "dawn, morning".
Norman English form of Cunobelinus or Cynbel.

Of unknown origin and meaning.The name was given to a boy in Düsseldorf, Germany, in 1998. The naming made public headlines because his mother wanted to register 12 names for her baby but a court cut the name list short. The Bundesverfassungsgericht (Constitutional Court of Germany) ruled that a restriction to 5 names does not violate the German constitutional rights. The courts did not issue any rulings on the selected names.

From the traditionally English surname, a variant of Chesney, or from the French habitational surname from a place in Yonne, derived from a Romano-Gallic estate, Caniacum, meaning "estate of a man named Canius".
From the Chinese 晨 (chén) meaning "early morning, daybreak" and 霏 (fēi) meaning "falling of snow and rain".

This name comes from the song “The Chenfeng Bird” (晨风) featured in the Classic of Poetry (诗经), a collection of poetic folk songs and hymns from the Zhou Dynasty (c. 1046 - 256 BCE). The song is a melancholy piece describing the feelings of a spurned lover. “Chenfeng” appears in the opening verse, and possibly refers to a sort of raptor, most likely a falcon.
From the Chinese 承 (chéng) meaning "bear, hold; inherit, receive; succeed" and 彪 (biāo) meaning "tiger".

column3: 程彬, 成斌, 承斌, 程斌, 晟斌, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From the Chinese 程 (chéng) meaning "journey" or 晟 (chéng) meaning "clear, bright; splendor, brightness" and 斌 (bīn) meaning "refined". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From the Chinese 程 (chéng) meaning "journey" or 晟 (chéng) meaning "clear, bright; splendor, brightness" and 博 (bó) meaning "rich, win, gain; play games; wide, plentiful" or 波 (bō) meaning "waves".

From the Chinese 承 (chéng) meaning "bear, hold; inherit, receive; succeed" or 晟 (chéng) meaning "clear, bright; splendor, brightness" and 才 (cái) meaning "ability, talent" or 财 (cái) meaning "wealth, riches".

From the Chinese 成 (chéng) meaning "become; succeed; completed, finished" or 承 (chéng) meaning "bear, hold; inherit, receive; succeed"and 焯 (chāo) meaning "clear and thorough" or 超 (chāo) meaning "leap over, surpass".

column3: 成成, 诚诚, 承承, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From a repetition of Chinese 成 (chéng) meaning "completed, finished, succeeded", 诚 (chéng) meaning "sincere, honest, true" or 承 (chéng) meaning "inherit". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From the Chinese 晟 (chéng) meaning "clear, bright; splendor, brightness" and 聪 (cōng) meaning "intelligent, clever, bright".
From the Chinese 承 (chéng) meaning "bear, hold; inherit, receive; succeed" and 德 (dé) meaning "heart, mind, morals, virtue, ethics".
From the Chinese 程 (chéng) meaning "journey" and 迪 (dí) meaning "enlighten, advance, progress".
From the Chinese 程 (chéng) meaning "journey" and 冬 (dōng) meaning "winter" or 东 (dōng) meaning "east".

From Chinese 承 (chéng) meaning "inherit" combined with 恩 (ēn) meaning "kindness, mercy, charity". Other hanzi combinations are possible. A notable bearer was Ming dynasty novelist Wu Cheng'en (1500–1582), the author of Journey to the West.
From the Chinese 程 (chéng) meaning "journey" and 帆 (fān) meaning "sail, boat".
From the Chinese 程 (chéng) meaning "journey" and 方 (fāng) meaning "direction, power".
From the Chinese 成 (chéng) meaning "become; succeed; completed, finished" or 晟 (chéng) meaning "clear, bright; splendor, brightness" and 富 (fù) meaning "abundant; rich, wealthy".

column3: 成钢, 承罡, 程钢(Chinese)
column12: From the Chinese 成 (chéng) meaning "become; succeed; completed, finished", 承 (chéng) meaning "bear, hold; inherit, receive; succeed" or 程 (chéng) meaning "journey" and 钢 (gāng) meaning "steel; hard, tough, strong" or 罡 (gāng), the name of certain stars, especially those in the handle of the Big Dipper.
From the Chinese 成 (chéng) meaning "become; succeed; completed, finished" and 功 (gōng) meaning "achievement, merit, good result".
From the Chinese 晟 (chéng) meaning "clear, bright; splendor, brightness" and 光 (guāng) meaning "light, brilliant, shine".

column3: 承翰, 诚汉, 成瀚, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 承 (chéng) meaning "inherit", 诚 (chéng) meaning "sincere, honest, true" or 成 (chéng) meaning "completed, finished, succeeded" combined with 翰 (hàn) meaning "brush, pen, writing", 汉 (hàn) meaning "Han, Chinese" or 瀚 (hàn) meaning "expansive, vast, wide". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 成皞, 成浩, 承颢, 程浩, 程皓, 程灏, 程颢, 晟浩, 晟豪(Chinese)
column12: From the Chinese 成 (chéng) meaning "become; succeed; completed, finished", 承 (chéng) meaning "bear, hold; inherit, receive; succeed", 程 (chéng) meaning "journey" or 晟 (chéng) meaning "clear, bright; splendor, brightness" and 皞 (hào) meaning "bright, brilliant", 浩 (hào) meaning "great, numerous, vast, abundant", 颢 (hào) meaning "luminous, white", 皓 (hào) meaning "bright, luminous, clear", 灏 (hào) meaning "large, vast, grand, expansive" or 豪 (háo) meaning "brave, heroic, chivalrous".
Circassian form of Genghis used in the past. Not seen for a long time.
From the Chinese 承 (chéng) meaning "bear, hold; inherit, receive; succeed" and 宏 (hóng) meaning "great, grand, magnificent; wide, vast" or 弘 (hóng) meaning "enlarge, expand; great".
From the Chinese 晟 (chéng) meaning "clear, bright; splendor, brightness" and 侯 (hóu) meaning "marquis, lord".

column3: 천사(Korean Hangul)|天使, 天師(Korean Hanja)
column12: From the Korean word 천사 (Cheon-Sa), which comes from Sino-Korean 天使. The character 天 (Cheon (천)) primarily means "Heaven" and by extension, "Sky," and the character 使 (Sa (사)) means "Messenger." The name means "Angel" or "God's Messenger," but can also be interpreted in a more literal sense as "Heavenly Messenger" or "Messenger of the Sky." There also is the alternate meaning, coming from Sino-Korean 天師, which means "Celestial Master (Leader of Zhengyi Dao)" in Taoism. This name can also be spelled with the Hanja 千 meaning "Thousand" or 川 meaning "River; Stream" for Cheon (천), and 史 meaning "History," 絲 meaning "Silk; Thread" and 賜 meaning "Gift" for Sa (천).
From the name of a biblical town, one of the four named in Joshua 9:17 along with Gibeon, Beeroth, and Kiriath-Jearim.

Cherith was a brook or wadi mentioned in the Old Testament. The prophet Elijah hid himself on the banks of the Cherith and was fed by ravens during the early part of the three years' drought which he announced to King Ahab.

Meaning and origin uncertain. It might possibly be an invented name, in which case it might (for example) consist of an Asian name element (such as Japanese chi meaning "wisdom, intellect") and the name Ana. Another possibility is that the name is of Italian origin, in which case it is probably derived from the name of the Chiana Valley in central Italy. The valley is known as Val di Chiana in Italian, which literally means "valley of the Chiana". The valley was named after the river that flows through it, namely the Chiani (sometimes also called Chiana). The river was known as Clanis in ancient Roman times: the name was a latinization of the original Etruscan name, as the river was located in what was once Etruria. It is uncertain what the river's name originally meant in the Etruscan language, although one source claims that the meaning is "standing pool". Also compare Chiara, but only for the fact that it is an example of how Latin Cl- became Chi- in Italian - which is what happened with the river's name as well, given how Clanis ultimately became Chiani.In popular culture, Chiana is the name of a female character from the Australian-American science fiction television series "Farscape" (1999-2003).

column12: From Japanese 智 (chi) meaning "intellect; knowledge; wisdom" or 千 (chi) meaning "1,000" combined with 津 (dzu), the joining form of 津 (tsu) meaning "harbor; port; haven, ferry; ford" or 鶴 (dzu), the joining form of 鶴 (tsu) meaning "gruidae" combined with 夫 (o) meaning "man, husband", 雄 (o) meaning "man, male, husband, large; powerful", 男 (o) meaning "man, male", or 生 (o), the root form of 生う (ou) meaning "to grow; to spring up".Other character combinations are possible.

From Sino-Vietnamese 佔 (chiếm) meaning "to seize, to usurp, overthrow".
Short form of Joachim, although there have been cases where it was a variant form of Chaim. A known bearer of this name is the Dutch actor and screenwriter Chiem van Houweninge (b. 1940).

column12: This is a name that is given among the Igbos usually it has a celebratory undertone to it. It is formed by joining two words "CHI-EMEELA" - "God thank you" Chi-God and Emeela-thank you/well done Usually it is given to baby boys when the parents are satisfied or do not wish to have more children, especially if the gender of the child was sought after.

column3: ちえみ(Japanese Hiragana)|チエミ(Japanese Katakana)|散笑, 知愛見, 智枝未, 茅江弥, 茅絵永, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

Wade-Giles romanization of Jianhong used in Taiwan.

column12: Wade-Giles romanization of Jianren used in Taiwan.
From Sino-Vietnamese 戰略 (chiến lược) meaning "strategy, strategic", composed of 戰 (chiến) meaning "to fight, war" and 略 (lược) meaning "plan, strategy, brief".
Alternate transcription of Jianxuan (using ad hoc romanization that does not belong to any standard system).
Means "to defeat, triumph, overcome", from Sino-Vietnamese 戰 (chiến) meaning "war, fight" and 勝 (thắng) meaning "victory".
From Sino-Vietnamese 戰術 (chiến thuật) meaning "tactic, tactical", composed of 戰 (chiến) meaning "to fight, war" and 術 (thuật) meaning "art, skill, technique".
From Sino-Vietnamese 戰場 (chiến trường) meaning "battlefield", composed of 戰 (chiến) meaning "to fight, war" and 場 (trường) meaning "place, area".
From Sino-Vietnamese 戰線 (chiến tuyến) meaning "battleline, battlefront", composed of 戰 (chiến) meaning "to fight, war" and 線 (tuyến) meaning "thread, line, ray".

column3: ちえり(Japanese Hiragana)|智愛莉, 千依里, 千瑛里, 千英莉, 千絵里, 千枝莉, 知衿, 知恵里, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 智 (chi) meaning "intellect, wisdom" and 衿 (eri) meaning "lapel, collar, neckband, nape". Other kanji combinations can be used.
From Sino-Vietnamese 照 (chiếu) meaning "to shine, illuminate", 詔 (chiếu) meaning "imperial decree", or 釗 (chiếu) meaning "to encourage".
Means "late afternoon, early evening" in Vietnamese.
From Sino-Vietnamese 照 (chiểu) meaning "shine, illuminate, reflect".
Means "Ruellia simplex (a flower)" in Vietnamese, from chiều meaning "evening" and tím meaning "purple".

Borrowing from French chiffon, from Middle French chiffe "cloth, old rag" from Old French chipe "rag", from Middle English chip, chippe "chip, shard, fragment" from Old English ċipp "chip, splinter, beam" from Proto-Germanic kippaz, kipaz (“log, beam”). Akin to Old Saxon kip "beam, post", Old High German kipfa "axle-rod, stave".

column3: 之鋒, 至鋒, 志豐, 智峯, 梓峰, 子豐, etc.(Chinese)
column12: Cantonese romanisation of Zhifeng or Zifeng.
From Japanese 千 (chi) meaning "thousand" and 冬 meaning (fuyu) "winter". Other kanji combinations can spell this name.

column3: 千賀, 市雅, 千雅, 智雅, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 千 (chi) meaning "thousand" combined with 賀 (ga) meaning "congratulate, greet, celebrate". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 千賀子, 智雅子, 稚芽子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 千 (chi) meaning "thousand", 賀 (ga) meaning "congratulate, greet, celebrate" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: ちがや(Japanese Hiragana)|茅, 千萱, 千賀耶, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 茅, 萱 (chigaya,gaya) meaning "miscanthus reed" or from 千 (chi) meaning "thousand", 賀 (ga) meaning "congratulations, joy" combined with 耶 (ya), an interjection, as well as other kanji or kanji combinations.
Igbo man and he is from Anambra state,Nigeria

column3: チギリ(Japanese Katakana)|ちぎり(Japanese Hiragana)|千桐, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 千 (chi) meaning "thousand" combined with 桐 (giri) meaning "paulownia tree". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Means "may God plead my case" in Igbo.

column3: 千種, 千草, 智草, 知草, 千久紗, 智久紗(Japanese Kanji)|ちぐ沙(Kanji/Hiragana)|ちぐさ(Japanese Hiragana)|チグサ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name can be used as 千種, 千草, 智草 or 知草 with 千 (sen, chi) meaning "thousand," 智 (chi) meaning "intellect, wisdom," 知 (chi, shi.raseru, shi.ru) meaning "know, wisdom," 種 (shu, -gusa, tane) meaning "class, kind, seed, species, variety" and 草 (sou, kusa, kusa-, -gusa) meaning "grass, herb, weed."Examples of Chigusa with 3 kanji include 千久紗 and 智久紗 with 久 (kyuu, ku, hisa.shii) meaning "long time" and 紗 (sa, sha, usuginu) meaning "gauze, gossamer."Chigusa can also be used by combining 2 phonetic characters (ちぐ) making up Chigu and 沙 (sa, sha, suna, yonageru) meaning "sand."As a word, Chigusa (千種 & 千草) refers to a great variety of flowering plants. Also, it's an abbreviation of 千草色 (chigusairo/ちぐさいろ) which resembles a light greenish-blue colour.Chigusa is also used as a surname.

column3: 茅波, 千羽, 千葉, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 茅 (chi) meaning "miscanthus reed" or 千 (chi) meaning "thousand" combined with 波 (ha) meaning "wave", 羽 (ha) meaning "plume, feather" or 葉 (ha) meaning "leaf, needle, blade (of a plant)". Other kanji combinations can be possible.

column3: チハギ(Japanese Katakana)|ちはぎ(Japanese Hiragana)|千萩, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 千 (chi) meaning "thousand" combined with 萩 (hagi) meaning "Japanese bush clover". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 千伯, 知白, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 千 (chi) meaning "thousand" or 知 (chi) meaning "wisdom" combined with 伯 (haku) meaning "eldest brother" or 白 (haku) meaning "white (colour)". Other kanji combinations are also possible.

column3: 茅華, 智華, 茅花, 千華, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 茅 (chi) meaning "miscanthus reed" combined with 華 (hana) meaning "flower". Other combinations of kanji characters can form this name.

column3: 千春子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|ちはるこ(Japanese Hiragana)|チハルコ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Chiharu combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child."This name is very rarely used.

column3: 千早, 千隼(Japanese Kanji)|ちはや(Japanese Hiragana)|チハヤ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name can be used to combine 千 (sen, chi) meaning "thousand" with 早 (sat', sou, sa-, haya, haya.i, haya.maru, haya.meru) meaning "early" (mainly feminine) or 隼 (shun, jun, hayabusa, haya) which refers to a falcon (especially the peregrine falcon) (mainly masculine).It has been seeing rather uncommon usage among both genders in recent decades.

Alternate transcription of شهاب الدين (see Shihab ad-Din), chiefly used in Tunisia.
Wade-Giles romanization of Zhihao used in Taiwan.
Wade-Giles romanization of Zhixiong used in Taiwan.

column3: 志宏, 志红, 智宏, 智弘, 治宏, 治洪, etc.(Chinese)|志宏, 志紅, 智宏, 智弘, 治宏, 治洪, etc.(Traditional Chinese)

column3: 千穂, 千帆, 千歩, 知保, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 千 (chi) meaning "thousand" or 知 (chi) meaning "knowledge, wisdom" combined with 保 (ho) meaning "to defend, to guard, to protect", 帆 (ho) meaning "sail" or 歩 (ho) meaning "advance, progress, walk, step". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 千穂子, 知穂子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 千 (chi) meaning "thousand", 穂 (ho) meaning "grain", and 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations can be used.

Probably derived from Nahuatl chihua "to do, to make" and the diminutive suffix -ton.

column3: 子雄, 志雄, 志鴻(Chinese)

column3: 志文, 智文, 芝文, etc.(Chinese)
column12: Wade-Giles romanization of Zhiwen used in Taiwan.
From Sino-Korean 値 (chi) meaning "value" and 孝 (hyo) meaning "filial piety".

ちいちろう(Japanese Hiragana)|チイチロウ(Japanese Katakana)|千壱郎, 智逸呂, 治市朗, 知一路, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 知 (chi) meaning "wisdom", 逸 (ichi) meaning "one" combined with 郎 (rou) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 千意子, 千映子, 千英子, 千恵子, 千重子, 千榮子, 知永子, 知重子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 千 (chi) meaning "thousand", 意 (i) meaning "mind, heart" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.

This name means " the close one "

column3: ちかげ(Japanese Hiragana)|愛華, 愛希, 千陰, 千加景, 薙景, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 愛 (chika) meaning "love, affection" combined with 華 (ge) meaning "flower". Other kanji combinations can also form this name.

column3: 親彦, 悠彦, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 親 (chika) meaning "parent, elder" or 悠 (chika) meaning "permanence" combined with 彦 (hiko) meaning "prince". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 愛救, 愛平, 悠平, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 愛 (chika) meaning "love, affection" or 悠 (chika) meaning "permanence" combined with 平 (hira) meaning "peace, flat, level, even" or 救 (hira) meaning "salvation, save, reclaim, help, rescue". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 親博, 親弘, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 親 (chika) meaning "parent, elder" or 悠 (chika) meaning "permanence" combined with 寛 (hiro) meaning "tolerant, generous", 裕 (hiro) meaning "abundant". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Chika can mean "amiable" and hisa can mean "long time ago, long lasting".

column3: 致佳人, 親人, 悠人, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 親 (chika) meaning "parent, elder" or 悠 (chika) meaning "permanence" combined with 人 (hito) meaning "person". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 愛輔, 皆誉, 知可星, 散夏秀, 智果浦, 千華宝, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 愛 (chika) meaning "affection, love" or 皆 (chika) meaning "pledge, vow" and 浦 (ho) meaning "bay, inlet" or 甫 (ho) meaning "beginning, for the first time". Other kanji combinations can be used.
Means "We’ve committed it to God" / "In God’s hands" in Igbo.
Means "God knows best" or "God is wisdom" in Igbo.

column3: 愛美, 及美, 京美, 近美, 周美, 慎美, 千賀美, 千頭, 地花実, 智加美, 智花美, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

Means "God is the best" in Igbo.

column3: ちかの(Japanese Hiragana)|千香乃, 千華乃, 千花乃, 千夏乃, 誓乃, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 愛 (chika) meaning "affection, love" or 誓 (chika) meaning "pledge, vow" combined with 乃 (no), a possessive particle. Other combinations of kanji characters can form this name.

column3: 周延, 史信, 近信, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 史 (chika) meaning "history" and 信 (nobu) meaning "trust, faith, believe". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 親典, 親則, 親範, 親憲, 親儀, 睦典, 睦則, 睦範, 睦憲, 睦儀, 愛典, 愛則, 愛範, 愛憲, 愛儀(Japanese Kanji)|ちかのり(Japanese Hiragana)|チカノリ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name combines 親 (shin, oya, oya-, shita.shii, shita.shimu, chika) meaning "parent, intimacy, relative, familiarity, dealer (of cards)", 睦 (boku, moku, mutsu.bu, mutsu.mu, chika) meaning "friendly, harmonious, intimate" or 愛 (ai, ito.shii, o.shimu, kana.shii, mana, me.deru, chika) meaning "affection, favourite, love" with 典 (ten, den, nori) meaning "ceremony, code, law, rule", 則 (soku, no'to.ru, noku) meaning "rule, follow, based on, model after", 範 (han, nori) meaning "pattern, example, model", 憲 (ken, nori) meaning "constitution, law" or 儀 (gi, nori) meaning "ceremony, rule, affair, case, a matter."This name is very rarely given to boys, if given at all.

column3: ちかお(Japanese Hiragana)|誓雄, 千佳央, 周男, 親夫, 千禾生, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: Japanese masculine given name derived from 誓 (chika) meaning "pledge, vow" or 親 (chika) meaning "parent, founder" and 雄 (o) meaning "man, manly". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Chikaou is an alternate spelling of Chikaō. Chi (ち) is "千", which means "thousand". Ka (か) is "佳", which means "excellent". Ou (おう) is "桜", which means "cherry blossom".
Means "bird" in Ainu. Chikap Kamuy is Ainu god "God of Birds".

column3: 千佳里, 知佳莉, 愛里, 愛理, 知華李, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|ちかり(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: From Japanese 千 (chi) meaning "thousand", 佳 (ka) meaning "beautiful, good" combined with 里 (ri) meaning "village". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 近, 親, 愛, 隣, 誓, 近志, 力士, 愛志, 誓志, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|ちかし(Japanese Hiragana)|チカシ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From classical adjective 近し/親し (chikashi) meaning "near, close; friendly, intimate," also written as 愛 meaning "beloved, dear(est)," 隣 meaning "neighbouring," both related to the aforementioned adjective, or 誓 meaning "oath, vow." These kanji, along with 力 meaning "strength, power," can be combined with a shi kanji, like 志 meaning "will, aim, goal" or 士 meaning "samurai."

column3: 千花俊, 愛利, 親利, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 愛 (chika) meaning "love, affection" or 悠 (chika) meaning "permanence" combined with 利 (toshi) meaning "benefit". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: ちかよ(Japanese Hiragana)|チカヨ(Japanese Katakana)|近蓉, 皆代, 哉與, 愼誉, 周詠, 悠葉, 尋依, 親夜, 慎余, 元容, 致香陽, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 愛 (chika) meaning "love, affection" or 誓 (chika) meaning "vow, pledge" combined with 世 (yo) meaning "world". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From 千 (chi) meaning "thousand" and 風 (kaze) meaning "wind". Other kanji combination can be used.

column3: 志強, 自強, 子強, etc.(Chinese)
column12: Cantonese romanisation of Zhiqiang or Ziqiang.
Means "may God grant our fair portion" in Igbo.

column3: ちこ(Japanese Hiragana)|チコ(Japanese Katakana)|千香, 智子, 知湖, 千己, 千胡, 稚恋, 緻琴, 茅仔, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 千 (chi) meaning "thousand", 智 (chi) meaning "wisdom, intellect" or 散 (chi) meaning "scatter" combined with 仔 (ko) meaning "offspring, fine, detailed", 呼 (ko) meaning "to call out, to invite" or 湖 (ko) meaning "lake". Other kanji combinations are also possible.
From Japanese 千 (chi) meaning "thousand" combined with 琴 (koto), which refers to a type of musical instrument similar to a harp. Other kanji combinations are possible.
Meaning unknown. This is the name of poet and writer Tikasuk Brown's mother.

column3: 其宽, etc.(Chinese)|其寬, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: Varient transcription of Qikuan (using Yale romanization).
Means "God agrees to life", taken from the Igbo phrase o buru na chukwu kwe ndu ga-adi "if god agrees there will be life".

column3: 志剛, 志光, 致光, etc.(Chinese)
column12: Cantonese romanisation of Zhigang or Zhiguang.
From Nahuatl chilcanauhtli "cinnamon teal (bird)", literally "chilli duck" due to its red colouring.

column3: ชิลชิตพยัค(Thai)

column12: Transferred use of the surname Childe. This name was borne by American painter Childe Hassam (1859-1935) who helped introduce impressionism to North America. His paintings often depicted urban scenes.
Variant of Hildebrand. Childebrand was an 8th-century Frankish duke, the son of Pepin of Herstal and brother of Charles Martel.
Italian, Spanish and Portuguese form of Childeric.
Danish, Dutch, Norwegian and Swedish form of Childeric. The name is only used in translations of historical documents.
Likely from the English vocabulary words child and love.
English translation of Latin Creatura Christi (see Creature), a name typically given to children expected to die during birth or immediately afterwards.

From Sino-Korean 七 "seven" and 炫 "shine, glitter; show off, flaunt".
Probably from Akilina which itself comes from Latin Aquilina "eagle".
Means "Float of fish net" in Mbunda.

Derived from Hebrew כִּלְיוֹן "failing, pining". In the Book of Ruth, Chilion is mentioned as the youngest son of Elimelech of the tribe of Judah and his wife Naomi 1. He married the Moabite convert Orpah.

Named for the spicy fruit from Central and South America used in cooking. The word is from the Nahuatl language. Has gained some interest in Australia since restaurateur Pete Evans chose this name for his eldest daughter around 2005.
Means "Place wear items are left to soak or be dyed" in Mbunda.
From Ancient Greek χεῖλος (kheîlos) meaning “lip”. This was the name of Chilon of Sparta, one of the Seven Sages of Greece.
Italian, Spanish and Portuguese form of Chilperic.
Dutch, Norwegian and Swedish form of Chilperic. The name is only used in translations of historical documents.
Possibly means "little chilli" in Nahuatl, or alternately, refers to a kind of small fly.
Means "northern cardinal" in Nahuatl, from chilli "chilli pepper" (figuratively "red") and tototl "bird".
Means "the one who is lost" in Bemba.
During the Edo Period, it was written with the kanji that modernly means "space time, leave".
Means “god has provided for me” in Igbo.
Derived from Nahuatl chimalli "shield" and ayahuitl "fog, mist, vapour".
Means "shield snake" or "rattlesnake, pit viper" in Nahuatl, derived from chimalli "shield" and cōātl "snake, serpent".
Possibly means "yellow shield" or "shield turned yellow", from Nahuatl chimalli "shield" and cozahui "to turn yellow".
Means "shield eagle" in Nahuatl, from chimalli "shield" and cuauhtli "eagle".

Possibly means "war shield" in Nahuatl, from chimalli "shield" and cuexyo, a specific war shield design. Alternatively, the second element could derive from cueyoni "to glow, to shine; to boil, to swarm".
Derived from Nahuatl chimalli "shield" and cuixin "kite (bird of prey)".
Probably derived from Nahuatl chimalli "shield" and ecatoco "to be pushed or carried away by the wind".

Chiminigagua was a universally good god and represented the only light that existed when it was night time. When the world was created there was only darkness and the only light was given by Chiminigagua. When Chiminigagua decided to shine light across the Universe, he first opened his gigantic belly from where light was shining. He then created two large black birds and launched them into space. The birds spread light from their beaks which produced light in the cosmos. Thus he created light and everything in the world. Chiminigagua showed the importance of his important gods Chía (the Moon), Sué (the Sun) and Cuchavira (rainbow). Adoring the Moon and the Sun for the Muisca was praising Chiminigagua. The creation of the Sun and Moon gave rise to mother goddess Bachué.The solar cult and belief in the supreme being is comparable to other indigenous peoples of the Americas and elsewhere in the world. Tezcatlipoca was a similar deity for the Aztec and Viracocha was his counterpart for the Incas. Solar cults and gods are found in other religions as well; Horus, Ra and Aton for the Egyptians, Mitra for the Persians, Shamash for the people in Mesopotamia, Helios for the Greeks and Surya in India. Quetzalcoatl and Huitzilopochtli represented the Sun for the Aztec and the Mayas praised Kinich Ahau, while the Incas believed Inti symbolised the Sun and created the Inca civilization.The most important sanctuaries established in pre-Columbian Colombia were erected in Sugamuxi, present-day Sogamoso, Guatavita, Bacatá (currently Colombian capital Bogotá) and Guachetá. Zaque Goranchacha constructed a temple in Hunza, today known as Tunja, and honouring him the people placed the Cojines del zaque ("Zaque Pillows"), two circular stones made of the same rock, there. Every day before sunrise the zaque with his priests and some of the indigenous people gathered and prayed the Sun would rise in the east. The ruler of the Muisca kneeled down on the Pillows and the people prayed, sang and danced. In some occasions there were human sacrifices where the hearts of twelve-year-old children were taken from their bodies and offered to the holy Sun.Sogamoso was considered a sacred city in the Eastern Ranges of the Colombian Andes and was known as the "City of the Sun", blessed by Bochica. It was here the pilgrims gathered to adore Chiminigagua. When the Spanish conquistadores led by Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada reached the area of the Muisca they were searching for gold and the legendary El Dorado. Their torches burnt the sacred Sun Temple, destroying one of the most elaborated religious works of the Muisca. The Sun Temple has been reconstructed in the Archeology Museum of Sogamoso, see image.Chiminigagua has been described at the end of the 16th century by the Spanish chroniclers Pedro Simón and Juan de Castellanos.The supreme being of the Muisca was a static deity without body who ruled over all the other gods. He was however never praised directly, yet through his lesser gods of the Sun, Moon and fertility; Chía, Sué and Chaquén. Chiminigagua's messenger god was Bochica. When the Spanish arrived in Muisca territory they were described as "children of the Sun".

column3: ちさ(Japanese Hiragana)|智佐, 千冴, 知冴, 知佐, 千佐, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 千 (chi) meaning "thousand" and 桜 (sa) meaning "cherry blossom". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 千紗惠, 千早恵, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 千 (chi) meaning "thousand", 紗 (sa) meaning "gauze, thin silk" or 早 (sa) meaning "already, now" combined with 惠, 恵 (e) meaning "favour, benefit". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: ちさき(Japanese Hiragana)|治咲季, 小桜季, 茅早季, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 治 (chi) meaning "cure, manage, govern, reign, administer, rule", 小 (chi) meaning "small, little", 茅 (chi) meaning "cogon grass (Imperata cylindrica), thatch" combined with 咲 (saki) meaning "blossom". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: ちさこ(Japanese Hiragana)|千紗子, 智佐子, 知佐子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 千 (chi) meaning "thousand", 紗 (sa) meaning "gauze, gossamer" and 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From 千 (chi) meaning "thousand" and 雨 (same) meaning "rain". Other kanji combinations are possible.
The singer Chisane Shiraishi is a notable bearer.

column3: ちさの(Japanese Hiragana)|千茶乃, 千佐乃, 愛咲乃, 知沙乃, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 千 (chi) meaning "thousand", 茶 (sa) meaning "tea" combined with 乃 (no), a possessive particle. Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.

column3: 千聖, 千里, 知里, 雅里(Japanese Kanji)|ちさと(Japanese Hiragana)|チサト(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From the Japanese kanji 千 (chi) meaning "thousand" or 雅 (chi) meaning "elegant" or 知 (chi) meaning "wisdom" combined with 聖 (sato) meaning "holy, sacred" or 里 (sato) meaning "village; hometown".Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: ちさよ(Japanese Hiragana)|チサヨ(Japanese Katakana)|千紗代, 千佐世, 知沙代, 智沙代, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 千 (chi) meaning "thousand", 紗 (sa) meaning "gauze, thin silk" combined with 代 (yo) meaning "generation". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 智世, 知世, 茅瀬, 千星(Japanese Kanji)|ちせ(Japanese Hiragana)|チセ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From the Japanese kanji 智 or 知 (chi) meaning "wisdom; knowledge" combined with 世 (se) meaning "epoch; generation". It can also derive from 茅 (chi) meaning "miscanthus reed" and 瀬 (se) meaning "current, rapids" or 千 (chi) meaning "thousand" with 星 (se) meaning "star".Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: ちせい(Japanese Hiragana)|チセイ(Japanese Katakana)|治声, 地成, 散世, 薙靖, 茅勢, 千生, 稚聖, 知星, 智性, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 千 (chi) meaning "thousand" and 星 (sei) meaning "dot, star". In vocabulary, 知性 (chisei) means "intelligence, intellect" and 治世 (chisei) means "regime, govern, rule". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 千世子, 千勢子, 千征子, 千成子, 千聖子, 知世子, 知是子, 智勢子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 千 (chi) meaning "thousand", 知 (chi) meaning "wisdom" or 智 (chi) meaning "knowledge, wisdom", 世 (se) meaning "generations", 勢 (se) meaning "forces, energy, military strength", 征 (se) meaning "to go on a long journey", 成 (se) meaning "to become", 聖 (se) meaning "holy, sacred" or 是 (se) meaning "justice, right" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.

The name Chishimba originates from the Bemba people of Zambia, a Bantu-speaking ethnic group. It holds cultural and linguistic significance in Zambia. The name derives from the Bemba language and carries meanings rooted in positivity and charm.Meaning:The name Chishimba means "charm" or "attraction" and signifies someone with a captivating and warm personality. It describes "a pleasing personality, manner, or appearance that makes someone captivating or enchanting to others." In some contexts, it is interpreted as a "gift from God" or a reflection of divine favor.It also reflects "the power of attraction or influence," meaning a special ability to win affection, admiration, or attention, often effortlessly. Chishimba embodies qualities such as kindness, grace, and beauty, and it is associated with individuals who bring light and positivity to those around them.

column3: 千尚, 知尚, 智将, 智昭, 智正, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column3: 千早, 智宗, 耻叟, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

From the Mao chisû meaning "wisdom" and zhü meaning "good".

column3: 千鈴, 千紗, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

Derived from Old Persian čiça "to shine, to appear" (equivalent to Avestan čiθra) combined with Old Persian farnah "glory, splendour, fortune".
Means "shadow, picture" in Tumbuka, often given after repeated deaths in the family.

From Japanese 千 (chi) meaning "thousand" combined with 棘 (toge) meaning "thorn".This is the name of Chitoge Kirisaki, a fictional character from the Japanese romantic comedy manga and anime series Nisekoi ニセコイ(English: Nisekoi: False Love) written and illustrated by Naoshi Komi.

Derived from Middle English chitte "a young animal, cub, whelp" and chit "a child or babe; a young, small, or insignificant person or animal" as well as "a pert or sassy young person, especially a young woman".

column3: ちとせ(Japanese Hiragana)|千歳, 千才, 千年, 千都世, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

From Sanskrit चित्र (citra) meaning "bright, clear, ornament, picture" and गुप्त (gupta) meaning "hidden, secret". This is the name of a Hindu god who maintains a record of each person's actions on Earth (all kept in a book called the Agrasandhanī). He is the registrar of Yama, the god of death, who uses his records to decide the fates of the deceased.

Means "decorated with brilliant bracelets" from Sanskrit चित्र (citra) meaning "bright, clear, excellent" and अङ्गद (aṅgada) meaning "bracelet worn on the upper arm, armband". In the Hindu epic the Mahabharata this is the name of a Chandravamsha (Lunar dynasty) king of Kuru and a son of Shantanu.

column3: 秩子, 智都子, 知豆子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column3: 千絃, 千鶴, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column3: 千畝(Japanese Kanji)|ちうね(Japanese Hiragana)|チウネ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 千 (chi) meaning "thousand" and 畝 (une) meaning "ridge in a field". A notable bearer of this name was the Japanese diplomat Chiune Sugihara (1900-1986), who helped thousands of Jews flee Europe during World War II. Other kanji combinations can also form this name.

column3: 千浦(Japanese Kanji)|ちうら(Japanese Hiragana)|チウラ(Japanese Katakana)

column3: 千和, 智和, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column3: ちわ子(Kanji/Hiragana)|千羽子, 千和子, 知和子, 智和子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column3: 千代恵, 千代枝, 千代江, 千代栄(Japanese Kanji)|ちよえ(Japanese Hiragana)|チヨエ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name combines 千 (sen, chi) meaning "thousand" and 代 (tai, dai, ka.eru, ka.waru, kawa.ru, -gawa.ri, -ga.wari, shiro, yo) meaning "age, change, charge, convert, fee, generation, period, rate, replace, substitute" with 恵 (e, kei, megu.mi, megu.mu) meaning "blessing, favour, grace, kindness", 枝 (shi, eda, e) meaning "bough, branch, twig, limb", 江 (kou, e) meaning "bay, creek, inlet" or 栄 (ei, you, e, saka.eru, ha.e, ha.eru, -ba.e) meaning "flourish, glory, honour, prosperity, splendour."This name was most commonly used from the Meiji Period (1868-1912) to the first half of the 20th century but nowadays, it's rarely given to girls, if given at all.

column3: 千世穂, 千代保, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 千 (chi) meaning "thousand", 代 (yo) meaning "generation" or 世 (yo) meaning "world" combined with 穂 (ho) meaning "grain" or 保 (ho) meaning "protect, maintain". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 千代丸, 智誉丸, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|ちよまる(Japanese Hiragana)|チヨマル(Japanese Katakana)
