Dain II Ironfoot was the Lord of the Iron Hills and King Under the Mountain in J.R.R. Tolkien's works. Tolkien derived it from Dáinn, the name of a dwarf in Norse mythology.

column3: 乃菜, 乃奈, 奈凪, 奈菜, 大尚, 泰那, 浩那, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 乃 (dai), a possessive particle combined with 菜 (na) meaning "vegetables, greens". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Short form of Veralidaine. The name of character in the The Immortals books series by Tamora Pierce.
Derived from the Lithuanian noun dainius meaning "poet" as well as "bard, singer", which is ultimately derived from the Lithuanian noun daina meaning "song" (see Daina).

Means "died" in Old Norse (the past participle of the verb deyja "to die"). This is the name of three characters in Norse mythology: a dwarf, a representative of the elves, and one of the stags that graze on the branches of Yggdrasill.

Means "desire for a song" (and thus refers to someone who either wishes to sing or desires to hear a song), derived from the Lithuanian noun daina meaning "song" (see Daina) combined with the Lithuanian noun noras meaning "wish, desire", which is ultimately derived from the Lithuanian verb norėti meaning "to wish, to want, to desire".

column3: 大之助, 台之助, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 大 (dai) meaning "big, great", 之 (no), a possessive marker, combined with 助 (suke) meaning "assistance". Other kanji combinations are possible.

Derived from Dainotis, which could be considered to be a diminutive of masculine names that start with Dain- (such as Dainius and Dainoras), because it contains the masculine suffix -otis, which is sometimes listed as a diminutive suffix and other times as a derivative suffix. Also compare Dainutis.
Likely transferred use of the surname Dainton.
Diminutive of feminine given names that start with Dain- (such as Dainė and Dainora), since this name contains the feminine diminutive suffix -utė.This name is not to be confused with Danutė.
Diminutive of masculine given names that start with Dain- (such as Dainius and Dainoras), since this name contains the masculine diminutive suffix -utis.
Dainya is thought to mean “Bravery” in Uzbek. But a submission from Jamaica claims it means “Thanks”. Dainya is a Aboriginal name.

Can mean "warlike, fiery" or "wise prudent", derived from Ancient Greek φρήν (phren) meaning "mind, heart, emotions" combined with either δάϊς (dais) meaning "war, battle" (perhaps related to δαίω (daio) "to burn") or a conjugated form of ἐδάην (edaen) meaning "to learn, to teach, to know". In Greek mythology, this was the name of two sons of King Aegyptus, both of whom married a Danaid (Adiante and Scaea respectively) and were killed by their new wife on their wedding night.

column3: 代泉, 代权, etc.(Chinese)|代權, etc.(Traditional Chinese)

column12: From the English word daiquiri for the alcoholic drink, which was taken from a Cuban place name.

column3: 大六, 大禄, 第六, 大禄, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 大 (dai) meaning "big, great" combined with 六 (roku) meaning "six". Other kanji combinations are possible.A famous bearer was Dairoku Harada, a Japanese archaeologist who studied in the Fukuoka area.
From Japanese 大 (dai) meaning "big, great" combined with 郎 (rou) meaning "son". Other combinations of kanji characters are also possible.

column3: 大作, 代作, 大左久, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 大 (dai) meaning "big, great, large" combined with 作 (saku) meaning "build, make, prepare, production". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Possibly meaning "ear of the chief", from Manchu ᡩᠠ (da) meaning "root, head, chief" and ᡧᠠᠨ (šan) meaning "ear". This was the name of the second son of Nurhaci.

The first element of this name is uncertain, as there are several possible etymologies for it. It could be derived from the Greek noun δάϊς (dais) meaning "war, battle", but it could also be derived from the Greek noun δαΐς (dais) meaning "torch" as well as "pinewood". Another option is the Greek noun δαίς (dais) meaning "meal, food" as well as "banquet, feast". The second element of this name is derived from the Greek noun ἀνήρ (aner) meaning "man".
Variant of Deja influenced by the phonetic elements day and sha.
From Japanese 大 meaning "large, great" and 師 meaning "master".

column3: だいしん(Japanese Hiragana)|ダイシン(Japanese Katakana)|乃伸, 第進, 台信, 代心, 題真, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 大 (dai) meaning "big, great" combined with 伸 (shin) meaning "lengthen". Other kanji combinations are possible.A famous bearer is Japanese baseball outfielder, Daishin Nakamura (1966-).

column3: 大志郎, 大四郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 大 (dai) meaning "big, large, great", 志 (shi) meaning "aspiration, determination", and 郎 (ro) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations can spell this name.
Possibly a combination of Daisy and Ana.
From the name Daisy, with the suffix -ann at the end.
Combination of Daisy and the popular suffix -lyn.
From Japanese 大 (dai) meaning "big, great" combined with 太 (ta) meaning "thick, big", as well as other kanji combinations having the same pronunciation.

column3: 醍太郎, 醍太朗, 大太郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
代太郎, 大太朗, 大太郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 代 (dai) meaning "era, age, decade" or 大 (dai) meaning "big, great", 太 (ta) meaning "thick, big" combined with 郎 (rou) meaning "son" or 朗 (rou) meaning "bright, clear". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Vietnamese form of Dashizhi, from Sino-Vietnamese 大勢至 (đại thế chí). This is the Vietnamese name for the bodhisattva Mahasthamaprapta.

column3: 大斗, 大翔, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 大 (dai) meaning "big, great" combined with 斗 (to), which refers to a Chinese constellation or 翔 (to) meaning "soar, fly". Other kanji combinations are also possible.
Alternate transcription of Sanskrit देव (see Deva).

column3: 大也, 大哉, 乃椰, 多衣耶, 輝, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|ダイヤ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 大 (dai) meaning "big, great" combined with 也 (ya) meaning "also". Other kanji combinations are possible.-------------------------------------From japanese katakana ダイヤ, meaning ''Diamond''.
Of uncertain origin, name borne by a consort of Nurhaci.

column3: 黛玉, 岱舆, 戴玉, 代玉, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 黛 (dài) meaning "a black pigment used by women in ancient times to paint their eyebrows" combined with 玉 (yù) meaning "jade". Other hanzi combinations are possible. Lin Daiyu (also spelled Lin Tai-yu, Chinese: 林黛玉; pinyin: Lín Dàiyù, rendered Black Jade in Chi-chen Wang's translation) is one of the principal characters of Cao Xueqin's classic 18th-century Chinese novel Dream of the Red Chamber.

column3: 大斬, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|だいざん(Japanese Hiragana)|ダイザン(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 大 (dai) meaning "big, strong, great" and 斬 (zan) meaning "slash, kill". It can also be composed of different kanji that have the same pronunciations.

column3: ダイゼン(Japanese Katakana)|大然, 大全, 大善, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 大 (dai) meaning "big, great, large" combined with 然 (zen) meaning "however, therefore, so" or 全 (zen) meaning "complete, whole". Other kanji combinations can be used.
From Chinese 代 (dài) meaning "generation, era" and 中 (zhōng) meaning "middle".

column3: 代传, etc.(Chinese)|代傳, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 代 (dài) meaning "generation, era" combined with 传 (zhuàn) meaning "biography". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: だいぞ(Japanese Hiragana)|ダイゾ(Japanese Katakana)|台象, 大三, 第造, 太蔵, 題雑, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 代 (dai) meaning "era, generation, decade and 雑 (zo) meaning "miscellaneous" or 像 (zo) meaning "vision, image, form of a thing." Other kanji combinations can be used.
Variant of Dasia or Deja. It's the name of one of the main characters in Tamora Pierce's Circle of Magic series.

Modern German name of disputed origin.Suggested theories include:1.) A phonetic spelling reflecting the English pronunciation of Diana.2.) A variant of Dayana.3.) A modern coinage based on Turkish dayanmak "to resist".4.) A modern coinage based on Arabic daya "foster mother; nurse".5.) A borrowing of the Croatian and Serbian name Dajana.The name has been used in Germany since the 1960s.
Originally a short form of names containing the element dag "day".
From Sino-Korean 多 "much, many; more than, over" and 貞 "virtuous, chaste, pure; loyal".
Combination of the names Da and Jian.

column3: 大金, 大锦, 大津, 大进, 达进, 达锦, etc.(Chinese)
column12: Combination of the names Da and Jin 1.

From Chinese 大 (dà) meaning "big, great, vast, high" combined with 靖 (jìng) meaning "calm, quiet, peaceful" or 经 (jīng) meaning "pass through, endure". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
From the Chinese 大 (dà) meaning "big, great" and 炯 (jiǒng) meaning "bright, brilliant, clear; hot".

Means "deceiver" in Arabic, a derivative of دَجَلَ (dajala) meaning "to deceive, to cheat". In Islamic eschatology this is the name of a figure who will appear before the Day of Judgment and falsely claim to be the Messiah and later, God. He is referred to in full as المسيح الدجال (al-Masīḥ ad-Dajjāl) meaning "the deceitful Messiah".
Combination of the prefix Da and John.
Variation of the words du jour.
Variant of Dejuan. It can be spelled Dajuan or with a capitalized third letter as DaJuan.
Combination of the prefix Da and the name Juwan.
Short form of Dakota. A notable bearer is Dallas Cowboy's quarterback Dak Prescott.
Meaning unknown. Jamamadí language is spoken in Acre and Amazonas State in Brazil.
From the Chinese 大 (dà) meaning "big, great" and 凯 (kǎi) meaning "triumphant; triumph, victory".

In the Marvel comics universe, Daken is the son of Wolverine and his wife Itsu. Logan thought he died in womb when Itsu was attacked one night while he was away, but he is removed and secretly left in the care of a local Japanese couple. While they name him Akihiro, he is called Daken (駄犬) by others, meaning "bastard dog" or "mongrel", in reference to his mixed race. Eventually he is taken by the villain Romulus and adopts Daken as his name.
Likely an invented name, possibly an elaboration of Dakota or Kenna
Means "to enter, to sieze" or "foreign, exotic; foreigner, stranger" in Arabic.
This name is a masculine version of the korean female name Dahyun, or Da-hyeon.
Transferred use of the surname Dakin, a pet form of the English surname Day, itself derived from a pet form of David.
An invented name of unknown origin. This name is borne by American football player, Dakorien Moore.
From Tibetan གྲགས་པ (grags-pa) meaning "renown, fame, honour".
Means "daughter of Daksha" in Sanskrit. This is another name of the Hindu goddess Sati.
The most able on this earth, goddess DurgaSanskrit origin- Daksh+Ira
Derived from the Korean word for "moon".
This name is of Somali origin and means "guide" or "leader." It often carries a sense of someone who leads others in a positive or wise way.

column3: Далан(Yakut)|达兰, 达岚, 大兰, 大岚, etc.(Chinese)

column12: From the Chinese 大 (dà) meaning "big, great" and 朗 (lǎng) meaning "clear, bright, distinct".
Means "green, verdant, young" or "vegetation" in Armenian.
Meaning uncertain, perhaps an elaboration of Dalia 1. This was used by Mexican-American singer Larry Hernandez for his second daughter born 2013. His other daughters are named Daleyza and Dalett.
Meaning uncertain, however likely derives in part from the element ດາລາ (dà:lá "star").
From the name of the city in Vietnam, Đà Lạt.
From Tuvan далай (dalay) meaning "sea, ocean" and кыс (kys) meaning "girl, daughter".
From Tuvan далай (dalay) meaning "sea, ocean" and оол (ool) meaning "son, boy".

Latinized form of the Germanic given name Talaberht or Dalabert, probably derived from bald "bold, brave" combined with either tal "valley, dale" or dal "bright, proud". Also compare the first element of Talbot "to destroy".
From an alternative Sakha word for "skylark".

Possibly derived from the Germanic name Dalbert, composed of dalaz "dale, valley" and berhtaz "bright". Alternatively, it could be a new combination taken directly from the Old Norse elements dalr "dale, valley" and bjartr "light, shining".
From native Korean 달빛 (dalbit) meaning "moonlight," from a combination of 달 (dal) meaning "moon" and Bit.
Means "satellite" from 달 (dal, “moon”) combined with 별 (byeol, “star”).
Combination of the Old Norse name elements dalr "dale, valley" and dís "goddess; woman, lady; sister" or dis "wise woman, seeress; woman, virgin".
Slavic masculine name, composed of the name elements dalĭ "far, distant; to move away" and borti "fight, battle".
Feminine variant of Daley and diminutive of Darlene.
From Chinese 大 (dà) meaning "big" combined with 雷 (léi) meaning "thunder". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Short form of Magdalena or a variant of Delina. Apparently this is also used as a feminine elaboration of Dale.
From the name of the fourth letter in the Hebrew alphabet ד

Meaning uncertain, perhaps an elaboration of Dalia 1. This was used by Mexican-American singer Larry Hernandez for his third and youngest daughter born 2020. His other daughters are named Daleyza and Dalary.
An old Polish masculine name, composed of two parts: Dale- "far away", and -win, meaning "uncle". Therefore it means "one whose uncle is far away", "one whose mother's family is far away".
Combination of the Old Norse name elements dalr "dale, valley" and ey "island; flat land along a coast" or ey "good fortune".

Dalga is a name embodying the relentless, rhythmic energy of the ocean. It evolves from the archaic talkaġ or talkan, meaning "ripple" or "wave." This traces back to the Middle Turkic verb talka- ("to ripple, to churn"), which finds its origin in the Old Turkic tal- ("to strike," "to whip"). Like a wave that strikes the shore and returns to the sea, this name symbolizes constant movement, power, and the cyclical nature of life.
Transferred use of the surname Dalgliesh.

column3: დალი(Georgian)|大力, 达理, etc.(Chinese)|ဒါလီ(Burmese)
column12: Diminutive of Dalia 1 and variant of Dolly.
Portuguese, Hungarian, and Slovak form of Dahlia.

Meaning uncertain. This name might be a masculinization of Dalia 1 or Dahlia, but it could also be a combination of Dale with either Ian or the English suffix -ian, which is ultimately derived from the Latin suffix -ianus.A known bearer of this name was the English soccer player Dalian Atkinson (1968-2016).
Elaboration of Dalia 1 using the popular name suffix -ana.

column5: D EY L IY AH N AH S
column12: Derived from the Greek name 'dalianis' meaning "strong" or "valiant"

A good knight and friend of Gawaine.Galahad and Yvain the Bastard lodged at his father’s house during the Grail Quest. Dalides arrogantly and rashly attacked Galahad and was defeated. In shame, he killed himself with his own sword, prompting his father to likewise commit suicide.His body was taken to the Strange Castle, owned by Dalides’ paramour. Gawaine, learning of the incident, tried to take revenge on Galahad, but failed.
In the Septuagint, this name is used instead of Eliel in chapter 11 of 1 Chronicles.
Possibly a masculine form of Dalila, popular in Mozambique.
Means "new praise", deriving from the Akkadian elements dalīlu ("praise, thanks") and eššu ("new, modern").
Slovak form of Dalimir. A known bearer of this name is Dalimír Jančovič, a Slovakian professional ice hockey player.
Derived from Slavic dal "far away" combined with Slavic mir "peace".
Chinese form of Darin or a combination of the names Da and Lin 1.
Variant of Delinda, particularly found in the Abruzzo region of Southern Italy.
Possibly a variant of Delicia via its other variant Delisha.
A variant of Dalitso.Daliso Chaponda is a Malawian comedian who came third on Britain's Got Talent in 2017.

Around the world, Dalissa is a rare primarily female, but very seldom masculine first name. The first name Dalissa is characteristic of the Dominican Republic, where it is a rare female name, the United States, where it is a very rare predominantly feminine, but very infrequently boy's name, and Brazil, where it is a very rare girly name.
Probably a variant form of Dalit. Also compare Dalida, which is a similar but unrelated name.A known bearer of this name is the Armenian singer Dalita Avanesian (b. 1999).
Masculine form of Dalia 2. A known bearer of this name is the Lithuanian career diplomat Dalius Čekuolis (b. 1959).
Named after Vladimir Dal (1801–1872), Russian lexicologist and ethnographer.
Walloon borrowing of Adalie and Odalie.
From Sanskrit दल (dala) meaning "division, portion, troops" combined with जिति (jiti) meaning "victory, conquering".
Alternate transcription of Punjabi Gurmukhi ਦਲਜੀਤ (see Daljeet).

A demon first mentioned by Joseph Gikatilla ben Abraham (1248-1305) in his book "Baraita de Massachet Gehinnom".According to him, Dalkiel is an angel of Hell, the ruler of Sheol, a place that is said to be four hundred twenty times hotter than fire. His task is to drive the souls of the damned to the seventh circle of Hell.
Old Norse name and byname, From Old Norse dálkr meaning "dagger, knife".
From either native Korean 달래 (dallae), referring to the Korean wild chive, or the root of verb 달래다 (dallaeda) meaning "to soothe, calm, comfort."

Means "little blind one", from Irish dall "blind" combined with a diminutive suffix. This was the nickname of an Irish poet saint of the 6th century, whose given name was Eochaid; he acquired the nickname after losing his eyesight, allegedly as a result of studying intensively.
The ancient wizard in The Chronicles of Prydain by Lloyd Alexander as well as a character in Disney's The Black Cauldron.
Possibly a variant of Darlene or Dalene.

Dallia is a common feminine name in Arabic (Arabic: داليا) and Hebrew (Hebrew: דַּלְיָה). The name in Arabic stems from the word for grape vine and in Hebrew from the word for "(tip of a) branch", especially that of a grapevine or an olive tree. Dalia is also said to mean "a strong branch.Dallia is mainly known of being a flower.
Diminutive of names beginning with the sound Dal-, such as Delilah and Dallas.
Combination of the Old Norse name elements dalr "dale, valley" and lilja "lily".
Transferred use of the surname Dallin. This name is prevalent to the Latter-day Saints in the US, where it is used in honour of Dallin H. Oaks (1932–).
Transferred use of the surname Dallon.
Short form of Dallas. Dallas 'Dally' Winston from the novel The Outsiders by S.E Hinton bears this name.
French and Provençal form of Dalmatius.
Spanish and Galician form of Dalmatius.
Derived from Albanian dalmat "Dalmatian (member of the people)", ultimately going back to the name of the Dalmatae, a group of Illyrian tribes in Dalmatia.
From Latin Dalmatia meaning "Dalmatian, of Dalmatia".
From Latin Dalmatius meaning "Dalmatian, of Dalmatia". This was the name of a 4th-century Roman emperor who was a nephew of Constantine. It was also borne by several early saints.
Catalan form of Dalmatius. The Blessed Dalmau Moner was 14th-century hermit from Santa Coloma de Farners.
In Korean mythology, she is the moon. She is the sister to the sun, Hae-nim.
Dalphon, meaning "to weep," was one of the ten sons of Haman, killed along with Haman by the Jews of Persia.
Derived from Old Norse dalr meaning "dale, valley" and rós meaning "rose".
Derived from the Old Norse elements dalr "dale, valley" and rún "secret lore, rune".
Transferred use of the surname Dalrymple.

Daluka is the name of legendary queen of Egypt who ruled before the Great Flood according to medieval Coptic and Islamic folklore. She was part of the so-called "Soleyman dynasty", which also included Surid Ibn Salhouk, a king who was once believed to have built the Great Pyramid of Giza. She was sometimes called Zulaikha.
Diminutive of Dahlia, not used as a given name in its own right.
Brazilian Portuguese form of Dalvin. Borrowed from English.
Transferred use of the Scottish surname Dalziel. As a given name it was borne by Dalziel Hammick (1887-1966), an English chemist.
From Sino-Vietnamese 談 (đàm) meaning "to talk, discuss".
From Sino-Vietnamese 潭 (đạm) meaning "deep pool, lake" or 淡 (đạm) meaning "light, pale".
From Sino-Vietnamese 擔 (đảm) meaning "to bear, to carry" or 膽 (đảm) meaning "courage, bravery, strength".
From Sino-Vietnamese 擔 (đam) meaning "to carry, to bear".
Means "son" in Bahnar. Like Rade Dam, this is used before the given name as a masculine marker.

column3: 담(Korean Hangul)|潭, 倓, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Means "man" in Rade. In ancient times, this was used in place of surnames in male names.
Probably a variant form of Damian.
Doric Greek form of Demandros, because it contains δᾶμος (damos), which is the Doric Greek form of δῆμος (demos) meaning "people" as well as "country, land".
From the Arabic surname الدمنهوري (al-Damanhūrī) borne by 18th-century Egyptian scholar and scientist Ahmad al-Damanhuri. The name indicates that he was from the Egyptian city of Damanhur.
Perhaps an invented rhyming variant of Amani using the popular prefix da-.
Combination of Daman 2 and Sanskrit जिति (jiti) "victory".
Combination of the prefix D' and the name Amante.
Means "resin, sap" or "resinous torch, lamp" in Indonesian and Javanese.
In Celtic mythology, Damara was a fertility goddess worshipped in Britain. She was associated with the month of May (Beltaine).
Combination of the popular prefix Da- and Amari.
Derived from Ancient Greek δῆμος (demos) meaning "the people" and ἄριστος (aristos) meaning "best, noblest".
Combination of the popular name prefix da and Marius, in a similar fashion to Damarion.
A magician killed by Betis. After this feat, Betis’s name was changed to Perceforest.
MEANING : a sort of drumOther Usage : Sanskrit, Indian, Tamil, Telugu, Nepali, Sinhala, Hindi, Sikh, Buddhist, Marathi
As a feminine name, it may be a variant of Damaris.
Catalan form of Damaskenos via it's Latinized form Damascenus.
French form of Damaskenos via it's Latinized form Damascenus.
Italian, Portuguese, and Spanish form of Damaskenos via it's Latinized form Damascenus.
Latinized form of Damaskenos. Used in honor of Saint John of Damascus.
Latinized form of Δαμάσκιος (Damaskiós), meaning "of Damascus", the now capital city of Syria. This was the name of the last of the Athenian Neoplatonists during the 4th Century.

Derived from Ancient Greek δαμάζω (damazo) meaning "to tame, subdue" (compare Damian, Damon). This was the name of a giant hero in Lydian myth whom the Greeks may have identified with Herakles. Damasen killed a dragon that had been ravaging the kingdom of Lydia in Anatolia.

Derived from Greek δαμασήνωρ (damasenor) meaning "man-slaying", which consists of δαμάζω (damazo) meaning "to tame, subdue, overpower, kill" (see Damasos) and ἀνήρ (aner) meaning "man".This name was borne by an ancient Greek tyrant of Miletus from the 6th century BC.

Derived from Greek δαμασίχθων (damasichthon) meaning "earth-subduer", which consists of δαμάζω (damazo) meaning "to tame, subdue, overpower, kill" (see Damasos) and χθών (chthon) meaning "ground, soil" as well as "earth, world".In Greek mythology, this was an epithet of the sea-god Poseidon. It was also the name of several other characters, among which was a king of Thebes.

Derived from the Greek adjective δαμάσιππος (damasippos) meaning "horse-taming", which consists of the Greek verb δαμάζω (damazo) meaning "to tame, subdue, overpower, kill" (see Damasos) and the Greek noun ἵππος (hippos) meaning "horse".
Latinized form of Damasippos. A known bearer of this name was the Roman commander Lucius Junius Brutus Damasippus (1st century BC).
Derived from Ancient Greek δάμασις (damasis) meaning "taming, subduing", itself from δαμάζω (damazo) "to tame".
Derived from Greek δαμάζω (damazo) meaning "to tame" and θυμός (thymos) meaning "soul, spirit", "desire", or "wrath, fury".
Russian and Ukrainian form of Damasos.
Transferred use of the surname Damask.
Means "Damascene, of or from Damascus" in Ancient Greek.
Hellenized form of Old Persian Jamaspi combined with the adjectival suffix -𐎹 (-ya).
Norman form and French variant of Damase.

Means "tamer", derived from Ancient Greek δαμάζω (damazo) meaning "to tame, subdue". This was the name of several figures in Greek mythology, including one of the Giants (or Gigantes) who fought in the Gigantomachy.
Doric Greek form of Demetrios (see Demetrius). Also compare Damater.This is also the name of the 10th month of the Boeotian calendar.
Archaic local name found in the Bourgogne-Franche-Comté region.
South Indian and Sinhala form of Damayanti.
MEANING : great noise, verbosity, beauty, entanglement, course
From a dam hanja, e.g. 潭 meaning "deep pool; marsh, puddle." and Korean 비 (bi) "rain".
A Zambian feminine name borne by the economist Dambisa Felicia Moyo.
Means "troublesome" in Tumbuka, often given to babies whose mothers were unwell during pregnancy.
From Tibetan དམ་ཆོས (dam-chos) meaning "noble doctrine, sacred teachings".
Alternate transcription of Tibetan དམ་ཆོས (see Damcho).
From རྟ་མགྲིན (rta mgrin) meaning "horse-necked", the Tibetan form of Sanskrit Hayagriva.
Derived from the given name Damdin, from Tibetan རྟ་མགྲིན (rta mgrin) meaning "horse-necked", and the Tibetan term ཚེ་རིང (tshe ring) meaning "long life, longevity".
Tibetan name for Hayagriva, derived from རྟ (rta) meaning "horse" and མགྲིན (mgrin) meaning "neck, throat; voice".
Variant of Demeas, using δᾶμος (damos), the Doric form of δῆμος (demos) meaning "the people".
Czech diminutive of Adam and Damián, not used as a given name in its own right.
A character from "The Immortals" series by Alyson Noel and the main character of "The Captive Prince" Trilogy by C. S. Pacat bear this name.

The first name of a son (Damerei Raleigh) born out of the secret marriage of Elizabeth Throckmorton, a maid-of-honor and later Gentlewoman of the Privy Chamber to Elizabeth I of England, and Sir Walter Raleigh. The name was claimed to be derived from the D'Amerie family, who Raleigh claimed to be descended from.

Means "great wife of the prince", deriving from the Sumerian elements dam, meaning "spouse, husband or wife", 𒃲 gal, meaning "great, mighty", and nun, meaning "prince, noble, master". The prince was understood to be her husband Ea.Her character is poorly understood, although she is known to have been associated with ritual purification. She was occasionally equated with the goddess Ninhursag, although generally they were distinguished from each other. She was later incorporated into the Hurrian pantheon, and was worshipped in the city of Hattusa. In later Akkadian sources she was known as Damkina.

column3: 담희(Korean Hangul)|澹熙, 澹希, 湛希, 湛熙, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Alternate transcription of Korean Hangul 담희 (See Dam-hui).

column3: 담희(Korean Hangul)|澹熙, 澹希, 湛希, 湛熙, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 澹 (dam) meaning "tranquil, calm, peaceful, quiet" or 湛 (dam) meaning "clear, pure, deep" combined with 熙 (hui) meaning "bright, splendid, glorious" or 希 (hui) meaning "hope, rare, precious". Other Hanja combinations are possible.

Possibly derived from Ancient Greek δᾶ (da) meaning "earth, land, ground" and μαῖα (maia) meaning "good mother, dame", a form of address for a woman older than the speaker. This was the name of the goddess and Hora of the fertile earth, worshipped alongside Auxesia. She may have also been worshipped as Carpo. It was also an epithet of the goddess Demeter (while her daughter, Persephone, was occasionally afforded the title Auxesia).
Hungarian form of Damiana. The name coincides with the name of the plant damiána "damiana, turnera diffusa".
Corsican, Sardinian and Sicilian form of Damian.
A character in the medieval Esmoreit story, a princess
The name Damil means "to honor" or "to (give) respect" ("giver of respect).
It derives from the slavic form of Damian, name that means "tamer" and the diminutive suffix -lka
Means "God makes me wealthy" in Yoruba.

column3: 다민(Korean Hangul)|多旻, 多旼, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Combination of a da hanja, e.g. 多 meaning "a lot, much," and a min hanja, such as 旻 meaning "sky" or 旼 meaning "mild, temperate; peaceful."
Invented name based on the sounds in Tymir.
Derived from Persian ضمیر (zamir) meaning "heart, mind, secret", though it may also be from Turkic *temür meaning "iron".
Combination of the phonetic element da and the name Miracle.

Derived from Ancient Greek δᾶμος (damos), a Doric form of δῆμος (demos) meaning "the people". This was the name of several historical figures, including an Assyrian disciple of Apollonius, a Messenian general, and an Athenian diplomat.

Means "little lady" from the Spanish word damita, which is a diminutive of dama "lady, dame" (ultimately from Latin domina). This name was popularized in the 1960s by the American singer Damita Jo DeBlanc (1930-1998). It is a middle name of American singer Janet Jackson (1966-), full name Janet Damita Jo Jackson.
Derived from Sanskrit दमित (damita) meaning "tamed, calmed, conquered, subdued".

Means "true wife", deriving from the Akkadian element kīnu "honest, trustworthy, faithful". The Akkadian name for the goddess Damgalnuna. She was the consort of Enki and mother of the god Marduk. One of her titles was 'banat shimti' meaning 'creator of fate', influenced by the goddess Shimti.
Alternate transcription of Sinhala ධම්මික (see Dhammika).
Variant of Dagmar traditionally found in Småland.
Used by English dramatist Richard Brome for a character in his play The Weeding of Covent Garden (performed ca. 1633, printed 1659), where it is a diminutive of Damaris.
Diminutive of If-Christ-had-not-died-for-thee-thou-hadst-been-damned. Meaning, "condemned by God to suffer eternal punishment in hell."

Means "dominator", derived from Ancient Greek δαμνάω (damnao) meaning "to overpower, tame, conquer, subdue" (a variant of damazo). In Greek mythology, this was the name of a daughter of king Belus of Egypt. It was also used as an epithet of the moon.
Variant of Δημοκράτεια (Demokrateia), the feminine form of Demokrates. Damocrateia was a daughter of Zeus and Aegina.
In Gallo-Roman religion, Damona was a goddess worshipped in Gaul as the consort of Apollo Borvo and of Apollo Moritasgus. Her name is likely derived from Old Irish dam "cow, ox".

Derived from δᾶμος (damos), the Doric Greek form of δῆμος (demos) meaning "the people", combined with either an abbreviated form of νίκη (nike) "victory" (see Demonike) or ὄνη (one) "help", from ὀνίνημι (oninemi) "to help, support, be useful; to delight, please". Damonno was a possibly legendary queen of Lydia married to King Cadys, who indirectly caused her husband’s death by murdering his doctor, exiled his twin brother Ardys, and installed her lover Spermes on the throne. It’s unknown what happened to her after that, though Spermes was killed two years later and Ardys returned to rule.
Combination of the prefix Da and the name Mont.
Variant of Demophilus, using the Doric form of δῆμος (demos).
Variant of Demophon. This name was borne by an ancient Greek sculptor from the 2nd century BC.
Derived from Ancient Greek δᾶμος (damos), a Doric Greek variant of δῆμος (demos) meaning "the people", and σθένος (sthenos) meaning "strength, vigour" (see Demosthenes).

Derived from δᾶμος (damos) meaning "the people", a Doric Greek variant of δῆμος (demos), and the Greek adjective θάλεια (thaleia) meaning "rich, plentiful" (from the verb θάλλω (thallo) meaning "to blossom").
Derived from δᾶμος (damos), the Doric Greek form of δῆμος (demos) meaning "the people", and τιμάω (timao) meaning "to honour".
Probably derived from Greek δῆμος (demos) meaning "the people" and τύχη (tyche) meaning "fortune, chance, fate".
Derived from the Doric Greek noun δᾶμος (damos) meaning "people" as well as "country, land" combined with Greek ξένος (xenos) meaning "foreign, strange" as well as "foreigner, guest".
Latinized form of Damoxenos. This name was borne by a Greek comic playwright from the 3rd or 4th century BC.
Means "good", deriving from the Akkadian element damqu ("good, pretty, nice").
Damrey means "elephant" in Khmer.Damrey has also been used to name 5 tropical cyclones.

Recorded in medieval Pomerania and Kashubia, this name is of uncertain origin and meaning. Theories include a Kashubian dialectical form of Dąbrówka. The name was borne by a semi-legendary princess of the Sobieslaw dynasty (13th-century).
Means "to maintain, to uphold, to sustain" in Thai.
From Thai ดำรง (damrong) meaning "maintain, uphold, sustain" and ชัย (chai) meaning "victory".
From Thai ดำรง (damrong) meaning "maintain, uphold, sustain" and เดช (det) meaning "power, might, authority".
From Thai ดำรง (damrong) meaning "maintain, uphold, sustain" and ฤทธิ์ (rit) meaning "power".

column3: ดำรงศักดิ์(Thai)
column12: From Thai ดำรง (damrong) meaning "maintain, uphold, sustain" and ศักดิ์ (sak) meaning "power, honour".
From Thai ดำรง (damrong) meaning "maintain, uphold, sustain" and วิทย์ (wit) meaning "knowledge, science".
From the word which refers to "damson" (prunus insititia), an edible plum-like fruit. Notable bearers are British actor Damson Idris, and fashion brand Damson Madder.
From Sino-Vietnamese 旦 (đán) meaning "morning, sun, day".
From Sino-Vietnamese 彈 (đàn) referring to various musical instruments, especially string instruments, or meaning "to play (an instrument)".
From Sino-Vietnamese 亶 (đản) meaning "sincere, truthful" or 憻 (đản) meaning "flat, level, open-hearted, honest".
From Sino-Vietnamese 民 (dân) meaning "people, citizens, nation".
From Sino-Vietnamese 寅 (dần) referring to the third Earthly Branch (3 AM to 5 AM), which is itself associated with the tiger of the Chinese zodiac.

column3: 단(Korean Hangul)|亶, 旦, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 亶 (dan) meaning “sincere, truthful” or 旦 (dan) meaning “early morning, dawn”, as well as other hanja characters that are pronounced in the same way.

column3: Дана(Russian, Ukrainian, Belarusian, Bulgarian, Serbian, Bosnian Cyrillic, Macedonian)|Дана(Croatian Cyrillic, Serbian, Bosnian Cyrillic, Montenegrin)|다나, 단아(Korean Hangul)|Дана(Ukrainian)
column12: Feminine short form of Danuta, Danisława, Bohdana and Danijela or Daniella and masculine short form of Danijel.
A vassal of Emperor Filimenis of Constantinople, father of Sir Floriant.
Czech, German, Italian and French form of Danaë.
From Kazakh дана (dana) meaning "wise, advisable" and гүл (gul) meaning "flower" (both of Persian origin).
Means "son" in Thai, ultimately from Sanskrit तनय (tanaya).

A knight and nephew of Sir Daras. He guarded Daras’s castle against interlopers. They lodged several renowned knights of Arthur’s court, including Lancelot, Palamedes, and Tristan. Danaim hated Lucan the Butler and challenged him twice, but Lucan was victorious on both occasions.
Feminine form of Danaus. This was the name of a naiad of a well or fountain in the region of Pisa in Elis, Greece. It may have also been the name of one of the fifty daughters of Danaus.

column3: ดนัยศักดิ์(Thai)
column12: From Thai ดนัย (danai) meaning "son" and ศักดิ์ (sak) meaning "power".
Croatian and Serbian form of Danaos (also see Danaus).
Croatian, Serbian and Slovene form of Danaë.
Worldwide, Dana-Jo is an extremely rare female given name. Parts of the name also exist independently as a first name Dana 2, and a first name Jo.
Derived from Javanese lanang meaning "man, boy, husband".
Alternate transcription of Sinhala ධනංජය (see Dhananjaya).
Means "fair, light (of one's complexion)" in Javanese.
Of unknown meaning. This was the name of Toghon Tëmur's first empress, who was of Kipchak origin.
Modern name, probably based on the sounds found in other names such as Deja, Danae 2 and Denisha.
Coptic Christian (Ge'ez) word for the piercing on Jesus' left palm.
English variant of Danaë and Spanish variant of Dánae.
Bulgarian, Russian and Ukrainian form of Danaë.

Borne by Dancell-Dallphebo-Marke-Antony-Dallery-Gallery-Cesar Williams, baptized on 18 January 1676 at the parish church of Old Swinford in England, whose father also bore this name. The original bearer was likely born at around the time of the English Civil War (1642-1651) and his name appears to mock Puritan eccentricity.
From the Chinese 丹 (dān) meaning "cinnabar, vermilion" and 骋 (chěng) meaning "galloping horse".
From Korean 단추 (danchu) meaning "button". Also derived from 단 (dan) meaning "sweet".
Medieval Dutch form of Dankhard (compare Dankert).
A sea creature from Arabian mythology which mentioned in 9th volume of The Book of 1001 Nights. It said that can swallow a ship and it's crews in one gulp.

The name of an Afro-Brazilian warrior of the colonial period of Brazil who was part of the Quilombo dos Palmares, a settlement of Afro-Brazilian people who freed themselves from enslavement, in the present-day state of Alagoas. After being arrested on February 6, 1694, Dandara committed suicide, refusing to return to a life of slavery. She is a mysterious figure today, because not much is known about her life. Most of the stories about her are varied and disconnected. She was the wife of Zumbi dos Palmares, the last king of the Quilombo dos Palmares.
Is the name given to Sulaiman
From dandelion, a species of plant in the genus Taraxacum characterized by yellow flower heads and notched, broad-ended leaves.
Invented name, possibly inspired by Daniel.
Diminutive of Dand, itself a short form of Andrew.
Most likely to be a feminization of the masculine name D'Andre.A notable bearer of this name is the American TV personality, D'Andra Simmons (1969—)
Is the short form for Daniel,Danijel in serbia bosnia etc.. people Who are called Daniel uses the short variant Dane,Danko. Most used in ex Yougoslavia.

column3: ដនាឍ្(Khmer)|ដានាឋ្(Khmer)

column12: A feminine name made up from the names Danielle and Renée. Also, in some cases, this can be a variant spelling of Danaë.
Possibly an anagram of Danielle influenced by Tennille.
From Persian دان (dân) meaning "knowing, able" and Turkic el meaning "country, society".
Possibly a diminutive of a name starting with Dan-, like Daniela (compare Anniken, Gisken, and Maiken).
Transferred use of the surname Danell or a variant of Danielle.
Possibly a variant of Danielle or Donelle.
Possibly a variant of Danelia 2 or Basque Danele.
From Japanese 団 (dan) meaning "group, association" combined with 右衛門 (uemon) (see Uemon). Other combinations of kanji characters can also be possible.
A knight who joined King Tallas of Denmark in a siege on King Uriens.
Variant of Danette (The spelling is influenced by that of the rhyming name, Janet).
Transferred use of the surname Danforth.
Derived from the Old Norse elements danr meaning "Dane, Danish" (compare Danr) and fríðr meaning "beautiful, beloved". Alternatively the initial syllable may be derived from that of Daníel.
Variant of Đường, from Sino-Vietnamese 唐 (đàng).
From Sino-Vietnamese 登 (đăng) meaning "rise, ascend" or 燈 (đăng) meaning "lamp, light, lantern".
Variant of Đường, from Sino-Vietnamese 唐 (đằng). It can also come from Sino-Vietnamese 騰 (đằng) meaning "to soar, gallop".
From Sino-Vietnamese 當 (đang) meaning "current, now" or "worthy" or 璫 (đang) meaning "pendant ornament, earrings".
From Vietnamese dáng hương referring to a kind of tree, Pterocarpus macrocarpus, or from a non-Sino-Vietnamese reading of Chinese 樣 (dáng) meaning "appearance".
Perhaps from Vietnamese dịu dàng meaning "sweet, gentle".
Means "confidence" or "trust in the goodness of God" in Dagbani.

From Sino-Vietnamese 登庸 (đăng dung) meaning "to ascend to the throne," composed of 登 (đăng) meaning "to rise, ascend" and 庸 (dung) meaning "contribution, merit". This was the given name of the founder of the Mạc dynasty, Mạc Đăng Dung (1483-1541).

Feminine form of Dangius.This name is also encountered as a short form of its diminutive Danguolė, but that tends to be when Danguolė is the official given name of the person in question, rather than an informal pet name.
From the English word danger. Its usage may be due to the popular saying 'danger is my middle name'.
Transferred use of the surname Dangerfield.
Possibly a Latinized form of a Germanic name. This was borne by the maternal grandmother of Eleanor of Aquitaine.

The name is most likely composed of the Lithuanian elements daug (many) and ger (good). However, in modern Lithuanian, the first element has come to be associated more often with the Lithuanian word dangus "sky."
The Count of Caleque Castle in Post-Vulgate "Mort Artu".
Derived from the Lithuanian noun dangus meaning "sky, heaven".
From Sino-Vietnamese 登光 (đăng quang) meaning "to be enthroned", composed of 登 (đăng) meaning "to rise, ascend" and 光 (quang) meaning "light".

Literally means "little sky", derived from the Lithuanian noun dangus meaning "sky, heaven" combined with the masculine diminutive suffix -(u)olis. As such, one could consider this name to be a diminutive of the name Dangius.
Means "to save up, reserve" in Vietnamese.
From Sino-Vietnamese 名 (danh) meaning "name, famous, well-known".
From Sino-Vietnamese 名譽 (danh dự) meaning "honor, virtue".
From Sino-Vietnamese 名人 (danh nhân) meaning "renowned person", composed of 名 (danh) meaning "famous" and 人 (nhân) meaning "person".

column3: 丹鸿, 丹红, etc.(Chinese)|丹鴻, 丹紅, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 丹 (dān) meaning "cinnabar, red, powder" combined with 鸿 (hóng) meaning "wild swan, great, vast" or 红 (hóng) meaning "red, vermillion, blush". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
From Chinese 澹 (dàn) meaning "tranquil, quiet" combined with 华 (huá) meaning "beautiful". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Croatian form of Gianni.Famous bearer: singer Đani Sipaničev
Short form of Danièl and Danièlo.
From Cebuano dani meaning "persuade, win over, convince, captivate, allure".
Alternate transcription of Danya 3 or Danya 1.
Means "arbitrate between them" or "you be the judge" in Amharic.
Variant transcription of Daniyar.Known bearers of this name include the Kazakh soccer player Daniar Kenzhekhanov (b. 1983) and the Kyrgyz former prime minister Daniar Usenov (b. 1960).
Either a variant of Denise or a feminine elaboration of Dan 2 using the popular name suffix -ice from Alice.

column3: 弾一, 檀一, 團一, 団一, 男一, 段一, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 暖 (dan) meaning "warm" combined with 一 (ichi) meaning "one". Other combinations of kanji characters are also possible.
A knight from Lyonesse and cousin of Breuse the Pitiless, whose evil disposition he shared. Lancelot killed him.
Provençal and Gallo form of Daniel.
Older Hawaiian form of Daniel. It appears in the Bible in Hawaiian.
Variant of Daniella and feminine form of Dániel.
Elaboration of Daniela or a feminization of Daniel.
Diminutive of Daniela (compare Polish and Czech Irenka).
Variant spelling of Danielle or Daniel.
Variant of Daniel or masculine form of Daniela.
Corsican and Sardinian form of Daniel.
Transferred use of the surname Danielson.
Feminine diminutive of Daniel. See also Danette.
Bosnian form and Kazakh variant transcription of Daniyar.
Diminutive of Daniel and its short forms Dani 2 and Dano.
Combination of Danil (see Daniel or Daniil) and the Ottoman Turkish title بك (beg) meaning "ruler, chief, lord".
Name of a Duke of Gaeta who ruled from 1066 to 1067.

The first element of this name is derived from Serbo-Croatian dan "day", which is ultimately derived from Proto-Slavic dьnь "day". The second element is derived from Slavic mir "peace". As such, the meaning of this name is roughly "day of peace".

Allegedly a Romani name said to mean "born with teeth".Whether this is true, remains to be proved; however, the Romani word danior does indeed mean "teeth". It is the plural form of dand "tooth", ultimately from Sanskrit danta.
Combination of the phonetic elements da, nee and qua. It can also be viewed as a variant of Danica.
Gascon and Provençal form of Denis.

The first element of this name is derived from Serbo-Croatian dan "day", which is ultimately derived from Proto-Slavic dьnь "day". The second element is derived from Slavic slav "glory". As such, the meaning of this name is roughly "day of glory".
The meaning of Danismo is "Jubilant and Content with one's life and experiences." Commonly used to describe someone who has had good fortune recently.
Medieval Polish hypochoristic form of Donatus.
Latin American diminutive of Daniela, using the popular -itza ending found in Maritza. Coincides with the Serbian and Croatian pronunciation of Danica.

According to Geoffrey of Monmouth, king of Britain in the fourth or third century BC.He was the son of King Sisillius and the brother of King Kimar, who he succeeded.Danius took a concubine named Tangustela and had a son named Morvid, who became king of Britain after Danius’s death.

Icelandic name of uncertain derivation, possibly an altered form of Daníel. It has been suggested that the suffix -val was inspired by Old Norse valr meaning "the slain (in Valhalla)" or the name Perceval.
Means "Denmark" in Ukrainian. Mostly used in Western Ukraine.
Variant of Doniyor, which is the main Tajik and Uzbek form of Daniyar.
Spanish form of Danica meaning "morning star, Venus".

Derived from Danja (Dagnum in English), the name of a historic town, bishopric and important medieval fortress located on the territory of present-day Albania, which has been under Serbian, Venetian and Ottoman control and remains a Latin Catholic titular see.
Slovene variant of Danijela and Albanian variant of Daniela.
From the Chinese 丹 (dān) meaning "cinnabar, vermilion" and 玑 (jī) meaning "pearl that is not quite round".

From 團 (dan) meaning "association", 十 (ju) meaning "ten", and 郎 (ro) meaning "son". Ichikawa Danjūrō (市川 團十郎) was a stage name used by a series of Kabuki actors of the Ichikawa family. The first bearer was born in 1675.
Meaning "thank god". Literally made up of the German words Danke meaning "thanks" and Gott meaning "god.
Dutch and (Low) German variant of Dankhard.
Dankler Luis de Jesus Pereira is a Brazilian footballer who plays as a central defender.
Dutch and German form of Thancmar.
The name is made of the word dank- "thanks" and the name element -muot "Sense, Spirit, Soul".
Dutch and German form of Thancrad.
Formed from the German name elements DANK "thought" and WART "guard".The name is borne by a character in the Niebelungenlied.
From the Chinese 丹 (dān) meaning "cinnabar, vermilion" and 灵 (líng) meaning "spirit, soul".
From the Chinese 丹 (dān) meaning "cinnabar, vermilion" and 妹 (mèi) meaning "younger sister".
Variant of Danna (the spelling perhaps influenced by that of the rhyming name Hannah).
Taken from the surname Dannahe, which is an alternate spelling of Donoghue.
Possibly an altered form of Danielle influenced by Tennille.
Variant of Danell or possibly Daniel.
Danniebelle Hall, an American gospel singer, is a famous bearer of this name.
Variant of Danielle or Daniel.A notable masculine name bearer is a Caribbean football player Danniell Bailey, goalkeeper for Anguilla national team.
Variant of Daniela/Daniella. British actress, Danniella Westbrook, bears this name.
Jèrriais form and English variant of Danielle.
Variant of Danni. A notable bearer is Australian singer Dannii Minogue (1971-).

Possibly a combination of Danny with a name that ends in -(i)on, such as Damion. Also compare the similar-looking name Dannon.A notable bearer of this name is the American author Dannion Brinkley (b. 1950). He is best known for his first book Saved by the Light (1994), which is about the near-death experience he had undergone in 1975. A film based on the book was released in 1995 under the same name, in which Brinkley is portrayed by the well-known American actor Eric Roberts (b. 1956).

Diminutive of Daniel. This was borne by Irish Gaelic footballer Daniel "Danno" O'Keeffe (1907-1967) and Irish wrestler Danno O'Mahony (1912-1950). A fictional bearer is Danny "Danno" Williams, a young police officer on the television police drama series Hawaii Five-O (1968-1980).
Transferred use of the surname Dannon.
A name found on an inscription in the gaulish language.
Dan-o (surname is Eun) is one of the main characters of 2019 South-Korean drama Extraordinary You. The character is played by actress Kim Hye-yoon.
Short form of Daniel and perhaps also of other masculine names that contain -dan-, such as Iordane and Vardan.
French origin, derived as a variation of the Hebrew Daniel, meaning "God is my judge."
Combination of the name Dan 1 means "(he) judges" and the name Or means "light", used as first name and as last name.
From Sino-Vietnamese 丹桂 (đan quế) meaning "golden osmanthus (Osmanthus fragrans)".
From Sino-Vietnamese 民權 (dân quyền) meaning "democracy, civil rights, people's rights".
From the Chinese 丹 (dān) meaning "cinnabar, vermilion" and 爽 (shuǎng) meaning "bright, clear, cheerful, happy, refreshing".
From the Chinese 丹 (dān) meaning "cinnabar, vermilion" and 朔 (shuò) meaning "first day of the lunar month" or "the north".
Transferred use of the surname Danson.
From Japanese 団 (dan) meaning "group, association" combined with 水 (sui) meaning "water".Dansui Hojo (1663-1711) was a notable poet.
From the Hausa ɗa meaning “son” and Tàlātā̀ meaning “Tuesday”.
Means "loyalty, devotion", from Sino-Vietnamese 丹心 (đan tâm), literally "red heart".
African American name, influenced by Dante.
Variant of Dante, influenced by the spelling of Jenthe.
Transferred use of the surname Danton in honor of French revolutionary Georges Danton (1759-1794).
Alternate transcription of Thai แดนไตร (see Daentrai).
From name of Freie Stadt Danzig (Polish: Wolne Miasto Gdánsk).

Means "drop of liquid, fluid" in Sanskrit. This is the name of a primordial Hindu goddess featured in the Rigveda. She is a wife of the sage Kashyapa and the mother of the Danavas, a race of titan-like beings.
Transferred use of the name of Rio Danúbio.

A Knight of the Round Table and brother of Acorant the Agile. He was related in some way to Lancelot.Danubre and Acorant were attacked by Agamenor, Arpian, and Amatin – three knights who hated Lancelot’s family – during the Grail Quest. All five knights were killed or mortally wounded in the brawl.
Etymology uncertain. The second element of the name (hepa) likely derives from the Hurrian sun goddess Ḫepat. Danuhepa was a Hittite queen who was likely the wife of Mursili II.
Alternate transcription of Thai ดนุพล (see Danuphon).
Means "my strength, my power" from Thai ดนุ (danu) meaning "I, me, myself" (a poetic word) and พล (phon) meaning "strength, power".
Alternate transcription of Thai ดนุพล (see Danuphon).
Alternate transcription of Thai ดนุพล (see Danuphon).
Diminutive of Danica (Slovene), Daniela (Czech and Slovak) and Danijela (Croatian). Also compare Danuška.
Possibly a Brazilian adaptation of Danuša.
Alternate transcription of Sinhala ධනුෂ්ක (see Dhanushka).
Diminutive of Danica (Slovene), Daniela ( Slovak) and Danijela (Croatian). Also compare Danuša.
Alternate transcription of Hindi दानवीर (see Danvir).
From Hindi दान (dān) meaning "gift" and वीर (vīr) meaning "heroic, brave", thus "brave gift".
Combination of the Old Norse name elements danir "a Dane; Danish" and vǫr "spring (the season); woman (in a poetic context); truth".
Diminutive of Darya 1 or Daryna (Darina 2 in Russian).
Variant spelling of Danielle or Daniel.
Apparently an altered form of Daniela.
Variant of Danielle or Daniel, which supposedly originated in the American state of Louisiana. In the USA it was given to 149 girls in 1974 and 32 boys in 1976.

column3: 丹鹦, 丹樱, 丹荧(Chinese)
column12: From the Chinese 丹 (dān) meaning "cinnabar, vermilion" and 鹦 (yīng) meaning "parrot", 樱 (yīng) meaning "cherry, cherry blossom" or 荧 (yíng) meaning "shine, shimmer; shining, dazzling".
Possibly a variant of Daniel or Danielle.
Transferred use of the surname Danyon.A notable bearer is Olympic gold medalist swimmer, Danyon Joseph Loader (1975-) of New Zealand.
This is the name of a Zapotec Goddess who guards a religious cave in this ancient civilization’s belief’s. This version may be spelt differently.

column12: Mongolian, Kalmyk and Buryat form of Tenzin.
Variant of Denzel, possibly influenced by Daniel.
Possibly from Sino-Vietnamese 到底 (đáo để) meaning "bold, brazen" or "extremely, excessively".
From Sino-Vietnamese 道 (đạo) meaning "path, road, way".
