column12: Means "star" in Thai and Lao. It is only a feminine name in Thailand while it is unisex in Laos.
Name of Irish origin, formed by "daor", meaning "famous" or also "free" and "ri", meaning "king", so the meaning is "famous king" or "free king", "free person".
meaning "All Happiness Will Come". from korean "Da (다 / All)" + "OL (올 = 오다 / Come)". Kim Da-OL is Korean Voice Actor, who played Sinclair in the Limbus Company.
From the Chinese 道 (dào) meaning "path, road, method, way" and 娈 (luán) meaning "lovely, beautiful, docile".
From Sino-Korean 多 (da) meaning "many" combined with 穩 (on) meaning "peaceful, serene". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
Alternate transcription of Urdu داؤد (see Daud).
From ດາວ (Dao) meaning "star" in Lao and ຜາສຸກ (phasouk) meaning "joy, happiness, prosperity".

From Chinese 道 (dào) meaning "path, road, way" or 悼 (dào) meaning "lament, mourn, grieve" combined with 平 (píng) meaning "level, even, peaceful". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
From Chinese 刀刃 (daoren) meaning "blade". Shortened form is Ren (刃), meaning the same.
In Greek mythology, Daortho is the daughter of Illyrios.
Means "bottle gourd (Crescentia cujete)" in Vietnamese, from Sino-Vietnamese 桃 (đào) meaning "peach" and 仙 (tiên) meaning "fairy".
From Lao ດາວ (dao) meaning "star" and ວົງ (vong) meaning "lineage, family, ring, circle".
From Chinese 道 (dào) meaning "path, road, way" combined with 行 (xíng) meaning "behaviour, conduct". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 道一, 道艺, etc.(Chinese)|道一, 道藝, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 道 (dào) meaning "path, road, way" combined with 一 (yī) meaning "one" or 艺 (yì) meaning "art, talent, craft". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

From Chinese 达 (dá) meaning "achieve, arrive at, intelligent" (which is usually only masculine), 大 (dà) meaning "big, great, vast, high", combined with From Chinese 鹏 (péng) referring to a large, legendary bird in Chinese mythology or 蓬 (péng) meaning "flourishing, prospering, vigorous". Other character combinations can be used.
Meaning as of yet unknown. It is likely of Mingrelian origin, as the few existing bearers all have a Mingrelian surname.

From Ancient Greek δάφνη (daphne) meaning "laurel tree". In Greek mythology, Daphnis was a Sicilian herdsman, usually the son of Hermes and an unnamed nymph, said to be the inventor of pastoral poetry. He was cursed with blindness as consequence of being unfaithful to a naiad. A shepherd moon of Saturn was named after him. Daphnis was also the name of an Oread nymph of Mount Parnassus, a prophet of Gaia before Apollo took control of Delphi.
French form of Dafrosa (via Latin Daphrosa).
Georgian form of Daphne. Also compare Dafina.
From Chinese 大 (dà) meaning "big, great, vast, high" combined with 娉 (pīng) meaning "beautiful, charming, graceful" Other character combinations are possible.
From Chinese 大千世界 (dàqiānshìjiè), a Buddhism term meaning "trichiliocosm, the boundless universe". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Feminine elaboration of Daquan using the same suffix found in names such as Yolanda, LaWanda and Lashonda.
From Sino-Vietnamese 夜光 (dạ quang) meaning "luminous, moonlight, starlight", composed of 夜 (dạ) meaning "night" and 光 (quang) meaning "light".
Feminine form of Daquan or elaboration of Quanna.
Combination of the phonetic element da and Aquarius.
Combination of the phonetic element da and the name Quasha.
Possibly an Anglicized spelling and subsequently transferred use of the surname Daqué.
Combination of the phonetic element da and Queen.
Elaboration of Quisha using the popular prefix Da-.
Short form of Darinka in Slovene and Croatian and Dariya or Daryna in Ukrainian.
Means "glory, power, wealth" in Persian. This is the name of a character in the Persian epic 'Shahnameh'.

Allegedly means "daughter of Áine" (from the Old Irish prefix der "daughter" and the name of the Irish goddess Áine). This is borne by Irish television presenter Daráine Mulvihill (c. 1983-), whose father, Liam Mulvihill, served as director general of the Gaelic Athletic Association (GAA) from 1979 until 2008.
A combination of Dara and Lyn.According to Forebears.Io, 556 people worldwide have this name.
A combination of Dara and Lynn.According to Forebears.Io, 142 people worldwide have this name.

According to the legend of the Aboriginals, the original settlers of Australia, Darana was one of the Deities during Dreamtime (the time before humans occupied Earth).According to legend, Darana created witchetty grubs and put two in a bag. He then hung the bag from a tree in Australia. Later, two human young men killed the grubs with a boomerang. Apparenty, this was a no-no because the dust of the destroyed grubs glowed with a light that turned the sunset red, which alerted evil spirits who killed the humans.Daran felt bad for this, and turned the young men's bodies into sacred stones. If the stones are scratched, there will be famine. And if they are destroyed, the universe will turn to dust. For this reason, the stones were hidden in a bag in a secret location where they remain untouched to this very day.
Alternate transcription of Thai ดารณี (see Darani).
Means "boat, ship" in Thai, ultimately from Sanskrit तारणि (tāraṇi).
Linked to the name Tariq. South Sudanese name used in wars in Arabian territories and deeper in African territories. Ghana mostly uses the name Daraq as a borrowing name for little male babies.

An old knight who lived with his nephew, Danaim, and harbored sick and injured knights in his castle, including Tristan, Mordred, and Palamedes.While Tristan was healing there, Daras discovered that Tristan had slain three of his sons at the Castle of Maidens tournament, and had maimed his other two. Enraged, he threw Tristan, Palamedes, and Dinadan into his prison. When Tristan grew deathly ill, Daras relented and released him on Tristan’s pledge of friendship.He later became a Knight of the Round Table.
the name come from Nigeria and it can be use for any gender and it mean god love you
Lithuanian form of Dorothea via its Polish form Dorota. It should be noted, though, that some Lithuanian sources state that Darata is a short form of Dorotėja.
From the French surname, Darcel, a variant of the surname Darcy/D'Arcy (see Darcy)

Either a diminutive or a variant of დარჩილ (Darchil), which is the Georgian form of the Middle Persian name Dartsihr (see Dachi).This name is archaic and now only survives in the patronymic surnames of დარჩია (Darchia) and დარჩიაშვილი (Darchiashvili) meaning "child of Darchia".

In English-speaking countries, this name is probably a variant of Darcy, one that may have been inspired by the name Marcia.Outside of the anglophone world, there is more uncertainty surrounding the meaning and etymology of the name, since Darcy as a given name is predominantly used in the English-speaking world. Perhaps in other countries (where the name Darcia is even rarer than in the anglophone world), the name is simply a combination of any name starting with D- with Marcia.Known bearers of this name include the Swiss ice hockey player Darcia Leimgruber (b. 1989) and Darcia Narvaez, an American (of Puerto Rican descent) professor of psychology at the University of Notre Dame (which is located in the United States).
Possibly an altered form of Drusilla, or an elaboration of Darcy with the clearly feminine ending illa.
Possibly a blend of the names Darius and Marcus. A known bearer of this name is Darcus Howe, a British broadcaster, columnist and civil rights campaigner.
Meaning "pearl of wisdom," he was one of the exemplars of wisdom than whom Solomon was wiser. (I Kings 4:31)

From the name of the Dardanelles, one of the straits that separate European Turkey from Asian Turkey. The place name apparently derives from the name of Dardanos, son of Zeus and Electra in Greek myth."Dardanella" was also the name of a popular song in 1919.
Italian and Portuguese form of Dardanos.
Transferred use of the surname Dare. It was borne by Canadian American photographer and author Dare Wright (1914-2001).

The sister of St. Patrick in Jocelyn’s Life of St. Patrick. She was said to have been Patrick’s youngest sister and to have had seventeen sons.Gallet makes her an ancestor of Arthur. Gallet makes Dareca’s sister Tigridia marry Grallo, Conan’s grandson, thus connecting her with Arthur, she is said to have married Conan himself.

Darin was a historic port town in the eastern Gulf region (present-day Bahrain). The town was famous in early Arabic sources as a trade center, commonly associated with perfumes and spices. Ancient Arabic poetry references Darin and the musk of Darin.Derived from the place name Dareen. It is interpreted symbolically as connected to (Dara) درى: “to know”; giving it connotations of “knowledge”, “wisdom”, or “one who knows.”In a spiritual sense, (DAR-AYN) reflects the Quranic concept of al-dunya wa al-akhirah; “this life and the Hereafter.”It can be connected to (Dar-) دار “house”, or “dwelling.” In this interpretation, the suffix -ayn is understood as a dual marker, giving the symbolic meaning “two houses.”
In Hebrew it’s a combination of the name Dar, means "(mother of) pearl, nacre" and El, reference to God. In English it’s used as variant of Darell.
Saint Darerca of Ireland was a sister of Saint Patrick.

Uncertain etymology, possibly derived from Ancient Greek δαρείς (dareis) meaning "the beaten", a participle of δέρω (dero) meaning "to skin, flay; to cudgel, thrash". Dares Phrygius is the name of a Trojan priest of Hephaestus in Homer’s Iliad, later becoming known as the author of a lost eyewitness account of the fall of Troy. It’s also the name of a young Trojan boxer in Virgil’s Aeneid.

Basically means "acting strong" or "working to be(come) strong", derived from Lithuanian daryti meaning "to do, to act" as well as "to work" combined with old Lithuanian gailas, which usually means "strong, potent" but has also been found to mean "sharp, jagged" as well as "angry, fierce, violent" and "miserable, sorrowful, remorseful". Also compare the modern Lithuanian noun galia meaning "power, might, force".

The first element of this name is derived from Lithuanian daryti meaning "to do, to act" as well as "to work". The second element is either derived from the Lithuanian verb gaudyti meaning "to take" as well as "to catch, to hunt" or from the Lithuanian adjective gaudus meaning "sonorous, resonant, ringing, loud, echoing".
Basically means "working to protect", derived from Lithuanian daryti meaning "to do, to act" as well as "to work" combined with Lithuanian ginti meaning "to defend, to protect".
the history of this name is unknown, but the meaning is "grace, or to be graceful"
Spanish form of Daria. The name coincides with the first-person singular conditional form and third-person singular conditional form of dar, meaning "I would give" or "he / she would give".
Derived from Slavic dar, meaning "gift". It is sometimes also considered a derivative of Darius.
Possibly an elaborated form of Dariana.
Intended to be a feminine form of Darius, using the name suffix ice.
Possibly a feminine form of Dariel or an elaborated form of Daria.
the origins and meaning of this name isn't exact but pretty sure it's of Puerto Rican origins and means "passionate" and/or "faithful"
Feminine variant of Dariel using the feminine name suffix ys.
Possibly a variant of Darien or taken from the name of the Darién Gap, a rainforest region located between the countries of Colombia and Panamá.

Derived from an expression of sadness intended to mean "pity!" or "alas!" in Kazakh. The word itself is either of Arabic origin from a word meaning "pity, regret, surprise" or from a Persian expression meaning "beautiful". It was traditionally given to girls when her parents were expecting a son (used in the context of "what a pity that it was not a boy").
Alternate transcription of Russian Дарий or Ukrainian Дарій (see Dariy).
Meaning unknown, though it is probably of Tibetan-Sanskrit origin.
Croatian and Serbian form of Darius.
Derived from Thai ดารา (dara) meaning "star".
Possibly from the Karachay-Balkar дарий (dariy) meaning "silk" and the diminutive suffix -ко (-ko).
A Saxon warrior. He was the son of King Bramangue and the brother of Haram and Orient.He assisted his brother Haram with the siege of Arundel in the early days of Arthur’s reign.
Likely an invented name made to rhyme with names like Marilyn.
Derived from Thai ดารา (dara) meaning "star".
Catalan and Georgian form of Darius.
Alternate transcription of Persian داریوش (see Dariush).
From Ilocano darisay meaning "of good quality, pure, clear" and from Maranao darisay meaning "greatness".

Means "door of Isfahan", derived from the Persian noun در (dar) meaning "door, gate" combined with Spahān, which is the Middle Persian name for the modern city of اصفهان (Isfahan) in Iran.In Georgian literature, Darispan is the father of the famed warrior Sepedavle from the 12th-century Georgian romance Amiran-Darejaniani written by Moses of Khoni.
Corsican and Sicilian form of Darius.
Slovak and Hungarian form of Darius.
Languedocian and Gascon form of Darius.
Either a form of Darian or a derivative of the Slavic element dar meaning "gift".

Literally taken from the English word dark, which is ultimately derivwd from Middle English derk, from Old English deorc, from Proto-West Germanic *derk meaning "dark", according to Wiktionary.This is the first middle name of Exa Dark Sideræl Musk (2021—), daughter of Elon Musk and Grimes.
Either a feminine form of Darko or a short form of other feminine dar- names like Darinka or, as some sources suggest, even Darija.

Means "gallant, strong, sturdy" in Kazakh. It may also be derived from tarkhan, an ancient military title used by Mongol, Turkic and Iranian leaders, which is of uncertain origin. In the Mongol Empire this title granted exemption from taxation.
Combination of the prefix dar with Kisha.
Either a Romani corruption of Dorcas or derived from the English word darkless "free from darkness".
Darkseid (pronounced "Darkside'') is a fictional supervillain appearing in American comic books published by DC Comics.
Combination of Darla or Darlene and Anne 1.
Variant of Darlene using the popular name suffix lee.
Spanish variant of Darlene in the same fashion as Marlén.
Variant of the name Darlene. This name was giving to former Bad Girl Darlen Escobar. Darlen featured in the show Bad Girls Club (2006-2017).
English variant and Polish borrowing of Darlene.
Elaboration of Darla or Darlene with the common feminine suffix -ette
Meaning unknown, possibly derived as a variant Darling (Compare Darlene).
French and Flemish borrowing of Darlene, as well as an English variant.
Transferred use of the surname Darling, or else derived directly from the word.
Transferred use of the surname Darlington.
From Indonesian darma meaning "good deed, duty" combined with adi meaning "first" in Indonesian or "beautiful, good, valuable" in Javanese.

The first element of this name is derived from Lithuanian daryti meaning "to do, to act" as well as "to work". The second element is either derived from Lithuanian mantus meaning "intelligent" (see Daumantas) or from Lithuanian manta meaning "property, estate" as well as "wealth, riches, fortune".
From Indonesian darma meaning "good deed, duty", ultimately from Sanskrit धर्म (dharma), combined with the masculine suffix -wan.
From Indonesian darma meaning "good deed, duty", ultimately from Sanskrit धर्म (dharma), combined with the feminine suffix -wati.

The first element of this name is derived from Lithuanian daryti meaning "to do, to act" as well as "to work". The second element is derived from the Lithuanian noun mintis meaning "thought", which is related to the Lithuanian verb minti meaning "to remember, to recall".
From Javanese darma meaning "good deed, duty" combined with either the masculine suffix -na or the word ana meaning "being, having, holding".

Darna is a fictional character and superheroine created by Filipinokomiks (Philippine colloquial term for comics) legend Mars Ravelo. In her more popular incarnations, she is a warrior from outer space manifesting herself through a girl from Earth, named Narda.Darna was originally known as Varga and first appeared in Bulaklak Magazine, Volume 4, #17, on July 23, 1947. Ravelo had differences with the editors of Bulaklak Magazine and Varga's name was changed to "Darna", because it was an anagram of Narda. The character was re-launched on May 13, 1950. Nestor Redondo drew the first Darna.Since then, Darna has become a Philippine cultural icon and the most recognizable character among Ravelo's creations.
Feminine form or variant of Darnell.
Likely an invented name. It might possibly be a variant of Danielle, possibly influenced by Darnell. Also may be transferred usage of the surname Darnielle.
Elaboration of the feminized version of Darnell.
From Kirby, an action-platformer video game series developed by HAL Laboratory and published by Nintendo.

Variant of Darrell and the name of American violinist Darol Anger (1963-) as well as that of American born, Canadian educated physicist Darol Kenneth Froman (1906-1997), Deputy Director of Los Alamos National Laboratory in the 1950s and early 1960s.

This given name originated in the United States, where it is a combination of a name starting with Dar- (such as Darrell, Darryl and Darren) with Harold. Also compare the name Derald, which in some cases can be a variant form of this name.Known bearers of this name include the American rapper ASAP Ferg (who was born as Darold Ferguson, Jr. in 1988) and the American track athlete Darold Williamson (b. 1983).

The first element of this name is derived from Slavic dar "gift, present", which in turn is derived from Proto-Slavic darъ "gift, present". Compare modern Polish darować "to donate, to gift" and Czech darovat "to donate, to give", as well as Proto-Slavic dati "to give". The second element of this name is derived from Slavic mir "peace". As such, this name roughly means "to gift peace" or "peace is a gift".
Variant of Darren. A known bearer of this name was the American country singer Daron Norwood (1965-2015).

The first element of this name is derived from Slavic dar "gift, present", which in turn is derived from Proto-Slavic darъ "gift, present". Compare modern Polish darować "to donate, to gift" and Czech darovat "to donate, to give", as well as Proto-Slavic dati "to give". The second element of this name is derived from Slavic slav "glory". As such, this name roughly means "to gift glory" or "glory is a gift".
A modern invented name of unknown meaning, possibly influenced by Marquise.
Combination of prefix dar with Quinton.

A Paeonian god of healing worshipped by the ancient Macedonians, later identified with Asclepius. Possibly a Macedonian form of Ancient Greek Θάρρων (Tharron), which likely derives from θαρρέω (tharreo) meaning "to be of good courage, have confidence; to inspire with confidence, make bold". Alternatively, it could be related to the name of the Derrones, a Thracian or Paeonian tribe residing in the upper Strymon valley in North Macedonia.
Either a variant form of Derrick, or a blend of a name starting with Dar- (such as Darren or Darryl) with Rick.
The name Darroch is said to derive from Macdara which is Scottish Gaelic for ''son of oak''.
Transferred use of the surname Darrow.
Diminutive of Darrell or other names beginning with the element Darr.
Feminine form of Darryl influenced by Darlene.
Possibly means "pearl of great price" from Arabic دُرّ‎ (durr) "pearl" (compare Durr) and ثَمِين‎ (ṯamīn) "valuable, precious" (compare Sameen).
A knight whom Arthur freed from the castle Causuel when he defeated the Merciless Lion, Darsenois’s jailer. In return, Darsenois gave Arthur a charger.
From Javanese darsana meaning "example, pattern, model", ultimately from Sanskrit दर्शन (darśana).
Transferred use of the surname Dart.
Anglicized form of D'Artagnan. A known bearer of this name is the American up-and-coming child actor Dartanian Sloan.
Basically means "(a) working people", derived from Lithuanian daryti meaning "to do, to act" as well as "to work" combined with Baltic tauta meaning "people, nation" (see Vytautas).

Likely a blend of the English words dark and death. In the Star Wars universe, it is used as a title for Sith Lords (see Darth Vader). Since the release of the first Star Wars film in 1977, it has been borne by at least 22 men in the United States.
Either a variant of Dorthula or from the poem by Scottish poet James Macpherson of the same name.
Means "blizzard mother" in Vainakh. Dartsa-Naana was the Chechen and Ingush goddess of blizzards and avalanches. Like Sela, she lives on top of Mount Kazbek.
Daruk (Called Darukeru in Japan) is one of the four champions in the video game The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild.
From Chinese 大 (dà) meaning "big, great, vast, high" combined with 闰 (rùn) meaning "intercalary". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Diminutive of Darya 1, not ususally used as a given name in its own right.
Derived from Arabic دار السلام (dar as-salam) meaning "abode of peace", used as an epithet for various places.
Origin unknown. This may be considered a feminine form of Darvin.
Derived from Lithuanian daryti meaning "to do, to act" as well as "to work" combined with the old Lithuanian noun vaina meaning "cause, reason" as well as "fault".
Basically means "working to hope", derived from Lithuanian daryti meaning "to do, to act" as well as "to work" combined with Baltic vil meaning "hope" (see Viltautas).
Variant and Russian form of Darwin.

Basically means "working to see", derived from Lithuanian daryti meaning "to do, to act" as well as "to work" combined with Baltic vyd meaning "to see" (see Vytautas). Also compare other names that end in -vydas, such as Alvydas and Tautvydas.A known bearer of this name is the Lithuanian professional soccer player Darvydas Šernas (b. 1984).
Alternate transcription of Arabic درويش (see Darwish).
Combination of the name Darwina and the feminine suffix -wati.
Means "dervish, Sufi mystic" in Arabic, derived from Persian درویش (darvesh) meaning "poor, needy, indigent".

Darwood Kaye (born Darwood Kenneth Smith) was an American child actor known for his role of Waldo in the series of short films The Little Rascals (aka Our Gang) between 1937 - 1940. Later in life he became a pastor.
Variant of Darwin chiefly used in Venezuela.
Combination of the name Dar, means "(mother of) pearl" with the letters יה (ya) (which are part of the name of God) means "Pearl of God" in Hebrew.
Means "river, sea" in Pashto, from Persian درياب (daryāb).
A compound of the names Daryl and Ann borne by a recurring character in 'Hill Street Blues' played by the actress Deborah Richter.
Combination of Daryl and the popular name suffix lyn.
Composed of Tajik дарё (daryo), Uzbek daryo meaning "river" and Tajik гул (gul), Uzbek gul meaning "flower".
Diminutive of Darya 1, not usually used as a given name in its own right.
From Javanese darya meaning "character, heart, happiness" or "firmness" combined with either the masculine suffix -na or the word ana meaning "being, having, holding".
Alternate transcription of Persian داریوش (see Dariush).
Alternate transcription of Persian داریوش (see Dariush).
Daryun is a main character from "The Heroic Legend of Arslan", which is a novel series and anime show.
Diminutive of Darya 1, not usually used as a given name in its own right.
Diminutive of Darya 1, not usually used as a given name in its own right.

The first element of this name is derived from Polish darzyć "to bestow, to grant, to endow", which is ultimately derived from Slavic dar "gift, present" (which in turn is derived from Proto-Slavic darъ "gift, present"). Compare modern Polish darować "to donate, to gift" and Czech darovat "to donate, to give", as well as Proto-Slavic dati "to give". The second element of this name is derived from Slavic slav "glory". As such, this name roughly means "to bestow glory", making it more or less a cognate of Darosław.
Javanese form of Dashamukha, used as another name for the demon king Rahwana.

Means "the mountain of tea" from Sino-Korean 茶山.A noted bearer is Jeong Yak-yong (1762-1836), most commonly known by his pen name Dasan. He was one of the greatest thinkers of the later Joseon period, wrote highly influential books about philosophy, science and theories of government, held significant administrative positions, was a close confident of King Jeongjo (ruled 1776-1800), and was noted as a poet. His philosophical position is often identified with the Silhak (practical learning) school, his concerns are better seen as explorations of Neo-Confucian themes.

Dasan, the high god-ancestor of the northern Pomo, came out of the ocean and called the world into being with his words and then created the first people.While it's unknown if Dasan was used as a given name historically, it is a name used by the Pomo in present day.
From the name of the bottled water brand Dasani, itself inspired in the Latin word sanus ("healthy"). This name was first recorded in the US in 1999, the year the brand was launched.
From the name of a southeastern Illyrian tribe.

Variant transcription of Dasha (for Russia and the Ukraine) as well as the main form of Dasha in Germany and the Netherlands.A known bearer of this name is the Dominican-American actress Dascha Polanco (b. 1982).
Possibly derived from Ancient Greek δάσκω (dasko) meaning "teach", derived from διδάσκω (didasko) "to teach, instruct, train", or perhaps δάσκιος (daskios) meaning "thick-shaded, bushy".
From Azerbaijani daş meaning "stone" and dəmir meaning "iron".
Contraction of да здравствуют строители ДнепроГЭСа (da zdravstvuyet stroiteli DneproGESa), meainign "long live the builders of Dnipro Hydroelectric Power Station".
Variant transcription of Dazdrapertrak. This name was used by Communist parents who were eager to reject traditional names.
Combination of the popular phonetic prefix da and the name Sean, making it a variant of Dashawn.

Probably derived from Ancient Greek δασύς (dasys) meaning "hairy, shaggy, rough; thickly wooded, bushy". This was the eponymous founder of the ancient town Daseae in Greek mythology, one of the fifty sons of King Lycaon.
From Tibetan ཟླ (zla) meaning "moon, month" and གསལ (gsal) meaning "clear, bright, brilliant".
Variant spelling of Dašenka. Used by Czech writer Karel Čapek in his book Dášeňka čili život štěněte (Dashenka, or the Life of a Puppy, 1933).
In Native Korean Meaning "Take Care". this name is derived from Korean Word "다스리다 (To Rule)".
Derived from Albanian dash "ram" and, figuratively, "healthy and good-looking person".
Derived from Albanian dashamir "well-wishing, benevolent; kind, friendly".
Means "ten faces" from Sanskrit दश (daśa) meaning "ten" and मुख (mukha) meaning "face". This is an epithet of the demon king Ravana, who is often depicted with ten heads.
Possibly a variant spelling of Dashauna or Dashawna, which are feminine forms of Deshaun and Deshawn.
Usage and/or origin might be related to Dashana and Deshawn.
Combination of the phonetic elements da and shay. It can be spelled Dashay or with a capitalized third letter as DaShay.
From Tibetan བཀྲ་ཤིས (bkra shis) meaning "good fortune, good luck" (see Tashi) and རྡོ་རྗེ (rdo rje) meaning "diamond, vajra" (see Dorji).
Combination of the popular name prefix Da- and Sheena.
From the Chinese 大 (dà) meaning "big, great" and 升 (shēng) meaning "arise, go up, advance" or 圣 (shèng) meaning "holy, sacred".
Derived from Tibetan བཀྲ་ཤིས (bkra-shis) meaning "happiness" or "success" combined with དགེ་ལེགས (dge-legs) meaning "sacred virtue."
Buryat form of Tashi, commonly used as an element in compound names.
Diminutive of Darya 1. See also Dasha.

From Chinese 大 (dà) meaning "big, great", 势 (shì) meaning "power, force" and 至 (zhì) meaning "reach, arrive", a calque of Sanskrit महास्थामप्राप्त (mahāsthāmaprāpta). This is the Chinese name for the bodhisattva Mahasthamaprapta.
Russian diminutive of Darya 1. (Also compare Dasha.)
Either transferred from the surname Dashley, or a combination of Dash and the popular name suffix lee, likely taking inspiration from Ashley.
Combination of the popular prefix da and the name Shonda. It can be spelled DaShonda or Dashonda.
Combined with Dash and -ton (from names like Kingston).
From the Chinese 大 (dà) meaning "big, great" and 帅 (shuài) meaning "commander".
Diminutive of Darya 1, not usually used as a given name in its own right.
Diminutive of Darya 1, not usually used as a given name in its own right.
Derived from Albanian dashuri "love, affection; enthusiasm".
Diminutive of names like Hadas and Hadasa.
Italian and Spanish form of Dasius.
An Illyrian name of uncertain etymology, possibly related to Albanian Dash meaning "ram". This was the name of two martyred Christian saints, both Roman soldiers.
Ukrainian and Russian form of Dasius.
Variant form of Dascha, which is the Dutch main form of the Russian and Ukrainian given name Dasha.
From Sino-Korean 多 (da) meaning "many" combined with 率 (sol) meaning "lead, command" or native Korean 솔 (sol) meaning "pine (tree)". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
From obsolete native Korean 다솜 (dasom) meaning "love." As a word, it is replaced by Sarang.
In Greek mythology, Dassaro is the daughter of Illyrios.
Means "bouquet of flowers, roses" in Azerbaijani, ultimately from Persian دسته (daste) meaning "group, bunch" and گل (gol) meaning "flower, rose". Also see Güldəstə.
Means "story, legend" in Persian. This is another name for Zal, a character in the Shahnameh epic.
Combination of Dastan with the Turkish military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".
Variant of Doston, which is the main Uzbek form of Dastan.
Variant of Dostonbek, which is the main Uzbek form of Dastanbek.

From Sino-Vietnamese 逸 (dật) meaning "leisurely, indulgent, beautiful", 溢 (dật) meaning "overflowing, to flood, vigorous", or 鎰 (dật) referring to an ancient unit of measurement equal to twenty or twenty-four taels.
Short form of Davit and perhaps also of Datua. In Georgian literature, this is the name of the eponymous character of the popular novel Data Tutashkhia (1975) written by Chabua Amirejibi (1921-2013).

The first element of this name is derived from Old Persian dāta, which can mean "law" but also "gave, given" (as past tenses of the verb dadātuv "to give, to put"). The second element of this name is derived from Old Persian farnah "glory, splendour, fortune". As such, the name can either mean "glorious law" or "to be given glory".
Hellenized form of Datafarnah. This was the name of a Persian general from the 4th century BC.
Means "born better" or "created better", from Old Persian 𐎭𐎠𐎫 (data) meaning "given, created; born" and 𐎺𐏃𐎹𐏀 (vahyaz) "better", a comparative form of 𐎺𐎢 (vahu) "good".

From native Korean 닻별 (datbyeol), referring to the Cassiopeia constellation, from a combination of 닻 (dat) meaning "anchor" and Byeol.The weekend comedy drama series 'Dummy Mommy' (바보엄마 (Babo Eomma)), which features a young girl with this name, led to a temporary increase of the name's usage in 2012.
Short form of given names that contain the Proto-West Germanic element *dādi meaning "deed, act, action" as well as "work".
Derived from Arabic Al Dhāt al Kursiyy, meaning "the lady in the chair". Dath Elkarti is another name for Schedar.
From Dáði, an Old Norse diminutive of Davíð. Alternatively it may have been a diminutive of Dagr, or an Old Norse form of Irish Dáithí or Saxon Daþa.
An Olken mage from Karen Miller's Kingmaker, Kingbreaker trilogy
From the Chinese 大 (dà) meaning "big, great" and 天 (tiān) meaning "sky, heaven".

Diminutive of Davit. A known bearer of this name was the Georgian revolutionary Datiko Shevardnadze (1875-1909), who was a relative of the second president of Georgia, Eduard Shevardnadze (1928-2014).
Form of Dacius. This was the name of the Bishop of Milan who defended the will of Catholicism from the rampaging heresies of his day.
Feminine form of Dativus. This was the name of a 5th-century Christian martyr from North Africa. It is mostly used in Eastern Africa (mainly in Tanzania, Rwanda and Uganda).
French form of Dativa, mostly used in Rwanda.
From the Latin adjective datīvus meaning "giving."
Short form of Davit. A notable bearer of this name is the Georgian pop singer Davit "Dato" Khujadze (b. 1975).

Variant of Deitra. D'Atra Hicks, born Deitra Cherelle Hicks (1967-) is an American actress and singer. Hicks is best known for her role as Jackie Simmons in Tyler Perry's 2002 stage play 'Madea's Family Reunion'.

Diminutive or vernacular form of an unknown name. There were 147 cossacks with this name in 1649 Zaporozhian Army register.Datsko is still used in Transcarpathia as a diminutive of Andriy, so it may have been derived from this name in the 17th century as well. Other theories of origin include: Dasiy, Dariy, Danylo, Damian, other names containing d, such as Bohdan, Yordan. Alternatively it could have been derived from Dazhboh (see Dazhdbog) via its Polish form, Dadzbog.

Often listed as a diminutive of Davit (compare names like Datiko and Dato), this name might actually be of pagan origin, in which case it is derived from the Old Georgian noun დათჳ (datwi) meaning "bear".A known bearer of this name was the Georgian feudal lord Datua Biskaia (17th century).
From the Philippine title datu meaning "chief, leader" and the given name Ali 1.
Diminutive of Davit and of names that are possibly of pagan origin and derived from Old Georgian დათჳ (datwi) meaning "bear", such as Datua.
From Sino-Vietnamese 野象 (dã tượng) meaning "wild elephant". This was the name of a general of the Trần dynasty.
From the name of the poisonous flower, derived from Hindi धतूरा (dhatūrā).
Possibly derived from Latin datus, meaning "given, offered" or "gift". In the Netherlands, it was occasionally given as a middle name in the nineteenth century, but it is not used at all these days.
Ancient Aleut personal name meaning "Having a big eye" or "Having big eyes"
Means "God's religion" in Hebrew, from דָּת (dat) meaning "religion" and יָה (yah) referring to the Hebrew God.
From Sino-Vietnamese 鬥 (đấu) meaning "to battle, fight".
From Sino-Vietnamese 斗 (đẩu) meaning "dipper", which can refer to various groups of stars, including the Big Dipper and one of the Twenty-Eight Mansions in Chinese astronomy, Dipper.
From Sino-Vietnamese 酉 (dậu) referring to the tenth Earthly Branch (5 to 7 PM), which is itself associated with the rooster of the Chinese zodiac.
Transferred use of the surname Daubney.

Basically means "much strength", derived from Lithuanian daug meaning "much" (see Daumantas) combined with old Lithuanian gailas, which usually means "strong, potent" but has also been found to mean "sharp, jagged" as well as "angry, fierce, violent" and "miserable, sorrowful, remorseful". Also compare the modern Lithuanian noun galia meaning "power, might, force".

The first element of this name is derived from Lithuanian daug meaning "much" (see Daumantas). The second element is either derived from the Lithuanian verb gaudyti meaning "to take" as well as "to catch, to hunt" or from the Lithuanian adjective gaudus meaning "sonorous, resonant, ringing, loud, echoing".
Possibly a direct adoption of Latvian daugaviete "(woman) from the Daugava (the biggest river in Latvia)".
Basically means "a lot to defend", derived from Lithuanian daug meaning "much" (see Daumantas) combined with Lithuanian ginti meaning "to defend, to protect".

Basically has the (more or less) figurative meaning of "he who hears much", derived from Lithuanian daug meaning "much" (see Daumantas) combined with the Lithuanian noun girdas meaning "rumour", which is ultimately derived from the Lithuanian verb girdėti meaning "to hear". Also compare the related Lithuanian noun gandas meaning "rumour, hearsay".

The first element of this name is derived from Lithuanian daug meaning "much" (see Daumantas). The second element is derived from the Lithuanian noun mintis meaning "thought", which is related to the Lithuanian verb minti meaning "to remember, to recall".

Means "much hope", derived from Lithuanian daug meaning "much" (see Daumantas) combined with Baltic vil meaning "hope" (see Viltautas). In other words: this given name is basically the same as Vildaugas, but with the name elements in different places.
Derived from Lithuanian daug meaning "much" (see Daumantas) combined with Baltic vyd meaning "to see" (see Vytautas). Also compare other names that end in -vydas, such as Alvydas and Tautvydas.
Feminine form of Daugvydas. Also compare Daugaviete.
Old English form of David, deriving from Latin Dauid.
Late Greek form of Dauid (See David).

Derived from Lithuanian daug meaning "much" (see Daumantas) combined with the Lithuanian verb joti meaning "to ride horseback". In other words: this given name is basically the same as Jodaugas, but with the name elements in different places.
From the Arabic Davlat and feminine name element бикә (bikä).
Means "nothing can be compared to a father" in Ijaw.
From the words дәулет (daulet), meaning "wealth", and бек (bek), a military title.

Etymology uncertain, possibly derived from Greek δαῦλος (daulos) meaning "bushy, leafy, dense", "forest, thicket", and figuratively "intricate, inscrutable", or from the related δαλός (dalos) meaning "firebrand, torch". This was the name of a nymph in Greek mythology, the supposed namesake of an Ancient Greek settlement. She was a daughter of the local river-god Cephisus.
From Sino-Korean 多 (da) meaning "many" combined with 雲 (un) meaning “cloud”. Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

Means "much desire", derived from Lithuanian daug meaning "much" (see Daumantas) combined with the Lithuanian noun noras meaning "wish, desire", which is ultimately derived from the Lithuanian verb norėti meaning "to wish, to want, to desire".
The word dauntless can be traced back to Latin domare, meaning "to tame" or "to subdue."
The name of at least three different figures in Greek mythology.

Meaning unknown; it was found in a baptismal register from Seville in the 15th century, although the sex and age of the bearer were not recorded. It was revived in the 1970s in the Canary Islands as a feminine name.
From Kazakh дәурен (dauren) meaning "time, period, era" combined with the Turkic military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".
Short form or variant of Dauris. In the US it is likely used as a variant of Dory.
Albanian, Indonesian, Malay, Kabardian and Balkar form of Dawud (see David).

The name is composed of the Lithuanian elements 'daug-' meaning "many" and '-tarti' meaning "to say." Hence the name would roughly translate as meaning "talkative; loquacious" or as "someone who has a lot to say."
From Mongolian даваа (davaa) meaning "Monday" or "threshold, mountain pass" and дорж (dorj) meaning "diamond, vajra".
From Mongolian даваа (davaa) meaning "Monday" or "threshold, mountain pass" and жаргал (jargal) meaning "happiness, blessing".

Derived from Mongolian даваа (davaa) meaning "Monday" or "mountain pass, threshold" and жав (jav) meaning "salvation, deliverance"Probably of Tibetan Buddhist origin, meaning "moon of deliverance." The Mongolian definition of "Monday" for даваа (davaa) derives from Tibetan ཟླ་བ (zla ba) "moon, month; Monday". This is likely a reference to the bodhisattva "Moon of Deliverance" described in the Flower Garland Sutra of the Mahayana School of Buddhism.
From Mongolian даваа (davaa) meaning "Monday" or "threshold, mountain pass" and хүү (khüü) meaning "boy, son; child".
From Mongolian даваа (davaa) meaning "Monday" or "threshold, mountain pass" and ням (nyam) meaning "Sunday".
From Mongolian даваа (davaa) meaning "Monday" or "threshold, mountain pass" combined with Tibetan ཚེ་རིང (tshe ring) meaning "long life, longevity".
From Mongolian даваа (davaa) meaning "Monday" or "mountain pass, threshold" combined with the name Tseren.
Either a feminine form of David or an elaboration of Vada. A notable bearer was Davada "Dee" Stanley Presley (1925-2013), the stepmother of singer Elvis Presley.
Means “wanderer” in Maragoli, given to baby girls.
Davalon The Proud is one of Arthur’s knights in Heinrich von dem Türlin’s "Diu Crône". The name is corrupted and split from Guigomar d’Avalon, found in Chrétien’s Erec.
Allegedly a feminization of David via its short form Dave and the popular name suffix -lynn.
Possible variant of Devana or Devona, or from the name of a plant called Davana.

Derived from the archaic Persian word داور (davar) meaning "judge", which ultimately comes from Middle Persian dādwar meaning "judge".In Georgian literature, Davar is the name of a character from the 12th-century epic poem The Knight in the Panther's Skin written by the Georgian poet Shota Rustaveli. She is the sister of king Parsadan of India and aunt to his daughter Nestan-Darejan.
Variant of Davari, which is possibly an invented name based on names such as Davon, Dakari, Javari and Levar.
DaVarryl Williamson (b. 1968) is an American boxer.
Variant and feminine form of Davey.
Possibly a variant of Davina influenced by names like Maureen and Loreen.
Modern coinage, a feminine form of David. Actress Daveigh Chase is a famous bearer.
Presumably a feminization of David combining its short form Dave with the common feminine name suffix -line.
Davenie is the birth name of Joey Heatherton (born September 14, 1944), an American actress, dancer, and singer.
Transferred use of the surname Davenport.
Catalan and Aragonese form of David.
Feminine form of Davian or a combination of da and Aviana.
Diminutive of David, only used in European Spanish.
Occitan and Piedmontese form of David.
Sicilian and Sardinian form of David.
Extremely rare feminization of David by way of combining it with the popular feminine name suffix -ella.
Feminine form of David used in Prince Edward Island, Canada and possibly amongst Irish.
Sicilian and Campidanese Sardinian form of Davide.
Bulgarian and Vlach diminutive of David.
Variant of Dāvids without the macron.
Transferred use of the surname Davidson.
Medieval Italian diminutive of Davide, as -uccio is an Italian masculine diminutive suffix.
Elaboration of Dave with popular suffix -en.
Perhaps from Old Slavic давати (davati), meaning "to give".
Transferred use of the surname Davila.
Possibly a combination of David an the popular suffix -mar (cf. Leomar, Gladimar).

Derived from Leonardo da Vinci, with da Vinci meaning "of Vinci". Vinci is a village in Italy location near Florence, and it was the hometown of Leonardo da Vinci. The town's name is possibly derived from the Latin vincere 'to win or vanquish'.
Derived from Persian دولت (dowlat) meaning "state, government, country" combined with the name Ali 1.
From Uzbek davlat or Tajik давлат (davlat) both meaning "government, state" combined with the Turkic military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".
Derived from the Uzbek davlat meaning "country" or "wealth, fortune, happiness" and gul meaning "flower, rose".
Derived from the Uzbek davlat meaning "country" or "wealth, fortune, happiness" and jahon meaning "the world".
Derived from the Uzbek davlat meaning "country" or "wealth, fortune, happiness" and jamol meaning "beauty".
Derived from the Uzbek davlat meaning "country" or "wealth, fortune, happiness" and oy meaning "moon".
Derived from the Uzbek davlat meaning "country" or "wealth, fortune, happiness" and poshsha, an endearing name for a girl or woman.
Derived from the Uzbek davlat meaning "country" or "wealth, fortune, happiness" and safar meaning "trip, journey".
Combination of the prefix Da and the name Yvonne.
Name of a main character in George R. R. Martin's fantasy series, A Song of Ice and Fire.
Derived from Persian دوران (dowran) meaning "time, period, era".
Combination of Davran with the Turkish military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".
Tajik and Uzbek form of Davranbek.
Derived from the Uzbek davron meaning "ages, epochs" and gul meaning "flower, rose".
From the given name Davron combined with jon meaning "soul, life"
Derived from the Uzbek davron meaning "ages, epochs" and oy meaning "moon".
Allegedly a Yiddish form of Deborah.
Lithuanian form of David. Also compare Dovydas.A known bearer of this name is the Lithuanian soccer player Davydas Arlauskis (b. 1986).
Variant of Davin. Davynn was given to 6 girls in 2012 according to the SSA.
Variant of Duane, utilizing a combination of the prefix "Da-" and the name Wayne

column12: From Chinese 大 (dà) meaning "big, great, vast, high" combined with 为 (wéi) meaning "act, make, become", 卫 (wèi) meaning "guard, protect", 維 (wéi) meaning "maintain, preserve", 渭 (wèi) referring to the Wei River in Shaanxi province, 畏 (wèi) meaning "fear, dread, respect", or 伟 (wěi) meaning "great, robust, extraordinary", or 位 (wèi) meaning "place, position, location"; or from the English given name David. Other hanzi combinations are possible.
The name of the swing guittarist Daweli Reinhardt.
From the Arabic name of the Mediterranean fan palm tree.
Variant of Donna with the influence of Dawn.
Variant spelling of both Dawn and its diminutive Dawnie. The pronunciation of the name depends on which of the two Dawne is based on, which is something that will differ from person to person.
Most likely an elaboration of Dawn by way of combining it with the popular name suffix -elle.
Elaborated form of Dawn. Also compare Dawna, Donetta and Donnetta.
Possibly an elaborated form of Dawn influenced by Danette.
Diminutive of Daniel, Andrew and occasionally Donald.
Variant form of Dawn, which may possibly have come into being via its diminutive Dawnie. Also compare Dawnya.
Combination of Dawn and Danielle. Per the SSA 13 girls were given this name in 1975.
Rare variant of Dawn. A notable bearer is American actress Dawnn Lewis (1961-).
A variant of Dawn with the name suffix -ya, perhaps influenced by Sonya.
Variant of Danielle, perhaps inspired by Dawn.
From Sino-Korean 多 "much, many; more than, over" (da), and 元 "first; dollar; origin; head" or 媛 "beauty, beautiful woman" (won).
From Sino-Korean 多 "much, many; more than, over" and 運 "luck, fortune; ship, transport" or 雲 (un) "clouds".
Transferred use of the surname Dawsey. Also a diminutive of Dawes. It was the name of a character in the novel 'The Guernsey Literary and Potato Peel Pie Society' (2008) by Mary Ann Shaffer.
Medieval Russian, Medieval Ukrainian form of David. Also an alternate transcription in Ukrainian language.
Derived from Circassian дахэ (dāxă) meaning "beautiful, pretty" and нагъуэ (năġ°ă) meaning "brown-eyed". Daxenaghwe is a minor character in the Circassian Nart sagas.
From the Chinese 大 (dà) meaning "big, great" and 效 (xiào) meaning "result, effect".
From Chinese 大 (dà) meaning "big, great, vast, high" and 燮 (xiè) meaning "to harmonize, harmonious".
From the Chinese 大 (dà) meaning "big, great" and 星 (xīng) meaning "star, planet, point of light".
An invented name, made to rhyme with Jaxon influenced by Dax.
A variant of Dexter likely influenced by the name Daxton.
From the Chinese 大 (dà) meaning "big, great" and 学 (xué) meaning "learning, knowledge".
From the Chinese 大 (dà) meaning "big, great" and 勋 (xūn) meaning "meritorious deeds, merits".
From the Old English dæġ, from the Proto-Germanic dagaz, from the Proto-Indo-European dʰegʷʰ- meaning 'to burn'.
Meaning unknown. Dayami Sánchez (1994-) is a Cuban volleyball player.
Perhaps intended to be the masculine form of Dayana or a femenine variant of Diane reflecting the English pronunciation.
Derived from an Arabic word meaning "mister".
Derived from Kalmyk даянч (dayanch) meaning "hermit, monk".
From daýanç meaning "support" and gylyç meaning "sword".
Means "young lady, girl, maid" in Malay. It is usually used as an honorific, not an actual given name.
This name means “Goddess of Compassion”, and originated from Sanskrit.
Dayaw has no exactly one translation in English language because it can mean extremely beautiful or friendly or strongor have an extremely comely face and appearance
Means "moon" in Somali. A well-known bearer is Dayax Dalnuurshe, an award-winning Somali musical artist.
Presumably a feminine form of Dadrian, the spelling altered to resemble the word daydream. This spelling appears to be unique.
Means "diverse, versatile, multi-talented" from Sino-Korean 多樣.
From Sino-Vietnamese 夜宴 (dạ yến) meaning "evening banquet".
A more phonetical spelling of Diane, perhaps based on Dayana or Cheyenne.
From Sino-Korean 多 (da) meaning "much, many" combined with 英 (yeong) meaning "flower, petal, brave, hero". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
Dayindi is a main character in Australian film "Ten Canoes".
Possibly a feminine form of Dale, or a variant of Dahlia.
An invented name made to sound like the names Kaylani or Jaylani.
Variant of Dale. Famous masculine bearer was an actor Dale Robertson whose birth name was Dayle Lymoine Robertson.

Variant of Daley or a combination of Dale or the element day with the name element suffix lee found in names such as Kaylee.According to the USA Social Security Administration, 27 baby girls were given the name Daylee in 2010.
Combination of Day and the popular name suffix -leen or variant of Daylene.
Feminine elaboration of Dale using the popular suffix lene.
Variant of Dahlia reflecting the DAYL-yə pronunciation.
Plural of daylily. A flower that bears large yellow, red, or orange flowers, each flower lasting only one day.
From a type of flower. A lily that bears large yellow, red, or orange flowers, each flower lasting only one day.
Likely an invented name based on the sound of Aylín, possibly influenced by Dayana.
Possibly an invented name blending Dale and Waylon, perhaps influenced by Dylan.

Medieval form of the Old English name Dæglufu deriving from the Old English name element dæg meaning "day" and the Old English name element lufu meaning "love". For the name with the same elements but reversed see Loveday
Variant of Daelyn using the word day.
Most likely a variant of Dion.
From Sino Korean 多 (da) meaning "a lot, much" and and 潤 (yun) meaning "soft, sleek".
Diminutive of Dayotchanculle, notably borne by the French soccer player Dayot Upamecano (1998-).

Meaning as of yet unknown. This is the full first name of the French soccer player Dayot Upamecano (b. 1998), who is of Bissau-Guinean descent. He was named after his great-grandfather, who was the leader of a village on the island of Jeta in Guinea-Bissau.
From the Chinese 大 (dà) meaning "big, great" and 佑 (yòu) meaning "help, protect".
Alternate transcription of Korean Hangul 다영 (see Da-yeong).
An invented name, using the phonetic elements day and quan, and sharing a sound with other names such as Daquan and Raekwon.
Variant of Deja, or simply a combination of the popular phonetic elements day and sha.
Combination of the phonetic elements day, sha and nay. Also compare Dejanae, Dajanae.
Combination of the phonetic element day with the name Shawn.
A combination of the English word day and the popular suffix -shia.
Spanish and Portuguese variant of Daisy.
Transferred use of the surname Dayson.
Referring to the sun; a famous bearer being Canadian rapper Daystar Peterson, professionally known as Tory Lanez.

Possibly from the name of Daytona Beach, a coastal city in northeastern Florida (U.S.), which was founded in 1870 by Mathias Day, Jr., and is famous for its car races. It could also be thought of as a feminine variant of Dayton.

column3: 다율(Korean Hangul)|多律, 多聿, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 多 (da) meaning "many" combined with 律 (yul) meaning "law" or 聿 (yul) meaning "(paint) brush". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
A pet form for Darren in Britain and Australia, paralleling similar constructions such as Gaz for Gary, Caz for Caroline, Shaz for Sharon or Charlotte, etc.
An ancient name of unknown etymology. This was the original name of Galerius Valerius Maximinus (270-313).
Contraction of да здраствует первое Мая (da zdrastvuet pervoye Maya) meaning "long live the first of May". This date refers to the International Workers' Day.

Contraction of Russian Да здравствует первый трактор! (Da zdravstvuet pervyy traktor!) meaning "Long live the first tractor!" This name was created by Communist parents who were eager to reject traditional names. It was used to celebrate and/or commemorate the production of tractors, which in Russia first began in 1923.
Variant of Dazdrapertrak. This name was used by Communist parents who were eager to reject traditional names.
From the Chinese 大 (dà) meaning "big, great" and 昭 (zhāo) meaning "bright, luminous, illustrious".

Contraction of the Soviet slogan Да здравствует мировая революция! (Da zdravstvuet mirovaya revolyutsiya!) meaning "Long live the world revolution!" as well as of Да здравствует мир! (Da zdravstvuet mir!) meaning "Long live the peace!" This name was created by Communist parents who were eager to reject traditional names.
Feminine form of Dazmir. This name was created by Communist parents who were eager to reject traditional names.
A frequentative of the Middle English word *dasen*, meaning "be stunned, be bewildered".
From the English word dazzling combined with the ending lyn.

In the case of former American football player D'Brickashaw Ferguson (1983-), it is inspired by de Bricassart, the surname of a character in the 1977 novel and 1983 television miniseries 'The Thorn Birds'. The character, Irish priest Father Ralph de Bricassart, claims his surname is of Norman origin, however it appears to be invented.
From Sino-Vietnamese 提 (đề) meaning "to lift, increase, nominate", 媞 (đề) meaning "at ease", or 題 (đề) meaning "title".
Perhaps a variant of Đế. It also means "to place, set, in order to" in Vietnamese.
From Chinese 德 (dé) meaning "virtue; morality; favor; mind", or other characters with similar pronunciations.
Derived from Latin dea "goddess". This is also a diminutive of Andréa and Dorotéia.
Means "goddess" in Italian. It can also be used as a short form of Dorotea, Andrea 2 and Desideria.
Combination of the popular name prefix de and Aaron.
Combination of the popular name prefix da and Adrian.
Personal name of uncertain origin. It may be a compound of deagh- ‘good’ + ádh ‘luck’, ‘fate’.

Means "apt to hide, secretive" in Old English. This name was invented by J.R.R. Tolkien for a minor character in his novel 'The Lord of the Rings' (1954). This is the Old English translation or cognate of the "true" Westron name Nahald (as Tolkien pretended that his writings were translated from the fictional 'Red Book of Westmarch'). In the first volume, 'The Fellowship of the Ring', the hobbit Déagol discovers the One Ring, after its being lost for hundreds of years, in the Gladden river while fishing with his friend Sméagol. He is choked to death by Sméagol after refusing to give it up; his body is hidden and never found.
Variant of DeAsia or Deja. It can be spelled Deajah or with a capitalized third letter as DeAjah.
Variant of Deacon or a transferred use of the surname Deakin.
Diminutive of Medea via its short form Dea.
Transferred use of the surname Deakon and variant of Deacon.

Dealgnait was the name of a minor goddess worshipped in Deal, Kent in present-day England. Her functions are not entirely clear: it has been specualted that she was either a fertility goddess or a goddess of death.
From English phrase "the love". Its usage is popularized by the love song Dealova by Opick in Indonesia.
Elaboration of Dea and variant of Dejana.
Combination of the popular name prefix De and Andrea 2 (compare Deandra, DeAndre, Deanna).
Combination of the popular name prefix de and Andreas.
Combination of the popular name prefix de and Andrew.
Elaboration of Deandra or combination of popular prefix De- with Andrea 2.
Combination of the prefix De- and the given name Angel (See also DeAngelo and Deangela).
Combination of Angela with the prefix De-, making it the feminine form of DeAngelo.
Variant of Danica, influenced by Dean.
Feminization of Dean, used rarely but steadily.
Most likely a diminutive of Dean (compare Danno), or possibly an anglicized variant of Dino.
Variant of Deonte. It can be spelled DeAntae or Deantae.
Combination of the prefix De- and Anthony.
Possibly a variant of Darrell and similar names, or from the surname Dearle.
Variant of Diara. It can be spelled as Dearra or De'arra.
Combination of the popular name prefix de and Asia 1, or a variant of Deja.
Transferred use of the surname Deaton.
Combination of the popular name prefix De and Avery.
A spelling variant of Devin and Devon Uncommon spelling, pronounced the same.
Vietnamese form of Devadatta, from Sino-Vietnamese 提婆達多 (đề-bà-đạt-đa).
Korean and Odia form of Devadatta, used only to refer to the Buddhist figure in Korean.
From the Chinese 德 (dé) meaning "heart, mind, morals, ethics, virtues" and 帮 (bāng) meaning "help, assist, defend".
Possibly an Hispanic variant of Devany. This is chiefly used in Monterrey, Nuevo León, Mexico.
Alternate transcription of Bengali দেবাশীষ or Odia ଦେବାଶିଷ (see Debasish).
Alternate transcription of Bengali দেবাশীষ or Odia ଦେବାଶିଷ (see Debasish).
debashree "devi" means goddess "shree" means beautiful the whole is debashree is most beautiful among all the goddess in the heaven.
Alternate transcription of Bengali দেবাশীষ or Odia ଦେବାଶିଷ (see Debasish).
Means "blessing of the gods" from Sanskrit देव (deva) meaning "god" combined with आशिष (āśiṣa) meaning "prayer, blessing".
Probably a blend of Debbie with the suffix -on. Debbon Ayer bears this name, who is Rob Morrow's spouse.
Diminutive of Deborah. A notable bearer is Debbye Turner Bell (1965-), a TV host, veterinarian and former pageant winner.
From the Chinese 德 (dé) meaning "heart, mind, morals, ethics, virtues" and 炳 (bǐng) meaning "bright, luminous, glorious".
A hypocoristic form of Debora.Debinha is a Brazilian football player and member of the 2019 FIFA women 's world cup team.
From French débonnaire meaning ''suave and refined''.
Catalan and Piedmontese form of Deborah.
Icelandic and Hungarian form of Debora.
Possibly a masculine form of Deborah.
A combination of the names Debra and Ana, the fusion possibly influenced by the name Brianna.

Combination of the prefix de- and the name Cameron.This name coincides with the word decameron, which comes from Italian Decamerone, a collection of 100 novellas supposedly told over 10 days by Italian author Giovanni Boccaccio, meaning "ten days" (from Ancient Greek δέκα (déka) meaning "ten" combined with ἡμέρᾱ (hēmérā) meaning "day.")
Used on a video game character from the Street Fighter series. It is likely derived from дека́брь (dekábrʹ), the Russian word for December.
Transferred use of the surname DeCarlo, or a combination the popular name element da and the given name Carlo.
Combination of the popular name prefix de and Carlos.
Probably transferred use of the surname Decater
Transferred use of the surname Decatur.
Likely a variant of Deca, influenced by the famous record label Decca Records, founded in 1929 in England. Could also be a variable for any name containing the element -dec/k-.
Deceneus was a priest of Dacia during the reign of Burebista (82/61–45/44 BC).
Late Roman female equivalent to Decentius

Probably derived from the Latin noun decentia meaning "decency, comeliness", which is related to Latin decens "fitting, appropriate, decent, worthy". Both words are ultimately derived from the Latin verb decēre "to be fitting, to be suitable, to be worthy". A bearer of this name was Magnus Decentius, a Roman usurper from the 4th century AD.
Decetto or deceit is an enemy of Timias in Book 6, Canto 5 of "The Faerie Queene". He is in league with the Blatant Beast.
Derived from Thai เดช (det), meaning "power, might, authority".
Means "power" or "heat, fire" in Thai, ultimately from Sanskrit तेजस् (tejas).

From Chinese 德 (dé) meaning "ethics, morality, virtue" combined with 昌 (chāng) meaning "flourish, prosper, good, sunlight" or 常 (cháng) meaning "common, frequent, regular". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
Variant of Deshaun as a combination of da and Chaun. It can be spelled DeChaun, De'Chaun or Dechaun.
From Chinese 德 (dé) meaning "ethics, morality, virtue" combined with 成 (chéng) meaning "success or achieve"
Possibly a variant spelling of Dessie or a short form of names containing dec.
Spanish and Portuguese form of Decimus.
Transferred use of the surname Decker. This was used for a character on the American soap opera General Hospital: Decker Moss, a character that debuted on the show in 1989.

An important goddess (or perhaps god, known as Declunus) of the Volscians, an ancient people of Italy who were frequently at war with the Romans and subsequently conquered and assimilated. Specific knowledge of the god has been lost but he (or she) was perhaps a fertility deity.

An important god (or perhaps goddess, known as Decluna) of the Volscians, an ancient people of Italy who were frequently at war with the Romans and subsequently conquered and assimilated. Specific knowledge of the god has been lost but he (or she) was perhaps a fertility deity.
A variant of Declan sometimes used as a feminized form.
Short for "decoration". Comes from a YouTube video by Ben Wheele.
Variant of Diegu via the form Diecu.
From the Chinese 德 (dé) meaning "heart, mind, morals, ethics, virtue" and 翠 (cuì) meaning "green, kingfisher".
Means "large, chief" in Latin, derived from Latin decumanus meaning "tenth". This was the name of one of the Celtic saints who came to Somerset from Pembrokeshire (-706).
Croatian, Polish and Romanian form of Daedalus.

Dedalij is a giant and mighty figure in Albanian mythology (similar to Gigantes, Titans in Greek mythology). The name itself is of uncertain origin and meaning; theories include a derivation from an older form of Albanian tëtanë "everyone; all; of the people" (ultimately derived from an earlier *tetan ""of the people").
Spanish and Portuguese form of Daedalus.
From the Chinese 德 (dé) meaning "heart, mind, morals, ethics, virtues" and 道 (dào) meaning "path, road, way".
East Frisian from of Theoda and other names containing the name element þeoda "people".

Portuguese (Brazilian) diminutive of Anderson. A famous bearer is Brazilian footballer Anderson Vital da Silva who is known as Dedé. He plays as a centre back or sweeper for Cruzeiro and the Brazilian national football team.
A fictional character and the primary antagonist in Nintendo's Kirby video game series.
Sundanese diminutive of feminine names containing the sound deh (or other similar sounds), such as Rosidah or Faridah.
Diminutive of names with Diet- such as Dieter or Dietlinde.
From the Javanese aristocratic title radèn given to descendants of nobility or royalty.
Feminine form of Dederico (Italian and Spanish), English variant of Dedericka and Dutch variant of Diederika.
Italian and Spanish form of Dederick. Also see Teodorico.
English variant of Dedericka and Dutch variant of Diederika.
Means "little mother" in Georgian. It is derived from the Georgian noun დედა (deda) meaning "mother" combined with the Georgian diminutive suffix -იკა (-ika). Also compare Mamuka.

Means "mother's hope" in Georgian. It is derived from Georgian დედის (dedis) meaning "of the mother" combined with the Georgian noun იმედი (imedi) meaning "hope" (see Imeda).This name was borne by a 16th-century princess consort of Samtskhe.

The first element of this name is probably derived from Old Church Slavonic dědŭ "grandfather", which is ultimately derived from Proto-Slavic dědъ "grandfather". The second element is derived from Slavic mir "peace". As such, the meaning of this name would roughly be "grandfather of peace".

The first element of this name is probably derived from Old Church Slavonic dědŭ "grandfather", which is ultimately derived from Proto-Slavic dědъ "grandfather". The second element is derived from Slavic slav "glory". As such, the meaning of this name would roughly be "grandfather of glory".
Short form of Dédéric, a variant form of Didéric. Also compare Déric.
Variant spelling of Dedrick (also compare Dédric). A known bearer of this name is Dedryck Boyata (b. 1990), a Belgian professional soccer player of Congolese descent.
Means "little mother" in Georgian. It is derived from the Georgian noun დედა (deda) meaning "mother" combined with the Georgian diminutive suffix -უკა (-uka). Also compare Mamuka.
Variant of Diandra or combination of Dee and Andra.
Variant of Deanna. It can be spelled Deeanna, DeeAnna or Dee Anna.
Means "silk, or eye of a mistress" in Sindhi. Also In the case of Pakistani film actress Deeba (1947-) and Indian-Muslim writer Deeba Salim Irfan (1969-).
This is the name of a prominent elf in the anime and games series 'Lodoss Wars'.
Dutchization of the English name Dave.
Transferred use of the surname Deegan.
Phonetic spelling of the initials DJ.
Probably a variant of Deacon or transferred use of the surname Deekin.
The combination of Dee and Lana
The name Deema comes from the Arabic origin. In Arabic the meaning of the Deema is Rain cloud

This was the personal name of a mistress (this is English translation of her rank within the imperial harem, this relationship wasn't considered extra-marital) of Hong Taiji. She was from the Cilei clan and was the mother of his fourteenth daughter.
Diminutive of feminine names ending in deen, dene or dine. For example, Wilmadeene 'Deenie' Fenner is the protagonist of Judy Blume's young adult novel Deenie (1973).

Deeown comes from the names Declan, Deecan, Owen and Wesley. It’s a name most commonly used by African Americans in the 1960s with three children being named Deeown from 1961-1965. No one has been named Deeown since 1992 when it suddenly disappeared.
From Sanskrit दीप (dipa) meaning "lamp, light" and शिखा (śíkhā) meaning "plume; peacock's crest."
This means "light, glow, shine and brilliant". It can also mean "a person who spreads light in the world"
South Indian and Sinhala form of Dipti.
Elaboration of Eric using popular prefex De-.
Short form of Desiderius and Désiré (masculine) as well as Desideria and Désirée (feminine).
Alternative Santali name of the Hindu goddess Lakshmi.
Combination of the popular name prefix de and Etta.
its a historical name its used for a policeman.
From the Chinese 德 (dé) meaning "heart, mind, morals, ethics, virtues" and 放 (fàng) meaning "release, free, liberate".

Probably a combination of the popular name prefix De (see Deshawn) with a name that ends in -fano, such as Stefano.Although he spells his name with a diacritic, a known bearer of this name is Défano Holwijn (b. 1992), a Dutch rapper of Surinamese descent.

Derived from Late Latin defendere meaning "to defend, to protect". The soldier-saint Defendens of Thebes (Italian: San Defendente di Tebe) was, according to Christian tradition, a member of the Theban Legion, and thus martyred at Agaunum. He is venerated as a martyr by the Catholic Church.

column3: 德锋, etc.(Chinese)|德鋒, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 德 (dé) meaning "ethics, morality, virtue" combined with 锋 (fēng) meaning "pointed edge, flattening edge". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
Defetto or defect is an enemy of Timias in Book 6, Canto 5 of "The Faerie Queene". He is in league with the Blatant Beast.
Derived from the English word denoting a disposition to resist.
Transferred use of the surname Deford. Notable namesake is Tennessee blues musician DeFord Bailey (1899-1982).
Derived from Albanian dëfrim "entertainment, amusement; fun".
From the Chinese 德 (dé) meaning "heart, mind, morals, ethics, virtue" and 芙 (fú) meaning "hibiscus".

Means "Two River Currents Flowing Together" in Iroquois. This was the name of a historical figure commonly known as the Great Peacemaker as he was known as, along with Jigonhsasee and Hiawatha, the founder of the Haudenosaunee, commonly called the Iroquois Confederacy. As a mark of respect, some Iroquois avoid using his personal name except in special circumstances.

Means "two rivers running" in Oneida. Possibly from the Oneida tékni 'two' and -wyhuhatatye- 'river running along'.A noted bearer is the Great Peacekeeper, whose birthname was Deganawida. He was, along with Hiawatha, by tradition the founder of the Haudenosaunee, commonly called the Iroquois Confederacy, a political and cultural union of several Native American tribes residing in the present-day state of New York. The union created a powerful alliance of related Iroquoian peoples around the Great Lakes. Historians believe the confederacy may have formed in the 13th or 14th centuries.
From the Chinese 德 (dé) meaning "heart, mind, morals, ethics, virtues" and 高 (gāo) meaning "high, tall, lofty".

Combination of the Chinese character 德 (see De) and 根 (see Gen).Other characters combinations are also possible.A famous bearer is Chen Degen, a Chinese cross-country skier who competes internationally. He represented his country at the 2022 Winter Olympics.
From the Chinese 德 (dé) meaning "heart, mind, morals, ethics, virtues" and 耿 (gěng) meaning "bright, shining".
Derived from the Old High German elements degan "soldier, warrior" and heri "army".
Italian and Sardinian form of Digna. In modern Italian, degna also means "worthy, deserving".
Transferred use of the surname De Graft.
Meaning famous, great, a star in hebrew.
From 德 (dé) meaning "virtue, ethics, morality" and 行 (haang) meaning "to walk".
From the name of British politician and MP Dehenna Davison.
Variant of Daylani likely inspired by the spelling of Kehlani.

column3: 德鸿, 德宏, 德洪, etc.(Chinese)|德鴻, 德宏, 德洪, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 德 (dé) meaning "ethics, morality, virtue" combined with 鸿 (hóng) meaning "wild swan, great, vast", 宏 (hóng) meaning "wide, spacious, great, vast" or 洪 (hóng) meaning "flood, deluge, great, vast". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 德华, etc.(Chinese)|德華, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 德 (dé) meaning "ethics, morality, virtue" combined with 华 (huá) meaning "splendid, illustrious, flowery, Chinese". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From the Chinese 德 (dé) meaning "heart, mind, morals, ethics, virtues" and 欢 (huān) meaning "joyous, merry, happy".
Originally a diminutive of Dafydd and Dewi 1, used as a given name in its own right.
Possibly from Old Irish deich, meaning "ten", and tine meaning "fire" or tíre, "land, country". This was the name of the mother of Cúchulainn, whom she conceived with Lugh.
French form of Deicolus. Even though the saint was male, this name was also occasionally used on women.

Of uncertain origin and meaning; theories include a Latinization of the Irish Dícuil. Deicolus was a Christian saint of Irish origin who lived in the 7th century during the pontificate of Pope Vigilius. He may have been a brother of Saint Gallus and is said to have accompanied Columbanus to Luxeuil, France. When Columbanus was expelled in 610, Deicolus was too ill to accompany him and remained behind in the Vosges where he built a hermitage in the vale of Orignon. His cult survived in the areas of Lure, Alsace, Bourgogne and Franche-Comté into the twentieth century.
Means "deity" in Spanish, a word derived from Latin deitās (which in turn was coined by Augustine of Hippo, who derived it from Latin deus meaning "god").

From Greek Δηιδάμεια (Deidameia), possibly derived from δηιόω (dêioô) "to destroy" (cf. Deianira) and δαμάζειν (damazein) "to tame". This was the name of several historical women, including the daughter of King Pyrrhus II of Epirus, the last surviving representative of the royal Aeacid dynasty who was assassinated in the Temple of Artemis (c.239/229 BCE). Another was a daughter of Aeacides, king of Epirus and his wife, Queen Phthia, and sister of King Pyrrhus, who was at one time betrothed by her father to Alexander IV, the son of Roxana and Alexander the Great.In Greek mythology, this is another name of Hippodamia, Laodamia; and possibly the mother of Iphicles. Deidamia is also the name of one of King Lycomedes's daughters who gave sanctuary to Achilles, and with whom she had a son Neoptolemus. She is mentioned by Dante in his 'Inferno' (14th century). This name is also borne by the main character in the opera of the same name by Georg Friedrich Händel (1740), which is about the Deidamia who married Achilles.

Deidara means clay bender in japanese-------------------------------------The origin of the name is unknown, however, it is the name of a fictional antagonist from the animated series "Naruto".The meaning of "Deidara" is mud.
Russian, Bulgarian, Ukrainian and Serbian form of Deiphobus.
Romanian, Polish and Norwegian form of Deiphobus.

From Japanese 庭 (dei) meaning "garden" combined with 司 (jii) meaning "to take charge of; to control; to manage". Other kanji combinations are possible.Usage of this name is, most likely, influenced by the name and word Daisy.
Local form of Deicolus found in the Bourgogne-Franche-Comté region up until the 1800s.

Derived from Ancient Greek δήϊος (deios) meaning "burning, blazing, destroying, hostile" and λέων (leon) meaning "lion". This was the name of a son of King Deimachus of Thessaly in Greek mythology, also called Demoleon by Plutarch. It was also the name of a Greek soldier in the Trojan war.

The first element of this name is derived from the Epic Greek adjective δήϊος (deios) meaning "hostile, destructive" as well as "unhappy, wretched". It is related to the Greek verb δηϊόω (deioo) meaning "to slay, to cut down" (see Deianeira).The second element of this name is derived from the Greek noun λόχος (lochos) meaning "ambush", a word that later came to signify a tactical sub unit of the ancient Greek army. The word is ultimately derived from the Greek verb λοχάω (lochao) meaning "to lie in wait for, to waylay" as well as "to snare".
Latinized form of Deilochos. In Greek mythology, this is the name of two separate characters who were both slain by Tydeus during the War of the Seven against Thebes.
Feminine form of Deile found in the Bourgogne-Franche-Comté region up until the 1800s.
Means "white leaves" from Welsh dail "leaves" (singulative deilen) combined with gwen "white, fair, blessed".

Latinized form of the Greek name Δηΐμαχος (Deimachos), derived from δηιόω (deioo) meaning "to slay" (compare Deilochos) and μάχη (mache) meaning "battle". A noted historical bearer was Deimachus, a 3rd-century BC Greek of the Seleucid Empire who became an ambassador to the court of Bindusara 'Amitragata' (son of Chandragupta Maurya) in Pataliputra in India. He apparently wrote extensively on ancient India and is quoted as a reference in geographical matters, but his works are now lost. This was also the name of several men in Greek mythology.
Masculine form of Deimantė. Known bearers of this name include the Lithuanian soccer players Deimantas Bička (b. 1972) and Deimantas Petravičius (b. 1995).
Allegedly a Hispanicized form of Deiñe.
Derived from Greek δεινός (deinos) meaning "terrible, fearsome; mighty, powerful" and ἀρχός (archos) meaning "ruler, leader, master".
Derived from either Basque dei "call; announcement" or deikunde "announcement; Annunciation", this name is considered a Basque equivalent of Anunciación.
Possibly derived from Greek δεινός (deinos) meaning "fearful, terrible, dread, dire" or δίνη (dine) meaning "whirlpool, eddy". This was the name of several characters in Greek myth.
Means "terrible power", derived from the Greek elements δεινός (deinos) "fearful, terrible" and κρατος (kratos) "power".
Derived from Greek δεινός (deinos) meaning "terrible, fearsome; mighty, powerful" and λόχος (lochos) meaning "ambush, trap".
Feminine form of Deinomachos. This was the name of Alcibiades' mother.
Derived from Ancient Greek δεινός (deinos) meaning "fearful, terrible" as well as "mighty, skilful, wondrous" combined with μάχη (mache) meaning "battle".
Means "terrible strength", derived from the Greek elements δεινός (deinos) "fearful, terrible, marvellous, skilful" and μένος (menos) "mind, courage, strength, spirit".
Derived from Ancient Greek δεινός (deinos) meaning "fearful, terrible" as well as "mighty, powerful" combined with φίλος (philos) meaning "friend, lover; beloved, dear".
Derived from Greek δεινός (deinos) meaning "terrible, fearsome; mighty, powerful" and σθένος (sthenos) meaning "vigour, strength".
Means "terrible army", derived from the Greek elements δεινός (deinos) "fearful, terrible" and στρατος (stratos) "army".
Hellenized form of Old Persian Dahyuka. This was the name of the first king of the Medes according to Herodotus.

Said to mean "ravager", from Ancient Greek δηιόω (dêioô) "to cut down, slay; to waste or ravage a country" (compare the first element in Deianeira). This was the name of several characters in Greek mythology.
A modern invented name, based on Deion.
Theorised original form of Leipephilene, perhaps derived from Ancient Greek δήϊος (deios) meaning "hostile, destructive; burning" and φίλος (philos) meaning "friend, lover; beloved".

Feminine form of Deiphobos. In Greek and Roman mythology, Deiphobe was a daughter of the seer Glaukos, an oracle of Apollo at Cumae in Italy, and later became known as the Cumaean Sybil. It was from her that the last king of Rome, Tarquin the Proud, received the three Sybilline Books that contained such important prophecies concerning Rome. She is mentioned in Virgil's "Aeneid."
Latinized form of Deiphobos. In Greek mythology, this is the name of one of the sons of king Priam of Troy.

Probably derived from Ancient Greek δάϊος (daios) meaning "hostile, destructive, burning" and the suffix φόντης (phontes) meaning "slayer of" (see φόνος (phonos) "murder, slaughter"). This was the name of a king of Argos in Greek mythology.
Derived from Ancient Greek δηιόω (dêioô) meaning "to destroy" and πύλη (pyle) meaning "gate, door".

Dejah Thoris is the name of a fictional character and princess of the Martian city-state/empire of Helium on the planet Barsoom (Mars) in American author Edgar Rice Burroughs's series of Martian novels (the first of which was published in 1912). She is the love interest and later the wife of John Carter, an Earthman mystically transported to Mars, and subsequently the mother of their son Carthoris and daughter Tara. She plays the role of the conventional damsel in distress who must be rescued from various perils, but is also portrayed as a competent and capable adventurer in her own right, fully capable of defending herself and surviving on her own in the wastelands of Mars. She is also the star of Dynamite's comic series 'Warlord of Mars: Dejah Thoris'. She was portrayed by American actress Traci Lords in the straight-to-DVD adaptation 'Princess of Mars', and by American actress Lynn Collins in the Disney film 'John Carter'.Usage of this name may be because of the character, or as a variant of Deja.

Dēkla is a Latvian goddess of fate and the sister of the goddesses Laima and Kārta. In old Latvian folk songs Laima and Dēkla are often considered one and the same goddess and their names are used interchangeably. Occasionally, however, the three sisters are ascribed their own, separate functions: Kārta holds power over the adult's life, Laima is concerned with mothers and childbirth and Dēkla is in charge of children.While the original meaning of the name is lost to time, folk etymology, along with earlier studies, often considers Dēkla a Latvian variant of Tekla, no doubt thanks to their phonetic similarity.
